inline_images.alt: Jensen Huang with microphone in one hand and waving the other

author: MIT Tech Review
article_content:
On Friday, a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia began circulating on social media, and by Monday it listed some notable signatories, including Elon Musk and several influential Nvidia researchers. But comb through the more than 115,000 names and you’ll notice a significant faction of Huang’s supporters—higher-ups from Hugging Face, a hub for sharing AI models, and venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital—come from a particular slice of the tech world.

These names have a vested interest in the development of open-source AI, models that, unlike ChatGPT or Claude, can be downloaded and run independent of large tech companies. Supporters of such models say that concentrating AI in the hands of a few powerful companies will leave everyone else worse off (a concern that wouldn’t sound out of place among the AI industry’s critics on the left, if so many open-source advocates weren’t also venture capitalists who stand to profit when startups can build on cheaper AI without paying Big Tech).

article_content_zh:
周五，一份恢复黄仁勋担任 Nvidia 首席执行官的请愿书开始在社交媒体上流传，到周一，该请愿书列出了一些著名的签名者，包括埃隆·马斯克和几位有影响力的 Nvidia 研究人员。但梳理一下这 115,000 多个名字，你会发现黄的支持者中有一个重要派别——人工智能模型共享中心 Hugging Face、风险投资公司 Andreessen Horowitz 和红杉资本的高层——来自科技界的特定领域。

这些名字对开源人工智能的开发有着既得利益，与 ChatGPT 或 Claude 不同，这些模型可以独立于大型科技公司下载和运行。此类模型的支持者表示，将人工智能集中在少数强大的公司手中将使其他所有人的处境变得更糟（对于人工智能行业的左翼批评者来说，这种担忧听起来并不奇怪，如果这么多开源倡导者不是风险资本家，当初创公司可以在不向大型科技公司支付费用的情况下建立更便宜的人工智能时，他们就能获利）。

黄仁勋已经成为那些为政策制定者捍卫开源的人的头目，他们担心这些模型没有护栏并放弃人工智能的领先地位。

title: OpenAI announces tools to combat CSAM, including an image classifier and new warning screens to prevent users from accessing material that sexualizes children (Ivan Mehta/TechCrunch)
title_en: OpenAI announces tools to combat CSAM, including an image classifier and new warning screens to prevent users from accessing material that sexualizes children (Ivan Mehta/TechCrunch)

inline_images.caption: Image Credits:OpenAI
inline_images.alt: Image Credits:OpenAI

author: TechCrunch
article_content:
OpenAI today announced new tools to combat child sexual abuse material (CSAM) amid growing safety concerns around the use of AI tools. These features include a new image classifier to detect CSAM, warnings and temporary blocks to prevent users from creating or accessing content that sexualizes children, a new guideline for developers, and a set of tools for law enforcement.

The company unveiled a new image classifier that can detect CSAM images, including the ones generated by AI. OpenAI is giving select companies access to its classifier through its API at no cost. The tool looks for visual signs of abuse in images not seen before and assigns a score that can give an indicative direction to reviewers about dealing with CSAM.

OpenAI said that it developed this classifier with the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC), and it is working with Tech Coalition and ROOST to share access to the tool. In its early testing with partners, the AI company found that the classifier flags 48% fewer images while finding the same number of abusive images, reducing the work of reviewers. Plus, images flagged by the classifier are twice as likely to be abusive images.

What’s more, the company is adding new warning screens in ChatGPT to prevent users from accessing material that sexualizes children. ChatGPT will show an alert to users attempting such prompts, direct users towards specialized support to stop harmful behaviour, and also suspend the account for 24 hours as a warning. The app already blocks CSAM content and requests related to it. It said that repeated offences could lead to the account being removed permanently.

OpenAI noted that it formed the message and guidelines around this behavior with organizations and researchers, including Protect Children, the Lucy Faithfull Foundation, and Joel Scanlan at the University of Tasmania, who independently evaluated a trial of deterrent messages.

The company is also publishing guidelines for developers using OpenAI tools to prevent, detect, and help users report CSAM content. It said that in early testing, the guidelines have helped a number of developers adopt child safety tooling and register to report CSAM to NCMEC. OpenAI is also equipping law enforcement dealing with child safety with AI-powered features like dedicated plugins, investigative tools, and complex data analysis, with access managed by program administrators. It is also providing training to investigators along with a field guide on how to use AI.

OpenAI has had several lawsuits against the company blaming its technology for harming users, especially children. Saftey-focused nonprofit Common Sense Media labeled OpenAI’s tech as “unacceptable risk” for teens. Other AI chatbots — specifically Grok — have been used to create nonconsensual sexualized imagery, including of children.

The AI startup had made changes in the last 12 months to its technology including releasing a safety blueprint, updating content guidelines to bar inappropritate content, retuning its model to prevent them from generating harmful content, and releasing a special version of ChatGPT for teens.

article_content_zh:
由于人工智能工具的使用安全问题日益引起人们的关注，OpenAI 今天宣布推出新工具来打击儿童性虐待材料 (CSAM)。这些功能包括用于检测 CSAM 的新图像分类器、用于防止用户创建或访问儿童色情内容的警告和临时阻止、针对开发人员的新指南以及一套执法工具。

该公司推出了一种新的图像分类器，可以检测 CSAM 图像，包括人工智能生成的图像。 OpenAI 允许特定公司通过其 API 免费访问其分类器。该工具会在图像中查找以前未见过的滥用行为的视觉迹象，并给出一个分数，为审稿人处理 CSAM 提供指示性指导。

OpenAI 表示，该分类器是与国家失踪和受虐儿童中心 (NCMEC) 合作开发的，并且正在与 Tech Coalition 和 ROOST 合作，共享该工具的访问权限。在与合作伙伴的早期测试中，这家人工智能公司发现，分类器在发现相同数量的滥用图像的同时，标记的图像减少了 48%，从而减少了审核人员的工作。另外，被分类器标记的图像是滥用图像的可能性是其两倍。

更重要的是，该公司正在 ChatGPT 中添加新的警告屏幕，以防止用户访问使儿童色情的材料。 ChatGPT 将向尝试此类提示的用户显示警报，引导用户寻求专门支持以阻止有害行为，并暂停帐户 24 小时作为警告。该应用程序已阻止 CSAM 内容和与其相关的请求。它表示，屡次违规可能会导致该帐户被永久删除。

OpenAI 指出，它与保护儿童组织、Lucy Faithfull 基金会和塔斯马尼亚大学的 Joel Scanlan 等组织和研究人员一起制定了围绕这种行为的信息和指南，后者独立评估了一项威慑信息试验。

该公司还为使用 OpenAI 工具的开发人员发布了指南，以防止、检测和帮助用户报告 CSAM 内容。它表示，在早期测试中，该指南已帮助许多开发者采用儿童安全工具，并注册向 NCMEC 报告 CSAM。 OpenAI 还为处理儿童安全问题的执法部门配备了人工智能驱动的功能，如专用插件、调查工具和复杂的数据分析，并由程序管理员管理访问权限。它还为调查人员提供培训以及如何使用人工智能的现场指南。

OpenAI 已对该公司提起多起诉讼，指责其技术伤害用户，尤其是儿童。专注于安全的非营利组织 Common Sense Media 将 OpenAI 的技术标记为青少年“不可接受的风险”。其他人工智能聊天机器人——特别是 Grok——已被用来创建未经同意的性图像，包括儿童图像。

这家人工智能初创公司在过去 12 个月中对其技术进行了更改，包括发布安全蓝图、更新内容指南以禁止不当内容、重新调整其模型以防止生成有害内容，以及为青少年发布特殊版本的 ChatGPT。

title: Altman Says AI Industry ‘Will Be Fine’ After Huang’s Ouster
title_en: Altman Says AI Industry ‘Will Be Fine’ After Huang’s Ouster
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Jensen Huang helped power the AI boom. But can the industry keep moving without him at Nvidia?

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman believes it can. Speaking at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event in San Francisco, Altman said the artificial intelligence industry would be “fine” without Huang leading Nvidia.

He also acknowledged the former CEO’s extraordinary contribution to the sector, calling him a hero while adding that “heroes have flaws”. The comments mark Altman’s first public comments on Huang’s sudden resignation from Nvidia last week.

They come at a time when the chipmaker’s leadership transition has raised questions about the future of a company central to the global AI ecosystem.

OpenAI's CEO said it was difficult to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen Huang and the company he built. Nvidia’s graphics processing units, or GPUs, have become essential for training and running large AI models, making the company a critical supplier to OpenAI and other AI firms.

However, Sam Altman stopped short of saying whether Huang should return to the company. Asked about the possibility, he said he did not know enough to answer.

His response acknowledged Huang’s influence without taking a position on Nvidia’s internal leadership decisions. Altman also expressed empathy for Huang, drawing a parallel with his own removal from OpenAI by its board in 2023.

Jensen Huang resigned after reports of extramarital relationships, including one involving Alice Huang, a woman who is not related to him and is reportedly suspected by US officials of passing information to Chinese intelligence.

Nvidia appointed its Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while its board searches for a permanent successor. The transition matters because Nvidia has become more than a chip supplier to the AI industry.

OpenAI and Nvidia have developed a close relationship over the past decade, spanning chips, data centres and financing.

Nvidia has also agreed to guarantee up to $105 billion to support OpenAI’s new data centre project in Ohio, according to the report. Asked whether he was concerned about Nvidia honouring its commitments after Huang’s departure, Altman said he was not.

He described Nvidia as a “behemoth of a company” and said people continued to trust its financial guarantees.

Who will succeed Jensen Huang? The race to find Nvidia's next chief begins

Huang’s exit has unsettled parts of Silicon Valley. Some technology executives and investors fear Nvidia could become more cautious about the large financial commitments that have helped fund the AI boom.

A campaign urging the company’s board to reinstate Huang has also attracted support from prominent industry figures. Sam Altman, however, pointed to the strength of demand and revenue across AI products.

He said the industry was growing strongly enough to withstand the uncertainty around Nvidia’s leadership.

His words do not diminish Jensen Huang’s role in building the AI ecosystem. Instead, they point to a distinction between the influence of one leader and the momentum of an entire industry.

Nvidia’s next chapter will show whether the company can maintain its pace without the person who led it for decades.

article_content_en:
Jensen Huang helped power the AI boom. But can the industry keep moving without him at Nvidia?

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman believes it can. Speaking at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event in San Francisco, Altman said the artificial intelligence industry would be “fine” without Huang leading Nvidia.

He also acknowledged the former CEO’s extraordinary contribution to the sector, calling him a hero while adding that “heroes have flaws”. The comments mark Altman’s first public comments on Huang’s sudden resignation from Nvidia last week.

They come at a time when the chipmaker’s leadership transition has raised questions about the future of a company central to the global AI ecosystem.

OpenAI's CEO said it was difficult to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen Huang and the company he built. Nvidia’s graphics processing units, or GPUs, have become essential for training and running large AI models, making the company a critical supplier to OpenAI and other AI firms.

However, Sam Altman stopped short of saying whether Huang should return to the company. Asked about the possibility, he said he did not know enough to answer.

His response acknowledged Huang’s influence without taking a position on Nvidia’s internal leadership decisions. Altman also expressed empathy for Huang, drawing a parallel with his own removal from OpenAI by its board in 2023.

Jensen Huang resigned after reports of extramarital relationships, including one involving Alice Huang, a woman who is not related to him and is reportedly suspected by US officials of passing information to Chinese intelligence.

Nvidia appointed its Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while its board searches for a permanent successor. The transition matters because Nvidia has become more than a chip supplier to the AI industry.

OpenAI and Nvidia have developed a close relationship over the past decade, spanning chips, data centres and financing.

article_content_zh:
黄仁勋帮助推动了人工智能的繁荣。但如果没有他在英伟达，这个行业还能继续发展吗？

OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 相信它可以。 Altman 在旧金山举行的 Semafor 硅谷与世界活动上发表讲话时表示，如果没有黄仁勋领导 Nvidia，人工智能行业也会“很好”。

他还承认这位前首席执行官对该行业的非凡贡献，称他为英雄，同时补充说“英雄也有缺点”。这是奥特曼首次就黄仁勋上周突然从英伟达辞职一事发表公开评论。

它们出现之际，这家芯片制造商的领导层换届引发了人们对这家全球人工智能生态系统核心公司的未来的质疑。

OpenAI 首席执行官表示，很难想象如果没有黄仁勋和他创建的公司，人工智能革命将会发生。 Nvidia 的图形处理单元（GPU）对于训练和运行大型人工智能模型至关重要，这使得该公司成为 OpenAI 和其他人工智能公司的重要供应商。

不过，山姆·奥尔特曼没有透露黄是否应该回到公司。当被问及这种可能性时，他说他不知道如何回答。

他的回应承认了黄仁勋的影响力，但没有对英伟达的内部领导决策表明立场。 Altman 也表达了对黄的同情，并与 2023 年他自己被 OpenAI 董事会除名的情况进行了类比。

黄仁勋因婚外情报道而辞职，其中包括一名与黄仁勋没有亲属关系的女性黄仁勋，据报道美国官员怀疑她向中国情报机构传递信息。

英伟达任命其首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)为临时首席执行官，同时董事会也在寻找永久继任者。这一转变很重要，因为英伟达已经不仅仅是人工智能行业的芯片供应商。

OpenAI 和 Nvidia 在过去十年中在芯片、数据中心和融资领域建立了密切的合作关系。

Nvidia 还同意提供高达 1050 亿美元的担保，以支持 OpenAI 在俄亥俄州的新数据中心项目。当被问及他是否担心黄仁勋离开后英伟达兑现承诺时，奥特曼表示不担心。

他将英伟达描述为“一家庞然大物”，并表示人们仍然信任其财务担保。

谁将接替黄仁勋？寻找英伟达下一任首席执行官的竞赛开始

黄仁勋的退出让硅谷的部分地区感到不安。一些技术高管和投资者担心，英伟达可能会对为人工智能热潮提供资金的巨额财务承诺变得更加谨慎。

一项敦促公司董事会恢复黄先生职位的运动也吸引了业内知名人士的支持。然而，山姆·奥尔特曼指出了人工智能产品的需求和收入的强劲。

他表示，该行业的增长势头足以承受英伟达领导地位的不确定性。

他的话并没有削弱黄仁勋在构建人工智能生态系统中的作用。相反，他们指出了一位领导者的影响力与整个行业的势头之间的区别。

英伟达的下一章将展示该公司是否能够在没有几十年来领导该公司的人的情况下保持其步伐。

author: CNBC
article_content:
Nvidia's board of directors is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC.

The board is focused on a national security investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back, the person said.

Last week, Huang resigned from Nvidia, the company he founded, after 33 years as CEO. The resignation came under a week after Huang had admitted to an affair, and news stories alleged he had an affair with Alice Huang, who worked for a customer, as well as employees at Nvidia.

Over the weekend, the Financial Times said Huang had discussed coming back with allies. Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner told CNBC on Monday that Huang had not discussed a comeback with him.

A representative for Huang declined to comment on speculation on Sunday.

Many in the tech world have called for Huang to return as Nvidia CEO.

An online petition calling for his reinstatement has drawn 180,000 signatures as well as support from major figures including Elon Musk, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney.

On Friday, a representative for Nvidia's board said that it was in the process of selecting a search firm for the Nvidia CEO role.

title: Anthropic cuts its coordinated vulnerability disclosure window from 90 to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, in response to AI-driven bug discovery (Anthropic)
title_en: Anthropic cuts its coordinated vulnerability disclosure window from 90 to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, in response to AI-driven bug discovery (Anthropic)

inline_images.caption: Two-panel illustration: on the left, a black-and-white photograph of a large boulder, tinted yellow, balanced on smaller rocks; on the right, a blue line drawin
inline_images.alt: Two-panel illustration: on the left, a black-and-white photograph of a large boulder, tinted yellow,

author: Anthropic
article_content:
Over the last several months, frontier models have become much better at discovering vulnerabilities. We remain optimistic that this will help defenders find and fix vulnerabilities faster than ever before. However, the speed at which AI is improving has changed how we think about our own disclosure practices.

We’re shortening the disclosure window in our coordinated vulnerability disclosure (CVD) policy from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all other issues. The new timelines apply to vulnerabilities reported to vendors and maintainers on or after January 1, 2027. In-progress reports as of that date will keep their existing deadlines.

In addition to shortening the disclosure window, we are making two related changes. First, we will aim to escalate to an external vulnerability coordinator after 15 days instead of 30 if a maintainer does not respond to our initial vulnerability report. Second, we will wait 30 days instead of 45 after a patch is available before sharing full technical details. The rest of our policy remains the same.

Finally, there are high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities that we reported over 90 days ago and that now exceed the deadline in our current CVD policy that have not yet been disclosed publicly. We are now notifying the maintainers of these projects that we are providing them an additional 30 days, after which time we will publish these reports on our dashboard in line with our updated policy starting January 1, 2027.

Many coordinated disclosure norms, including those found in our own policy, were developed well before AI could discover vulnerabilities. These policies assumed that fixes moved at human speed and that independent rediscovery of the same bug was unlikely. Neither assumption holds today. Models can now help develop fixes, and a bug that one model can find is increasingly likely to be found by another. We are seeing a higher rate of vulnerability rediscovery as these capabilities increase. A 90-day window made sense when a vulnerability could be expected to stay private for months. We no longer believe it can, and these changes are intended to keep pace with progress in AI capabilities and strike the right balance for defenders.

Some vulnerabilities still can’t be fixed quickly. Flaws in hard-to-deploy software, such as critical infrastructure, and flaws that require changes to a specification or RFC can’t always be resolved in 30 or 45 days. In these cases, we will work with the vendor on a remediation timeline. Our seven-day disclosure window for any vulnerability under active exploitation remains unchanged. This new policy update will not apply to AI-discovered findings that have not received human review, such as those found by OSS Scanner.

We recognize that shorter timelines may put more pressure on software maintainers. To reduce that burden, we will continue to include actionable guidance with each report, along with a patch or mitigation where possible, to best enable the maintainer to confirm a finding and fix the vulnerability. We will also continue to agree on a sustainable pace with maintainers before sending a large volume of findings to a single project.

We offer programs to help maintainers and defenders work at this new pace. Maintainers of critical open-source projects can apply to OSS Scanner, a no-cost service that periodically scans their code with our strongest models and sends them findings directly. Eligible maintainers and contributors can apply to the Claude for Open Source Program for six months of Claude Ultra at no cost. And security professionals, including open-source maintainers, can apply to our Cyber Verification Program, which tailors Claude’s safeguards to enable legitimate defensive work.

article_content_zh:
在过去的几个月里，前沿模型在发现漏洞方面变得更加出色。我们仍然乐观地认为，这将帮助防御者比以往更快地发现和修复漏洞。然而，人工智能改进的速度改变了我们对自己的披露实践的看法。

我们将协调漏洞披露 (CVD) 政策中的披露窗口从 90 天缩短到 30 天（对于高严重性和关键严重性问题），对于所有其他问题则从 45 天缩短。新的时间表适用于 2027 年 1 月 1 日或之后向供应商和维护人员报告的漏洞。截至该日期正在进行的报告将保留现有的截止日期。

除了缩短披露窗口外，我们还进行了两项相关的更改。首先，如果维护人员未对我们的初始漏洞报告做出回应，我们的目标是在 15 天（而不是 30 天）后将问题升级给外部漏洞协调员。其次，我们将在补丁发布后等待 30 天而不是 45 天，然后再分享完整的技术细节。我们政策的其余部分保持不变。

最后，我们在 90 多天前报告了一些高危和危急严重的漏洞，这些漏洞现在已经超过了我们当前 CVD 政策的截止日期，但尚未公开披露。我们现在通知这些项目的维护者，我们将为他们提供额外的 30 天时间，之后我们将根据自 2027 年 1 月 1 日起更新的政策在我们的仪表板上发布这些报告。

许多协调一致的披露规范，包括我们自己政策中的规范，都是在人工智能发现漏洞之前就制定的。这些政策假设修复工作以人类的速度进行，并且独立地重新发现相同的错误是不可能的。这两种假设在今天都不成立。模型现在可以帮助开发修复程序，并且一个模型可以找到的错误越来越有可能被另一个模型发现。随着这些功能的增强，我们发现漏洞重新发现率更高。当漏洞预计会在数月内保持私密状态时，90 天的窗口是有意义的。我们不再相信它可以，这些变化旨在跟上人工智能能力的进步，并为防御者取得适当的平衡。

一些漏洞仍然无法快速修复。难以部署的软件（例如关键基础设施）中的缺陷以及需要更改规范或 RFC 的缺陷并不总能在 30 或 45 天内得到解决。在这些情况下，我们将与供应商合作制定补救时间表。我们对任何被主动利用的漏洞的 7 天披露窗口保持不变。此新政策更新不适用于人工智能发现的未经人工审核的结果，例如 OSS Scanner 发现的结果。

我们认识到，较短的时间可能会给软件维护人员带来更大的压力。为了减轻这种负担，我们将继续在每份报告中提供可操作的指导，并在可能的情况下提供补丁或缓解措施，以最好地使维护人员能够确认发现并修复漏洞。在向单个项目发送大量调查结果之前，我们还将继续与维护人员就可持续的步伐达成一致。

我们提供计划来帮助维护者和防御者以这种新的节奏工作。关键开源项目的维护者可以申请 OSS Scanner，这是一项免费服务，可以使用我们最强大的模型定期扫描他们的代码，并直接向他们发送结果。符合条件的维护者和贡献者可以向 Claude 开源计划免费申请六个月的 Claude Ultra。安全专业人员，包括开源维护人员，可以申请我们的网络验证计划，该计划定制克劳德的保护措施以实现合法的防御工作。

title: Broadening access to AI for scientists
title_en: Broadening access to AI for scientists

inline_images.caption: Waitlist signups by country or territory as of November 12, 2026. Darker colors indicate more signups on a logarithmic scale.
inline_images.alt: Waitlist signups by country or territory as of November 12, 2026. Darker colors indicate more signup

author: OpenAI 官方动态
article_content:
We’re expanding the ChatGPT for Academic Researchers program to give up to 200,000 researchers worldwide free access to ChatGPT.

The program began as a pilot in July. Applications for the next round open Monday, November 23. We’ll award 50,000 new grants to eligible researchers on a first-come, first-served basis. Each grant gives the recipient and up to two collaborators free access to ChatGPT Plus. If you’re already on the waitlist and qualify, we’ll email you before applications open with instructions for activating your account.

Participants can use OpenAI’s frontier models and get training on how to use ChatGPT in their research. By default, we don’t use data shared through the program to train our models.

Waitlist signups by country or territory as of November 12, 2026. Darker colors indicate more signups on a logarithmic scale.

20,000 researchers in 33 countries have joined the program since the pilot began in July. Shuqi Li, a researcher at Brigham and Women’s Hospital and Harvard Medical School, looks for new drug targets that could ultimately shorten tuberculosis treatment. He is exploring whether ChatGPT can help link lab and patient data to speed up antibiotic development. Arthur Porto, assistant curator of AI biodiversity at the Florida Museum of Natural History, and his team uses AI tools to turn photographs of museum specimens into searchable databases. They also created a 3D model of a butterfly whose wings change color as you turn it, just like the real specimen.

We’re also publishing Science at the Frontier: How Scientists Use ChatGPT, new research from our Economic Research team examining how more than 1,800 researchers used ChatGPT during the program’s summer pilot. Surveyed participants estimated that, without AI, the same research work at the same quality would have taken nearly twice as long.

The program’s summer pilot helped us understand how researchers use ChatGPT and how we can improve their experience. Based on feedback from researchers, we’re moving away from lottery-based selection. For the next round, we’ll provide access to the first 50,000 applications who meet the eligibility requirements.

The pilot gave researchers access to ChatGPT Pro. When we reviewed pilot usage, we found that most participants would have stayed within ChatGPT Plus usage limits. Based on that finding, we’re offering Plus for new grants so we can extend access to more research teams.

Each grant for this round covers the recipient and up to two collaborators, supporting up to 150,000 researchers. Our goal for the program as a whole is to reach 200,000 researchers, double the goal we announced when the pilot launched in July.

We’ll continue learning from participants about the application process, the capabilities they need, and the support that helps them use these tools in their research. This feedback will help us refine the program and shape future rounds.

Different scientific fields will use AI in different ways, and researchers will need different kinds and levels of support. We’re working with scientific communities to understand those needs and shape our tools, training, and programs around them.

Our support also includes helping scientific communities turn AI-generated results into deeper understanding and new discoveries. In mathematics, we contributed $5 million to a new Simons Foundation initiative⁠ to help mathematicians examine, understand, and build on results produced by AI.

We’re also providing different ways for researchers and institutions to access our tools. ChatGPT for Academic Researchers is just one way we’re helping researchers access advanced AI tools.

Through ChatGPT Edu⁠(opens in a new window), universities can give their campus communities access to ChatGPT for research, teaching, and learning, with tools for analyzing data and administrative controls for managing access.

For researchers working in biology, GPT‑Rosalind⁠ brings together specialized biological reasoning and access to scientific tools and databases. The Rosalind Academic Plan⁠ helps bring these capabilities to eligible labs at U.S. universities, offering up to 30 seats at no cost for up to 12 months. Access to GPT‑Rosalind requires approval through our trusted-access process.

Visit our researcher access guide to learn more about ChatGPT Edu, GPT‑Rosalind, and ChatGPT for Academic Researchers.

As these efforts grow, researchers’ experiences will help us understand where our tools are useful, where they fall short, and what support is needed. We’ll use that feedback to improve our programs, develop training and learning resources, and create opportunities for researchers to exchange approaches with one another.

Our goal is to give more researchers the tools and support to pursue ambitious questions—and to keep improving that support as their research and our capabilities evolve.

Learn more about the program⁠(opens in a new window).

key_points_en: Key Development: Broadening access to AI for scientists

article_content_zh:
我们正在扩大针对学术研究人员的 ChatGPT 计划，让全球多达 200,000 名研究人员免费访问 ChatGPT。

该计划于七月开始试点。下一轮申请将于 11 月 23 日星期一开放。我们将按照先到先得的原则向符合条件的研究人员提供 50,000 笔新资助。每笔资助都会让接受者和最多两名合作者免费访问 ChatGPT Plus。如果您已经在候补名单上并且符合资格，我们会在申请开放之前向您发送电子邮件，其中包含激活您帐户的说明。

参与者可以使用 OpenAI 的前沿模型，并接受如何在研究中使用 ChatGPT 的培训。默认情况下，我们不使用通过程序共享的数据来训练我们的模型。

截至 2026 年 11 月 12 日，按国家或地区列出的候补名单注册人数。较深的颜色表示对数标度上的注册人数较多。

自 7 月份试点开始以来，已有 33 个国家的 20,000 名研究人员加入了该计划。布莱根妇女医院和哈佛医学院的研究员 Shuqi Li 正在寻找最终可以缩短结核病治疗时间的新药物靶点。他正在探索 ChatGPT 是否可以帮助连接实验室和患者数据，以加快抗生素的开发。佛罗里达自然历史博物馆人工智能生物多样性助理馆长 Arthur Porto 和他的团队使用人工智能工具将博物馆标本的照片转化为可搜索的数据库。他们还创建了蝴蝶的 3D 模型，其翅膀会随着转动而改变颜色，就像真实的标本一样。

我们还发布了《科学前沿：科学家如何使用 ChatGPT》，这是我们经济研究团队的新研究，研究了 1,800 多名研究人员在该项目夏季试点期间如何使用 ChatGPT。接受调查的参与者估计，如果没有人工智能，相同质量的相同研究工作将花费近两倍的时间。

我们希望更多的研究人员拥有工具和支持来追求雄心勃勃的问题并做出改善人们生活的发现。这是我们确保通用人工智能造福全人类的使命的核心。

该计划的夏季试点帮助我们了解研究人员如何使用 ChatGPT 以及我们如何改善他们的体验。根据研究人员的反馈，我们正在放弃基于抽签的选择。在下一轮中，我们将向前 50,000 名符合资格要求的申请提供访问权限。

该试点项目让研究人员能够访问 ChatGPT Pro。当我们审查试点使用情况时，我们发现大多数参与者都会遵守 ChatGPT Plus 使用限制。基于这一发现，我们将向 Plus 提供新的资助，以便我们可以将访问范围扩大到更多的研究团队。

此轮的每笔资助涵盖接受者和最多两名合作者，支持多达 150,000 名研究人员。我们整个计划的目标是覆盖 200,000 名研究人员，是我们 7 月份试点启动时宣布的目标的两倍。

我们将继续向参与者了解申请流程、他们所需的功能以及帮助他们在研究中使用这些工具的支持。这些反馈将帮助我们完善计划并塑造未来的轮次。

不同的科学领域会以不同的方式使用人工智能，研究人员需要不同种类和水平的支持。我们正在与科学界合作，了解这些需求，并围绕它们制定我们的工具、培训和计划。

我们的支持还包括帮助科学界将人工智能生成的结果转化为更深入的理解和新发现。在数学方面，我们向西蒙斯基金会的一项新计划捐赠了 500 万美元，以帮助数学家检查、理解人工智能产生的结果并在其基础上进行构建。

我们还为研究人员和机构提供不同的方式来访问我们的工具。面向学术研究人员的 ChatGPT 只是我们帮助研究人员访问先进人工智能工具的一种方式。

title: Strengthening the fight against online child sexual abuse with new tools and support
title_en: Strengthening the fight against online child sexual abuse with new tools and support

inline_images.caption: ChatGPT warnings explain that sexualizing children is harmful and can be illegal, suspend the account for 24 hours, and offer specialist support.
inline_images.alt: ChatGPT warnings explain that sexualizing children is harmful and can be illegal, suspend the accoun

author: OpenAI 官方动态
article_content:
New tools, practical guidance, and partnerships will help prevent, detect and respond to online child sexual exploitation and abuse.

Today, we’re releasing a new tool to detect child sexual abuse material (CSAM), interventions that interrupt harmful behavior and point people toward help, practical resources for developers, and support for child-safety law enforcement investigators. These efforts build on our Child Safety Blueprint and our ongoing work to detect, block, and report abuse. For parents, the goal is simple: technology that helps keep children safe, with people in control.

It is well⁠(opens in a new window) established⁠(opens in a new window) that combatting online child predators requires coordination across many organizations. Individual companies like OpenAI have a responsibility to prevent our technology from being exploited by predators to harm children, and we also must work together with the broader industry, child safety organizations and law enforcement to advance our collective efforts to protect children online.

We’re building on our current protections with the release of a new image classifier that can detect potential CSAM, including AI-generated material. This new classifier looks for visual signs of abuse, helping teams identify novel images that may not have been seen before. It returns scores that help reviewers decide which images may need attention first. This is the first CSAM classifier with broad availability that has a specific signal on indicating if CSAM may be AI generated.

Our teams trained, evaluated, and designed the classifier for real-world deployment with assistance from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC)⁠(opens in a new window), a nonprofit that operates the CyberTipline, a centralized reporting hub for the online exploitation of children.

We’re offering access to the classifier to vetted organizations through the OpenAI API at no cost, making CSAM detection more accessible to child safety organizations and the broader industry, including those with teams of varying sizes.

Child safety is an industry-wide issue that requires strong collaboration across organizations and a variety of solutions. We’ve engaged the Tech Coalition⁠(opens in a new window) and ROOST⁠(opens in a new window) to help us share access to this new tool, and we are strong supporters of tools developed by others such as Thorn’s Safer⁠(opens in a new window) CSAM detection system. In addition, we recently began participating in the Tech Coalition's Lantern program⁠(opens in a new window), where we will share and receive signals relating to online child sexual exploitation and abuse to strengthen cross- platform collaboration.

We’ve tested the classifier internally and with early partners to measure how much abusive material it detects, how often it flags other images, and how it can support safety teams. Their feedback helped us identify weaknesses and improve the system.

Early tests suggest the classifier can help reviewers focus on abusive images while reducing review of false positives. In an evaluation of user-uploaded images, we compared the new classifier with our current protections and found:

The new classifier could reduce review work: we estimated that it would flag 48% fewer images while finding roughly the same number of abusive images as the existing tool.

Images flagged by the new classifier were about twice as likely to contain abuse.

Early access partners have also evaluated how the classifier supports their own safety teams. In fal⁠(opens in a new window)’s testing on human-reviewed production images, reviewers confirmed 72% of the classifier’s high-confidence flags as novel CSAM. invideo AI⁠(opens in a new window)’s testing showed one in four flagged cases led to a ban. In SafetyKit⁠(opens in a new window)’s evaluations involving drawings or animations that sexualize children, the classifier detected 90% of cases.

More information about the classifier is available in the CSAM classifier model card⁠(opens in a new window). Organizations interested in the classifier will be able to request access through our intake form⁠. We’ll continue improving the classifier with feedback from those that use it.

We already prohibit CSAM, train our models to refuse requests for it, and take action against accounts that violate our policies. We’re building on those safeguards with new product warnings in ChatGPT that interrupt attempts to find abusive material, explain the consequences, and point people toward help to stop harmful behavior.

The warning makes clear that sexualizing children causes harm, including when the requested material is AI-generated. Alongside the warning, we’ll remove the flagged conversation and pause access to ChatGPT for 24 hours, while keeping specialist support available to help people stop harmful behavior. Repeated violations may lead to longer restrictions and ultimately account closure or reports to authorities.

We developed this approach with input from organizations and academic advisors that research and develop programs to prevent child sexual abuse, including Protect Children⁠(opens in a new window), the Lucy Faithfull Foundation⁠(opens in a new window), Dr. Caoilte Ó Ciardha, Researcher & Honorary Reader in Forensic Psychology at the University of Kent and Joel Scanlan at the University of Tasmania, who independently evaluated a trial⁠(opens in a new window) of deterrent messages.

The protection of children online doesn’t end with detection. We’ve published CSAM guidance⁠(opens in a new window) to give developers practical steps to prevent abuse, detect harmful content, and act on it. Developed with input from the Tech Coalition⁠(opens in a new window), Thorn⁠(opens in a new window), NCMEC⁠(opens in a new window), and the Internet Watch Foundation⁠(opens in a new window), it is designed for organizations at different stages of building their safety systems.

The guidance provides clear rules, ways for users to report concerns, detection tools, and processes for reviewing and reporting suspected abuse. It also explains how safety identifiers can help developers connect misuse to individual users and how to support the people reviewing sensitive content. Developers can use it alongside tools such as our new image classifier, Moderation API⁠(opens in a new window), ROOST’s self-hosted review console Coop⁠(opens in a new window), and dedicated CSAM detection services such as Thorn’s Safer⁠(opens in a new window).

Our commitment to collaboration and supporting the broader developer ecosystem also is reflected in our work with Anthropic and Google to jointly commission new guidance on responding to disclosures of child sexual exploitation and abuse in AI systems. Recently published by the Tech Coalition⁠(opens in a new window), this guidance provides developers with practical recommendations for addressing these sensitive situations.

We’ve already seen this guidance lead to increased numbers of developers accessing child safety tooling and registering to report CSAM to NCMEC.

Protecting children also means supporting the specialist child safety investigators working to find victims and stop abuse. As we’ve discussed publicly with Thorn⁠(opens in a new window), AI can help investigators organize and prioritize information and reduce unnecessary exposure to abusive material.

We’re also supporting child-safety law enforcement units with new tools and trainings on how to use AI in their investigations, including dedicated plugins, investigative tools, and complex data analysis, with access managed by program administrators. At launch, the first tool will help investigators review lengthy chat logs and legal process returns, identify potential connections, and create timelines, with findings linked to source material.

The initial training is planned as an overview and demonstration, supported by a practical field guide that teams can refer to afterward. It will introduce the tools and how they fit into investigative work. Access will depend on agency authorization and program requirements. Future iterations of the training will be proposed at regional, national and international conferences.

These efforts share one goal: preventing harm to children and strengthening the response when abuse occurs. We’ll continue improving our safeguards while empowering child protection organizations, developers, researchers, and investigators with the tools, resources, and expertise they need to protect children, combat exploitation, and bring perpetrators to justice. By working together, we can harness the power of AI to make a meaningful difference in the fight against child sexual exploitation and abuse.

article_content_zh:
新工具、实用指南和伙伴关系将有助于预防、发现和应对网上儿童性剥削和性虐待。

今天，我们发布了一种新工具来检测儿童性虐待材料 (CSAM)、阻止有害行为并引导人们寻求帮助、为开发人员提供实用资源以及为儿童安全执法调查人员提供支持的干预措施。这些努力建立在我们的儿童安全蓝图以及我们正在进行的检测、阻止和报告虐待行为的工作之上。对于父母来说，目标很简单：技术帮助确保孩子的安全，并让人们掌控。

众所周知，打击网络儿童掠夺者需要多个组织之间的协调。像 OpenAI 这样的个体公司有责任防止我们的技术被掠夺者利用来伤害儿童，我们还必须与更广泛的行业、儿童安全组织和执法部门合作，推进我们保护上网儿童的集体努力。

我们在当前的保护措施基础上发布了新的图像分类器，该分类器可以检测潜在的 CSAM，包括人工智能生成的材料。这个新的分类器会寻找虐待的视觉迹象，帮助团队识别以前可能从未见过的新图像。它返回的分数可以帮助审阅者决定哪些图像可能需要首先关注。这是第一个具有广泛可用性的 CSAM 分类器，具有指示 CSAM 是否可以由 AI 生成的特定信号。

我们的团队在国家失踪和受虐儿童中心 (NCMEC)（在新窗口中打开）的协助下，训练、评估和设计了用于现实世界部署的分类器。NCMEC 是一家运营 Cyber​​Tipline 的非营利组织，Cyber​​Tipline 是在线儿童剥削的集中举报中心。

我们通过 OpenAI API 免费向经过审查的组织提供分类器的访问权限，使儿童安全组织和更广泛的行业（包括拥有不同规模团队的行业）更容易使用 CSAM 检测。

儿童安全是一个全行业的问题，需要跨组织和各种解决方案的强有力合作。我们已经与 Tech Coalition⁠(opens in a new window) 和 ROOST⁠(opens in a new window) 合作，帮助我们共享对这一新工具的访问，并且我们是其他人开发的工具的坚定支持者，例如 Thorn 的 Safer⁠(opens in a new window) CSAM 检测系统。此外，我们最近开始参与技术联盟的灯笼计划⁠（在新窗口中打开），我们将在该计划中分享和接收与在线儿童性剥削和性虐待有关的信号，以加强跨平台合作。

我们在内部并与早期合作伙伴一起测试了分类器，以测量它检测到的滥用材料的数量、它标记其他图像的频率以及它如何支持安全团队。他们的反馈帮助我们发现了弱点并改进了系统。

早期测试表明，分类器可以帮助审核者关注滥用图像，同时减少对误报的审核。在对用户上传图像的评估中，我们将新分类器与当前的保护措施进行了比较，发现：

新的分类器可以减少审查工作：我们估计，它将标记的图像数量减少 48%，同时发现的滥用图像数量与现有工具大致相同。

新分类器标记的图像包含滥用内容的可能性大约是原来的两倍。

早期访问合作伙伴还评估了分类器如何支持他们自己的安全团队。在 fal⁠(opens in a new window) 对人工审核的生产图像进行的测试中，审核者确认分类器 72% 的高置信度标记为新颖的 CSAM。 invideo AI（在新窗口中打开）的测试显示，四分之一的标记案例导致了禁令。在 SafetyKit(opens in a new window) 对涉及儿童性化图画或动画的评估中，分类器检测到了 90% 的案例。

有关分类器的更多信息，请参阅 CSAM 分类器模型卡⁠（在新窗口中打开）。对分类器感兴趣的组织将能够通过我们的接收表格请求访问。我们将根据使用者的反馈继续改进分类器。

我们已经禁止 CSAM，训练我们的模型拒绝 CSAM 请求，并对违反我们政策的帐户采取行动。我们正在这些保障措施的基础上，在 ChatGPT 中发布新产品警告，中断查找滥用内容的尝试，解释后果，并引导人们帮助制止有害行为。

title: Alibaba's Qwen4-Max takes on Opus 5.5, GPT-6, and Kimi K3.1 Pro at much lower prices
title_en: Alibaba's Qwen4-Max takes on Opus 5.5, GPT-6, and Kimi K3.1 Pro at much lower prices

author: THE DECODER
article_content:
Qwen4-Max is Alibaba's answer to Opus 5.5, GPT-6, and Kimi K3.1 Pro. The new flagship pairs a more efficient architecture with much lower prices and targets professional work in industry, science, and finance.

The mixture-of-experts model has 2.4 trillion parameters but activates only 71 billion per token, according to the Qwen team. It processes images natively and offers a one-million-token context window.

Qwen4-Max debuts the revamped architecture of the Qwen4 series. Instead of relying only on standard attention layers, Alibaba combines two methods. Three layers compress the prior context into a condensed state, and a fourth layer then picks out only the parts that matter. That sharply cuts compute costs on long inputs, since the model no longer has to give every part of the context equal attention.Ad

The architecture also adds four parallel connections between model layers, with dynamic gates meant to stabilize the flow of information. An N-gram embedding layer with 328 billion parameters supplies common token sequences as ready-made building blocks. According to Alibaba, training the 2.4-trillion-parameter configuration ran stably. Training loss fell steadily throughout the run with no sudden spikes.Ad

Alibaba's internal evaluations measure model quality in bits per byte across knowledge, code, question answering, and STEM. Qwen4-Max-Base scored best among the five checkpoints tested. It improved 5 to 13 percent over Qwen3.8-Max-Base while activating 25 percent fewer parameters per token.

The efficiency gains show up in operating costs. Work360 is Alibaba's own benchmark for industrial work tasks across 721 specialized fields. On it, Qwen4-Max uses roughly a quarter to a third fewer tokens than its predecessor to solve the same tasks. On the agent benchmark Terminal-Bench 4.0, token use drops by nearly half.Ad

According to Alibaba, the average cost per Work360 task falls 62 percent, from $4.43 to $1.67. The benchmark score climbs from 47.74 to 52.69 at the same time.

Results on external benchmarks are mixed. On long-horizon agent tasks like Agents' Last Exam v1.1, Qwen4-Max scores 46.7 points, the best result in the comparison group. It trails Opus 5.5 and the GPT models on Humanity's Last Exam. On HealthBench Professional, it falls behind the GPT models but edges past Opus 5.5.Ad

At its highest reasoning setting, Qwen4-Max scores 43 points on the current Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. That's nine more than Qwen3.8-Max and three behind Kimi K3.1 Pro, the top Chinese model at 46 points. The biggest gains over the predecessor come on HLE-Diamond (up 21 points to 45 percent), AA-Omniscience (up 18), and AutomationBench-AA (up 17).Ad

Artificial Analysis puts the cost of Qwen4-Max at $3.27 per Intelligence Index task. That's about a third of Qwen3.8-Max's $10.02 and roughly 11 percent less than Kimi K3.1 Pro's $3.68. The savings come from three places. Token prices are 25 percent lower than the predecessor's, cache hits cost 70 percent less, and the model burns through fewer tokens. Qwen4-Max needs about 105,000 output tokens per benchmark task, compared with 171,000 for Qwen3.8-Max.

Tencent's Hy4 is much cheaper at $1.03 per task but scores eight points lower on the index. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Qwen4-Max scores 48 percent, behind Kimi K3.1 Pro at 67 percent. On Cognition's coding benchmark FrontierCode 2.0, it ties Kimi at 26 percent and trails Tencent Hy4 at 31 percent.

Through its own API, Alibaba charges $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens. Cache hits cost $0.075.

Like much of the AI industry, Alibaba builds this release around agents that handle long tasks on their own. If users only see results at the end, they have almost no way to fix mistakes. Alibaba's answer is "Live Delivery." The model delivers a usable first version early and builds it out in later passes. Users can step in and change course at any point. Alibaba has open-sourced the accompanying Qwen-Live-Delivery-Plugin.

Alibaba cites several partner deployments. Automotive partners SANF and Pacific Union reportedly used Qwen4-Max to cut manual programming time for a single workpiece from about 475 minutes to 24. In finance, the model taps 90 MCP tools to pull market data from multiple sources. It delivers the results as verifiable Excel and PowerPoint files, and every number traces back to its original source.

Alibaba also uses the model internally to run its own cloud infrastructure more efficiently. According to the company, Qwen4-Max worked with the in-house solver MindOpt to cut the cost of allocating compute jobs for data annotation by an average of 10.42 percent. When distributing CPU tasks in data centers, it found optimal solutions more than 14 times faster than the comparison method.

Alibaba also shows the Qwen4 generation at work in physical labs. Paired with Mira, a system from startup Deep Principle, the model ran autonomously for 48 hours, according to Alibaba. In that time, it designed, synthesized, and tested a new coolant for high-performance data center chips. It searched 2.7 million molecular candidates, controlled an automated lab, and completed four full cycles of design, synthesis, and measurement.

Qwen4-Max also worked with PharmMaster, a platform from Beijing-based AI drug discovery startup DP Technology. The target was a compound aimed at an inflammatory response linked to Alzheimer's disease. Over several rounds of literature review, design, and computation, the model optimized 24 candidate molecules. According to Alibaba, the final candidate binds to the target protein about 3.6 times better than the known starting compound from a patent. DP Technology's experts consider the result promising enough to pursue further lab tests.

Alibaba also shows Qwen4-Max working with established game engines like Unity, Unreal Engine, and Godot. From a single natural-language description, the model is supposed to handle the entire development process. That covers scene setup, game logic, and matching external assets, along with materials, UI, and visual effects, until the game is playable.

During development, the model runs the game itself and uses visual and interactive feedback to tweak camera work, character animations, hit reactions, and lighting. Alibaba's sample project is "Meow of Magic," an Unreal Engine adventure about a cat wizard in which players cast spells and fight waves of enemies. According to Alibaba, Qwen4-Max also builds 3D models in Blender that can be reused for games and 3D printing.

Anthropic recently moved its coding assistant Claude Code in the opposite direction. After a wave of unofficial Halo and GTA: Vice City clones, it barred the tool from recreating existing games.

On the safety benchmark Last Secure Code Bench, the share of code that is both functional and secure rose from 22 to 31.8 percent, according to Alibaba. The share rated secure at all three testing levels nearly doubled, from 8 to 14.7 percent. Alibaba also tested for CBRN risks (chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear). Internal reviewers went through the model's full chains of thought, the company says. They found no real capacity for innovation that would give a user a significant boost in capability.

Qwen4-Max is available through QwenCloud and in QwenWork, Qoder, and QwenStudio. Alibaba plans to release smaller Qwen4 models as open source later.

In August, Alibaba released Qwen3.8-Max, its first Max model built for autonomous tasks that run for days. It also has 2.4 trillion parameters, but 95 billion are active per token. At the time, Artificial Analysis found that the model needed 64 steps per task instead of 14 and cost more than twice as much per task as Qwen3.7-Max.

In late August, Alibaba previewed the Qwen4 architecture with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, which already used an N-gram embedding layer with 51 billion parameters. The company had released the Qwen3.8-Max weights in mid-August. For Qwen4, only the smaller models will get open weights for now.

Moonshot AI followed in October with Kimi K3.1 Pro. At 2.8 trillion parameters, it's even larger, and Moonshot says it sits just behind Claude Opus 5.5 on Terminal-Bench 4.0. Like Alibaba, DeepSeek uses a hybrid attention design with sparse attention in V4-Pro to process long contexts more cheaply. Zhipu AI took a different route and got GLM-5.3's gains entirely from extra post-training.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: Qwen4-Max的架构优化反映出头部厂商正在从单纯堆砌参数转向追求‘单位推理成本的边际效用最大化’。通过压缩上下文状态而非简单的全局注意力，阿里正在试图建立一套适配Agent复杂长链路任务的低成本算力基准，这将对追求高性价比的企业级AI部署产生直接的市场分流效应。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Qwen4-Max’s architectural optimization signals a shift from raw parameter scaling to maximizing marginal utility per inference unit. article_content_zh:
Qwen4-Max 是阿里巴巴对 Opus 5.5、GPT-6 和 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的回应。新的旗舰产品结合了更高效的架构和更低的价格，面向工业、科学和金融领域的专业工作。

据 Qwen 团队称，专家混合模型有 2.4 万亿个参数，但每个代币仅激活 710 亿个参数。它本机处理图像并提供一百万个令牌的上下文窗口。

Qwen4-Max 首次推出了 Qwen4 系列的改进架构。阿里巴巴并没有仅仅依赖标准的注意力层，而是结合了两种方法。三层将先前的上下文压缩为压缩状态，然后第四层仅挑选出重要的部分。这大大降低了长输入的计算成本，因为模型不再需要给予上下文的每个部分同等的关注。

该架构还在模型层之间添加了四个并行连接，动态门旨在稳定信息流。具有 3280 亿个参数的 N-gram 嵌入层提供通用标记序列作为现成的构建块。据阿里巴巴介绍，2.4万亿参数配置的训练运行稳定。在整个跑步过程中，训练损失稳步下降，没有突然上升。

阿里巴巴的内部评估以每字节位数衡量知识、代码、问答和 STEM 方面的模型质量。 Qwen4-Max-Base 在测试的五个检查点中得分最高。与 Qwen3.8-Max-Base 相比，它的性能提高了 5% 到 13%，同时每个令牌激活的参数减少了 25%。

效率的提高体现在运营成本上。 Work360是阿里巴巴自己的行业工作任务标杆，涵盖721个专业领域。在其上，Qwen4-Max 解决相同任务时使用的令牌比其前身少大约四分之一到三分之一。在代理基准 Terminal-Bench 4.0 上，代币使用量下降了近一半。

据阿里巴巴称，每个 Work360 任务的平均成本下降了 62%，从 4.43 美元降至 1.67 美元。基准分数同时从47.74攀升至52.69。

外部基准的结果好坏参半。在 Agents' Last Exam v1.1 等长期代理任务中，Qwen4-Max 得分为 46.7 分，是对照组中的最佳成绩。它在人类最后考试中落后于 Opus 5.5 和 GPT 模型。在 HealthBench Professional 上，它落后于 GPT 模型，但略高于 Opus 5.5.Ad

在最高推理设置下，Qwen4-Max 在当前的人工智能分析智能指数中得分为 43 分。这比 Qwen3.8-Max 多了 9 分，比中国排名第一的 Kimi K3.1 Pro 低了 3 分（46 分）。与前身相比，涨幅最大的是 HLE-Diamond（上升 21 个百分点，达到 45%）、AA-Omniscience（上升 18）和 AutomationBench-AA（上升 17）。

人工分析显示，Qwen4-Max 每项智力指数任务的成本为 3.27 美元。这大约是 Qwen3.8-Max 售价 10.02 美元的三分之一，比 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的 3.68 美元便宜约 11%。节省的资金来自三个地方。令牌价格比前身低 25%，缓存命中成本降低 70%，并且该模型消耗的令牌更少。 Qwen4-Max 每个基准测试任务需要大约 105,000 个输出令牌，而 Qwen3.8-Max 需要 171,000 个。

腾讯的 Hy4 便宜得多，每任务 1.03 美元，但该指数得分低 8 分。在 Terminal-Bench 4.0 上，Qwen4-Max 得分为 48%，落后于 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的 67%。在 Cognition 的编码基准 FrontierCode 2.0 上，它与 Kimi 持平，为 26%，落后于腾讯 Hy4，为 31%。

通过自己的 API，阿里巴巴对每百万个输入代币收取 1.50 美元的费用，对每百万个输出代币收取 4.50 美元的费用。缓存命中成本为 0.075 美元。

与人工智能行业的许多公司一样，阿里巴巴围绕能够自行处理长时间任务的代理构建了此版本。如果用户只在最后看到结果，他们几乎没有办法修复错误。阿里巴巴的答案是“直播带货”。该模型尽早提供了可用的第一个版本，并在以后的过程中对其进行构建。用户可以随时介入并改变路线。阿里巴巴开源了配套的 Qwen-Live-Delivery-Plugin。

阿里巴巴列举了多个合作伙伴的部署情况。据报道，汽车合作伙伴 SANF 和 Pacific Union 使用 Qwen4-Max 将单个工件的手动编程时间从约 475 分钟缩短至 24 分钟。在金融领域，该模型利用 90 个 MCP 工具从多个来源提取市场数据。它将结果以可验证的 Excel 和 PowerPoint 文件形式提供，并且每个数字都可以追溯到其原始来源。

【起因与机理】应对大模型长文本处理的高昂计算成本与推理效率瓶颈
【关键数据与实测】核心模型架构：2.4万亿总参数/710亿激活参数的MoE架构。
【各方立场与态度】性能表现：Work360基准下任务成本下降62%，推理效率显著优于前代产品。

title: Harvard study: just 403 US data centers operational between May 2024 and April 2025 consumed as much electricity annually as the state of Michigan (Molly Taft/Wired)
title_en: Harvard study: just 403 US data centers operational between May 2024 and April 2025 consumed as much electricity annually as the state of Michigan (Molly Taft/Wired)

inline_images.caption: Image may contain Cable Power Lines Person and Electric Transmission Tower
inline_images.alt: Image may contain Cable Power Lines Person and Electric Transmission Tower

author: Wired
article_content:
The study, published Monday in Nature Sustainability, also finds that the majority of that electricity was generated using fossil fuels, and data center emissions are three times higher than they were before the AI boom.

Federal and state governments do not track data center use separate from the rest of the power sector, despite mounting projections that data centers are putting serious strain on the American power grid. Individual data centers’ power use is often considered proprietary business information, and data center operators and utilities do not have to disclose specific numbers to the public.

The Harvard study specifically focuses on hyperscale data centers—the largest types of facilities, which have become flashpoints in community opposition across the country. While often used for AI inference or training, not all of the hyperscalers surveyed in this study are being used for AI.

“Hyperscalers have been growing fast, even before the AI boom,” says Jon Koomey, an energy researcher who was not a part of the study.

To assemble their dataset, the Harvard researchers put together a list of 403 hyperscale data centers around the country that were operational between May 2024 and April 2025 using a mix of industry research and satellite data. The team then modeled these facilities’ energy use in a variety of scenarios and calculated the energy mix of the regional grids to estimate individual facilities’ carbon emissions. Not all regions were created equal: Data centers in Virginia, Oregon, Ohio, and Iowa—the first of which is home to Data Center Alley—were responsible for more than 50 percent of the energy use in the study.

“Knowing for certain data centers how much they use over a year is a really useful thing,” says Koomey, who notes that a peer-reviewed study is more rigorous than some back-of-the envelope calculations. Koomey has been involved in a regular report from Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory since 2007 that approximates the energy and water use of the industry. “Sometimes we know it, but sometimes it’s behind an NDA, and no one ever sees it.”

While based on recent data, the study may already be outdated—a reflection of how fast the data center industry is moving. The average size of a facility in the new study is 40 megawatts, which is relatively small compared to some of the data centers under development today. Developers are building campuses that are hundreds or even thousands of megawatts, and there are proposals for still larger data centers.

“Some of the massive campuses being proposed today are substantially larger than the typical facility in our dataset,” says Gianluca Guidi, a postdoctoral research fellow at Harvard’s T. H. Chan School of Public Health and the lead author of the study.

The study also does not look at developers who choose to build power plants onsite, known as behind-the-meter power—a factor Koomey calls a “wild card” in accurately assessing total data center power use. Plans for behind-the-meter power generation have skyrocketed at proposed data center sites across the US over the past year, with as many as 189 gigawatts in the pipeline earmarked for data centers alone. Many of these plants rely increasingly on inefficient natural gas turbines. BloombergNEF estimated last week that if all of the behind-the-meter power plants in the development queue in the US get built, it could increase overall US emissions by 10 percent.

While the federal government hasn’t tracked data center energy use to date, that could change soon, and it could be a boon to researchers and the public. The Energy Information Agency, the arm of the federal government that tracks energy use across various sectors, conducted three pilot surveys of data center power use across 10 states this year. Those pilot surveys are now complete, EIA spokesperson Lee Tucker tells WIRED, and the agency is currently using them to design a potential voluntary survey for the sector.

title_zh: 哈佛研究：全美403座超大规模数据中心能耗激增
summary_zh: 哈佛大学研究显示，美国403座超大规模数据中心年耗电量已等同于密歇根州，且碳排放较AI爆发前增长三倍
article_content_zh:
这项周一发表在《自然可持续发展》杂志上的研究还发现，大部分电力是使用化石燃料产生的，数据中心的排放量是人工智能繁荣之前的三倍。

尽管越来越多的预测表明数据中心给美国电网带来了严重压力，但联邦和州政府不会将数据中心的使用情况与电力行业的其他部门分开来进行跟踪。各个数据中心的用电量通常被视为专有商业信息，数据中心运营商和公用事业公司不必向公众披露具体数字。

哈佛大学的这项研究特别关注超大规模数据中心——最大类型的设施，这些设施已成为全国各地社区反对的热点。虽然经常用于人工智能推理或训练，但并非本研究中调查的所有超大规模都用于人工智能。

“甚至在人工智能繁荣之前，超大规模企业就一直在快速增长，”未参与该研究的能源研究员乔恩·库米 (Jon Koomey) 表示。

为了收集数据集，哈佛大学的研究人员结合行业研究和卫星数据，汇总了全国 403 个超大规模数据中心的列表，这些数据中心在 2024 年 5 月至 2025 年 4 月期间运行。然后，该团队对这些设施在各种情况下的能源使用情况进行了建模，并计算了区域电网的能源结构，以估算各个设施的碳排放量。并非所有地区都是平等的：弗吉尼亚州、俄勒冈州、俄亥俄州和爱荷华州的数据中心（其中第一个数据中心是数据中心巷的所在地）占该研究中 50% 以上的能源使用量。

虽然基于最近的数据，但这项研究可能已经过时了——这反映了数据中心行业的发展速度。新研究中设施的平均规模为 40 兆瓦，与目前正在开发的一些数据中心相比相对较小。开发商正在建设数百甚至数千兆瓦的园区，并且有人建议建设更大的数据中心。

“今天提议的一些大型校园比我们数据集中的典型设施要大得多，”哈佛大学陈曾熙公共卫生学院博士后研究员、该研究的主要作者吉安卢卡·吉迪 (Gianluca Guidi) 说。

这项研究也没有考虑选择在现场建造发电厂的开发商，即所谓的“表后电力”——库米称这一因素是准确评估数据中心总用电量的“通配符”。过去一年，美国各地拟议的数据中心站点的用户侧发电计划猛增，仅数据中心专用发电量就高达 189 吉瓦。许多工厂越来越依赖低效的天然气涡轮机。彭博新能源财经上周估计，如果美国正在开发的所有用户侧发电厂都建成的话，美国的总体排放量可能会增加 10%。

虽然联邦政府迄今为止尚未跟踪数据中心的能源使用情况，但这种情况可能很快就会改变，这可能对研究人员和公众来说是一个福音。能源信息局是联邦政府负责跟踪各个部门能源使用情况的机构，今年对 10 个州的数据中心电力使用情况进行了三项试点调查。 EIA 发言人 Lee Tucker 告诉《连线》杂志，这些试点调查现已完成，该机构目前正在利用它们为该行业设计一项潜在的自愿调查。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 哈佛大学研究人员利用工业数据与卫星影像，量化评估了2024年5月至2025年4月间美国403座超大规模数据中心的电力消耗，发现其年耗电量足以匹敌密歇根州的用电规模。报告指出，由于行业用电数据多以商业机密为由不予披露，且缺乏针对性的监管统计，数据中心正对全美电网构成严重负荷压力，其碳排放强度较AI普及前已增长两倍。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Researchers at Harvard University, using a combination of industry data and satellite imagery, quantified the energy consumption of 403 hyperscale data centers in the U.S. between May 2024 and April 2025, revealing annual electricity usage equivalent to the entire state of Michigan. The study highlights that due to proprietary data secrecy and a lack of regulatory transparency, these facilities are placing critical strain on the U.S. power grid, with carbon emissions three times higher than pre-AI boom levels.

author: OpenAI
article_content:
We have signed agreements with four independent assessors—Apollo Research, METR, Transluce, and Goodfire—for our first phase of embedded assessments. As AI capabilities advance rapidly and the potential risks grow, public reporting from independent assessments can give people a clearer view of how labs are evaluating and managing those risks.

Embedded assessments give independent experts deep access to a lab’s internal models and systems to assess model alignment and the effectiveness of safeguards over an extended period of time, especially where relevant to our safety cases. Based on what each evaluation needs, assessors receive access to some of the same internal resources our researchers use, including model checkpoints, source code, training and evaluation data, monitoring systems, technical documentation, and discussions with the researchers and engineers responsible for the work. This access gives assessors the evidence and context to pursue independent evaluations and uncover failures we may not have anticipated.

Our initial assessments focus on alignment and safeguards for models during training and internal use, complementing our safety cases. They build on our priorities and principles for third party assessments and years of work with third party evaluators, including a recent pilot assessment of our internal monitoring systems⁠(opens in a new window) with deep internal access and an investigation of the Hugging Face incident⁠(opens in a new window). We’ll use what we learn to deepen our work with independent experts in the coming months. These efforts also support our commitments under the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, where we agreed to independent assessments of our safety controls. These collaborations can contribute to stronger shared standards for independent assessment and public transparency across the industry.

In this pilot assessment, Apollo Research⁠(opens in a new window) will assess whether models could covertly work against their developers’ intentions and whether our safeguards would detect such behavior. Drawing on evidence from training, safety testing, and internal use. Apollo will assess four claims in two stages:

Training did not incentivize subversion.

Strong evaluations and red teaming do not elicit subversion.

Models have not attempted subversion during internal use.

Reasoning behind subversion would be detectable.

For the first stage of Apollo’s assessment, we’ll provide access to selected public and unreleased models and training checkpoints, relevant training data and evaluation results, training intervention records, monitoring systems and flagged behaviors, and researchers who can provide context, alongside the tools and compute needed to conduct independent testing.

Goodfire⁠(opens in a new window) will embed interpretability researchers and use the Goodfire platform to analyze model internals. The main objective of their assessment is training run monitoring, debugging, and alignment. The primary audience for their assessments are internal OpenAI researchers, who will use their findings to make safety improvements. Goodfire will also publish learnings and findings as the collaboration progresses.

Alignment assessment: For the first phase, METR will assess misaligned behavior in our largest reinforcement learning run to date, including failures that our existing tests and monitors may have missed. Within the selected run and agreed access, resources, and safety arrangements, METR would independently set assessment priorities and iterate on searches, analyses, and elicitation experiments. Access will include sampling relevant checkpoints, training and eval rollouts, and misalignment monitoring records for this run. For this first phase, the assessment will focus on our largest frontier RL run.1

Monitor assessment: We recently worked with METR to conduct a monitor stress testing exercise2. We have preliminarily agreed to conduct another monitor assessment⁠(opens in a new window) which we intend to be broader, but this is pending mutual agreement on the assessment scope.

Transluce will conduct an initial assessment of our post-training alignment evaluations, examining their quality and coverage. For the initial assessment, we will provide Transluce with access to selected public and unreleased models, our post-training alignment evaluations and relevant results, supporting model behavior data and safety case documentation, and researchers who can provide context, alongside the tools and compute needed to conduct independent testing.

OpenAI and Transluce also share the intent to conduct a follow-on assessment of approximately eight weeks in early 2027, with broader access to additional models, deeper access to our alignment evaluations, and information on how evaluation results inform model release decisions.

We’ve developed protocols and processes with input from the assessors to balance deep access with security, confidentiality, oversight, and the independence and integrity of assessments. We are sharing them to shed light on how we will work with embedded assessors, and to advance discussion about norms for embedded assessments, which have yet to be standardized. We expect that these will need to evolve as we learn more about how to best conduct these assessments. Especially in the early stages of embedded assessments, we expect technical access challenges, space constraints, evolving security protocols, and other unexpected issues to arise. We hope to work through these challenges collaboratively with our embedded assessors and share lessons learned.

Each engagement begins with an agreed scope and the access, resources, and safety arrangements needed to conduct a rigorous assessment. Some assessments test specific safety claims; others give assessors room to discover unexpected failure modes within a defined system or training run. In both cases, assessors need the freedom to follow evidence, refine their methods, and propose further assessments when findings warrant it. We also have a process for addressing additional access needs as assessments develop. When direct access could expose our most sensitive IP, such as model weights or architecture, we will consider alternatives, including pairing assessors with OpenAI researchers to run analyses.

Assessors who need access to sensitive confidential information will work on site at OpenAI offices and be provided OpenAI devices to conduct their work. The primary purpose is to protect the security of the information they access. Working onsite also gives assessors the opportunity to engage with dedicated staff who can help them navigate their access and provide context for their assessments. We also expect our embedded assessors to follow at minimum3 the same security standards as OpenAI employees when running experiments and evaluations.

Our Safety and Security Committee (SSC), an independent oversight committee of the OpenAI Foundation’s Board, will have visibility into the embedded assessment and the ability to exercise their oversight responsibilities before, during, and at their conclusion. They will receive unredacted reports, and both the assessors and the SSC will be able to speak with each other during the assessment, including privately. Disagreements among OpenAI and any evaluator will be escalated to the Safety Advisory Group and OpenAI executives, who will have a specified time period to resolve them, and the SSC will be notified of any such disagreements promptly when escalated. If a disagreement remains, the matter will be referred to the SSC for resolution.

Discussions with employees help assessors understand internal information and the context behind the work. OpenAI will authorize and provide guidance to staff members who can speak to assessors, and assessors may request additional staff to speak with as needed. To encourage open, candid conversations and protect the privacy of our staff, these discussions are off the record, meaning that they can inform the assessments but cannot be published or attributed to employees. Through a separate attestation pathway, assessors can request OpenAI-attested statements verifying, correcting, or clarifying something they learned in conversation with employees. These statements are not attributed to individuals or intended to characterize individual views. Assessors may publish statements that OpenAI attests to, or disclose that OpenAI declined to attest to a statement.

Managing conflicts of interest clearly and transparently—including those involving personal relationships, financial interests4, and other issues—is important to the integrity and independence of evaluations. Cool-off periods5 also need to be designed carefully, so assessors can work responsibly across labs while handling competitive information sensitively. We are working with our assessors to develop clear processes for both conflicts and cool-off periods, including allowing for flexibility in mitigations and transparency in decisions to request recusal.

Assessors maintain independence in publishing their assessments, but we will retain the right to redact confidential information, consistent with our previous third-party engagements. We may also request responsible disclosure delays to allow time to act on findings that could pose security or safety risks and remediate issues that remain.

Public reporting will help people understand the findings and their limitations, while more detailed confidential reports give oversight bodies the evidence they need to act. We want these assessments to improve how we identify and address risks, and give the public a clearer basis for judging our safety work.

These assessments bring an independent perspective to our ongoing alignment and safety work. Public reporting on their findings will make that work more transparent and provide greater assurance about how risks are being identified and addressed. We expect this first phase of assessments to lead to longer-term, consistent embedded engagements over time that can continuously provide third party safety signals and recommended improvements on our most load bearing safety claims and safety cases.

We’ll continue working with multiple independent third parties to help build a healthy assessment ecosystem with diverse expertise and approaches. Some investigations need sustained, on-site work with sensitive systems; others primarily evaluate deployed or soon to be deployed models or review public documentation.

In the coming months, we’ll support external assessments across a broader range of safety questions. We are also exploring future embedded assessments that would examine compliance with our safety frameworks, as well as our organizational culture and processes. We are committed to expanding this work and helping build the capacity and shared standards needed to sustain it.

This scope is less expansive than what METR outlines in their alignment assessment proposal⁠(opens in a new window), which envisions a broad survey of misalignment.

We recently conducted a 3 week long monitor red teaming exercise with METR, which granted them access to our codebase, monitors, relevant trajectories, and discussions with OpenAI research staff for the purpose of better understanding our monitors. https://metr.org/blog/2026-10-22-red-teaming-openai-agent-monitoring/⁠(opens in a new window)

In some cases, there will be more stringent standards applied depending on the conditions of the experiment to allow for careful security vetting.

but we believe it is important to disclose this.

We ask staff at third party organizations who participate in an embedded assessment to observe a brief cool-off period before embedding with another AI developer, to reduce the risk of inadvertent disclosure of confidential information.

article_content_zh:
我们已与四家独立评估机构（Apollo Research、METR、Transluce 和 Goodfire）签署了嵌入式评估第一阶段的协议。随着人工智能能力的快速发展和潜在风险的增加，独立评估的公开报告可以让人们更清楚地了解实验室如何评估和管理这些风险。

嵌入式评估使独立专家能够深入访问实验室的内部模型和系统，以评估模型的一致性和保护措施在较长时间内的有效性，特别是与我们的安全案例相关的情况。根据每次评估的需求，评估人员可以访问我们的研究人员使用的一些相同的内部资源，包括模型检查点、源代码、培训和评估数据、监控系统、技术文档以及与负责工作的研究人员和工程师的讨论。这种访问为评估人员提供了证据和背景，以进行独立评估并发现我们可能未预料到的失败。

我们的初步评估重点是培训和内部使用期间模型的一致性和保障措施，以补充我们的安全案例。它们建立在我们第三方评估的优先事项和原则以及与第三方评估人员多年的合作基础上，包括最近对我们的内部监控系统进行的试点评估⁠（在新窗口中打开）以及深入的内部访问以及对拥抱脸事件的调查⁠（在新窗口中打开）。在接下来的几个月里，我们将利用我们学到的知识来深化与独立专家的合作。这些努力也支持我们根据《白宫超级情报协议》做出的承诺，我们同意对我们的安全控制进行独立评估。这些合作有助于为整个行业的独立评估和公共透明度制定更强有力的共享标准。

在这次试点评估中，Apollo Research⁠（在新窗口中打开）将评估模型是否可以秘密地违背开发人员的意图，以及我们的防护措施是否会检测到此类行为。借鉴培训、安全测试和内部使用的证据。 Apollo 将分两个阶段评估四项索赔：

培训并没有激励颠覆。

强烈的评价和红队不会引发颠覆。

模型在内部使用过程中没有尝试颠覆。

颠覆背后的推理是可以察觉的。

在阿波罗评估的第一阶段，我们将提供对选定的公开和未发布的模型和训练检查点、相关训练数据和评估结果、训练干预记录、监控系统和标记行为的访问权限，以及可以提供背景信息的研究人员以及进行独立测试所需的工具和计算。

Goodfire⁠（在新窗口中打开）将嵌入可解释性研究人员并使用 Goodfire 平台来分析模型内部结构。他们评估的主要目标是训练运行监控、调试和对齐。他们评估的主要受众是内部 OpenAI 研究人员，他们将利用他们的发现来改进安全性。随着合作的进展，Goodfire 还将发布经验和发现。

一致性评估：在第一阶段，METR 将评估我们迄今为止最大的强化学习运行中的不一致行为，包括我们现有的测试和监视器可能遗漏的失败。在选定的运行和商定的访问、资源和安全安排内，METR 将独立设置评估优先级并迭代搜索、分析和启发实验。访问权限将包括对相关检查点进行采样、培训和评估部署以及本次运行的偏差监控记录。对于第一阶段，评估将重点关注我们最大的前沿强化学习运行。1

监控评估：我们最近与 METR 合作进行了监控压力测试2。我们初步同意进行另一次监测评估⁠（在新窗口中打开），我们打算扩大范围，但这有待双方就评估范围达成一致。

Transluce 将对我们的培训后对齐评估进行初步评估，检查其质量和覆盖范围。对于初步评估，我们将为 Transluce 提供对选定的公开和未发布模型的访问权限、我们的训练后一致性评估和相关结果、支持模型行为数据和安全案例文档，以及可以提供背景信息以及进行独立测试所需的工具和计算的研究人员。

OpenAI 和 Transluce 还同意在 2027 年初进行大约八周的后续评估，更广泛地访问其他模型，更深入地访问我们的一致性评估，以及有关评估结果如何为模型发布决策提供信息的信息。
