article_content_zh:
踏上它……侠盗猎车手 VI 即将呼啸进城。插图：Matt Taylor/The Guardian 全屏查看图片 踏上它……侠盗猎车手 VI 即将呼啸进城。插图：Matt Taylor/卫报 十年、数千名员工和十亿美元：《侠盗猎车手 VI》的独家内幕故事史诗犯罪传奇的最新一期终于来了。我们访问 Rockstar Games，亲身体验这十年来的文化盛事 – 并可以证实它的真实性，而不是像宣传的那样

许多人仍然感到惊讶的是，侠盗猎车手是一款明目张胆的美国犯罪系列游戏，过去 20 年来一直是世界上最受欢迎和最具争议的视频游戏之一，但它主要是在苏格兰制作的。但如果你在爱丁堡长大，开发商 Rockstar North 就是这个地方背景神话的一部分。在 2000 年代的某个时候，很多人作为游戏测试人员或员工都曾来过这个工作室。当时作为爱丁堡的一名学生，我经常听到高管家里举办疯狂派对的传闻，就像游戏中的那样颓废。在酒吧、生日或乔迁庆典上，你可能会遇到一个人，他声称自己想出了一种幼稚的双关语，为游戏内的生意增色不少（例如日本餐厅 Nutsaki 或炸鸡连锁店 Cluckin' Bell）。 《侠盗猎车手》现在是由全球近 5000 人的庞大团队制作的，但它的中枢神经系统仍然在荷里路德，在亚瑟王宝座的阴影下。

最新的侠盗猎车手游戏的背景确实离苏格兰首都不远了。侠盗猎车手 6 将我们带到列奥尼达州的罪恶城，这是对佛罗里达州迈阿密的模仿。这是一座霓虹灯笼罩的大都市，充满了肮脏和斗争，过度的狂欢派对与几乎不被掩盖的黑社会和不可预测的佛罗里达疯狂并存。

距离发售还有一个月，Rockstar 总部一片安静。许多人已经完成了这款游戏的工作，并在发布前准备休息——经过 10 多年的开发，这是当之无愧的休息。那些留在这里的人在完成一件艺术品和将其发布到世界之间时陷入了奇怪的无人区。当《GTA VI》问世时，预计将成为有史以来最赚钱的娱乐作品，预计第一年销量将达到数千万份，收入达数十亿美元；它的前身，2013 年的 GTA V，售出了 2.3 亿份。在游戏行业面临着一个可怕的时期，工作室倒闭、裁员和开发成本飙升的情况下，整个行业都在依靠《GTA VI》来打一剂强心剂。在一个几乎空无一人的楼层，屏幕上显示着发布日期的倒计时。

与此同时，对于许多玩家来说，等待新侠盗猎车手 13 年已经变得难以忍受。当 GTA VI 的片段在 N​​etflix 上精彩首映时，这家流媒体巨头的服务器几乎瘫痪了。仅在 YouTube 上，其第一部预告片的观看次数就已达 3 亿次。世界各地的人们都预订了 11 月 19 日的休息日，共同体验这一活动——在我们都生活在自己的算法内容泡沫的时代，这是越来越罕见的共享全球文化时刻之一。

Rockstar North 的气氛有些紧张，这不仅仅是因为即将发布的 GTA VI 的压力。在格拉斯哥，Rockstar 还在为一起备受瞩目的就业法庭案件进行辩护，该案件涉及去年解雇 34 名员工的事件，这些员工声称自己因参与工会组织活动而被解雇。该案原定于 10 月份结束，但现在将一直拖到《侠盗猎车手 VI》发布为止。在我访问的前几天，出版主管詹妮弗·科尔贝 (Jennifer Kolbe) 正在法庭上作证，而英国独立工人联盟 (IWGB) 的前雇员及其代表则在法庭外抗议。

查看全屏图片 犯罪是有代价的……侠盗猎车手 VI 的露西亚和杰森。照片：Rockstar Games 今天，Kolbe 和 Rob Nelson 坐在我面前，他是 Rockstar North 的联合工作室负责人，也是《GTA VI》的三位创意主管之一，向我展示了该工作室十多年来的花费，以及根据 Rockstar 不愿证实的独立估计，收入超过 10 亿美元。屏幕上，杰森和露西亚——两名在逃的年轻罪犯——正从酒吧前往夜总会，穿过罪恶都市市中心，最后一丝阳光消失，街道沐浴在荧光之中。他身材高大，方肩，穿着T恤和短裤。她把头发扎成马尾辫，穿着一件几乎没人能脱下的无情长袖露脐上衣。

在俱乐部里，一群穿着霓虹灯紫外线反应网状上衣旋转的虚拟人物中，彼此跳舞后，他们每个人都会戴上帽子，戴上墨镜，在脸上戴上头巾，举起一家珠宝店，然后开着一辆破旧的汽车逃入夜色，后备箱里塞满了装满现金和大型枪支的旅行袋，开车穿过玉米地躲避警察，这恰如其分地呼应了《邦妮和克莱德》。

露西娅是第一个在 GTA 游戏中登上头条的女性，她是众多犯罪主角中的一员，这些主角的范围从直率的精神变态者（GTA V 的 Trevor）到出人意料的同情心（GTA IV 的 Niko Bellic 和 San Andreas 的 CJ）。 《GTA VI》既是她的故事，也是杰森的故事。对于这款游戏的某些行为，你会被锁定在一个角色的视角中，但大多数时候你可以在它们之间自由切换。当他们分开时，您可以确保他们互相发短信和打电话。当他们在一起时，你可以带他们进行一些小约会：去健身房、去酒吧、去冥想静修处或去酒类商店。作为玩家，你成为他们关系的管理者，如果你忽视了这一点，就会产生后果。 “你融入了他们的生活，”尼尔森解释道，露西娅在高速公路上飞驰，杰森探出窗外，向追赶他们的警车的轮胎开枪。 “这种关系是由你来培养的，还是由你来失去的。是否仍然是一段浪漫的关系取决于你自己。”

这种动态不仅有趣，而且对侠盗猎车手来说也是变革性的。该系列以黑色幽默和无方向的暴力混乱而闻名，让玩家在纽约、迈阿密或洛杉矶的虚拟模仿中自由地撞毁被盗的汽车并恐吓行人。 《侠盗猎车手 V》尤其是一个奢侈的平等机会犯罪者，它的目标是所有人和一切，从美国政府到自恋的科技兄弟，从被宠坏的洛杉矶小孩到乡下人，从超级富豪到住在大篷车里的浪费者。在 GTA 游戏中，没有人非常关心任何人。然而，在这里，我们不仅被要求关心这些角色，还要表现出他们如何互相关心。当他们在一起时，你可以按一个按钮让他们牵手。

这款游戏已经存在这么久了，仅仅只是热切的谣言，但现在看到这款游戏的实际运作，实在令人难以置信。自 2015 年以来，《GTA VI》一直在以某种形式进行开发，当时团队首次前往迈阿密进行考察（当时，游戏的代号是“美洲计划”，反映了后来放弃的跨越两大洲的雄心）。但直到 2023 年 12 月才宣布，此后已两次推迟。我的印象是，Rockstar 的人基本上被迫放下了他们的隐喻画笔。 “如果有选择的话，他们永远不会停止开发这款游戏，”科尔贝有些遗憾地说道。 “关闭它真的很难，”尼尔森承认。 “如果你离开并从中获得一点空间，你就可以客观地看待它并说：‘我为我们所做的事情感到自豪’。但最终，它会被从你身边夺走，你会尽最大努力在被告知的时间内完成它。”

通常，在发布之前播放视频游戏时，人们会看到精心设计的动作片段，旨在展示游戏的最佳状态，但这不是这里发生的情况。我们只是在人口稠密的罪恶都市里闲逛，几乎我建议的任何事情我们都能做到。从杰森和露西亚的火烈鸟壁纸公寓走出，走进佛罗里达州的阳光下，我们首先看到的是一个遛狗的女人。我问我们是否可以抚摸它；尼尔森按下按钮，杰森说：“我抚摸你的狗很酷吗？” “当然，她喜欢向公众打招呼，”这位女士回答道，然后杰森弯下腰去惹这只小狗。当你经过时，你可以无意中听到行人的谈话，打断他们可能会导致困惑“我们见过吗？”或一连串谩骂。后来，我看到一只海鸥坐在海滩边的柱子上，为了惹恼我，我就问它是什么鸟。 Jason 拿出一副双筒望远镜，海鸥被记录在野生动物日志中，我自豪地得知有 62 种鸟类可供观赏。

如果不做这些事情，混乱就会迅速加剧。在发生了几次小规模的犯罪事件后，我们带杰森和露西娅去了一家戒备森严的珠宝店，露西娅在那里用手枪指着保安，紧张了几秒钟，然后他们投降了。然而，在楼上，杰森正把保险箱里的钱塞进手提包里，另一名警卫决定开枪而不是投降。随后发生了一场绝望的争夺，杰森用枪托打了那个人，把他打晕了，而露西娅在商店前面大喊大叫，当他们爬上一辆偷来的摩托车逃跑时，警察赶到了。追捕行动绕了半个街区，警车和直升机紧随其后。当杰森和露西娅最终回到车上时，他们把现金存起来，换了衣服，在市郊躺了一会儿，等待炎热的天气过去。

title: Tech startups and VC firms are hiring for "ecosystem" roles, like "startup ecosystem lead", to prioritize in-person networking and cut through AI marketing slop (Lora Kelley/New York Times)
title_en: Tech startups and VC firms are hiring for "ecosystem" roles, like "startup ecosystem lead", to prioritize in-person networking and cut through AI marketing slop (Lora Kelley/New York Times)
author: New York Times
article_content:
This as-told-to essay is based on a conversation with Ibrahim Noon, 20, a San Francisco-based associate at venture capital firm Forerunner. The following has been edited for length and clarity. I was raised on a small farm in Pakistan.

My father is a farmer, but a historian at heart, so I grew up reading about Alexander, Napoleon, Hannibal, and, later, Silicon Valley figures like Steve Jobs. I was always fascinated by how a few people end up shaping what comes next. My first exposure to the US was a two-month remote research program with Stanford’s Graduate School of Education.

I worked on augmented- and virtual-reality simulations designed to teach students environmental science. I came to the University of California, Berkeley, at 17 to study economics and data science. During university, I interned at KPMG in carbon markets, then did sales at a brokerage firm in Miami and later on Wall Street.

I had been this tech-savvy person who was not very social or open, and the finance and sales experiences helped me become more comfortable talking to people. I left the internship early to work on two startups back-to-back. I didn't end up pursuing them long-term, but I learned so much from doing discovery calls with customers and building both products from scratch.

With the startups wrapped, I felt clueless about what I wanted to do. I had a very broad interest toward venture capital. This was initially noticed by one of my professors at the entrepreneurship and technology center, and I was nicknamed "VC Noon" in my class, after my last name.

A lot of my friends who were pitching to VCs would come to me for feedback and advice before going to them. Throughout college, I had been building relationships with investors, just informally and without any incentive. While working on my first startup, I met people at Afore Capital and began sending them founders I met through clubs and classes.

I liked being the bridge between ambitious people and the firms that could help them. After graduating in May, I had an offer from Morgan Stanley and was supposed to start this August. In mid-July, I saw that a tech VC firm called Forerunner had been hiring an associate, but the application had already been paused for more than two months.

I was frustrated that I had found it late because it seemed like a great fit for me. But I thought: I need to get in front of them regardless. I spent a full day on a thoughtful email, my résumé, and a one-page investment thesis on consumer AI, and wrote all of it without using any AI.

I read Forerunner’s website and all of its published prospectuses and developed my own investment thesis. My first call with a Forerunner partner felt natural because I was mindful not to just list my accolades but to have a real person-to-person conversation. I met more of the investment team in person over the next few days and reached an interview round, which involved a case study walkthrough.

For that case study, I had to map my network: who I knew, what they were building, and how Forerunner could benefit from those relationships. My thesis was simple: the next generation of founders is increasingly young, and it helps to build a real relationship with them before they have a company or even a solid idea.

“I want to find people before they find themselves” was the way I put it. They may work at OpenAI, Anthropic, Cognition, or another ambitious company before starting their own company. The goal is to stay in touch so that, when they begin building, we are already among the first people they call.

I learned that it matters less to have thousands of LinkedIn connections than to keep the right relationships warm. I have about 6,000 connections, but that does not mean I can ask every person for a favor. Looking back, what worked for me is being in the right spaces, trying to be genuinely useful to others, and following up.

I'd suggest anyone else looking to get into the industry young go to events, hackathons, and big conferences and introduce yourself. One small thing I do is keep my LinkedIn QR code as my phone lockscreen because people are always in a hurry at events. I've also learned not to be afraid of outreach.

At my brokerage internship, I sent 250 outbound messages a day, with most people not getting back, and I applied that to my life too. I tell myself: "Worst-case scenario, they just won't text back — and that's totally fine."
summary_en: The people ushering in the artificial intelligence revolution are also doubling down on in-person relationships in their own industry.

article_content_zh:
这篇文章是基于与 20 岁的易卜拉欣·努恩 (Ibrahim Noon) 的对话，易卜拉欣·努恩是风投公司 Forerunner 驻旧金山的合伙人。为了篇幅和清晰度，以下内容已被编辑。我在巴基斯坦的一个小农场长大。

我的父亲是一名农民，但本质上是一名历史学家，所以我从小就阅读有关亚历山大、拿破仑、汉尼拔以及后来的史蒂夫·乔布斯等硅谷人物的故事。我总是着迷于少数人最终如何塑造接下来的事情。我第一次接触美国是在斯坦福大学教育研究生院进行的为期两个月的远程研究项目。

我致力于增强现实和虚拟现实模拟，旨在教授学生环境科学。 17 岁时，我来到加州大学伯克利分校学习经济学和数据科学。大学期间，我在毕马威碳市场实习，然后在迈阿密的一家经纪公司从事销售工作，后来又在华尔街从事销售工作。

我曾经是一个精通技术的人，但不太善于交际或开放，财务和销售经验帮助我变得更自在地与人交谈。我提前离开了实习岗位，连续在两家初创公司工作。我最终并没有长期追求它们，但我从与客户进行发现电话以及从头开始构建这两种产品中学到了很多东西。

随着初创公司的成立，我对自己想做什么一无所知。我对风险投资有着非常广泛的兴趣。这最初是由我在创业和技术中心的一位教授注意到的，我在班上被昵称为“VC Noon”，以我的姓氏命名。

我的很多向风险投资人推销的朋友在去找他们之前都会向我寻求反馈和建议。在整个大学期间，我一直在与投资者建立关系，只是非正式的，没有任何激励。在我的第一家初创公司工作时，我遇到了艾伏资本的人，并开始向他们派遣我通过俱乐部和课程认识的创始人。

我喜欢成为雄心勃勃的人和可以帮助他们的公司之间的桥梁。五月份毕业后，我收到了摩根士丹利的录用通知，预计今年八月开始工作。 7月中旬，我看到一家名为Forerunner的科技风投公司正在招聘一名合伙人，但申请已经暂停了两个多月。

我很沮丧，因为我发现它太晚了，因为它看起来非常适合我。但我想：无论如何我都需要走到他们面前。我花了一整天的时间写了一封深思熟虑的电子邮件、我的简历和一篇关于消费者人工智能的一页投资论文，并且在没有使用任何人工智能的情况下写下了所有这些内容。

我阅读了先行者的网站及其所有已发布的招股说明书，并形成了自己的投资论文。我与先行者合作伙伴的第一次通话感觉很自然，因为我注意不只是列出我的荣誉，而是进行真正的人与人之间的对话。在接下来的几天里，我亲自见到了投资团队的更多成员，并进行了一轮面试，其中涉及案例研究演练。

对于该案例研究，我必须绘制我的网络图：我认识谁，他们正在构建什么，以及先行者如何从这些关系中受益。我的论点很简单：下一代创始人越来越年轻，这有助于在他们拥有一家公司甚至一个可靠的想法之前与他们建立真正的关系。

“我想在人们发现自己之前找到他们”，这是我的说法。在创办自己的公司之前，他们可能会在 OpenAI、Anthropic、Cognition 或其他雄心勃勃的公司工作。我们的目标是保持联系，以便当他们开始建造时，我们已经是他们最先打电话的人之一。

我了解到，拥有数千个 LinkedIn 连接比保持正确的关系更重要。我有大约 6,000 个联系人，但这并不意味着我可以向每个人请求帮助。回顾过去，对我有用的是处于正确的位置，努力真正对他人有用，并跟进。

我建议其他想要进入这个行业的年轻人去参加活动、黑客马拉松和大型会议并介绍自己。我做的一件小事就是将 LinkedIn 二维码保留为手机锁屏，因为人们总是匆忙参加活动。我也学会了不要害怕外展。

在我的经纪实习期间，我每天发送 250 条出站消息，大多数人都没有回复，我也将这一点应用到了我的生活中。我告诉自己：“最坏的情况是，他们只是不回短信——那完全没问题。”

title: Amazon's Prime Air drone service, which operates across 18 sites in 10 US states, is drawing local opposition; its Baton Rouge hub launches ~30 drones per hour (Kris Maher/Wall Street Journal)
title_en: Amazon's Prime Air drone service, which operates across 18 sites in 10 US states, is drawing local opposition; its Baton Rouge hub launches ~30 drones per hour (Kris Maher/Wall Street Journal)
author: Wall Street Journal
article_content:
Amazon’s Prime Air drone delivery option launched recently in the south and southwest suburbs, catching some residents and officials off guard and raising questions about noise and safety.

Drone delivery began from Amazon’s Markham location Oct. 12, and is available in a 7.5-mile radius around the distribution center, 2201 W. 159th St. Communities in the radius include Homewood, Harvey and South Holland.

“It’s new,” said Homewood Mayor Rich Hofeld. “You just don’t know until you look up and there it is.”

Homewood didn’t receive any warning or communication from Amazon before the service launched, Hofeld said.

The Prime Air service will soon begin from the Matteson location, 7001 Vollmer Road, Amazon economic development manager Sam Bailey said, though he didn’t give an exact date.

“What we’ve found is this service is in high demand here in Markham,” Bailey said.

The Markham site has generally hit its maximum capacity of 300 drone orders daily, Bailey said, with thousands of orders delivered by 21 drones across the 7.5-mile radius.

Scaling up is “something that we’re always considering,” Bailey said.

“For right now, we’ve thrilled to have launched the site just in time for the holidays,” Bailey said. “We’re also excited to be launching Matteson, which will also add to our capacity as well.”

Amazon received approval from Markham to construct the drone takeoff and landing site as well as from the Federal Aviation Authority to use the airspace, he said.

The drones are relatively loud when they are close to the ground, with the sound of takeoffs and landings occasionally drowning out speakers at a ribbon-cutting event Tuesday at the Markham center.

“At the point of delivery they top out at 68 decibels,” Bailey said. “It’s very brief exposure and it only occurs during daytime hours.”

The drones can deliver packages up to 5 pounds. Sixty percent of the inventory at the Markham center is deliverable by drone, Bailey said.

The drones have forward-facing cameras, Bailey said, which are strictly used for navigation.

“This drone does not have surveillance-like technology,” he said. “The footage would only be utilized in the event of an incident or an emergency, but that footage is not viewed, and the drone does not have the ability to view license plates, faces, scan, take pictures.”

Bailey cast Prime Air as an option for people to order small necessities at urgent times.

“Think of parents, seniors, those who might not be able to leave their home,” Bailey said. “That sick kid, and you find that your children’s medicine is expired, diapers, the essentials you need in that moment.”

Markham Mayor Roger Agpawa and members of the Markham City Council cut a ribbon Tuesday to symbolize the program’s launch.

“We’re all benefiting,” Agpawa said. “This is another piece of economic development, and a very strong piece, at that, because it’s providing a different type of a service.”

Agpawa compared the drone program to “The Jetsons.” He said he had ordered drone delivery shortly after the program launched.

“I think it might have been vitamins,” Agpawa said. “My neighbors came out, and I was turning the corner to come home and I was taking a picture of it. It was pretty exciting.”

Some people have voiced safety concerns, he said, though he didn’t view Amazon’s drones as any more dangerous than smaller recreational drones.

Residents have also expressed concerns about the noise, he said.

“When you have thousands of people in a community, there’s going to be a couple that just don’t want the noise, and some that are going to question whether it’s going to run into my house or you’re going to hit the dog or the kids,” Agpawa said.

He said Amazon addressed those concerns to his full satisfaction, he said.

“Nothing is ever foolproof,” Agpawa said.

Homewood has already heard complaints from some residents, Hofeld said. In the comments responding to Homewood’s social media post about the drones, reactions ranged from enthusiasm to outright hostility.

“People were questioning why they were being flown,” Hofeld said. “They were questioning about notification and how they were going to be aware of them.”

Bailey said customers should clear the area when a drone delivery is incoming. The drones drop packages from about 12 feet. If the drone detects movement in the area, he said, the delivery will be canceled.

“You want your kids inside the house,” Bailey said. “We will not drop a package in an unsafe location. People who want to stand below and try to catch it, don’t do that.”

The village of Thornton Recreation Department said preschool children witnessed a drone delivery to Cora Court.

Several municipalities, including Homewood and Dolton, issued statements encouraging residents to contact amazondronefeedback@amazon.com with any concerns about drone noise, deliveries and property damage.

Safety concerns can also be reported to the Federal Aviation Administration at hotline.faa.gov, officials said.

Amazon said in August it planned to bring Prime Air almost 500 cities and towns by the end of the year.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 无人机配送的规模化扩张正从技术验证转向市政治理博弈，其核心卡点在于低空空域的“邻避效应”而非技术指标。随着运营半径扩大，亚马逊面临的监管压力将从联邦航空管理局的准入许可转向属地行政区的噪音法规及隐私审查，这要求其在物流效率与社区许可（Social License to Operate）之间寻求新的商业平衡。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The scaling of drone delivery is shifting from technical validation to a conflict of municipal governance, where the bottleneck is 'NIMBYism' regarding low-altitude airspace rather than technical specs. As operations expand, Amazon's primary challenge is pivoting from FAA regulatory compliance to securing a social license through community-level noise management and privacy transparency.

article_content_zh:
亚马逊的 Prime Air 无人机送货选项最近在南部和西南郊区推出，让一些居民和官员措手不及，并引发了有关噪音和安全的问题。

无人机送货服务于 10 月 12 日从亚马逊位于万锦市的地点开始，在配送中心 2201 W. 159th St 周围 7.5 英里的范围内提供服务。半径内的社区包括霍姆伍德、哈维和南荷兰。

“这是新的，”霍姆伍德市长里奇霍菲尔德说。 “你只是不知道，直到你抬头一看，它就在那里。”

霍菲尔德说，在该服务推出之前，霍姆伍德没有收到亚马逊的任何警告或通信。

亚马逊经济发展经理萨姆·贝利 (Sam Bailey) 表示，Prime Air 服务很快将从马特森地点 (7001 Vollmer Road) 开始，但他没有给出具体日期。

“我们发现万锦市对这项服务的需求量很大，”贝利说。

贝利表示，万锦市站点已基本达到每日 300 份无人机订单的最大容量，21 架无人机在 7.5 英里半径范围内交付了数千份订单。

贝利说，扩大规模是“我们一直在考虑的事情”。

贝利说：“就目前而言，我们很高兴能在假期前及时推出这个网站。”“我们也很高兴推出马特森，这也将增加我们的产能。”

他说，亚马逊获得了万锦市的批准，可以建造无人机起飞和着陆场，并获得了联邦航空局的批准，可以使用该空域。

周二在万锦中心举行的剪彩活动中，无人机靠近地面时的声音相对较大，起飞和着陆的声音偶尔会淹没扬声器。

“在交付时，噪音最高可达 68 分贝，”贝利说。 “这是非常短暂的暴露，而且只发生在白天。”

无人机可以运送重达 5 磅的包裹。贝利说，万锦中心百分之六十的库存是通过无人机交付的。

贝利说，这些无人机配有前置摄像头，仅用于导航。

title: Fan fiction website AO3, run by nonprofit Organization for Transformative Works, returns online after a "security incident", ahead of its four-week timeline (Adeel Hassan/New York Times)
title_en: Fan fiction website AO3, run by nonprofit Organization for Transformative Works, returns online after a "security incident", ahead of its four-week timeline (Adeel Hassan/New York Times)

inline_images.caption: The AO3 website was restored on Sunday, welcoming readers after an outage that started last month.Credit...David Keyton/Associated Press
inline_images.alt: The AO3 website was restored on Sunday, welcoming readers after an outage that started last month.Cr

author: New York Times
article_content:
It’s a library of nearly 19 million works, more than double the circulating materials of the New York Public Library, so when it was knocked offline in a “security incident” more than two weeks ago, its 12 million users were aghast.

The volunteers who run the fan fiction site AO3, short for “Archive of Our Own,” had quickly assured its enormous community that no data — especially all those works — had been lost and that it would be restored in four weeks.

But on Sunday, the repository of homespun stories based on works like “Harry Potter,” “Twilight” and “Heated Rivalry” was mostly back online, with some features — like importing external work — temporarily disabled, to help the site return earlier than expected.

“The intensity of the response speaks to how deeply fan fiction has become woven into our lives,” Dana Bryce, a writer and cultural commentator in Toronto, said on Sunday afternoon.

“The AO3 outage has shown how deeply participatory storytelling is now embedded in everyday cultural life,” Ms. Bryce said. “And its absence made the importance of that relationship visible.”

The works hosted on the nonprofit, noncommercial archive are inspired by books, films and even celebrities, like the members of K-pop bands. It is run entirely by volunteers, and operated by the Organization for Transformative Works.

She said that fan fiction democratizes storytelling, and that AO3 readers were not limited by long publishing cycles or a single author’s pen.

“It’s a shared experience,” she said. “Instead of reading in silos, audiences can read and write as a collective, reimagining, revising, reinterpreting and expanding fictional worlds, becoming active participants in storytelling.”

AO3 said on Sunday that it would not disclose what had happened to the site, referring to the outage as a “security incident.”

It said it would not share specifics of mitigating changes it was putting in place but did say it was consulting with a security firm.

It recommended that users change their passwords, while noting that “we have no reason to believe that the user database was compromised.”

There was so much site traffic on Sunday that some users faced delays loading it. “This is an intentional measure to help manage traffic,” AO3 said.

Ms. Bryce was not surprised by readers’ response on Sunday, calling AO3 “a collective cultural archive.”

“It’s a living record of evolving audience desires and attachments,” she said.

article_content_zh:
该图书馆拥有近 1900 万册藏书，是纽约公共图书馆流通资料的两倍多，因此当它在两周前因“安全事件”而下线时，其 1200 万用户都惊呆了。

运营同人小说网站 AO3（“Archive of Our Own”的缩写）的志愿者很快向其庞大的社区保证，没有任何数据（尤其是所有这些作品）丢失，并且将在四个星期内恢复。

但周日，基于《哈利·波特》、《暮光之城》和《激烈竞争》等作品的朴素故事库大部分重新上线，但暂时禁用了一些功能（例如导入外部作品），以帮助该网站比预期更早恢复。

多伦多作家兼文化评论员达纳·布莱斯 (Dana Bryce) 周日下午表示：“反应的强烈程度说明了同人小说已经融入我们的生活有多深。”

布莱斯女士说：“AO3 的中断表明，参与式讲故事现在已经深深地融入到了日常文化生活中。” “它的缺席凸显了这种关系的重要性。”

该非营利性、非商业性档案馆中托管的作品灵感来自于书籍、电影，甚至是韩国流行乐队成员等名人。它完全由志愿者运营，并由变革工作组织运营。

“现代观众非常贪婪，”布莱斯女士说。 “我们总是想要更多。没有什么比故事更能体现这一点。我们对小说、电视剧和电影的结局越来越不满意。故事已经成为观众想要无限期重温的世界。”

她说，同人小说使讲故事变得民主化，AO3 的读者不受长出版周期或单一作者笔迹的限制。

“这是一次共同的经历，”她说。 “观众不再是孤岛阅读，而是可以作为一个集体来阅读和写作，重新想象、修改、重新解释和扩展虚构世界，成为讲故事的积极参与者。”

AO3 周日表示，不会透露该网站发生的情况，并将此次中断称为“安全事件”。

该公司表示不会透露正在实施的缓解措施的具体细节，但确实表示正在与一家安全公司进行咨询。

它建议用户更改密码，同时指出“我们没有理由相信用户数据库已被泄露。”

周日网站流量如此之大，以至于一些用户面临加载延迟的问题。 AO3 表示：“这是一项旨在帮助管理交通的有意措施。”

布莱斯女士对周日读者的反应并不感到惊讶，称 AO3 为“集体文化档案馆”。

【起因与机理】应对突发安全威胁并维护1900万篇作品的社区数据安全
【核心事实细节】转型作品组织作为核心管理方负责AO3安全修复。
【涉及范围与推进】建议用户立即更换登录密码，后续将持续进行安全加固。

title: Nvidia Was Already in Trouble Before the Jensen Huang Mess
title_en: Nvidia Was Already in Trouble Before the Jensen Huang Mess

inline_images.caption: Image may contain Smoke Pipe Game Baby Person and Chess
inline_images.alt: Image may contain Smoke Pipe Game Baby Person and Chess

author: Wired AI
article_content:
Nvidia played a key role enabling the AI gold rush thanks in large part to its recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang. Huang was a master of foreseeing technological changes, investing in chips to train AI earlier than most.

But just as he’s leaving, the company has a growing list of competitors with a range of new, advanced technology breathing down its neck. For Nvidia, where CFO Colette Kress has now taken the reins, the timing isn’t great.

“Everything sold today was designed two-to-three years ago,” says the CEO of a large AI company, who spoke to WIRED on condition of anonymity to avoid hurting business relationships. Kress, or whoever replaces her permanently, will have to chart the course that the chip industry will take two years from now, the CEO says.

Already, competitors have started to move in.

Nvidia dominates the market for AI accelerators, capturing 80 percent of sales, according to Silicon Analysis. Longtime nemesis AMD is now making a concerted effort to build competitive AI chips. Its share of the market has crept up from just two percent in 2022 to between 7 and 10 percent in 2026.

Big US cloud players—Google, Amazon, and Microsoft—are all developing more specialized chips to power the training and serving of AI models. Each has seen similar gains. These companies are designing their own silicon to reduce costs and to gain some independence from Nvidia.

Several startups now offer more specialized chips that promise improvements over Nvidia’s core products. Cerebras, for instance, sells giant ones meant to power giant AI models. AMD recently bought Taalas, a company that burns models’ weights into silicon to make computations ultra efficient. Using these chips requires rewriting a lot of code, however, to make them work with cutting-edge AI models.

Patrick Moorhead, chief analyst at MoorInStrat, a company that tracks the chip industry, says the rise of AI agents makes inference, or running models that have already been trained, more important. That’s an area where Nvidia has less of an edge compared to cloud hyperscalers and startups. Nvidia did, however, acquire a startup making specialized chips, called Grok, in December of 2025.

And because of the rise in AI assistants and agents, there’s also growing demand for general purpose central processing units (CPUs), Moorehead said, an area where Nvidia barely competes.

Nvidia still maintains a huge lead in AI thanks to Huang’s foresight. Huang cofounded the company in 1993 to design graphics chips for PCs. In the mid-2010s, he saw the promise of AI. He funded academic research on the topic, developed software to support AI engineering, and gave hardware to labs and startups.

In 2022, ChatGPT took AI mainstream and sales of Nvidia chips skyrocketed. The company’s revenue went from $26.91 billion in January 2022 to $215.94 billion in January 2026. The challenges it faces may not be existential—but they do add up, especially on a global scale.

While Nvidia’s fortunes have risen in the US, they have declined in the world’s other big market for AI, China. Washington is trying to restrict access to its most advanced chips, while Beijing is trying to develop its own chip industry. Nvidia is not allowed to sell its most powerful chips in China, but it can sell previous generations. Sales of these chips as well as non AI chips doubled over the past year, but China now accounts for only eight percent of the company’s overall revenue, compared with 20 percent in 2024, according to its fillings. It remains unclear how many chips exported to other countries may either end up in China or end up being used remotely by Chinese firms.

Huawei, a Chinese tech giant targeted with US sanctions for several years, has developed new kinds of supercomputers that harness many more chips than usual to train and run AI models. Some Chinese AI companies, such as Z.ai, which makes one of the world’s best open source models, say they’ve trained their models entirely using Huawei’s chips. If Chinese open-weight models gain traction in other countries, it could create a market for Chinese chips elsewhere.

Huang’s dealings with China played a major role in his downfall. He had a romantic relationship with Huang Le, also known as Alice Huang, a Chinese executive at a Singaporean company called Megaspeed who the US government suspects of being an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Megaspeed and its subsidiaries have reportedly imported between $4.6 and $7.5 billion Nvidia chips into southeast Asia. Reports suggest that the company may have provided access to the chips to Chinese AI firms.

Babak Minovi, a senior analyst at the Eurasia Group, a consultancy that focuses on technology and geopolitics, says Huang was right to point out that cutting off access to China would empower domestic rivals. “Huang was taking a pragmatic line, and he knows competition,” he says.

Even in markets that it dominates, Nvidia may turn out to be a victim of its own success. The AI models built using Nvidia’s chip are automating the very elements of coding, data analysis, and scientific research that help design chips.

Most chip design firms use specialized AI models to arrange components on processors—something that traditionally required deep engineering expertise and experience. And both OpenAI and Anthropic have recently touted the ability of their newest models to design electronics from scratch.

Moorhead says the shift towards AI chip design may not pose a huge threat to Nvidia because it’s riding the same wave.“They have access to AI too,” he notes.

But Moorhead says the way AI models can now quickly rewrite code to run on different hardware may prove a problem. For years, Nvidia has attracted developers by providing software that makes it easy to write programs and build models for its silicon. Its Compute Unified Device Architecture, or CUDA, has long been seen as a moat to ensure AI companies continue to rely on Nvidia chips.

But AI models are now so good at reading and writing code that they can port an AI model over to a competitor's silicon at speed.

Wafer, a startup that uses AI to port models to AMD and then serves them more cheaply, has seen revenue grow spectacularly in recent months, boasts CEO Emilio Andere.

Every time a major new open weight model is released Wafer can have it running on AMD hardware at least 80 percent as efficiently within hours, he says. Andere says AI is getting so capable that his engineers barely have to edit or review the code.

Dan Hutchinson, a veteran chip analyst, says Nvidia may be entering its “Intel swan moment,” referring to the 2019 replacement of engineering-focused CEO Brian Krzanich with its CFO Bob Swan. (Sound familiar? Krzanich also resigned after a relationship with an employee; Huang is alleged to have had multiple.) From there, the company’s focus shifted to sales more than technical progress. Bureaucracy ballooned and revenue tanked.

“Nvidia is now an Intel waiting to happen,” he says.

article_content_zh:
英伟达在推动人工智能淘金热中发挥了关键作用，这在很大程度上要归功于其最近被罢免的首席执行官黄仁勋。黄仁勋是预见技术变革的大师，他比大多数人更早地投资芯片来训练人工智能。

但就在他离开时，该公司的竞争对手越来越多，他们采用了一系列先进的新技术。对于目前由首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)接任的英伟达来说，时机并不好。

一家大型人工智能公司的首席执行官表示：“今天出售的所有产品都是两三年前设计的。”为了避免损害业务关系，他不愿透露姓名。这位首席执行官表示，克雷斯或任何永久取代她的人都必须制定芯片行业两年后的发展方向。

竞争对手已经开始介入。

根据 Silicon Analysis 的数据，Nvidia 在人工智能加速器市场占据主导地位，占据了 80% 的销售额。长期以来的宿敌AMD现在正在齐心协力打造有竞争力的AI芯片。其市场份额已从 2022 年的 2% 攀升至 2026 年的 7% 至 10%。

美国大型云计算公司——谷歌、亚马逊和微软——都在开发更专业的芯片来支持人工智能模型的训练和服务。每个人都获得了相似的收益。这些公司正在设计自己的芯片，以降低成本并获得一定程度的独立于 Nvidia 的地位。

几家初创公司现在提供更专业的芯片，有望对 Nvidia 的核心产品进行改进。例如，Cerebras 销售旨在为巨型人工智能模型提供动力的大型产品。 AMD 最近收购了 Taalas，这家公司将模型的权重刻录到硅片中，从而使计算变得非常高效。然而，使用这些芯片需要重写大量代码，才能使它们与尖端的人工智能模型一起工作。

跟踪芯片行业的公司 MoorInStrat 的首席分析师帕特里克·穆尔黑德 (Patrick Moorhead) 表示，人工智能代理的兴起使得推理或运行已经训练过的模型变得更加重要。与云超大规模企业和初创公司相比，英伟达在这个领域的优势较小。然而，Nvidia 确实于 2025 年 12 月收购了一家生产专用芯片的初创公司 Grok。

摩尔黑德表示，由于人工智能助手和代理的兴起，对通用中央处理器（CPU）的需求也不断增长，而英伟达在这一领域几乎没有竞争。

得益于黄仁勋的远见，英伟达在人工智能领域仍然保持着巨大的领先优势。黄先生于 1993 年与他人共同创立了该公司，为 PC 设计图形芯片。 2010 年代中期，他看到了人工智能的前景。他资助了该主题的学术研究，开发了支持人工智能工程的软件，并向实验室和初创公司提供了硬件。

2022年，ChatGPT让AI成为主流，Nvidia芯片销量猛增。该公司的收入从 2022 年 1 月的 269.1 亿美元增至 2026 年 1 月的 2159.4 亿美元。它面临的挑战可能不是存在的，但它们确实会累积起来，尤其是在全球范围内。

尽管英伟达在美国的命运有所上升，但在世界另一个人工智能大市场中国却出现了下滑。华盛顿正试图限制其最先进芯片的使用，而北京则试图发展自己的芯片产业。英伟达不允许在中国销售其最强大的芯片，但它可以销售前几代芯片。根据其备案信息，这些芯片以及非人工智能芯片的销售额在过去一年中翻了一番，但中国目前仅占该公司总收入的 8%，而 2024 年将占 20%。目前尚不清楚有多少出口到其他国家的芯片可能最终进入中国或最终被中国公司远程使用。

多年来一直受到美国制裁的中国科技巨头华为开发了新型超级计算机，可以利用比平常更多的芯片来训练和运行人工智能模型。一些中国人工智能公司，例如拥有世界上最好的开源模型之一的再爱科技，表示他们已经完全使用华为的芯片来训练他们的模型。如果中国的开放式重量模型在其他国家获得关注，它可能会在其他国家为中国芯片创造市场。

黄与中国的往来在他的垮台中发挥了重要作用。他与黄乐（又名爱丽丝·黄）有过一段浪漫关系，黄乐是一家名为 Megaspeed 的新加坡公司的中国高管，美国政府怀疑该公司是中国国家安全部的资产。据报道，Megaspeed 及其子公司已向东南亚进口价值 4.6 至 75 亿美元的 Nvidia 芯片。有报道称，该公司可能已向中国人工智能公司提供了这些芯片的使用权。

【起因与机理】AI推理需求崛起与云巨头去英伟达化策略加速
【关键数据与实测】目前市场竞争不仅来自AMD（其市场份额已从2022年的2%增长至2026年的7-10%），还包括谷歌、微软及亚马逊通过自研定制芯片带来的垂直整合冲击，以及针对推理任务优化芯片的新兴创业公司竞争。
【各方立场与态度】云巨头自研芯片战略致使英伟达在推理市场面临份额流失压力。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Colette Kress (Interim CEO/CFO of Nvidia) (AI Accelerator Market): Assuming leadership while navigating market pressure from AMD, hyperscalers, and specialized chip startups
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Rising demand for inference and the strategic drive for vertical integration by cloud giants

title: Baidu Posts Sixth Straight Sales Drop After AI Drag Persists
title_en: Baidu Posts Sixth Straight Sales Drop After AI Drag Persists
author: Bloomberg
content_snippet: Baidu Inc. posted its sixth straight quarterly revenue drop, underscoring the urgency of its efforts to commercialize AI to offset a faltering legacy search business.
summary_en: Baidu Inc. reported Q3 revenue of approximately 33.6 billion yuan ($4.6 billion), a 1% year-over-year decline, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of revenue contraction. Despite the downturn in traditional search and legacy segments, AI-driven operations now account for over 50% of total revenue, highlighting a critical structural transition.
title_zh: 百度发布第三季度财报，营收同比微降至46亿美元

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 百度集团发布第三季度财报，季度总营收约336亿元人民币（约46亿美元），同比下滑1%，实现连续六个季度的收入负增长。尽管传统核心业务承压，但财报显示人工智能业务现已贡献超过50%的营收，标志着公司正处于向AI原生转型的关键调整期。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Baidu Inc. reported Q3 revenue of approximately 33.6 billion yuan ($4.6 billion), a 1% year-over-year decline, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of revenue contraction. Despite the downturn in traditional search and legacy segments, AI-driven operations now account for over 50% of total revenue, highlighting a critical structural transition.

elements_en.what: Q3 revenue ~$4.6B (-1% YoY), net income ~$210M; AI business contribution >50%
elements_en.why: Stagnant search advertising revenue necessitating a strategic pivot to AI-integrated business models.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 百度连续六季营收缩窄显示其核心搜索广告业务已触达存量增长天花板，传统变现路径难以覆盖AI研发高昂的沉没成本。AI业务占比过半的财务披露实质上是对市场证明其‘模型即服务’商业模型具备抗周期性，但需关注AI推理成本与边际利润率能否支撑其重估估值区间。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Baidu's six consecutive quarters of revenue contraction confirm that its core search advertising has reached a ceiling, failing to offset the high capital intensity of AI R&D. While the pivot to AI-driven revenue represents a necessary hedge, the ultimate valuation recovery hinges on whether these AI services can achieve sustainable margins beyond mere top-line contribution.

Revenue for the three months ended September slid 1% to 30.8 billion yuan ($4.6 billion), in line with the average analyst forecast. Net income came in at 1.4 billion yuan.

China's internet search leader is trying to reclaim its place in a hotly contested AI arena where longtime rivals such as Tencent Holdings Ltd. and Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. have pulled ahead. Its Ernie model series has fallen out of the top tier and lags upstarts like DeepSeek and Moonshot, while its consumer AI products have yet to catch on. Compounding the slump, Baidu's main online advertising business is losing eyeballs and marketers to newer social apps.

Billionaire founder Robin Li is betting that a surge in autonomous AI agents will create a new ecosystem from which Baidu can reap returns on its cloud computing and chip infrastructure. Its AI-driven business now accounts for more than half of its top line, a trend the company expects to persist. The company last week unveiled a token marketplace that connects idle compute with developers hungry for open-source models — a move aimed at displacing middlemen, known as transfer stations, with accredited providers.

The resource-constrained company lacks the scale to compete with China's tech platforms and the strain is beginning to show as Baidu simultaneously pursues leadership in China's AI, cloud and robotaxi sectors. The potential spinoff and IPO of the Kunlunxin AI chip unit won't improve its earnings prospects, which are highly challenged.

Its chip spinoff Kunlunxin is gearing up for an independent listing in Hong Kong, setting up a showdown against Alibaba's T-Head, which announced a similar move. But Kunlunxin's market debut could slip to next year because of broader market weakness and China's tighter controls on AI funding, Bloomberg News has reported.

Baidu last week released its latest foundation model, Ernie 5.5 Flash Preview, which it positioned for fast inference speeds and competitive pricing.

In autonomous driving, Baidu's Apollo Go robotaxi service now spans more than a score of cities globally, including fully driverless commercial operations in Dubai.

截至 9 月份的三个月收入下滑 1%，至 308 亿元人民币（46 亿美元），与分析师的平均预测一致。净利润为14亿元。

中国互联网搜索领导者正试图在竞争激烈的人工智能领域夺回自己的地位，腾讯控股有限公司和阿里巴巴集团控股有限公司等长期竞争对手已经领先。其Ernie模型系列已跌出顶级，落后于DeepSeek和Moonshot等新贵，而其消费级人工智能产品尚未流行。令业绩下滑雪上加霜的是，百度的主要在线广告业务正在失去眼球和营销人员，转向新的社交应用程序。

亿万富翁创始人李彦宏押注，自主人工智能代理的激增将创建一个新的生态系统，百度可以从中获得云计算和芯片基础设施的回报。其人工智能驱动的业务目前占其营收的一半以上，该公司预计这一趋势将持续下去。该公司上周推出了一个代币市场，将闲置计算与渴望开源模型的开发人员联系起来，此举旨在用经过认可的提供商取代中间商（称为传输站）。

这家资源有限的公司缺乏与中国科技平台竞争的规模，随着百度同时追求中国人工智能、云计算和机器人出租车领域的领先地位，压力开始显现。昆仑芯人工智能芯片部门潜在的分拆和IPO不会改善其盈利前景，该公司面临着严峻的挑战。

其芯片分拆公司昆仑芯正准备在香港独立上市，与宣布类似举措的阿里巴巴T-Head展开对决。但据彭博社报道，由于市场整体疲软以及中国对人工智能融资的更严格控制，昆仑欣的上市时间可能会推迟到明年。

百度上周发布了最新的基础模型 Ernie 5.5 Flash Preview，其定位是快速的推理速度和有竞争力的价格。

在自动驾驶方面，百度的Apollo Go机器人出租车服务现已覆盖全球数十个城市，其中包括迪拜的完全无人驾驶商业运营。

title: Apple is launching a video podcasts section on the Apple TV app, initially for developer testing, and plans to increase video podcasts on its Podcasts app (New York Times)
title_en: Apple is launching a video podcasts section on the Apple TV app, initially for developer testing, and plans to increase video podcasts on its Podcasts app (New York Times)

inline_images.caption: Apple will bring video podcasts to Apple TV and increase the number of video podcasts on its regular Podcasts app. Credit...Apple
inline_images.alt: Apple will bring video podcasts to Apple TV and increase the number of video podcasts on its regular

author: New York Times
article_content:
Apple helped turbocharge the rise of podcasts two decades ago, but as video podcasts reshape the industry it’s fallen behind competitors like YouTube and Spotify.

Now it’s playing catch up. On Monday, Apple will add a video podcasts section to Apple TV, initially just for testing with developers. They will soon be free to all users even if they don’t pay for Apple’s streaming service and will appear on over 1 billion devices that have the Apple TV app, including Rokus and smart TVs. Apple also plans to increase the number of video podcasts on its regular Podcasts app, where it introduced video nine months ago but has been working to bring some of the biggest shows on board.

“We want podcasts to be available wherever people want to enjoy them — the small screens, big screens,” said Oliver Schusser, a vice president at Apple who oversees services including podcasts, television and music. “It’s really about discovery and helping the creators to reach a new audience. We didn’t approach this in a way that would financially benefit us.”

Video podcasts have proliferated in the past few years as audio creators adapted their shows to reach consumers spending more time on video platforms like YouTube. The video format has proved attractive to celebrities, including Amy Poehler, Pete Davidson and Food Network’s Ina Garten. And the trend of “clipping” — creating short buzzy video clips from longer shows to post on social media platforms like TikTok and Instagram — has encouraged creators to add video to their podcasts.

The popularity of video podcasts, driven by YouTube and Spotify, and newer entrants like Hulu and Netflix, has pushed Apple down in the podcast platform rankings. Spotify passed Apple as the top platform among weekly podcast consumers in the United States at the end of 2022, according to survey data from Edison Research at SSRS. YouTube took over the top spot at the end of 2024. In Edison Research’s third-quarter survey, YouTube remained the most popular, followed by Spotify then Apple Podcasts. Netflix was No. 7.

Many in the industry had long awaited Apple’s move.

“It’s super smart that they’ve done it, but it’s after a lot of people in the space wanted them to make it available,” said Megan Lazovick, a vice president at Edison Research.

Apple’s addition of video to its regular app earlier this year has been encouraging, with overall audiences for top shows that added video growing by more than 20 percent on average. That includes shows like IMO with Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson and the comedy podcast Giggly Squad.

Sam Fragoso, the host of the show Talk Easy, had been “eager” for Apple to add video, saying it had doubled the audience of his show, which is also available on Spotify and YouTube.

“It’s so helpful that people can go on their phones, they see a clip on Instagram, TikTok or Twitter and open the Apple app and now watch it on video,” he said. “People are already on their iPhones and they’re used to watching videos on their phones so it was the next logical step.”

Apple’s history may help it catch up to competitors who were earlier to the video podcast boom.

“I love our YouTube audience but it feels not as intentional on that platform — Apple’s where people know where to find their favorite podcasts,” said Rachel Martin, the host of NPR’s Wild Card.

Her show’s audience has grown by more than 60 percent since Apple introduced video, which she called astonishing in an industry where “sometimes it can feel excruciating and really hard to get just another 100 subscribers.”

In 2005, podcasts were viewed as a way for Apple to sell more iPods, the popular audio player that connected to iTunes. (Tech journalists once compared it to a razor company trying to sell more products by distributing free razor blades.) Today, Apple still seems to view video podcasts as a sweetener for devices, including newer products like its iPhone Duo and the upcoming HomeView tablet.

Mr. Schusser said he envisions a future where people can listen to their favorite podcasts as they move through their day.

More than 35 percent of video podcast consumers actively switch between watching and listening to shows in a given month, Apple’s data shows. Some view it as a sign that video podcasts are the future.

“Everything is TV now, which is a little bit heartbreaking for a lifelong audio person to say,” Ms. Martin of NPR said. “I don’t think this is a flash in the pan.”

article_content_zh:
二十年前，苹果推动了播客的崛起，但随着视频播客重塑了该行业，它落后于 YouTube 和 Spotify 等竞争对手。

现在它正在迎头赶上。周一，苹果将在 Apple TV 中添加视频播客部分，最初只是为了与开发者进行测试。即使用户不支付 Apple 的流媒体服务费用，它们很快也将免费提供给所有用户，并将出现在超过 10 亿台装有 Apple TV 应用的设备上，包括 Rokus 和智能电视。苹果还计划增加其常规播客应用程序上的视频播客数量，该应用程序九个月前就推出了视频，但一直在努力将一些最大的节目引入其中。

苹果负责播客、电视和音乐等服务的副总裁奥利弗·舒瑟 (Oliver Schusser) 表示：“我们希望人们可以在任何想要享受播客的地方观看播客，无论是小屏幕还是大屏幕。” “这实际上是关于发现并帮助创作者接触新观众。我们并没有以一种能给我们带来经济利益的方式来处理这个问题。”

过去几年，随着音频​​创作者调整自己的节目以吸引在 YouTube 等视频平台上花费更多时间的消费者，视频播客激增。事实证明，这种视频格式对艾米·波勒、皮特·戴维森和食品网络的伊娜·加滕等名人很有吸引力。 “剪辑”的趋势——从较长的节目中创建简短的热门视频剪辑并发布到 TikTok 和 Instagram 等社交媒体平台上——鼓励创作者将视频添加到他们的播客中。

在 YouTube 和 Spotify 以及 Hulu 和 Netflix 等新进入者的推动下，视频播客的流行使得苹果在播客平台排名中下降。根据 SSRS 爱迪生研究中心的调查数据，到 2022 年底，Spotify 超过苹果，成为美国每周播客消费者中排名第一的平台。 YouTube 在 2024 年底占据了榜首。在爱迪生研究公司第三季度的调查中，YouTube 仍然是最受欢迎的，其次是 Spotify，然后是 Apple Podcasts。 Netflix 排名第七。

许多业内人士对苹果的举动期待已久。

爱迪生研究公司副总裁梅根·拉佐维克 (Megan Lazovick) 表示：“他们这样做非常聪明，但这是在该领域的很多人希望他们提供它之后。”

苹果公司今年早些时候在其常规应用程序中添加了视频，这令人鼓舞，添加视频的热门节目的总体观众数量平均增长了 20% 以上。其中包括米歇尔·奥巴马和克雷格·罗宾逊的《IMO》节目以及喜剧播客《Giggly Squad》。

Talk Easy 节目的主持人萨姆·弗拉戈索 (Sam Fragoso) 一直“渴望”苹果添加视频，称这使他的节目的观众人数增加了一倍，该节目也可以在 Spotify 和 YouTube 上观看。

“这非常有帮助，人们可以在手机上看到 Instagram、TikTok 或 Twitter 上的剪辑，然后打开 Apple 应用程序，然后在视频中观看，”他说。 “人们已经在使用 iPhone，并且习惯了在手机上观看视频，因此这是下一个合乎逻辑的步骤。”

苹果的历史可能有助于它赶上较早进入视频播客热潮的竞争对手。

“我喜欢我们的 YouTube 观众，但在这个平台上感觉并不是那么有意为之——人们知道在苹果平台上哪里可以找到他们最喜欢的播客，”NPR 节目 Wild Card 的主持人雷切尔·马丁 (Rachel Martin) 说道。

自从 Apple 推出视频以来，她的节目的观众数量增长了 60% 以上，她称这在一个“有时会让人感到痛苦且很难再获得 100 名订阅者”的行业中令人震惊。

2005 年，播客被视为苹果公司销售更多 iPod（连接 iTunes 的流行音频播放器）的一种方式。 （科技记者曾将其比作一家剃须刀公司，试图通过分发免费剃须刀刀片来销售更多产品。）如今，苹果似乎仍然将视频播客视为设备的甜味剂，包括 iPhone Duo 和即将推出的 HomeView 平板电脑等新产品。

title: A look at China's push for AI literacy by 2030, as schools adopt AI-focused curricula, classroom cameras, and AI-generated lessons to mitigate teacher shortages (Reuters)
title_en: A look at China's push for AI literacy by 2030, as schools adopt AI-focused curricula, classroom cameras, and AI-generated lessons to mitigate teacher shortages (Reuters)

author: Laurie Chen and Xiuyuan Ning
article_content:
BEIJING, Nov 16 (Reuters) - At a top private school in Beijing, 13-year-old Peng Gaodi has used artificial intelligence to build more than 200 apps, including a homework-submission platform and a secondhand marketplace. He pitches ideas to real investors, idolises Elon Musk and hopes to become a computer scientist.

Around him, classmates program humanoid robots to play soccer, attend coding workshops and train on flight simulators. Posters across the 30-acre (12-hectare) boarding school campus encourage students to "create a virtual world in five minutes with AI vibe coding."

"In the past, if I couldn't solve a problem at home, I'd have to call my teacher, which increases their workload," Peng said. "But now I can just ask AI to help me learn better. It noticeably improved my learning efficiency."

Rare access granted to Reuters at the $39,000-a-year Beijing New Talent Academy offered a window into China's push to weave AI into education. The school, which serves more than 2,000 students, has built its own digital innovation curriculum covering AI, robotics and programming, and developed a classroom AI model incorporating features from popular Chinese systems.

The academy represents the sharp end of a broader transformation. With almost 200 million students enrolled in primary and secondary education, China is undertaking one of the world's largest AI-assisted learning experiments, with the technology increasingly integrated into teaching nationwide.

By 2030, Beijing wants AI literacy to be universal among schoolchildren. Current broad AI education guidelines state that students should progress from understanding basic concepts in their early years to applying advanced tools and critical-thinking skills in complex projects.

A weeks-long Reuters examination, based on school visits, interviews with more than a dozen educators, parents and experts, and a review of more than 100 academic papers and government procurement records, paints one of the most detailed pictures yet of how AI is reshaping Chinese classrooms. It found a sweeping but uneven effort to build a generation of AI-savvy innovators, with little consensus on what AI literacy means, how it should be taught or measured.

China views the technology as central to its economic future and technological rivalry with the United States, hoping early exposure will nurture the homegrown innovation needed for major breakthroughs.

Beijing's state-led push far outpaces efforts in the West. President Xi Jinping has declared AI education fundamental to reform. By contrast, the US relies on decentralized, nonbinding guidance and lacks dedicated funding or state-level teacher standards, according to Stanford University's 2026 AI Index.

A Reuters review of provincial "AI+ education" blueprints reveals a degree of official coordination unseen elsewhere. Nearly half of China's provinces and municipalities have rolled out binding plans. Shanghai mandates at least 30 hours of annual teaching on AI skills per grade, while the Beijing city government plans to integrate AI into student health monitoring, as well as set up 100 AI pilot demonstration schools. Underscoring its importance, regions including Ningxia and Gansu plan to integrate AI literacy directly into high-stakes school entrance exams by 2027.

The documents also offer an early look at more expansive classroom applications. Beyond coding and tutoring, Guizhou is integrating AI facial recognition and behavioral analysis into classrooms, while Shanghai is deploying systems for mental and physical health monitoring. In Yunnan, 14,000 classrooms are slated to have lessons recorded and analysed by AI, turning Chinese schools into a high-stakes testing ground for the opportunities and risks confronting global education.

As AI spreads through Chinese classrooms, many educators are grappling with how to deploy the technology without reinforcing the rote-learning habits policymakers want to move beyond.

Reuters found starkly different approaches across the country. While some schools encourage students like Peng to build and create with AI, others are focused on using the technology to plug gaps in educational resources.

"Implementation is all over the place," said Ted Mo Chen, chief of staff at Chinese education technology startup ClassIn, adding that few schools he had visited had integrated AI into the curriculum effectively.

China's education ministry did not respond to a request for comment.

CLASSROOMS OF THE FUTURE

Headmaster Liu Wei said only a small minority of students at Beijing New Talent Academy would become AI scientists or engineers. For the rest, the objective is to make AI an everyday tool for learning and creating.

Hundreds of kilometres away in rural Anhui province, Funan County Qinqing High School is using the same technology to solve a problem affluent urban areas in China rarely face: a shortage of qualified teachers.

The school's 4,000 pupils, most of them children of migrant workers, learn core subjects through AI-generated lessons, according to headmaster Yang Tianliang. Students follow personalised classes on tablets, with AI agents posing questions rather than providing answers when they struggle.

"An AI agent doesn't suffer from fatigue, and it never makes a student feel stupid for asking a basic question," Yang said.

The school uses popular Chinese AI models from Alibaba's Qwen, ByteDance and Z.AI to generate text, images, interactive lessons and videos. Yang said it had also introduced small-group projects to encourage greater student interaction.

He credited the approach with helping lift university admission rates from below 60% to 90% in recent years, although Reuters could not independently verify the figures. Yang estimated at least 200 other Chinese schools were experimenting with similar systems.

An Alibaba spokesperson said its open-source AI models and Cloud for Youth Programme give students direct access to AI tools and education. ByteDance and Z.AI did not respond to requests for comment.

Schools such as Funan County Qinqing High School offer a glimpse of how quickly AI is spreading through China's education system.

Since 2024, China's education ministry has encouraged schools to introduce AI courses, train teachers and develop pilot programmes. Primary-school pupils are introduced to basic AI tools, while older students learn how AI systems work and apply them to increasingly sophisticated projects.

A Reuters review of more than 100 government procurement documents found authorities committed at least $31 million in the past year to AI classroom equipment, training and teaching platforms.

The true figure is likely far higher, scattered across thousands of local budgets and not officially tallied. Consultancy iResearch estimates 2025 spending on education digitalisation at just under $83 billion, with generative AI projects accounting for 46% of AI education procurement.

AN EXPERIMENT WITHOUT A CLEAR SCORECARD

China has yet to establish a standard framework for measuring AI literacy, leaving schools to experiment and making success difficult to assess.

"Mature, widely adopted assessment rubrics for compulsory school-level AI competency are still being built," said Selena Guo, portfolio lead at research firm China Policy.

Preliminary research into AI's effects on children's learning also offers mixed signals, with some studies suggesting short-term gains while raising questions about longer-term intellectual development.

A recent study examining nearly 27,000 Chinese teenagers found AI adoption was associated with an 18% increase in homework scores but a 20% decline in monthly examination scores within six months, with the biggest declines in social science subjects.

Another nationwide Chinese survey this year involving more than 320,000 pupils reported educational benefits from AI but also concerns about dependence and weaker independent thinking. Students using AI at least three times weekly showed lower memory, comprehension, analytical and creative skills than less frequent users.

The findings do not establish causation but reinforce teacher concerns about cognitive outsourcing, where children increasingly delegate mental tasks to technology rather than develop those skills themselves.

Chen from ClassIn warned that children's thinking processes could be "completely bypassed" if schools failed to prevent them from relying on AI for quick answers.

Chinese academic research reviewed by Reuters also suggested that students in rural areas may be particularly vulnerable to cognitive outsourcing and device addiction.

FINDING THE RIGHT BALANCE

Some educators and parents are already experimenting with safeguards to keep AI from replacing critical thinking.

At Beijing New Talent Academy, Peng said he tries to solve coding problems himself before asking AI for hints rather than complete answers. He said the technology has helped deepen his understanding of maths.

"I think AI is a tool that helps me, not something I depend on."

For Beijing parent Rita Luan, whose 11-year-old daughter attends a leading public school in the capital, the challenge is ensuring that AI strengthens rather than shortcuts learning.

She said her daughter's school still largely teaches AI concepts rather than practical applications, so she supplements lessons at home, teaching her daughter to prompt ByteDance's Doubao chatbot under close supervision.

Her rule: spend 15 minutes trying to solve a difficult maths problem before turning to AI. Days later, Luan asks her to solve the same problem without help.

"The point is to make sure she actually digested the solution," she said.

"In the past, if I couldn't solve a problem at home, I'd have to call my teacher, which increases their workload," Peng said. "But now I can just ask AI to help me learn better. It noticeably improved my learning efficiency."

Rare access granted to Reuters at the $39,000-a-year Beijing New Talent Academy offered a window into China's push to weave AI into education. The school, which serves more than 2,000 students, has built its own digital innovation curriculum covering AI, robotics and programming, and developed a classroom AI model incorporating features from popular Chinese systems.

The academy represents the sharp end of a broader transformation. With almost 200 million students enrolled in primary and secondary education, China is undertaking one of the world's largest AI-assisted learning experiments, with the technology increasingly integrated into teaching nationwide.

By 2030, Beijing wants AI literacy to be universal among schoolchildren. Current broad AI education guidelines state that students should progress from understanding basic concepts in their early years to applying advanced tools and critical-thinking skills in complex projects.

A weeks-long Reuters examination, based on school visits, interviews with more than a dozen educators, parents and experts, and a review of more than 100 academic papers and government procurement records, paints one of the most detailed pictures yet of how AI is reshaping Chinese classrooms. It found a sweeping but uneven effort to build a generation of AI-savvy innovators, with little consensus on what AI literacy means, how it should be taught or measured.

China views the technology as central to its economic future and technological rivalry with the United States, hoping early exposure will nurture the homegrown innovation needed for major breakthroughs.

Beijing's state-led push far outpaces efforts in the West. President Xi Jinping has declared AI education fundamental to reform. By contrast, the US relies on decentralized, nonbinding guidance and lacks dedicated funding or state-level teacher standards, according to Stanford University's 2026 AI Index.

A Reuters review of provincial "AI+ education" blueprints reveals a degree of official coordination unseen elsewhere. Nearly half of China's provinces and municipalities have rolled out binding plans. Shanghai mandates at least 30 hours of annual teaching on AI skills per grade, while the Beijing city government plans to integrate AI into student health monitoring, as well as set up 100 AI pilot demonstration schools. Underscoring its importance, regions including Ningxia and Gansu plan to integrate AI literacy directly into high-stakes school entrance exams by 2027.

The documents also offer an early look at more expansive classroom applications. Beyond coding and tutoring, Guizhou is integrating AI facial recognition and behavioral analysis into classrooms, while Shanghai is deploying systems for mental and physical health monitoring. In Yunnan, 14,000 classrooms are slated to have lessons recorded and analysed by AI, turning Chinese schools into a high-stakes testing ground for the opportunities and risks confronting global education.

As AI spreads through Chinese classrooms, many educators are grappling with how to deploy the technology without reinforcing the rote-learning habits policymakers want to move beyond.

Reuters found starkly different approaches across the country. While some schools encourage students like Peng to build and create with AI, others are focused on using the technology to plug gaps in educational resources.

"Implementation is all over the place," said Ted Mo Chen, chief of staff at Chinese education technology startup ClassIn, adding that few schools he had visited had integrated AI into the curriculum effectively.

China's education ministry did not respond to a request for comment.

CLASSROOMS OF THE FUTURE

Headmaster Liu Wei said only a small minority of students at Beijing New Talent Academy would become AI scientists or engineers. For the rest, the objective is to make AI an everyday tool for learning and creating.

Hundreds of kilometres away in rural Anhui province, Funan County Qinqing High School is using the same technology to solve a problem affluent urban areas in China rarely face: a shortage of qualified teachers.

The school's 4,000 pupils, most of them children of migrant workers, learn core subjects through AI-generated lessons, according to headmaster Yang Tianliang. Students follow personalised classes on tablets, with AI agents posing questions rather than providing answers when they struggle.

"An AI agent doesn't suffer from fatigue, and it never makes a student feel stupid for asking a basic question," Yang said.

The school uses popular Chinese AI models from Alibaba's Qwen, ByteDance and Z.AI to generate text, images, interactive lessons and videos. Yang said it had also introduced small-group projects to encourage greater student interaction.

He credited the approach with helping lift university admission rates from below 60% to 90% in recent years, although Reuters could not independently verify the figures. Yang estimated at least 200 other Chinese schools were experimenting with similar systems.

An Alibaba spokesperson said its open-source AI models and Cloud for Youth Programme give students direct access to AI tools and education. ByteDance and Z.AI did not respond to requests for comment.

Schools such as Funan County Qinqing High School offer a glimpse of how quickly AI is spreading through China's education system.

Since 2024, China's education ministry has encouraged schools to introduce AI courses, train teachers and develop pilot programmes. Primary-school pupils are introduced to basic AI tools, while older students learn how AI systems work and apply them to increasingly sophisticated projects.

A Reuters review of more than 100 government procurement documents found authorities committed at least $31 million in the past year to AI classroom equipment, training and teaching platforms.

The true figure is likely far higher, scattered across thousands of local budgets and not officially tallied. Consultancy iResearch estimates 2025 spending on education digitalisation at just under $83 billion, with generative AI projects accounting for 46% of AI education procurement.

AN EXPERIMENT WITHOUT A CLEAR SCORECARD

China has yet to establish a standard framework for measuring AI literacy, leaving schools to experiment and making success difficult to assess.

"Mature, widely adopted assessment rubrics for compulsory school-level AI competency are still being built," said Selena Guo, portfolio lead at research firm China Policy.

Preliminary research into AI's effects on children's learning also offers mixed signals, with some studies suggesting short-term gains while raising questions about longer-term intellectual development.

A recent study examining nearly 27,000 Chinese teenagers found AI adoption was associated with an 18% increase in homework scores but a 20% decline in monthly examination scores within six months, with the biggest declines in social science subjects.

Another nationwide Chinese survey this year involving more than 320,000 pupils reported educational benefits from AI but also concerns about dependence and weaker independent thinking. Students using AI at least three times weekly showed lower memory, comprehension, analytical and creative skills than less frequent users.

The findings do not establish causation but reinforce teacher concerns about cognitive outsourcing, where children increasingly delegate mental tasks to technology rather than develop those skills themselves.

Chen from ClassIn warned that children's thinking processes could be "completely bypassed" if schools failed to prevent them from relying on AI for quick answers.

Chinese academic research reviewed by Reuters also suggested that students in rural areas may be particularly vulnerable to cognitive outsourcing and device addiction.

FINDING THE RIGHT BALANCE

Some educators and parents are already experimenting with safeguards to keep AI from replacing critical thinking.

At Beijing New Talent Academy, Peng said he tries to solve coding problems himself before asking AI for hints rather than complete answers. He said the technology has helped deepen his understanding of maths.

"I think AI is a tool that helps me, not something I depend on."

For Beijing parent Rita Luan, whose 11-year-old daughter attends a leading public school in the capital, the challenge is ensuring that AI strengthens rather than shortcuts learning.

She said her daughter's school still largely teaches AI concepts rather than practical applications, so she supplements lessons at home, teaching her daughter to prompt ByteDance's Doubao chatbot under close supervision.

Her rule: spend 15 minutes trying to solve a difficult maths problem before turning to AI. Days later, Luan asks her to solve the same problem without help.

"The point is to make sure she actually digested the solution," she said.
title_zh: 中国部署AI教育普及：国家战略迈向2030
summary_zh: 北京新英才学校等基础教育学府全面普及AI生成课程、飞行模拟实验室与机器人训练，各级政府投入逾3100万美元采购AI教学装备，加速迈向2030国家AI教育战略普及
article_content_zh:
路透北京11月16日 - 在北京一所顶尖私立学校，13岁的彭高弟利用人工智能开发了200多个应用程序，包括作业提交平台和二手市场。他向真正的投资者推销想法，崇拜埃隆·马斯克，并希望成为一名计算机科学家。

在他周围，同学们编写人形机器人踢足球、参加编程研讨会以及飞行模拟器训练。占地 30 英亩（12 公顷）的寄宿学校校园内张贴的海报鼓励学生“利用 AI 氛围编码在五分钟内创建一个虚拟世界”。

“过去，如果我在家解决不了问题，我就得打电话给老师，这增加了他们的工作量，”彭说。 “但现在我可以要求人工智能帮助我更好地学习。它显着提高了我的学习效率。”

路透社罕见地访问了每年收费 39,000 美元的北京新英才学院，这为了解中国推动人工智能融入教育提供了一个窗口。该校为2000多名学生提供服务，建立了自己的数字创新课程，涵盖人工智能、机器人和编程，并开发了融合中国流行系统特点的课堂人工智能模型。

该学院代表了更广泛变革的尖端。中国有近2亿中小学学生，正在开展世界上最大的人工智能辅助学习实验之一，该技术越来越多地融入全国教学。

北京希望到 2030 年，学童能够普及人工智能知识。目前广泛的人工智能教育指南指出，学生应该从早年理解基本概念发展到在复杂项目中应用先进工具和批判性思维技能。

路透社为期一周的调查基于学校走访、对十几位教育工作者、家长和专家的采访，以及对 100 多篇学术论文和政府采购记录的审查，描绘了迄今为止人工智能如何重塑中国课堂的最详细的画面之一。研究发现，为培养一代精通人工智能的创新者，人们付出了广泛但不均衡的努力，但对于人工智能素养的含义、如何教授或衡量人工智能素养几乎没有达成共识。

中国将这项技术视为其经济未来和与美国技术竞争的核心，希望早期接触能够培育重大突破所需的本土创新。

北京政府主导的推动力度远远超过西方国家。习近平主席宣布人工智能教育是改革的基础。相比之下，根据斯坦福大学的 2026 年人工智能指数，美国依赖分散的、不具约束力的指导，缺乏专用资金或州级教师标准。

路透社对省级“人工智能+教育”蓝图的审查揭示了其他地方未见的官方协调程度。中国近一半的省市已经出台了约束性计划。上海要求每个年级每年至少有30个小时的人工智能技能教学，而北京市政府计划将人工智能融入学生健康监测，并建立100所人工智能试点示范学校。为了强调其重要性，宁夏和甘肃等地区计划到 2027 年将人工智能素养直接纳入高风险的入学考试。

这些文件还提供了对更广泛的课堂应用的早期了解。除了编码和辅导之外，贵州正在将人工智能面部识别和行为分析融入课堂，而上海正在部署心理和身体健康监测系统。在云南，14,000个教室将通过人工智能记录和分析课程，将中国学校变成全球教育面临的机遇和风险的高风险试验场。

随着人工智能在中国课堂上的传播，许多教育工作者正在努力解决如何在不强化政策制定者希望超越的死记硬背习惯的情况下部署该技术。

路透社发现全国各地的做法截然不同。虽然一些学校鼓励像彭这样的学生利用人工智能进行构建和创造，但其他学校则专注于利用该技术来填补教育资源的空白。

中国教育科技初创公司 ClassIn 的幕僚长 Ted Mo Chen 表示：“实施无处不在。”他补充说，他访问过的学校很少有将人工智能有效融入课程的。

中国教育部没有回应置评请求。

刘伟校长表示，北京新英才学院的学生中只有一小部分会成为人工智能科学家或工程师。至于其他方面，我们的目标是让人工智能成为日常学习和创造的工具。

数百公里外的安徽省农村地区，阜南县勤庆中学正在使用相同的技术来解决中国富裕城市地区很少面临的问题：合格教师短缺。

校长杨天亮表示，学校有 4000 名学生，其中大部分是农民工子女，他们通过人工智能生成的课程学习核心科目。学生们在平板电脑上学习个性化课程，人工智能代理会在他们遇到困难时提出问题，而不是提供答案。

杨说：“人工智能代理不会感到疲劳，而且它永远不会让学生因为问一个基本问题而感到愚蠢。”

学校使用阿里巴巴 Qwen、ByteDance 和 Z.AI 等中国流行的人工智能模型来生成文本、图像、互动课程和视频。杨说，学校还引入了小组项目，以鼓励更多的学生互动。

他称赞这种方法近年来帮助大学录取率从 60% 以下提高到 90%，尽管路透社无法独立核实这些数字。杨估计至少还有 200 所其他中国学校正在试验类似的系统。

阿里巴巴发言人表示，其开源人工智能模型和青年云计划让学生可以直接获得人工智能工具和教育。字节跳动和 Z.AI 没有回应置评请求。

阜南县沁青高中等学校让我们得以一窥人工智能在中国教育体系中的传播速度。

自2024年起，中国教育部鼓励学校引进人工智能课程、培训教师并开发试点项目。小学生将学习基本的人工智能工具，而年龄较大的学生将学习人工智能系统的工作原理并将其应用到日益复杂的项目中。

路透社对 100 多份政府采购文件的审查发现，当局在过去一年中为人工智能教室设备、培训和教学平台承诺了至少 3100 万美元。

真实数字可能要高得多，分散在数千个地方预算中并且没有官方统计。艾瑞咨询咨询公司估计，到 2025 年，教育数字化支出将接近 830 亿美元，其中生成式人工智能项目占人工智能教育采购的 46%。

没有明确成绩单的试验

中国尚未建立衡量人工智能素养的标准框架，让学校只能进行实验，也难以评估成功与否。

研究公司 China Policy 的投资组合主管 SelenaGuo 表示：“成熟的、广泛采用的学校必修人工智能能力评估标准仍在制定中。”

关于人工智能对儿童学习影响的初步研究也提供了混合信号，一些研究表明人工智能在短期收益的同时提出了有关长期智力发展的问题。

最近一项对近 27,000 名中国青少年进行的研究发现，人工智能的采用与六个月内家庭作业成绩提高 18% 相关，但每月考试成绩下降 20%，其中社会科学科目下降幅度最大。

今年另一项涉及超过 320,000 名学生的全国性调查报告了人工智能带来的教育益处，但也担心依赖和独立思考能力较弱。每周至少使用人工智能 3 次的学生的记忆力、理解力、分析能力和创造能力低于使用频率较低的学生。

研究结果并没有确定因果关系，但加剧了教师对认知外包的担忧，即孩子们越来越多地将脑力任务委托给技术，而不是自己发展这些技能。

ClassIn 的陈警告说，如果学校未能阻止孩子们依靠人工智能快速获得答案，他们的思维过程可能会被“完全绕过”。

路透社查阅的中国学术研究还表明，农村地区的学生可能特别容易受到认知外包和设备成瘾的影响。

寻找恰当的平衡点

一些教育工作者和家长已经在尝试采取保护措施，以防止人工智能取代批判性思维。

在北京新英才学院，彭表示，在向人工智能寻求提示而不是完整答案之前，他会尝试自己解决编码问题。他说这项技术帮助加深了他对数学的理解。

“我认为人工智能是一个帮助我的工具，而不是我所依赖的东西。”

北京家长丽塔·栾 (Rita Luan) 11 岁的女儿就读于首都一所顶尖的公立学校，对于她来说，面临的挑战是确保人工智能加强而不是阻碍学习。

她说，女儿的学校仍然主要教授人工智能概念，而不是实际应用，因此她在家补课，在密切监督下教女儿提示字节跳动的豆宝聊天机器人。

她的规则是：在求助于人工智能之前花 15 分钟尝试解决一道困难的数学问题。几天后，栾要求她在没有帮助的情况下解决同样的问题。

“关键是要确保她真正消化了这个解决方案，”她说。

subheadings: AN EXPERIMENT WITHOUT A CLEAR SCORECARD
paragraphs: BEIJING, Nov 16 (Reuters) - At a top private school in Beijing, 13-year-old Peng Gaodi has used artificial intelligence to build more than 200 apps, including a homework-submission platform and a secondhand marketplace. He pitches ideas to real investors, idolises Elon Musk and hopes to become a computer scientist.

Around him, classmates program humanoid robots to play soccer, attend coding workshops and train on flight simulators. Posters across the 30-acre (12-hectare) boarding school campus encourage students to "create a virtual world in five minutes with AI vibe coding."

"In the past, if I couldn't solve a problem at home, I'd have to call my teacher, which increases their workload," Peng said. "But now I can just ask AI to help me learn better. It noticeably improved my learning efficiency."

Rare access granted to Reuters at the $39,000-a-year Beijing New Talent Academy offered a window into China's push to weave AI into education. The school, which serves more than 2,000 students, has built its own digital innovation curriculum covering AI, robotics and programming, and developed a classroom AI model incorporating features from popular Chinese systems.

The academy represents the sharp end of a broader transformation. With almost 200 million students enrolled in primary and secondary education, China is undertaking one of the world's largest AI-assisted learning experiments, with the technology increasingly integrated into teaching nationwide.

By 2030, Beijing wants AI literacy to be universal among schoolchildren. Current broad AI education guidelines state that students should progress from understanding basic concepts in their early years to applying advanced tools and critical-thinking skills in complex projects.

A weeks-long Reuters examination, based on school visits, interviews with more than a dozen educators, parents and experts, and a review of more than 100 academic papers and government procurement records, paints one of the most detailed pictures yet of how AI is reshaping Chinese classrooms. It found a sweeping but uneven effort to build a generation of AI-savvy innovators, with little consensus on what AI literacy means, how it should be taught or measured.

China views the technology as central to its economic future and technological rivalry with the United States, hoping early exposure will nurture the homegrown innovation needed for major breakthroughs.

Beijing's state-led push far outpaces efforts in the West. President Xi Jinping has declared AI education fundamental to reform. By contrast, the US relies on decentralized, nonbinding guidance and lacks dedicated funding or state-level teacher standards, according to Stanford University's 2026 AI Index.

A Reuters review of provincial "AI+ education" blueprints reveals a degree of official coordination unseen elsewhere. Nearly half of China's provinces and municipalities have rolled out binding plans. Shanghai mandates at least 30 hours of annual teaching on AI skills per grade, while the Beijing city government plans to integrate AI into student health monitoring, as well as set up 100 AI pilot demonstration schools. Underscoring its importance, regions including Ningxia and Gansu plan to integrate AI literacy directly into high-stakes school entrance exams by 2027.

The documents also offer an early look at more expansive classroom applications. Beyond coding and tutoring, Guizhou is integrating AI facial recognition and behavioral analysis into classrooms, while Shanghai is deploying systems for mental and physical health monitoring. In Yunnan, 14,000 classrooms are slated to have lessons recorded and analysed by AI, turning Chinese schools into a high-stakes testing ground for the opportunities and risks confronting global education.
As AI spreads through Chinese classrooms, many educators are grappling with how to deploy the technology without reinforcing the rote-learning habits policymakers want to move beyond.

Reuters found starkly different approaches across the country. While some schools encourage students like Peng to build and create with AI, others are focused on using the technology to plug gaps in educational resources.

"Implementation is all over the place," said Ted Mo Chen, chief of staff at Chinese education technology startup ClassIn, adding that few schools he had visited had integrated AI into the curriculum effectively.
China's education ministry did not respond to a request for comment.
CLASSROOMS OF THE FUTURE

Headmaster Liu Wei said only a small minority of students at Beijing New Talent Academy would become AI scientists or engineers. For the rest, the objective is to make AI an everyday tool for learning and creating.

Hundreds of kilometres away in rural Anhui province, Funan County Qinqing High School is using the same technology to solve a problem affluent urban areas in China rarely face: a shortage of qualified teachers.

The school's 4,000 pupils, most of them children of migrant workers, learn core subjects through AI-generated lessons, according to headmaster Yang Tianliang. Students follow personalised classes on tablets, with AI agents posing questions rather than providing answers when they struggle.
"An AI agent doesn't suffer from fatigue, and it never makes a student feel stupid for asking a basic question," Yang said.

The school uses popular Chinese AI models from Alibaba's Qwen, ByteDance and Z.AI to generate text, images, interactive lessons and videos. Yang said it had also introduced small-group projects to encourage greater student interaction.

He credited the approach with helping lift university admission rates from below 60% to 90% in recent years, although Reuters could not independently verify the figures. Yang estimated at least 200 other Chinese schools were experimenting with similar systems.
An Alibaba spokesperson said its open-source AI models and Cloud for Youth Programme give students direct access to AI tools and education. ByteDance and Z.AI did not respond to requests for comment.
Schools such as Funan County Qinqing High School offer a glimpse of how quickly AI is spreading through China's education system.

Since 2024, China's education ministry has encouraged schools to introduce AI courses, train teachers and develop pilot programmes. Primary-school pupils are introduced to basic AI tools, while older students learn how AI systems work and apply them to increasingly sophisticated projects.
A Reuters review of more than 100 government procurement documents found authorities committed at least $31 million in the past year to AI classroom equipment, training and teaching platforms.

The true figure is likely far higher, scattered across thousands of local budgets and not officially tallied. Consultancy iResearch estimates 2025 spending on education digitalisation at just under $83 billion, with generative AI projects accounting for 46% of AI education procurement.
AN EXPERIMENT WITHOUT A CLEAR SCORECARD
China has yet to establish a standard framework for measuring AI literacy, leaving schools to experiment and making success difficult to assess.
"Mature, widely adopted assessment rubrics for compulsory school-level AI competency are still being built," said Selena Guo, portfolio lead at research firm China Policy.

Preliminary research into AI's effects on children's learning also offers mixed signals, with some studies suggesting short-term gains while raising questions about longer-term intellectual development.

A recent study examining nearly 27,000 Chinese teenagers found AI adoption was associated with an 18% increase in homework scores but a 20% decline in monthly examination scores within six months, with the biggest declines in social science subjects.

Another nationwide Chinese survey this year involving more than 320,000 pupils reported educational benefits from AI but also concerns about dependence and weaker independent thinking. Students using AI at least three times weekly showed lower memory, comprehension, analytical and creative skills than less frequent users.

The findings do not establish causation but reinforce teacher concerns about cognitive outsourcing, where children increasingly delegate mental tasks to technology rather than develop those skills themselves.
Chen from ClassIn warned that children's thinking processes could be "completely bypassed" if schools failed to prevent them from relying on AI for quick answers.
Chinese academic research reviewed by Reuters also suggested that students in rural areas may be particularly vulnerable to cognitive outsourcing and device addiction.
FINDING THE RIGHT BALANCE
Some educators and parents are already experimenting with safeguards to keep AI from replacing critical thinking.

At Beijing New Talent Academy, Peng said he tries to solve coding problems himself before asking AI for hints rather than complete answers. He said the technology has helped deepen his understanding of maths.
"I think AI is a tool that helps me, not something I depend on."
For Beijing parent Rita Luan, whose 11-year-old daughter attends a leading public school in the capital, the challenge is ensuring that AI strengthens rather than shortcuts learning.

She said her daughter's school still largely teaches AI concepts rather than practical applications, so she supplements lessons at home, teaching her daughter to prompt ByteDance's Doubao chatbot under close supervision.
Her rule: spend 15 minutes trying to solve a difficult maths problem before turning to AI. Days later, Luan asks her to solve the same problem without help.
"The point is to make sure she actually digested the solution," she said.
