title_zh: 美国国会拟立法封堵AI芯片海外云端访问漏洞
summary_zh: 鉴于英伟达前CEO黄仁勋涉情报安全丑闻，美国国会两党加速推进法案，严控高端芯片对华出口及云端访问权限
article_content_zh:
在英伟达创始人黄仁勋与一名涉嫌中国间谍的女性有染的消息曝光后，美国立法者正在加紧努力打击先进人工智能芯片进入中国。

民主党和共和党都支持一系列法案，限制敏感芯片在海外的销售，并赋予国会审查和可能阻止特朗普政府已经批准的销售的能力。

“鉴于最近的丑闻，这项立法的势头绝对增加了，”监督国会行动的华盛顿咨询公司灯塔政策顾问公司的高级研究分析师欧文·特德福德说。

曾为放宽出口规定而奋斗的黄仁勋在本周早些时候辞职，此前他被曝有婚外情，其中包括与新加坡英伟达客户 Megaspeed 高管的一名女性的婚外情。

美国一年多来一直在调查Megaspeed是否向中国走私芯片，而这名名叫Alice Huang的女子涉嫌为中国情报机构工作。

特德福德说：“英伟达可能觉得他们已经完成或试图继续前进，但华盛顿还没有准备好继续前进。”

Nvidia 芯片用于训练 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等实验室最先进的人工智能模型，支持者认为限制其出口对于保持美国的技术优势至关重要。

尽管这些提案已经在国会山取得进展，但特朗普政府未能阻止英伟达芯片出口到 Megaspeed 引发的政治愤怒加剧了相关努力。

其中一项名为《远程访问安全法案》的法案将阻止中国公司通过云服务远程访问海外芯片，即使它们被禁止购买实体芯片。

三名资深共和党议员周五敦促他们的同事立即通过几项限制人工智能芯片出口的法案。

众议院中国、外交和情报委员会主席、共和党人约翰·莫勒纳尔 (John Moolenaar)、布莱恩·马斯特 (Brian Mast) 和里克·克劳福德 (Rick Crawford) 写信给黄仁勋、英伟达总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特 (Tim Teter) 和负责出口管制的商务官员杰弗里·凯斯勒 (Jeffrey Kessler)，要求他们出席国会听证会。

他们写道：“我们需要了解我们的国家安全受到威胁的程度。”他们补充说，“这种情况是国会必须立即通过”四项旨在加强监督的法案的一个典型例子。

许多提案本周还吸引了即将离任的众议院议长、共和党人迈克·约翰逊及其可能的继任者哈基姆·杰弗里斯的支持。这些措施可能会附加到美国年度国防开支立法的最终版本中，立法者正在努力敲定最终文本。

《国防授权法案》(NDAA) 为美国国防部提供广泛资金，被认为是“必须通过”的法案，这意味着总统极不可能使用否决权来拒绝发送到他办公桌上的措施。

article_content:
Healthcare is fragmented, and teams often need to move information between systems manually before a patient can get care. When a clinician recommends an MRI, for example, the information an insurer needs may be in a patient’s medical record, but a team member still needs to retrieve it and enter it into a separate portal to complete an authorization request.

Computer-use agents carry out multi-step workflows by clicking, typing, and moving between applications. In healthcare, this enables AI to help with repetitive workflows in the software teams already use.

Today, we’re sharing new results measuring model performance, safety, and cost in clinical and administrative workflows. We’re also sharing the ways we’re working with leading healthcare organizations like Abridge, Ambience, Cigna Healthcare, and CVS Health to advance and apply computer use, across authorization requests, referrals, discharge planning, and outreach between visits.

Healthcare teams, developers, and individual clinicians can access these capabilities today through the OpenAI API, ChatGPT for Healthcare, and ChatGPT for Clinicians. Organizations can support HIPAA-compliant workflows, configure approvals and agent access, and record audit logs for secure deployments.

To show how a computer-use agent can help a clinician and an authorization specialist work on the same MRI request, we built a demo using synthetic patient data. A patient messages their clinician about lower back pain. A computer-use agent reviews the patient’s visit notes, physical therapy records, and prior imaging in the EHR. It drafts an MRI order, an encounter note, and a reply to the patient for the clinician to review. The agent then uses the same records to prepare a prior authorization request in the insurer’s portal for an authorization specialist to review.

We evaluated GPT‑6 Astra on tasks clinicians handle in their EHR inboxes. These tasks, shaped by physician input, require Astra to carry out multi-step workflows designed to test both clinical reasoning over longitudinal patient context and navigation of complex interfaces. Reviewers examined the model’s actions alongside the notes, orders, and patient messages it produced, assessing whether the work would be helpful and clinically safe in the context of the task.

Clinical safety was assessed by evaluating whether inaccuracies, omissions, or actions in the model’s work could plausibly lead to patient harm. Overall, 99% of 325 reviewed tasks were rated safe. Physicians rated helpfulness on a five-point scale, selecting “very helpful” or “extremely helpful” in 93% of 646 assessments.

We also evaluated computer-use agents for administrative tasks, such as prior authorizations, appeals, and medical equipment orders. On HealthAdminBench⁠(opens in a new window), an independent benchmark from Stanford researchers measuring performance on common administrative workflows, GPT‑6 Astra earned 94.3% of available rubric points, while GPT‑6 Luna earned 91.8%, despite costing 98% less at 8.5 cents per task. Both models were evaluated at maximum reasoning effort. These results show progress toward capable, affordable agents for high-volume administrative workflows.

Our partners build software used in hundreds of health systems, coordinate care for members globally, and deliver care to hundreds of millions of patients. The following examples showcase how organizations are developing, piloting, and deploying computer-use applications to save time, solve critical problems, and improve patient care.

CVS Health is using OpenAI’s computer-use capabilities to automate repetitive work across clinical systems, including sending documents, processing referrals, and supporting specialist consults. The agents navigate existing applications to complete steps that APIs do not fully support.

In one production workflow, an agent cleared a months-long document-sending backlog over a weekend. Another handles the system steps for tens of thousands of consults each day, helping team members focus on work that needs their expertise. CVS Health uses validation checks and human oversight, with screenshots and action records to verify actions and application state. CVS Health is open sourcing its Agent Kit⁠(opens in a new window), built with OpenAI’s Agents SDK, which packages this approach as a repeatable process for broader use.

Data remains within the CVS Health enterprise-controlled infrastructure, governed by their enterprise AI Governance team and established responsible AI policies. Production data is not used to train foundation models.

Abridge is developing computer-use agents to help clinicians carry out care plans across use cases and applications they use daily, including those without APIs. Their planned inpatient use case builds on the clinical conversation, adding EHR information and nurse and clinician context to identify what needs attention and to coordinate next steps.

For example, a clinician can ask the Abridge Assistant to help resolve a patient’s discharge barriers. Agents can work concurrently on medication access and home-health coordination, using computer interaction alongside calls and messages. The clinician stays focused on the patient and is brought in for decisions requiring clinical judgment.

As part of The Cigna Group’s broader collaboration with OpenAI, Cigna Healthcare is using OpenAI’s frontier models alongside its own clinical expertise to bring together relevant information across systems and give care teams more complete context about each member’s needs and experience. That can include information about benefits and coverage, providers, appointments and prior interactions, helping care teams better support members around care plans established by their treating providers.

Previously, Cigna Healthcare case managers had to navigate more than 10 separate clinical and administrative systems to gather this context. Computer use can now help navigate these systems and bring relevant information together in seconds, reducing the time spent searching for information – ultimately giving case managers more time to support members.

Computer use lets agents complete tasks in EHRs and payer portals that APIs don’t reach. In healthcare, that capability is only usable if every action is controlled and auditable. Ambience built additional controls to support that oversight.

In this demonstration, Ambience uses evidence from the patient’s chart to prepare a prior-authorization request on an insurer’s website. When the record is ambiguous, the agent stops and asks the clinician, then waits for approval before submitting. Health systems set which actions the agent can take, can pause it at any point, and get a step-by-step log for audit.

Healthcare startups are helping turn advances in computer use into new ways to support care teams. These five companies are combining AI agents with healthcare expertise to help teams navigate systems, coordinate next steps, and move care forward.

Computer-use agents in healthcare require evaluating clinical safety, protecting patient information, and setting clear limits on what agents can do without human review.

ChatGPT for Healthcare provides role-based access controls and audit logs to support oversight. Organizations can build additional review and approval steps into their workflows and configure the applications and environments agents use to limit access to the records and actions needed for each task. Organization data is not used to train OpenAI foundation models.

To support HIPAA-compliant workflows involving protected health information, organizations must use eligible services covered by their Business Associate Agreement with OpenAI and the required security and retention settings.

Computer-use agents for healthcare are available today in ChatGPT for Healthcare, ChatGPT for Clinicians, and the OpenAI API. Here’s how healthcare organizations, clinicians, and developers can get started.

Healthcare organizations: Contact our sales team⁠ to discuss using AI in your clinical and administrative workflows. Existing customers can ask their workspace administrator to enable computer use in ChatGPT Work and Codex.

Developers: Build healthcare applications with the OpenAI API⁠(opens in a new window), and explore our computer use guide⁠(opens in a new window) to build agents that work across existing software.

We hope these advances enable healthcare teams to spend less time moving information through systems and more time caring for patients.

article_content_zh:
医疗保健是分散的，团队通常需要在患者获得护理之前在系统之间手动移动信息。例如，当临床医生推荐 MRI 时，保险公司所需的信息可能位于患者的医疗记录中，但团队成员仍然需要检索该信息并将其输入到单独的门户中以完成授权请求。

计算机使用代理通过单击、键入和在应用程序之间移动来执行多步骤工作流程。在医疗保健领域，这使得人工智能能够帮助完成已经使用的软件团队中的重复工作流程。

今天，我们将分享衡量临床和管理工作流程中模型性能、安全性和成本的新结果。我们还分享了与 Abridge、Ambience、Cigna Healthcare 和 CVS Health 等领先医疗保健组织合作的方式，以在授权请求、转诊、出院计划和就诊之间的外展方面推进和应用计算机使用。

医疗保健团队、开发人员和个人临床医生现在可以通过 OpenAI API、ChatGPT for Healthcare 和 ChatGPT for Clinicians 访问这些功能。组织可以支持符合 HIPAA 的工作流程、配置审批和代理访问并记录安全部署的审核日志。

为了展示计算机使用代理如何帮助临床医生和授权专家处理同一 MRI 请求，我们使用合成患者数据构建了一个演示。一名患者向临床医生发送有关腰痛的信息。计算机使用代理会审查患者的就诊记录、物理治疗记录和电子病历中先前的成像。它起草一份 MRI 命令、一份就诊记录以及给患者的答复，供临床医生审查。然后，代理人使用相同的记录在保险公司的门户中准备事先授权请求，以供授权专家审核。

我们针对临床医生在 EHR 收件箱中处理的任务评估了 GPT-6 Astra。这些任务由医生输入决定，要求 Astra 执行多步骤工作流程，旨在测试纵向患者背景的临床推理和复杂界面的导航。评审员检查了模型的行为以及它产生的注释、命令和患者消息，评估这项工作在任务背景下是否有帮助和临床安全。

通过评估模型工作中的不准确、遗漏或行为是否可能导致患者伤害来评估临床安全性。总体而言，325 项审核任务中 99% 被评为安全。医生按照五分制对有用性进行评分，在 646 项评估中，93% 选择“非常有帮助”或“非常有帮助”。

我们还评估了计算机使用代理执行行政任务的能力，例如事先授权、上诉和医疗设备订单。在 HealthAdminBench（在新窗口中打开）（斯坦福大学研究人员衡量常见管理工作流程性能的独立基准）上，GPT-6 Astra 获得了 94.3% 的可用评分，而 GPT-6 Luna 获得了 91.8%，尽管每项任务的成本降低了 98%，为 8.5 美分。两种模型均以最大推理努力进行评估。这些结果表明，在为大容量管理工作流程提供功能强大、价格实惠的代理方面取得了进展。

我们的合作伙伴构建了用于数百个卫生系统的软件，协调全球会员的护理，并为数亿患者提供护理。以下示例展示了组织如何开发、试点和部署计算机应用程序以节省时间、解决关键问题和改善患者护理。

CVS Health 正在使用 OpenAI 的计算机使用功能来自动化跨临床系统的重复性工作，包括发送文档、处理转诊和支持专家咨询。代理导航现有应用程序以完成 API 不完全支持的步骤。

在一个生产工作流程中，一名代理在周末清理了长达数月的文档发送积压工作。另一个人每天处理数以万计的咨询的系统步骤，帮助团队成员专注于需要他们专业知识的工作。 CVS Health 使用验证检查和人工监督，并通过屏幕截图和操作记录来验证操作和应用程序状态。 CVS Health 正在开源其 Agent Kit（在新窗口中打开），该工具包使用 OpenAI 的 Agents SDK 构建，将该方法打包为可重复的流程以供更广泛的使用。

数据保留在 CVS Health 企业控制的基础设施内，由其企业 AI 治理团队管理并制定负责任的 AI 政策。生产数据不用于训练基础模型。

Abridge 正在开发计算机使用代理，以帮助临床医生跨日常使用的用例和应用程序（包括那些没有 API 的用例和应用程序）执行护理计划。他们计划的住院患者用例建立在临床对话的基础上，添加 EHR 信息以及护士和临床医生的背景信息，以确定需要注意的事项并协调后续步骤。

例如，临床医生可以要求 Abridge 助理帮助解决患者的出院障碍。代理可以利用计算机交互以及电话和消息，同时进行药物获取和家庭健康协调。临床医生始终关注患者并做出需要临床判断的决定。

article_content:
Introducing computer-use agents, improved clinical answers, and new healthcare plugins that work across healthcare software to get real work done.

Healthcare teams need to piece together information from the EHR, hospital policies, scheduling systems, and payer portals to deliver care and manage operations. With ChatGPT for Healthcare, we’re bringing the tools teams already use and the medical evidence they need into one platform to help them spend less time navigating systems and more time caring for patients.

Today, we’re sharing advances in computer-use agents⁠, which lets AI agents carry out multi-step work across existing healthcare software. We’re also improving trusted clinical search, which finds, evaluates, and cites medical evidence, and introducing more than 20 new plugins to the healthcare plugin ecosystem.

Together, these capabilities help healthcare teams find the information they need, make decisions grounded in medical evidence, and carry out next steps across the systems they already use.

Organizations often need to move information between disconnected systems to prepare documentation, coordinate care, and complete administrative tasks. Computer-use agents can help with these steps by navigating the software that teams already use: reading screens, clicking, typing, and moving between applications.

Today, we’re sharing advances in computer-use agents for healthcare, including more capable, safe, and affordable models for clinical and administrative workflows, and access controls and audit logs for secure deployments. We’re also sharing our work with healthcare organizations that are deploying agents, including Abridge, Ambience, Cigna Healthcare, and CVS Health, to process referrals, move documents between systems, and bring together the information care teams need. In the demo below, a clinician uses Voice in the ChatGPT app to ask for help following up on an MRI request. The agent reviews the chart and drafts an order and patient reply for review.

Healthcare organizations can start with a workflow that spans existing applications, set which applications agents can access, and establish clear controls for which steps require human review. To support HIPAA-compliant workflows involving protected health information, organizations must use eligible services covered by their BAA with OpenAI, apply required security and retention settings, and extend protections to connected systems. Content shared with ChatGPT for Healthcare is not used to train models.

Read more about our computer use research, customer stories, and demonstrations in Advancing computer-use agents for healthcare teams⁠.

We’re improving trusted clinical search in ChatGPT for Healthcare and ChatGPT for Clinicians, including how ChatGPT finds, evaluates, and cites medical evidence. These updates help clinicians connect relevant evidence to clinical questions and translate it into practical next steps, with citations they can inspect.

To measure the impact of these updates, in a blind evaluation, physicians reviewed responses to real-world clinical questions across multiple specialties, including multi-turn conversations. In over 1300 reviews, physicians rated the updated experience more highly across all eight dimensions evaluated, including factual correctness, safety, actionability, and source authoritativeness.

We’re expanding our healthcare plugin ecosystem with more than 20 new healthcare plugins from leading companies across clinical care, care coordination, and business operations. All of these are available today in ChatGPT for Healthcare, including through ChartGPT, which brings ChatGPT into the EHR workflow⁠.

These plugins let teams bring more of their work into the same conversation: reviewing patient records and hospital protocols, preparing prescriptions for clinician review, coordinating patient outreach, checking insurance eligibility, and analyzing healthcare costs and operational performance.

See how healthcare teams can use these plugins together in ChatGPT.

Use Luma Health to find tomorrow’s appointments that still need confirmation, then check those patients’ insurance eligibility with TriZetto. Build a call list showing what I need to confirm or resolve with each patient before their visit.

My patient was hospitalized elsewhere for heart failure - find the discharge summary using Metriport. Which medications changed? What follow-up monitoring does UpToDate recommend for those changes? Link me to both sources.

I’m admitting a patient who uses their own insulin pump, and the admitting team has requested endocrinology input. Pull up our hospital’s inpatient pump policy in AIVA, including required nursing checks and documentation, and use Amion to find the covering endocrinologist and how to reach them.

My patient can get a knee MRI without contrast at either of these two hospitals. Use IMO Health to identify the matching procedure code, check their insurance eligibility and benefits in Stedi, then show me their plan’s negotiated rate for that code at each hospital using Turquoise Health. Also identify any additional information needed to estimate what the patient would owe.

For our weekly referral review, use Assort Health to summarize referral volume, conversion trends, and our main referring practices. Use Ferry Health to show appointment tasks by status and link to those awaiting follow-up. Put the referral trends and outstanding scheduling work into a brief my team can use to prioritize patient follow-up.

The new plugins join ChatGPT’s broader ecosystem of plugins supporting work across industries, from healthcare data and research⁠ to documents, presentations, and software development.

With our plugin partners, we’re making it easier for care teams to bring clinical evidence, patient information, and their everyday tools into ChatGPT. We’re continuing to invest in this ecosystem and inviting more healthcare companies to build with us.

ChatGPT for Healthcare supports clinical, research, and administrative teams in a governed workspace. ChatGPT for Clinicians is free for eligible, verified clinicians in the U.S. to review medical evidence and prepare clinical documentation. Both products offer customers a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with OpenAI to support HIPAA-compliant workflows.

ChatGPT for Healthcare customers: Computer-use agents in ChatGPT Work and Codex and improved trusted clinical search are available today, subject to workspace settings. Ask your workspace administrator to enable new healthcare plugins.

Developers exploring computer use: Computer-use agent capability is available in the OpenAI API, ChatGPT Work, and Codex. Contact our sales team⁠ to discuss using these capabilities in your clinical and administrative workflows.

To purchase ChatGPT for Healthcare directly or through an AWS Marketplace private offer, contact our sales team⁠.

article_content_zh:
引入计算机使用代理、改进的临床答案以及跨医疗软件工作以完成实际工作的新医疗保健插件。

医疗保健团队需要将来自电子病历、医院政策、调度系统和付款人门户的信息整合在一起，以提供护理和管理运营。通过 ChatGPT for Healthcare，我们将团队已经使用的工具和他们所需的医学证据整合到一个平台中，以帮助他们花更少的时间浏览系统，而将更多的时间花在照顾患者上。

今天，我们将分享计算机使用代理的进步，它可以让人工智能代理在现有的医疗保健软件上执行多步骤工作。我们还改进了可信临床搜索，该搜索可以查找、评估和引用医学证据，并向医疗保健插件生态系统引入 20 多个新插件。

这些功能共同帮助医疗团队找到他们需要的信息，根据医学证据做出决策，并在他们已经使用的系统上执行后续步骤。

组织通常需要在断开连接的系统之间移动信息，以准备文档、协调护理和完成管理任务。计算机使用代理可以通过导航团队已使用的软件来帮助完成这些步骤：阅读屏幕、单击、键入以及在应用程序之间移动。

今天，我们将分享医疗保健计算机使用代理的进展，包括用于临床和管理工作流程的更强大、更安全和更实惠的模型，以及用于安全部署的访问控制和审核日志。我们还与正在部署代理的医疗机构（包括 Abridge、Ambience、Cigna Healthcare 和 CVS Health）分享我们的工作，以处理转诊、在系统之间移动文档以及汇集护理团队所需的信息。在下面的演示中，临床医生使用 ChatGPT 应用程序中的语音来请求帮助以跟进 MRI 请求。代理人审查图表并起草订单和患者答复以供审查。

医疗保健组织可以从跨越现有应用程序的工作流程开始，设置代理可以访问哪些应用程序，并为哪些步骤需要人工审核建立明确的控制。为了支持涉及受保护健康信息的符合 HIPAA 的工作流程，组织必须将其 BAA 涵盖的合格服务与 OpenAI 结合使用，应用所需的安全和保留设置，并将保护扩展到连接的系统。与 ChatGPT for Healthcare 共享的内容不用于训练模型。

阅读有关我们的计算机使用研究、客户案例和演示的更多信息，请参阅《为医疗团队推进计算机使用代理》。

我们正在改进 ChatGPT for Healthcare 和 ChatGPT for Clinicians 中的可信临床搜索，包括 ChatGPT 如何查找、评估和引用医学证据。这些更新可帮助临床医生将相关证据与临床问题联系起来，并将其转化为实际的后续步骤，并附上可供检查的引文。

为了衡量这些更新的影响，在盲目评估中，医生审查了多个专业对现实临床问题的回答，包括多轮对话。在 1300 多条评论中，医生在评估的所有八个维度（包括事实正确性、安全性、可操作性和来源权威性）上对更新后的体验给予了更高的评价。

我们正在通过来自临床护理、护理协调和业务运营领域领先公司的 20 多个新医疗保健插件来扩展我们的医疗保健插件生态系统。所有这些现在都可以在 ChatGPT for Healthcare 中使用，包括通过 ChartGPT，它将 ChatGPT 引入 EHR 工作流程⁠。

这些插件使团队可以将更多工作纳入同一对话中：审查患者记录和医院协议、准备处方以供临床医生审查、协调患者外展、检查保险资格以及分析医疗保健成本和运营绩效。

title: Alibaba says it filtered Qwen4-Max's training data to remove offensive cyber capabilities and mitigate chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear risks (Ann Cao/South China Morning Post)
title_en: Alibaba says it filtered Qwen4-Max's training data to remove offensive cyber capabilities and mitigate chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear risks (Ann Cao/South China Morning Post)

inline_images.caption: Alibaba’s Max series of models had always been closed-source until Qwen 3.8, which was made available as open source in August. Photo: Shutterstock
inline_images.alt: Alibaba’s Max series of models had always been closed-source until Qwen 3.8, which was made availabl

author: South China Morning Post
article_content:
Alibaba Group Holding has launched its most advanced artificial intelligence model to date, Qwen4-Max, with strict cybersecurity guardrails, as the tech giant balances safety with a continued commitment to open sourcing amid growing global concerns over AI-enabled cyberattacks.

The release highlights a growing focus on safety in China’s AI industry as Alibaba said it intentionally filtered the model’s training data to remove offensive cyberattack capabilities while retaining capabilities useful for cyber defence such as vulnerability detection.

The Hangzhou-based company also introduced dedicated data sets and post-training enhancements to mitigate chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear (CBRN) risks, it said on Monday.

Alibaba also highlighted the model’s improvements in scientific research, including the completion of a continuous 48-hour run to discover an experimentally validated coolant molecule for next-generation semiconductor chips, as well as autonomous research on Alzheimer’s disease.

There is heated debate about whether open-weight models, which are favoured by Chinese companies, could heighten CBRN risks more than the closed-source models championed by their US rivals such as OpenAI and Anthropic.

Some experts have warned that AI systems could eventually be powerful enough to enable malicious actors or states to develop CBRN weapons.

While Qwen4-Max is a closed model, Alibaba reaffirmed its open-source strategy by noting that smaller-scale, open-weight versions of the Qwen4 series would be released to global developers soon.

Alibaba’s Max series of models had always been closed-source until Qwen 3.8, which was made available as open source in August. The Max series is also the company’s largest model by parameter size. However, the company highlighted its achievements in making its latest model more cost-efficient when served to users.

Qwen4-Max boasts 2.4 trillion parameters, the same size as its previous Qwen3.8-Max, though it activates only 71 billion parameters per token – 25 per cent less than its predecessor.

That allows it to deliver superior reasoning capabilities while bringing down inference costs, cutting the average cost per task by 60 per cent, according to Alibaba, citing an internal benchmark called Work360, which evaluates model performance on various work tasks.

The model is currently available via QwenCloud, with input pricing set at 7.5 US cents per 1 million tokens.

Alibaba’s AI efforts have focused heavily on capturing the enterprise AI market and cultivating an open-source community to outpace local rivals like DeepSeek and Z.ai, as well as US competitors.

Liu Dayiheng, head of Alibaba’s Qwen large language model team, presented a road map outlining plans for the Qwen 4, Qwen 4.5 and Qwen 5 series in September, while stressing the team’s commitment to the open-source community earlier this month at the World Internet Conference in Wuzhen.

The company has said that its next-generation model, Qwen 5, would be scaled up to between 5 trillion and 10 trillion parameters.

Alibaba owns the South China Morning Post.

article_content_zh:
阿里巴巴集团控股有限公司推出了迄今为止最先进的人工智能模型Qwen4-Max，该模型具有严格的网络安全护栏，在全球对人工智能网络攻击日益担忧的情况下，这家科技巨头在安全与持续致力于开源之间取得了平衡。

此次发布突显了中国人工智能行业对安全性的日益关注，阿里巴巴表示，它有意过滤模型的训练数据，以消除进攻性网络攻击能力，同时保留对网络防御有用的功能，例如漏洞检测。

这家总部位于杭州的公司周一表示，还推出了专用数据集和培训后增强功能，以减轻化学、生物、放射性和核（CBRN）风险。

阿里巴巴还强调了该模型在科学研究方面的进步，包括完成了连续 48 小时运行，发现了经过实验验证的用于下一代半导体芯片的冷却剂分子，以及针对阿尔茨海默病的自主研究。

关于中国公司青睐的开放权重模型是否会比 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等美国竞争对手所倡导的闭源模型更大地增加 CBRN 风险，存在着激烈的争论。

一些专家警告说，人工智能系统最终可能强大到足以使恶意行为者或国家能够开发核生化武器。

虽然Qwen4-Max是一个封闭模型，但阿里巴巴重申了其开源战略，指出Qwen4系列的较小规模、开放重量版本将很快向全球开发者发布。

阿里巴巴的Max系列机型一直是闭源的，直到8月份Qwen 3.8成为开源版本。Max系列也是该公司参数尺寸最大的机型。然而，该公司强调了其最新型号在为用户提供服务时更具成本效益的成就。

Qwen4-Max 拥有 2.4 万亿个参数，与之前的 Qwen3.8-Max 大小相同，但每个代币仅激活 710 亿个参数，比其前身少了 25%。

阿里巴巴称，这使其能够提供卓越的推理能力，同时降低推理成本，将每个任务的平均成本降低 60%，并引用了一个名为 Work360 的内部基准，该基准评估模型在各种工作任务上的性能。

该模型目前可通过 QwenCloud 获得，输入价格设定为每 100 万个代币 7.5 美分。

阿里巴巴的人工智能工作主要集中在占领企业人工智能市场和培育开源社区，以超越 DeepSeek 和 Z.ai 等本土竞争对手以及美国竞争对手。

阿里巴巴Qwen大语言模型团队负责人刘大一恒在9月份的乌镇世界互联网大会上发布了Qwen 4、Qwen 4.5和Qwen 5系列的路线图，概述了Qwen 4、Qwen 4.5和Qwen 5系列的计划，同时强调了团队对开源社区的承诺。

该公司表示，其下一代模型 Qwen 5 将扩展到 5 万亿至 10 万亿个参数。

Qwen4 Max is above average in intelligence and reasonably priced when comparing to other models of similar price. The model supports text and image input, outputs text, and has a 984k tokens context window.

Qwen4 Max scores 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it above average among comparable models (median: 41). When evaluating the Intelligence Index, it generated 127M tokens, which is very verbose in comparison to the median of 78.6M.

Pricing for Qwen4 Max is $1.50 per 1M input tokens (moderately priced, median: $2.00) and $4.50 per 1M output tokens (moderately priced, median: $10.00). On average, it costs $3.27 per task to evaluate Qwen4 Max on the Intelligence Index.

title: Sources: the Trump admin plans to name Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Anthropic among 24+ AI "national champions" to help them win overseas business (Wall Street Journal)
title_en: Sources: the Trump admin plans to name Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Anthropic among 24+ AI "national champions" to help them win overseas business (Wall Street Journal)
author: Wall Street Journal
article_content:
The Trump administration plans to name more than two dozen artificial intelligence firms as U.S. “national champions,” the Wall Street Journal reported. People familiar with the plans said the announcement is expected within the next week.

BREAKING: 🇺🇸 Trump administration plans to designate Nvidia and other major AI companies as "National Champions" per WSJ. pic.twitter.com/tZx940kYl7

Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic are among the companies set to receive the label. The date could still slip, some of the people said.

Companies named national champions can get faster approvals for licenses to export chips and other technology. They can also receive government support for their work overseas and access to federal financing.

The Commerce Department’s website lists these benefits. The program was first announced about a year ago, but no champions had been named.

The goal is to package U.S. chips, models and other AI products so foreign customers can buy them together. The effort aims to get companies and countries to use U.S. technology instead of Chinese rivals.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is expected to announce the plan. He is also expected to join President Trump on a trip to China this week.

Critics say Lutnick’s agency has not closed loopholes that let Chinese firms reach high-end Nvidia chips. The agency is now set to move forward with new rules limiting chip diversion to China.

Nothing in the plan has been confirmed, and CoinDesk could not immediately verify the report.

Nvidia closed Friday at $162.85. That is about 33% below its Oct. 6 peak of $243.37.

The VanEck Semiconductor ETF, the largest chip-focused fund in the U.S. with about $65 billion in assets, closed at $486.75. That is about 28% below its 52-week high of $671.83.

The iShares A.I. Innovation and Tech Active ETF closed at $36.47, down 33% from its June record high of $54.46. It fell to its lowest level since March last week and holds about $11.7 billion in assets.

Nvidia has also been in the spotlight over reports that Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence source. She reportedly worked for a Singapore-based data-center company.

The reports have led hawks to renew calls to put national security ahead of market share, including by tightening chip export controls. Nvidia’s board opened an investigation into the relationship last week.

Huang resigned as CEO on Thursday, effective immediately. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is now interim CEO.

President Trump has repeatedly praised Huang for building a homegrown champion that powers the AI boom.

Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday after the market closes. It will be the company’s first report since Huang stepped down.

title_zh: 特朗普政府拟确立人工智能国家冠军企业名单
summary_zh: 特朗普政府拟将英伟达、亚马逊、微软、OpenAI及Anthropic等超24家企业列为人工智能“国家冠军”，以提升美国AI技术在全球市场的竞争力
article_content_zh:
特朗普政府计划将两打以上人工智能公司列为美国“国家冠军”。熟悉该计划的人士表示，预计将在下周内宣布这一消息。

突发新闻：据《华尔街日报》报道，特朗普政府计划将 Nvidia 和其他主要人工智能公司指定为“国家冠军”。 pic.twitter.com/tZx940kYl7

Nvidia、亚马逊、微软、OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等公司都将获得该标签。一些知情人士表示，这一日期仍有可能推迟。

被评为全国冠军的公司可以更快地获得出口芯片和其他技术的许可证。他们还可以获得政府对海外工作的支持以及联邦融资。

商务部的网站列出了这些好处。该计划大约在一年前首次宣布，但尚未确定冠军。

目标是将美国芯片、模型和其他人工智能产品打包，以便外国客户可以一起购买。此举旨在让企业和国家使用美国技术而不是中国竞争对手。

商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克预计将宣布该计划。预计他本周还将与特朗普总统一起访问中国。

批评人士称，卢特尼克的机构尚未堵住中国公司获得英伟达高端芯片的漏洞。该机构现在准备推进限制芯片转移到中国的新规则。

该计划中的任何内容尚未得到证实，CoinDesk 无法立即核实该报道。

Nvidia 周五收盘价为 162.85 美元。这比 10 月 6 日峰值 243.37 美元低约 33%。

VanEck Semiconductor ETF 是美国最大的芯片基金，资产约为 650 亿美元，收盘价为 486.75 美元。这比 671.83 美元的 52 周高点低约 28%。

iShares 人工智能Innovation and Tech Active ETF 收于 36.47 美元，较 6 月份的历史高点 54.46 美元下跌 33%。上周跌至3月份以来的最低水平，持有资产约117亿美元。

英伟达还因黄仁勋与一名疑似中国情报来源的女性有染的报道而受到关注。据报道，她在一家新加坡数据中心公司工作。

这些报告导致鹰派再次呼吁将国家安全置于市场份额之上，包括加强芯片出口管制。英伟达董事会上周对这种关系展开了调查。

title: AI agent management platform Kindo raised $30M led by Crosspoint and Forgepoint, bringing total funding to $57.6M, and says its revenue grew ~800% YoY in 2026 (Abhinaya Prabhu/Tech Funding News)
title_en: AI agent management platform Kindo raised $30M led by Crosspoint and Forgepoint, bringing total funding to $57.6M, and says its revenue grew ~800% YoY in 2026 (Abhinaya Prabhu/Tech Funding News)
author: Tech Funding News
article_content:
As businesses deploy AI agents across more departments, controlling what these systems can access, change and spend is becoming a growing challenge.

Kindo, an AI agent management platform, has raised $30 million in a funding round co-led by Crosspoint Capital and Forgepoint Capital, bringing its total funding to $57.6 million. The company did not name the round.

Kindo reported approximately 800% year-on-year revenue growth in 2026. It plans to use the capital to expand its go-to-market organisation and accelerate development of its enterprise AI Control Center and Deep Hat models and add-ons.

“Agent builders from the AI labs, hyperscalers, and thousands of startups make it easy to deploy powerful agents across the business. What’s missing is the tooling that lets an organization centrally control how those agents are built, what data they can reach, where that data can go, and what they cost, while also allowing support teams to reach in and fix an agent at any hour,” said Ron Williams, founder and CEO of Kindo.

Kindo was founded in 2022 by Williams, who serves as its CEO. He began his career as a programmer in the US Air Force before moving into IT and security leadership. According to Kindo’s website, he served as chief information officer and chief information security officer at Riot Games, Clover Health and Bird.

Kindo’s founding team also includes Bryan Vann, its co-founder and CTO. Vann was one of the original architects of Google Drive and left Google as a senior director managing most of the Drive engineering team, according to a 2024 Pulse 2.0 interview.

Kindo helps businesses discover AI agents already operating across their environments, including tools deployed without formal IT approval. It then provides a unified view of agent activity, data access, costs and outcomes.

Its gateways govern and audit calls made by agents to connected data sources, tools and approved AI models. Identity controls extend existing organisational permissions to both employees and agents, while allowing administrators to tighten access centrally.

For mission-critical applications, Kindo offers a purpose-built agent harness that provides continuous monitoring and support. Teams can directly intervene or take over an agent when something goes wrong.

The platform can connect to agents and models already in use, rather than requiring businesses to rebuild their AI infrastructure. It can run on-premises, in a customer’s cloud, through Kindo’s cloud or in air-gapped environments.

Kindo says it runs in production at large and mid-market enterprises in financial services, professional services, healthcare, and aviation and transportation. Aireon, a global aviation in-flight data provider, reported in May 2026 that using Kindo for threat hunting and Tier 1 and Tier 2 security operations centre work helped it save more than $2 million a year, according to the company.

Beyond security and compliance, the cost of running AI agents is becoming a major concern for businesses. Kindo’s AI Control Center gives finance teams visibility into token consumption, agent runs and their outcomes, including unsuccessful tasks.

Costs can be tracked by employee, agent, department and project. Businesses can also set budgets, trigger spending alerts and enforce hard limits. This helps identify agents that repeatedly fail, consume excessive resources or use expensive models for relatively simple tasks.

Kindo’s Deep Hat add-ons are designed to reduce these expenses further. Deep Hat Sift filters repetitive events from alert and ticket queues after human approval, while logging the activity and sending samples through to measure potential misses.

Deep Hat Tune adapts smaller, less expensive models to specific tasks, reducing reliance on larger models. Deep Hat Shrink converts repeatable workflow steps into code, eliminating model costs for those operations while routing exceptions back to an AI model. Deep Hat Attack provides private, lower-cost offensive security testing.

Kindo is entering a competitive market where startups and established technology companies are developing tools to secure, monitor and govern autonomous AI systems.

London-based Geordie AI raised $30 million in Series A funding led by Balderton Capital in May 2026 to build a security layer for AI agents. Barcelona-based NeuralTrust raised $20 million in seed funding led by Alstin Capital in June 2026 to govern enterprise agents.

Israel’s Zenity raised $125 million in a Series C led by Norwest in August 2026 to secure AI agents. GitGuardian raised $50 million in Series C funding in February 2026, led by Insight Partners, and is extending its non-human identity security to credentials used by AI agents. FriskAI raised $3.6 million in pre-seed funding led by MaC Venture Capital in August 2026 to record and review what agents do.

Alongside Crosspoint Capital and Forgepoint Capital, TFX Capital and CircleRock Capital joined the financing. Existing investors Drive Capital, Riot Ventures, RRE Ventures, Eniac Ventures, Marlinspike Partners, New Era Ventures and Sunset Venture also participated.

Andre Fuetsch, managing director at Crosspoint Capital, and Ernie Bio, managing director at Forgepoint Capital, will join Kindo’s board.

“2026 has been the year of the agent. Companies are putting AI agents into real business processes, but most still lack a reliable way to see what those agents are doing or control which systems they can reach. Kindo differentiates itself by giving the teams who need deep control the ability to see and take action while allowing AI transformation to move forward across the enterprise,” said Fuetsch.

“A company may start with one agent triaging security tickets. As more employees and teams put agents to work, the CIO needs a single place to manage what they can access, support what they do, and control the cost. We backed Kindo because it gives enterprises a way to rein in the tokenmaxxing madness with centrally managed, data-informed control policies,” added Bio.

With cost now as pressing as security, the question for Kindo is whether enterprises will buy one control layer for both, or keep separate tools for each.

article_content_zh:
随着企业在更多部门部署人工智能代理，控制这些系统可以访问、更改和支出的内容正成为越来越大的挑战。

人工智能代理管理平台 Kindo 在 Crosspoint Capital 和 Forgepoint Capital 共同领投的一轮融资中筹集了 3000 万美元，使其总融资达到 5760 万美元。该公司没有透露该轮融资的具体名称。

Kindo 报告称，2026 年收入同比增长约 800%。该公司计划利用这笔资金扩大其上市组织，并加速其企业 AI 控制中心和 Deep Hat 模型及附加组件的开发。

Kindo 创始人兼首席执行官 Ron Williams 表示：“来自人工智能实验室、超大规模企业和数千家初创公司的代理构建者可以轻松地在整个企业中部署强大的代理。现在缺少的是一种工具，可以让组织集中控制这些代理的构建方式、它们可以访问哪些数据、这些数据可以去往何处以及它们的成本，同时还允许支持团队随时介入并修复代理。”

Kindo 由 Williams 于 2022 年创立，并担任首席执行官。他的职业生涯始于美国空军的一名程序员，之后进入 IT 和安全领导岗位。据 Kindo 网站称，他曾在 Riot Games、Clover Health 和 Bird 担任首席信息官和首席信息安全官。

Kindo 的创始团队还包括联合创始人兼首席技术官 Bryan Vann。根据 2024 年 Pulse 2.0 的采访，范恩是 Google Drive 的最初架构师之一，离开 Google 后担任高级总监，管理大部分 Drive 工程团队。

Kindo 帮助企业发现已经在其环境中运行的人工智能代理，包括未经正式 IT 批准而部署的工具。然后，它提供代理活动、数据访问、成本和结果的统一视图。

其网关管理和审核代理对连接的数据源、工具和批准的人工智能模型发出的调用。身份控制将现有的组织权限扩展到员工和代理，同时允许管理员集中加强访问。

对于关键任务应用程序，Kindo 提供了专门构建的代理工具，可提供持续监控和支持。当出现问题时，团队可以直接干预或接管代理。

该平台可以连接到已经在使用的代理和模型，而不需要企业重建其人工智能基础设施。它可以在本地、客户的云中、通过 Kindo 的云或气隙环境中运行。

Kindo 表示，它在金融服务、专业服务、医疗保健、航空和运输领域的大中型市场企业中运行生产。全球航空飞行数据提供商 Aireon 于 2026 年 5 月报告称，使用 Kindo 进行威胁搜寻以及一级和二级安全运营中心工作帮助其每年节省了超过 200 万美元。

除了安全性和合规性之外，运行人工智能代理的成本正成为企业关注的主要问题。 Kindo 的人工智能控制中心使财务团队能够了解代币消耗、代理运行及其结果，包括不成功的任务。

可以按员工、代理、部门和项目跟踪成本。企业还可以设置预算、触发支出警报并实施硬性限制。这有助于识别反复失败、消耗过多资源或使用昂贵模型来完成相对简单任务的代理。

Kindo 的 Deep Hat 附加组件旨在进一步减少这些费用。 Deep Hat Sift 在人工批准后过滤警报和票证队列中的重复事件，同时记录活动并发送样本以测量潜在的遗漏。

article_content:
Big AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic have made their bets on offering chatbots that can answer health-related queries with specialized features. Apple is debuting a new study to understand how people use AI for health. But it isn’t quite following other AI startups just yet; it wants to study how clinically grounded answers can help people.

The iPhone maker is partnering with healthcare-focused AI company OpenEvidence to launch a new study app. Apple is inviting users in the U.S. over 21, using iPhone 15 or later, and running iOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled. The company is aiming to run this study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months.

The new app will allow users to ask health-related questions, as they do with ChatGPT or Claude, with answers grounded in clinical data, from sources including The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature. Apple said that the app will try to give simplified answers to everyday medical questions. Users can rate those answers and provide feedback about the responses; they’ll also be asked to participate in monthly surveys.

Participants can share data from HealthKit such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep, or lab results to get more personalized and pointed suggestions from the app. The company said the app can also help prepare participants better for a doctor’s visit, and it will guide users to specific providers for answers related to concerning medical issues.

party cloud provider, and it won’t be used to train any kind of AI models. The company said that OpenEvidence deletes the query and response data after 24 hours.

“At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding. Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in a statement, adding, “Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey.”

The app is available to download starting today for U.S. users. It’s not clear if Apple wants to release AI-powered answering to its Health app or Siri yet. The potential is huge — earlier this year, OpenAI said users were asking over 300 million health-related queries each week.

title_zh: 苹果启动健康AI应用研究计划
summary_zh: 苹果联合OpenEvidence推出健康AI研究应用，邀请20万美国用户参与，探索临床数据驱动的AI问答模式
article_content_zh:
OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等大型人工智能实验室已经押注于提供能够通过专门功能回答与健康相关的查询的聊天机器人。苹果公司推出了一项新研究，旨在了解人们如何利用人工智能来促进健康。但它还没有完全追随其他人工智能初创公司的脚步。它想要研究基于临床的答案如何帮助人们。

这家 iPhone 制造商正在与专注于医疗保健的人工智能公司 OpenEvidence 合作推出一款新的研究应用程序。 Apple 正在邀请年满 21 岁、使用 iPhone 15 或更高版本、运行 iOS 26 或更高版本并启用 Apple Intelligence 的美国用户。该公司的目标是对多达 20 万名参与者进行这项为期 12 个月以上的研究。

新应用程序将允许用户提出与健康相关的问题，就像使用 ChatGPT 或 Claude 一样，答案基于临床数据，来源包括《新英格兰医学杂志》、《美国医学会杂志》和《自然》等。苹果表示，该应用程序将尝试为日常医疗问题提供简化的答案。用户可以对这些答案进行评分并提供有关答复的反馈；他们还将被要求参加每月调查。

参与者可以共享 HealthKit 中的数据，例如静息心率、活动、睡眠或实验室结果，以便从应用程序中获得更加个性化和针对性的建议。该公司表示，该应用程序还可以帮助参与者更好地准备去看医生，并将引导用户向特定的提供商寻求与医疗问题相关的答案。

苹果明确表示，这些数据在发送给安全的第三方云提供商之前将进行匿名处理，并且不会用于训练任何类型的人工智能模型。该公司表示，OpenEvidence 会在 24 小时后删除查询和响应数据。

苹果健康与健身副总裁 Sumbul Desai 医学博士在一份声明中表示：“在苹果，我们相信负责任的创新始于科学严谨性和临床基础。健康是非常个性化的，进行专门的研究是了解人们如何在日常生活中参与、理解和评估健康人工智能的最深思熟虑的方式。”正在踏上健康之旅。”

该应用程序从今天开始可供美国用户下载。目前尚不清楚苹果是否想要为其健康应用程序或 Siri 发布人工智能驱动的应答功能。潜力巨大——今年早些时候，OpenAI 表示用户每周提出超过 3 亿个与健康相关的问题。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 苹果此次布局规避了通用大模型在医疗领域的盲目扩张，选择以封闭式科研闭环路径验证“临床证据链”的合规性，旨在建立极高行业壁垒的健康生态。通过严格限定数据匿名化处理及禁止用于模型训练的承诺，苹果试图在监管压力下，将HealthKit数据转化为核心竞争壁垒，为未来在Apple Intelligence中部署高附加值的医疗辅助功能进行合规化试探。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Apple is pursuing a conservative, closed-loop clinical validation strategy, prioritizing evidence-based accuracy over mass-market AI deployment to build an impenetrable moat in health-tech. By strictly isolating user data from model training and enforcing privacy compliance, Apple is positioning itself to integrate high-value medical assistance into its ecosystem while preempting stringent regulatory oversight.

title: Alibaba Unveils New Flagship AI Model in Riposte to US Rivals

The e-commerce giant-turned-AI player said its Qwen4-Max model scored near the top of coding benchmarks, outperforming Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 as well as homegrown rival Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro. Alibaba did not make the model open weight, which would allow users to download and customize it, but said it would make smaller versions of the series available soon.

Chinese firms including Alibaba, Moonshot and DeepSeek are challenging US dominance in artificial intelligence, unveiling a succession of new models with rapid improvements in coding and reasoning. Monday's release adds to a flurry of recent Chinese launches, including Tencent's Hunyuan 4 and Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro.

Alibaba's Qwen series is so far the most downloaded open-weight model family in the world following an ambitious push into the technology spearheaded by Chief Executive Officer Eddie Wu. The company is building a full AI ecosystem, from models to AI chips.

The CEO said in September that Alibaba's T-Head chipmaking unit, which recently filed for an IPO in Hong Kong, would roll out China's most powerful AI chips domestically.

The Hangzhou, China-headquartered firm has made attaining artificial general intelligence, or AGI, its primary goal. It is also rapidly expanding its computing power, with Wu setting a target of building 20 gigawatts of data center capacity globally by 2032.

The firm introduced upgraded security measures in its latest model, following a series of alarming incidents that have raised concerns over the cybersecurity risks of open-weight models. That follows similar moves from Tencent and Moonshot.

这家由电子商务巨头转型为人工智能的公司表示，其 Qwen4-Max 模型在编码基准测试中的得分接近最高，优于 Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5.1 以及本土竞争对手 Moonshot 的 Kimi K3.1 Pro。阿里巴巴并未开放该模型的重量，以便用户下载和定制，但表示将很快推出该系列的较小版本。

阿里巴巴、Moonshot 和 DeepSeek 等中国公司正在挑战美国在人工智能领域的主导地位，推出了一系列在编码和推理方面快速改进的新模型。周一的发布是中国最近推出的一系列产品的又一补充，其中包括腾讯的混元 4 和 Moonshot 的 Kimi K3.1 Pro。

阿里巴巴的 Qwen 系列是迄今为止全球下载量最大的开放式重量模型系列，在首席执行官吴宇森 (Eddie Wu) 的带领下雄心勃勃地推动了这项技术的发展。该公司正在构建从模型到人工智能芯片的完整人工智能生态系统。

这位首席执行官去年 9 月表示，最近在香港申请 IPO 的阿里巴巴 T-Head 芯片制造部门将在国内推出中国最强大的人工智能芯片。

这家总部位于中国杭州的公司已将实现通用人工智能（AGI）作为其首要目标。它还在迅速扩大其计算能力，吴设定的目标是到 2032 年在全球建设 20 吉瓦的数据中心容量。

在一系列令人震惊的事件引发人们对开放重量模型的网络安全风险的担忧之后，该公司在其最新模型中引入了升级的安全措施。腾讯和 Moonshot 也采取了类似的举措。

title: Sources: Jensen Huang had planned to pull back Nvidia's aggressive financing and told neoclouds to get upfront customer payments; Colette Kress may go further (Wall Street Journal)
title_en: Sources: Jensen Huang had planned to pull back Nvidia's aggressive financing and told neoclouds to get upfront customer payments; Colette Kress may go further (Wall Street Journal)
author: Wall Street Journal
article_content:
Nvidia is facing one the biggest crises in its 33 year history, with founder Jensen Huang resigning as CEO Thursday after multiple reported affairs, including one with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. Now CFO Colette Kress has taken the helm as Nvidia's interim CEO.

The implications of Huang's affair with Alice Huang run far deeper than infidelity. That's because her ties to Nvidia customer Megaspeed put her in the middle of a sprawling effort to accumulate AI chips across Southeast Asia. And Megaspeed is under investigation for possibly diverting restricted Nvidia chips into the hands of Chinese companies.

The relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang dates back to 2023, according to The New York Times. That was a "turbulent" period for Nvidia, Jensen Huang told CNBC during an interview at the time. Nvidia was in the midst of redesigning some chips to comply with the first in a series of strict export controls imposed by the U.S. government that restricted sales to China.

"The regulation is going to be just fine. We're going to be able to work through it," Huang told CNBC from Nvidia's headquarters in February 2023. The interview was for a documentary about how Huang created Nvidia and built it into the backbone of the AI boom.

That same day, CNBC also interviewed Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, with whom Jensen Huang reportedly had an affair.

It's not the first time Nvidia has faced an uncertain future. The company nearly went bankrupt in the early years after it was founded in 1993.

"Every company makes mistakes and I make a lot of them," Huang said in the 2023 interview. "And some of them put the company in peril."

In the early months of the AI boom, after OpenAI launched ChatGPT in November 2022, Nvidia was on the precipice of historic growth. Jensen Huang told CNBC he'd like to keep running the company for "three or four decades," as long as "I feel that I'm making a real contribution to the company."

Less than four years later, Jensen Huang is out, and we're taking a look back at our interviews with the Nvidia co-founder and other company executives as the chipmaker enters this next critical chapter. Watch the video for the full story.
content_snippet: Interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to rein in deals after a stretch in which Nvidia aggressively financed computing deals and startup investments

article_content_en:
Nvidia is facing one the biggest crises in its 33 year history, with founder Jensen Huang resigning as CEO Thursday after multiple reported affairs, including one with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. Now CFO Colette Kress has taken the helm as Nvidia's interim CEO.

The implications of Huang's affair with Alice Huang run far deeper than infidelity. That's because her ties to Nvidia customer Megaspeed put her in the middle of a sprawling effort to accumulate AI chips across Southeast Asia. And Megaspeed is under investigation for possibly diverting restricted Nvidia chips into the hands of Chinese companies.

The relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang dates back to 2023, according to The New York Times. That was a "turbulent" period for Nvidia, Jensen Huang told CNBC during an interview at the time. Nvidia was in the midst of redesigning some chips to comply with the first in a series of strict export controls imposed by the U.S. government that restricted sales to China.

"The regulation is going to be just fine. We're going to be able to work through it," Huang told CNBC from Nvidia's headquarters in February 2023. The interview was for a documentary about how Huang created Nvidia and built it into the backbone of the AI boom.

That same day, CNBC also interviewed Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, with whom Jensen Huang reportedly had an affair.

It's not the first time Nvidia has faced an uncertain future. The company nearly went bankrupt in the early years after it was founded in 1993.

"Every company makes mistakes and I make a lot of them," Huang said in the 2023 interview. "And some of them put the company in peril."

In the early months of the AI boom, after OpenAI launched ChatGPT in November 2022, Nvidia was on the precipice of historic growth. Jensen Huang told CNBC he'd like to keep running the company for "three or four decades," as long as "I feel that I'm making a real contribution to the company."

Less than four years later, Jensen Huang is out, and we're taking a look back at our interviews with the Nvidia co-founder and other company executives as the chipmaker enters this next critical chapter. Watch the video for the full story.

article_content_zh:
英伟达正面临其 33 年历史上最大的危机之一，创始人黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 因多起婚外情报道而于周四辞去首席执行官一职，其中包括与一名据称是中国间谍的女性的婚外情。现在，首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)已接任英伟达临时首席执行官。

黄与爱丽丝黄的恋情的影响远比不忠更深。这是因为她与 Nvidia 客户 Megaspeed 的联系使她陷入了在东南亚积累人工智能芯片的庞大努力之中。 Megaspeed 因可能将受限制的 Nvidia 芯片转移到中国公司手中而受到调查。

据《纽约时报》报道，黄仁勋和黄爱丽之间的关系可以追溯到 2023 年。黄仁勋当时在接受 CNBC 采访时表示，对于 Nvidia 来说，那是一个“动荡”的时期。英伟达正在重新设计一些芯片，以遵守美国政府实施的一系列严格出口管制中的第一项，限制对中国的销售。

2023 年 2 月，黄仁勋在 Nvidia 总部对 CNBC 表示：“监管会很好。我们将能够解决它。”这次采访是为了一部纪录片，讲述黄仁勋如何创建 Nvidia 并将其打造成人工智能热潮的支柱。

同一天，CNBC 还采访了英伟达医疗保健副总裁金伯利·鲍威尔 (Kimberly Powell)，据报道黄仁勋与她有染。

这并不是英伟达第一次面临不确定的未来。该公司成立于1993年，早年曾一度濒临破产。

“每个公司都会犯错误，我犯了很多错误，”黄在 2023 年的采访中说道。 “其中一些让公司陷入危险。”

在人工智能热潮的最初几个月，OpenAI 于 2022 年 11 月推出 ChatGPT 后，Nvidia 正处于历史性增长的悬崖上。黄仁勋告诉 CNBC，只要“我觉得自己为公司做出了真正的贡献”，他就愿意继续经营公司“三、四十年”。

不到四年后，黄仁勋离职了，随着芯片制造商进入下一个关键篇章，我们回顾一下对这位 Nvidia 联合创始人和其他公司高管的采访。观看视频了解完整故事。

title: Sources: Jensen Huang had planned to pull back Nvidia's aggressive financing and told neoclouds to get upfront customer payments; Colette Kress may go further (Wall Street Journal)
title_en: Sources: Jensen Huang had planned to pull back Nvidia's aggressive financing and told neoclouds to get upfront customer payments; Colette Kress may go further (Wall Street Journal)
author: Wall Street Journal
article_content:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

"Although we expect the company to fulfill all of its previously announced commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate new multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said in a note Thursday.

The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

Tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

On Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

Tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

It's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The company had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

Neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

CoreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, said CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

"We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he said.

"However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person."

"There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my company every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he said in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us."

Bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any big changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

The real issue is just how much money the company will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

"Big companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he said. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies."

— CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.
content_snippet: Interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to rein in deals after a stretch in which Nvidia aggressively financed computing deals and startup investments

title_zh: 英伟达CEO黄仁勋离职，AI基建融资模式承压
summary_zh: 英伟达CEO黄仁勋因丑闻辞职，现任CFO柯蕾特·克雷斯代理CEO，市场担忧英伟达对AI初创企业的激进融资支持将面临政策收紧
article_content_zh:
英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的离职并未对信贷市场造成广泛冲击，但该公司作为人工智能基础设施融资者的角色正受到审视。

周四因间谍和通奸丑闻辞职的黄仁勋在共同创立 Nvidia 的 33 年间，将 Nvidia 打造成一家人工智能巨头。由于公司正在寻找永久首席执行官，首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯 (Colette Kress) 已被任命为临时首席执行官。

英伟达不仅向超大规模企业和科技巨头提供图形处理单元，还向其他公司提供融资，以帮助该行业扩张。这一切都可能改变。

高盛分析师詹姆斯·施奈德(James Schneider)周四在一份报告中表示：“尽管我们预计该公司将履行之前宣布的所有承诺，但我们认为，展望未来，该公司在生态系统合作伙伴之间以迄今为止的规模进行新的多方投资谈判可能会更加困难。”

在黄仁勋辞职的消息传出之前，投资者已经对为人工智能基础设施提供资金而承担的巨额债务感到担忧。

科技债券收益率上升，信用违约掉期利差扩大，尤其是在评级较低的债券中。信用违约掉期是投资者在借款人无法偿还债务时支付保护费用的合同。利差扩大表明投资者认为这些债券风险更大。

周五，英伟达 2031 年到期的 4.5% 债券的收益率为 5.717%，较本周迄今上涨近 5%。债券收益率与价格成反比。

由于市场继续消化 Nvidia 的消息，科技股周五暴跌，纳斯达克 100 指数收盘下跌 1.2%。周五超大规模债券收益率小幅走高，表明对人工智能债务的更广泛担忧依然存在。

如果英伟达对其人工智能融资做出任何改变，最终可能会受到影响的是规模较小的人工智能公司。根据 7 月份的最后一个季度财务报告，该公司拥有价值 360 亿美元的表外 AI 云协议（或支持 Neoclouds）。

Neoclouds CoreWeave、Nebius 和 IREN 均属于 Nvidia 的产品组合。他们的股价周四大幅下跌。

CoreWeave 已成为人工智能债务担忧的典型代表，在周二的季度收益缓解了投资者的担忧后，其债券收益率有所回落。其2031年到期债券的收益率为9.75%，继上周攀升至16.7%后，周五为14.79%。其五年期 CDS 利差本周迄今也下降了 17% 以上，但仍保持在 1,000 以上——这通常被认为是陷入困境的迹象。

CreditSights 分析师 Andy Li 表示，目前尚不清楚 Nvidia 对这些公司的支持可能会如何改变。

“我们不知道英伟达的最终战略将会是什么，”他说。

“不过，我认为，从方向上看，鉴于詹森在推销英伟达的故事中发挥了如此重要的作用，并且是一位非常积极的交易撮合者，很多创造性的交易、循环融资以及股权和信贷支持很可能会放缓，”他补充道。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 英伟达创始人兼CEO黄仁勋因间谍与不当关系丑闻辞职，CFO柯蕾特·克雷斯出任代理CEO，引发市场对该公司深度参与AI基础设施信贷支持模式的深度重构。此前英伟达通过直接融资与背书，为CoreWeave、Nebius等“新云”厂商提供了约360亿美元的表外信贷背书，新管理层或将强制要求客户采取预付款模式以降低财务风险。

Nvidia has provided approximately $36 billion in off-balance-sheet credit support to 'neocloud' providers like CoreWeave and Nebius, and the new management is expected to pivot toward requiring upfront customer payments to mitigate credit risks.

Review of $36 billion in off-balance-sheet credit backstops for AI cloud firms

ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 英伟达过去通过资本链深度绑定云厂商的扩张策略本质上是“高杠杆加成下的硬件销售”，黄仁勋离职后的融资收缩将直接刺破AI基建领域的流动性泡沫。此举标志着AI产业从单纯的算力堆砌阶段转向财务自平衡考核，依赖英伟达直接信贷背书的二线算力集群将面临严峻的再融资压力与信用降级风险。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: Nvidia’s strategy of binding cloud providers through capital support functioned as hardware sales supercharged by high leverage; Huang’s departure and the subsequent financing contraction will likely expose the liquidity bubble in AI infrastructure. This pivot signals a shift from raw compute expansion to financial sustainability, placing severe refinancing pressure and credit risk on second-tier providers reliant on Nvidia’s balance sheet.

title_en: Mount Thor, which is building cloud infrastructure for agentic AI on Apple silicon, raised $45M in a seed round and a Series A co-led by CRV and Conviction (Bradley C/9to5Mac)
author: 9to5Mac

Mount Thor, a Bay Area startup building cloud infrastructure on Apple silicon, announced today that it has raised $45 million across Seed and Series A rounds. The pitch to its investors was simple: AI agents are incredible on Apple silicon, and nobody is renting them at data-center scale.

About Apple @ Work: Bradley Chambers managed an enterprise IT network from 2009 to 2021. Through his experience deploying and managing firewalls, switches, a mobile device management system, enterprise grade Wi-Fi, 1000s of Macs, and 1000s of iPads, Bradley will highlight ways in which Apple IT managers deploy Apple devices, build networks to support them, train users, stories from the trenches of IT management, and ways Apple could improve its products for IT departments.

CRV and Conviction co-led the Series A. Chad Byers and Offline Ventures co-led the Seed. CSC Leasing, Enea Capital, Long Journey Ventures, and Upper90 participated, along with angel investors from OpenAI, Meta, Cognition, Together AI, and Vercel. The company also raised separate non-dilutive financing for new hardware as well.

Mount Thor runs macOS on Apple silicon as elastic compute instances, just as a cloud provider rents Linux VMs. Customers get on-demand fleets of Macs for work that only happens on macOS: training computer-use models in reinforcement learning environments, running secure macOS sandboxes for agents, long-running instances that let an agent work across a user’s devices under one Apple ID, and build and test farms for Apple software.

There are two ways to use its solution. With managed compute, customers pick a machine class and image, and get either a full bare-metal Mac or an isolated macOS VM with administrator access, provisioned through a web portal, a command-line tool, Kubernetes, or the API, and billed per Mac on a 24-hour basis. With customer-managed compute, an organization runs its own Macs at a Mount Thor site using its own MDM, while Mount Thor operates the facility and provides inventory by serial number, problem reporting, and event notifications.

The argument is that agents are becoming macOS users, and the demand for Apple’s platform now scales with the number of agents rather than the number of people.

“Making Apple’s operating system and silicon available at datacenter-scale is a massive untapped opportunity in AI infrastructure,” said Peter Voell, Founder and CEO of Mount Thor. “Decades of investment in accessibility and human-computer interaction make macOS the best place for agents to work and for humans to hold them accountable. And with chips like the M5 Ultra, Apple silicon is becoming a high performance, more power- and cost- efficient platform for production inference.”

The other half of its pitch is inference. The M5 Ultra Mac Studio shipped in August with up to 512GB of unified memory, which puts large open-weight models within reach of a single machine at a fraction of the power draw of a traditional GPU-based server. Mount Thor says a focus of the new funding is building what it calls the best inference lab for open-source models on Apple silicon.

“Mount Thor sits at the intersection of two important shifts: the rapidly expanding capabilities of autonomous agents and the increasing demand for compute that can support both local and cloud workloads,” said Brittany Walker, General Partner at CRV. “We’re thrilled to back Peter and the team as they make it easier to use Apple’s platforms at scale for agentic AI.”

The team comes from Cerebras, CoreWeave, Fluidstack, Nebius, OpenAI, and xAI. The company was founded this year and deployed its first data center in under six months.

Macs in the cloud are not new as AWS has rented Mac instances for a few years, and MacStadium has been doing so longer than AWS. Mount Thor’s pitch is that the larger customer is an AI agent that needs a Mac to do its job, and that demand grows with the number of agents rather than the number of developers.

The company says the funding will go toward expanding its compute footprint and building out the team, and that it plans to add capacity quickly to keep up with customer demand.

article_content_zh:
苹果芯片上的人工智能代理令人难以置信，而且没有人在数据中心规模上租用它们。

关于 Apple @ Work：Bradley Chambers 从 2009 年到 2021 年负责管理企业 IT 网络。通过他在部署和管理防火墙、交换机、移动设备管理系统、企业级 Wi-Fi、数千台 Mac 和数千台 iPad 方面的经验，Bradley 将重点介绍 Apple IT 经理部署 Apple 设备、构建支持它们的网络、培训用户的方式、IT 管理一线的故事，以及 Apple 为 IT 部门改进其产品的方式。

CRV 和 Conviction 共同领投了 A 轮融资。Chad Byers 和 Offline Ventures 共同领投了种子轮融资。 CSC Leasing、Enea Capital、Long Journey Ventures 和 Upper90 参与其中，还有来自 OpenAI、Meta、Cognition、Together AI 和 Vercel 的天使投资者。该公司还为新硬件筹集了单独的非稀释性融资。

Mount Thor 在 Apple 芯片上运行 macOS 作为弹性计算实例，就像云提供商租用 Linux 虚拟机一样。客户可以按需获得一组 Mac 来完成仅在 macOS 上进行的工作：在强化学习环境中训练计算机使用模型、为代理运行安全的 macOS 沙箱、让代理在一个 Apple ID 下跨用户设备工作的长期运行实例，以及为 Apple 软件构建和测试场。

有两种方法可以使用其解决方案。通过托管计算，客户可以选择机器类别和映像，并获得完整的裸机 Mac 或具有管理员访问权限的独立 macOS 虚拟机，通过 Web 门户、命令行工具、Kubernetes 或 API 进行配置，并按 24 小时按 Mac 计费。通过客户管理的计算，组织可以使用自己的 MDM 在 Mount Thor 站点运行自己的 Mac，而 Mount Thor 则运营该设施并按序列号提供库存、问题报告和事件通知。

争论的焦点是，客服人员正在成为 macOS 用户，而对苹果平台的需求现在随着客服人员的数量而不是人数的增加而增加。

Mount Thor 创始人兼首席执行官 Peter Voell 表示：“在数据中心规模上提供苹果操作系统和芯片是人工智能基础设施领域一个尚未开发的巨大机遇。” “数十年在可访问性和人机交互方面的投资使 macOS 成为智能体工作和人类追究其责任的最佳场所。借助 M5 Ultra 等芯片，Apple 芯片正在成为一个高性能、更省电且更具成本效益的生产推理平台。”

它的另一半内容是推理。 M5 Ultra Mac Studio 于 8 月份发货，配备高达 512GB 的统一内存，这使得大型开放式重量模型可以在单台机器上运行，而功耗只是传统的基于 GPU 的服务器的一小部分。 Mount Thor 表示，新资金的重点是在苹果芯片上建立所谓的最佳开源模型推理实验室。

CRV 普通合伙人 Brittany Walker 表示：“Mount Thor 处于两个重要转变的交汇点：自主代理功能的快速扩展以及对支持本地和云工作负载的计算需求的不断增长。” “我们很高兴能够支持 Peter 和他的团队，因为他们让大规模使用 Apple 平台实现代理 AI 变得更加容易。”

该团队来自 Cerebras、CoreWeave、Fluidstack、Nebius、OpenAI 和 xAI。该公司成立于今年，并在不到六个月的时间内部署了第一个数据中心。

云中的 Mac 并不新鲜，因为 AWS 租用 Mac 实例已经有几年了，而且 MacStadium 这样做的时间比 AWS 还要长。 Mount Thor 的主张是，更大的客户是需要 Mac 来完成工作的 AI 代理，并且这种需求随着代理数量而不是开发人员数量的增长而增长。

该公司表示，这笔资金将用于扩大其计算范围和建设团队，并计划快速增加容量以满足客户需求。

title: Toronto-based Blue J, which provides AI-powered tax research software, raised a $176M Series E round led by JMI Equity at a $700M+ valuation (Alex Riehl/BetaKit)
title_en: Toronto-based Blue J, which provides AI-powered tax research software, raised a $176M Series E round led by JMI Equity at a $700M+ valuation (Alex Riehl/BetaKit)

inline_images.caption: A person working on a laptop holding a debit card.
inline_images.alt: A person working on a laptop holding a debit card.

author: BetaKit
article_content:
Toronto-based Blue J has raised a $176-million USD ($249-million CAD) Series E round after more than doubling its annual recurring revenue in just over a year.

The round, which Blue J announced on Tuesday morning, values the AI-powered tax research software provider at more than $700 million USD. US-based growth equity firm JMI Equity led the round, with existing investors Oak HC/FT, Sapphire Ventures, and Intrepid Growth Partners also participating.

Blue J CEO Ben Alarie told BetaKit in a Monday interview that the round featured a secondary capital component, buying out “long holders” and a small amount for long-term employees, but did not disclose how much of the round this included.

“I’m excited about building Canada’s next great tech company right here from Toronto.”

Founded in 2015 by Alarie, CTO Brett Janssen, Anthony Niblett, and Albert Yoon, Blue J aims to make the law more transparent and accessible for tax practitioners. Blue J claims its AI-powered platform can answer questions about federal, state, and local taxes in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom.

The company said the proceeds will help it scale its agentic AI for tax work feature, Workflows, as well as expand in the UK and internationally. While Blue J’s platform is versed in UK tax law, Alarie said the company still doesn’t have “boots on the ground” in the country.

“This will be about establishing a UK office and making a more concerted effort to take Blue J to market in the UK,” Alarie said, adding with a smirk that the office will be “probably big, in time.”

Alarie foresees the forthcoming upgrade to Blue J’s Workflows fundamentally changing his business. He wants Blue J to be able to produce hundreds of deliverables, from helping its accountant users draft a memo to responding to a notice of assessment from the Canada Revenue Agency. With these features, Blue J will move from an AI-powered tax research platform to a tax research and advisory platform.

“Our ambition is, by the end of next year, to have built out all of these workflow capabilities to effectively assist with just about any kind of work product that a tax professional routinely does in their practice,” Alarie said. “So it’s a big build.”

RELATED: Blue J raises $167.4-million CAD Series D after AI tax research platform more than doubles revenue

The Series E round comes just 15 months after Blue J raised a $122-million USD ($167.4-million CAD) Series D round, which was also on the heels of rapid growth, to expand its team, product, and market reach. While specific revenue figures weren’t disclosed (Alarie only said it’s in the “mid eight-figures”), Blue J claims its annual recurring revenue grew 165 percent since the Series D round, and that its revenue has grown 529 percent in the last three years. Blue J has added roughly 2,500 customers since the end of 2025, bringing it up to a total of 6,500 customers; growth that Alarie credits to Blue J’s effectiveness as a product.

“Tax technical stuff is really, really hard to research, and I can tell you this as somebody who’s been a tax professor for 22 years,” Alarie said. “It’s a painful problem to solve, and Blue J makes it, I like to think, rather delightful.”

As Alarie prepares Blue J to take flight, he said he’s excited to work with lead investor JMI, which has backed multiple scaling Canadian tech firms, including Clio, Safe Software, PointClickCare, Vena, and Jane.

“They’ve done a phenomenal job at helping companies like Blue J scale from where we are today to being much, much larger businesses,” Alarie said. “They really excel [at] helping people like me, a first-time founder, navigate as we scale this business to the next level.”

To support its growth, Blue J has doubled its head count over the past year, and expects to exceed 200 employees by year-end. While some of these may be in the UK or the US, Alarie expects the majority to be based in Blue J’s “center of gravity.”

“Our hearts are in Toronto,” Alarie said. “I’m excited about building Canada’s next great tech company right here from Toronto.”

title_zh: 多伦多AI税务研究平台Blue J获1.76亿美元E轮融资
summary_zh: 总部位于多伦多的Blue J完成1.76亿美元E轮融资，估值超7亿美元，资金将用于扩展代理人AI税务工作流及英国市场布局
article_content_zh:
总部位于多伦多的 Blue J 已在 E 轮融资中筹集了 1.76 亿美元（2.49 亿加元），其年度经常性收入在短短一年多的时间里就增加了一倍多。

Blue J 于周二上午宣布了这一轮融资，对这家人工智能税务研究软件提供商的估值超过 7 亿美元。美国成长型股权公司 JMI Equity 领投此轮融资，现有投资者 Oak HC/FT、Sapphire Ventures 和 Intrepid Growth Partners 也参与其中。

Blue J 首席执行官 Ben Alarie 在周一接受 BetaKit 采访时表示，本轮融资包含二级资本成分，即买断“长期持有者”股份和少量长期员工股份，但没有透露这轮融资的金额。

“我很高兴能够在多伦多建立加拿大下一家伟大的科技公司。”

Blue J 由 Alarie、首席技术官 Brett Janssen、Anthony Niblett 和 Albert Yoon 于 2015 年创立，旨在使法律对税务从业者来说更加透明和易于理解。 Blue J 声称其人工智能平台可以回答有关美国、加拿大和英国联邦、州和地方税收的问题。

该公司表示，所得收益将帮助其扩大其税务工作代理人工智能功能 Workflows 的规模，并在英国和国际范围内扩张。虽然 Blue J 的平台精通英国税法，但阿拉里表示，该公司在英国仍然没有“实地部署”。

阿拉里说：“这将是为了建立一个英国办事处，并更加一致地努力将 Blue J 推向英国市场。”他笑着补充说，这个办事处“迟早可能会变得很大”。

Alarie 预计 Blue J 工作流程即将升级，将从根本上改变他的业务。他希望 Blue J 能够生成数百份可交付成果，从帮助其会计师用户起草备忘录到回复加拿大税务局的评估通知。凭借这些功能，Blue J 将从人工智能驱动的税务研究平台转变为税务研究和咨询平台。

阿拉里说：“我们的目标是，到明年年底，建立所有这些工作流程功能，以有效协助税务专业人员在实践中日常执行的几乎任何类型的工作产品。” “所以这是一个很大的建筑。”

相关：人工智能税务研究平台收入增加一倍以上后，Blue J 筹集了 1.674 亿加元的 D 轮融资

距离 E 轮融资仅 15 个月前，Blue J 筹集了 1.22 亿美元（1.674 亿加元）的 D 轮融资，该轮融资也是在快速增长之后进行的，旨在扩大其团队、产品和市场覆盖范围。虽然具体收入数字没有披露（Alarie 仅表示在“八位数左右”），但 Blue J 声称自 D 轮融资以来其年度经常性收入增长了 165%，并且在过去三年中其收入增长了 529%。自 2025 年底以来，Blue J 已增加约 2,500 名客户，使其客户总数达到 6,500 名； Alarie 将这种增长归功于 Blue J 作为产品的有效性。

“税务技术问题真的非常难以研究，作为一个已经担任了 22 年税务教授的人，我可以告诉你这一点，”阿拉里说。 “这是一个很难解决的问题，但我认为 Blue J 让它变得相当令人愉快。”

当 Alarie 准备 Blue J 起飞时，他表示很高兴能与主要投资者 JMI 合作，JMI 已支持多家规模不断扩大的加拿大科技公司，包括 Clio、Safe Software、PointClickCare、Vena 和 Jane。

阿拉里说：“他们在帮助 Blue J 这样的公司从今天的规模发展成为规模更大的企业方面做得非常出色。” “他们非常擅长帮助像我这样的首次创始人，帮助我们将业务扩展至新的水平。”

title: SK Hynix Plans Chip Testing Hub to Boost Smaller Korean Players
title_en: SK Hynix Plans Chip Testing Hub to Boost Smaller Korean Players
author: Yoolim Lee
article_content:
By Kwanwoo Jun South Korean memory-chip giant SK Hynix plans to spend 1.4 trillion won, equivalent to $1.05 billion, over the next five years to support small local suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts and equipment, in order to strengthen the competitiveness of its supply chain.

As part of the plan, SK Hynix will open a semiconductor testing facility, jointly funded with about 875 billion won in investment, in May 2027 at its chip-making complex in Yongin, south of Seoul, the company said Monday. The facility now under construction, named Trinity Fab, is the result of a three-way partnership between SK Hynix, the central government and the Yongin municipal government, which have committed 443.2 billion won, 373.6 billion won and 57.7 billion won, respectively, the company said.

By sharing the facility, which will feature a large clean room and state-of-the-art testing equipment based on 12-inch wafers, domestic suppliers will be able to reduce the costs and time needed to bring their products to commercial production and market, it said. SK Hynix also plans to provide suppliers with technical and financial support, if needed, at the facility.

Write to Kwanwoo Jun at kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com (END) Dow Jones Newswires 11-15-26 2202ET

The initiative provides local material, component, and equipment suppliers with a 12-inch wafer testing environment, supported by a 2 trillion KRW (approx. $1.5 billion) guarantee program to lower entry barriers into the semiconductor supply chain.

title_zh: SK海力士斥资6.54亿美元共建芯片测试工厂
summary_zh: SK海力士与韩国政府合作建设Trinity Fab测试中心，通过提供12英寸晶圆测试环境助力本土半导体设备供应商提升竞争力
article_content_zh:
韩国存储芯片巨头 SK 海力士计划在未来五年内斥资 1.4 万亿韩元（约合 10.5 亿美元）支持本土小型半导体材料、零部件和设备供应商，以增强其供应链的竞争力。

SK 海力士周一表示，作为该计划的一部分，SK 海力士将于 2027 年 5 月在首尔南部龙仁市的芯片制造厂开设一家半导体测试设施，该设施由共同投资约 8750 亿韩元共同出资。该公司表示，目前正在建设的工厂名为 Trinity Fab，是 SK 海力士、中央政府和龙仁市政府三方合作的成果，三方分别投入了 4432 亿韩元、3736 亿韩元和 577 亿韩元。

据称，通过共享该设施，该设施将配备大型洁净室和基于12英寸晶圆的最先进的测试设备，国内供应商将能够减少将其产品推向商业生产和市场所需的成本和时间。 SK 海力士还计划根据需要在该工厂向供应商提供技术和财务支持。

写信给 Kwanwoo Jun，邮箱为 kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com （完）道琼斯通讯社 11-15-26 2202ET

title: SK hynix sets $1 billion chip-supplier support plan
title_en: SK hynix sets $1 billion chip-supplier support plan
author: Reuters
article_content:
SEOUL, Nov 16 (Reuters) - South Korea's SK Hynix said on Monday it plans to spend 1.4 trillion won ($1.05 billion) over the next five years to support domestic suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts and equipment, aiming to strengthen its supply chain as competition intensifies in the AI chip market.

The chipmaker also outlined plans for a jointly funded 874.6 billion won testing facility at its semiconductor complex in Yongin, south of Seoul, where smaller suppliers will be able to test products under conditions similar to those on commercial chip production lines.

Here are some details:

• SK Hynix said its supplier support programme covers four stages - research and development, testing, mass production and sales. It aims to help smaller companies overcome financing and technology hurdles.

• The testing facility, named Trinity Fab, is a partnership between SK Hynix, the central government and local governments. It is scheduled to open in May 2027. SK Hynix will contribute 443.2 billion won, the central government 373.6 billion won and local governments 57.7 billion won, according to the company.

• Trinity Fab will house around 50 semiconductor tools, including lithography and etching equipment, allowing suppliers to test materials and components on 12-inch wafers.

• To reduce financial risks for suppliers, SK Hynix said it will share development costs in advance and provide compensation if a joint project fails.

• An independent foundation will operate the test facility to protect the intellectual property of participating suppliers, the company said.

• The initiative also includes establishing an overseas marketing support centre to help domestic suppliers expand internationally and reduce reliance on imported chip components.

• SK Hynix and financial institutions will also provide 2 trillion won in financing backed by the Korea Trade Insurance Corporation, while other programmes offer low-interest loans and technical consulting to suppliers, including smaller subcontractors.

首尔，11月16日（路透社）- 韩国 SK海力士周一宣布，计划在未来五年内投入 1.4 万亿韩元（约合 10.5 亿美元），支持韩国本土半导体材料、零部件和设备供应商，旨在随着人工智能（AI）芯片市场竞争白热化，全面强化自身供应链韧性。

这家芯片制造商还公布了一项耗资 8746 亿韩元的测试中心联合投资规划，该设施位于首尔以南的龙仁半导体产业集群，将允许中小型供应商在与商业芯片生产线相似的实际工况下验证其产品性能。

以下为该扶持计划的核心细节：

• SK海力士表示，其供应商扶持方案涵盖研发、测试、量产和销售四个阶段，旨在帮助中小企业克服资金和技术门槛。

• 该测试中心被命名为“Trinity Fab”，由 SK海力士与韩国中央政府及地方政府共同联合出资建设，预计将于 2027 年 5 月正式投入运营。根据公司公布的数据，SK海力士出资 4432 亿韩元，中央政府出资 3736 亿韩元，地方政府出资 577 亿韩元。

• Trinity Fab 测试中心将部署约 50 台先进制程设备（包括光刻机和刻蚀机等关键机台），使供应商能够在 12 英寸（300毫米）标准硅片上完成材料和组件的工艺验证。

• 为了降低供应商的研发财务风险，SK海力士表示将提前垫付部分开发成本，并在联合研发项目未能成功时提供专项补偿。

• 公司表示，该测试设施将由一家独立非营利基金会负责日常运营，以严格保护参与供应商的核心知识产权与商业机密。

• 该倡议还包括设立海外营销支持中心，协助韩国本土供应商拓展国际市场，并逐步降低对海外进口半导体关键零部件的依赖度。

• SK海力士还将与金融机构合作，在韩国贸易保险公社的担保下提供 2 万亿韩元的融资支持，同时开展其他项目向供应链企业（包括小型分包商）提供低息贷款和技术咨询服务。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] The program is intended to strengthen the company’s supply chain amid intensifying competition in the market for artificial intelligence chips, Channel NewsAsia reports.

[Key Metrics] --> South Korean company SK Hynix plans to allocate 1.4 trillion won, or $1.05 billion, over the next five years to support domestic suppliers of materials, components and equipment for semiconductor production.

paragraphs: SEOUL, Nov 16 (Reuters) - South Korea's SK Hynix said on Monday it plans to spend 1.4 trillion won ($1.05 billion) over the next five years to support domestic suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts and equipment, aiming to strengthen its supply chain as competition intensifies in the AI chip market.

The chipmaker also outlined plans for a jointly funded 874.6 billion won testing facility at its semiconductor complex in Yongin, south of Seoul, where smaller suppliers will be able to test products under conditions similar to those on commercial chip production lines.
Here are some details:

• SK Hynix said its supplier support programme covers four stages - research and development, testing, mass production and sales. It aims to help smaller companies overcome financing and technology hurdles.

• The testing facility, named Trinity Fab, is a partnership between SK Hynix, the central government and local governments. It is scheduled to open in May 2027. SK Hynix will contribute 443.2 billion won, the central government 373.6 billion won and local governments 57.7 billion won, according to the company.
• Trinity Fab will house around 50 semiconductor tools, including lithography and etching equipment, allowing suppliers to test materials and components on 12-inch wafers.
• To reduce financial risks for suppliers, SK Hynix said it will share development costs in advance and provide compensation if a joint project fails.
• An independent foundation will operate the test facility to protect the intellectual property of participating suppliers, the company said.
• The initiative also includes establishing an overseas marketing support centre to help domestic suppliers expand internationally and reduce reliance on imported chip components.

• SK Hynix and financial institutions will also provide 2 trillion won in financing backed by the Korea Trade Insurance Corporation, while other programmes offer low-interest loans and technical consulting to suppliers, including smaller subcontractors.
