title: Sources: Jensen Huang has discussed a comeback as Nvidia CEO with confidants, as allies form a "war room" to lobby for his return and seek White House support (Financial Times)
title_en: Sources: Jensen Huang has discussed a comeback as Nvidia CEO with confidants, as allies form a "war room" to lobby for his return and seek White House support (Financial Times)
author: Financial Times
article_content:
Jensen Huang is considering a return as Nvidia's chief executive, days after he resigned over reports that he had affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate, the Financial Times reported Sunday.

Huang has discussed the possibility with confidants, according to the FT, which cited people familiar with the matter. One ally told the paper they were putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby Nvidia's board for his return and would try to win support from the White House. The ally said Huang backed the effort.

Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have backed a public letter calling on Nvidia's board to "Bring Jensen Back." On Friday, Nvidia shareholders Brad Gerstner of Altimeter Capital and Gavin Baker of Atreides Management urged the board in an open letter to keep "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang."

A spokesperson for Nvidia and a spokesperson for Huang declined to comment to the FT. Huang doesn't hold a controlling stake in Nvidia and can't overrule its board.

The push runs into opposition from Washington. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia and urged its board to look outside the company for a new CEO.

"I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?" Bessent said on Fox News, CNBC reported. He said he wants "answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel," according to Axios.

"If this were a bank and they hadn't complied like this, the OCC would be in there right now, and a lot of the executives would be removed," Bessent said. Nvidia has said it complies with U.S. export laws.

Bessent has also blamed the Commerce Department, led by Secretary Howard Lutnick, for not restricting Megaspeed, the Singapore-based firm at the center of the scandal. "Treasury, War, USTR and State, they were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the Entity List for months, but Commerce has the pen," Bessent told CNBC on Friday. Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10, CBS News reported.

Nvidia reports quarterly earnings Tuesday, its first since Huang's resignation. Interim CEO Colette Kress has scheduled a company-wide meeting for Wednesday, CNBC reported. The board said Friday it has not yet hired a search firm or "formally engaged any potential candidates" to replace Huang, according to CNBC. The FT reported Friday that the board had approached Arm CEO Rene Haas.

Huang resigned Thursday after revelations that he had extramarital affairs with multiple women, one of whom was an alleged Chinese spy. The company said in a statement that Kress, Nvidia's executive vice president and chief financial officer, will serve as interim CEO. Harvey C. Jones was appointed chair of the board.

Nvidia's stock plunged 13% at the market open Thursday. The company has lost more than $1.2 trillion in market value since the scandal broke in late October, Axios reported.

In its statement, the board thanked Huang for his "immeasurable contributions to the company." The chipmaker is at the center of the global AI economy and has multiple agreements with the U.S. government. Huang, who founded Nvidia in 1993, led the company through the AI boom that made it one of the world's most valuable publicly traded companies.

Last Sunday, Nvidia's board of directors said it was launching an investigation into Huang being the target of an alleged Chinese spy, with whom he had an affair.

Huang admitted to the affair in an email to Nvidia employees and said he is cooperating with the investigation. Reports have identified Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at tech firm Megaspeed, as the woman he had the relationship with.

"I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," Jensen Huang said in a statement.

The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, a married Nvidia executive who reported directly to him. Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, joined the company in 2008.

On Thursday, Reuters reported that Huang also had an "intimate relationship" with another Nvidia employee. Reuters did not identify the woman, and Nvidia declined to comment.

Rep. Brian Mast, the Republican chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told reporters Thursday that Huang had agreed to testify before Congress after being threatened with a subpoena. House Republicans have asked Huang to sit for a closed-door interview on Dec. 1, CNBC reported.

Here's what we know so far, and why the scandal matters.

Jensen Huang founded Nvidia, one of the biggest makers of specialized computer chips in the world. Its chips were first designed for computer graphics, but demand for Nvidia's hardware has skyrocketed with the AI boom of the past few years. China and the U.S. are in a heated competition for AI technology, and that includes access to chips like the ones Nvidia makes.

Huang is an American citizen who was born in Taiwan. He founded Nvidia in 1993 and served as its president and CEO until Thursday.

According to the New York Times, it's unclear when Jensen Huang met Alice Huang, but the two were photographed together in 2024 at a bar in Taipei, Taiwan. That was roughly when Megaspeed, the AI company she worked for, began its push into the AI sector. News reports have not confirmed whether Alice Huang still works at Megaspeed. Megaspeed has touted its membership in Nvidia's partnership program, which would give it access to Nvidia's latest technology.

Huang apologized for the affair in a message to Nvidia employees and asked for privacy for his family. "I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused," Huang wrote, "and I accept the criticism that comes with it."

He pledged to earn back his employees' confidence and said he was cooperating fully with the board's investigation. "I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security," he wrote.

The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was gathering information for the Chinese government. China denied that it was spying, calling the allegation unsubstantiated. "It is nothing but smears against China," a Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said.

The New York Times also reported that Nvidia executives contacted the U.S. Commerce Department last year seeking information about the department's investigation into Megaspeed. The investigation was later transferred to the Justice Department, which is reportedly looking into whether Megaspeed illegally routed Nvidia products into China.

AI is the biggest thing in tech right now, from chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude to software development and bioengineering. Governments are trying to work out how to use AI for security and across the economy, and China and the U.S. are racing to lead its development. The technology has moved so fast that some CEOs of AI companies have suggested a pause before it develops beyond what humans can control.

Nvidia has contracts with the U.S. government to use its technology in several areas, and Huang has a close relationship with President Trump. U.S. officials are trying to determine whether the affair allowed the Chinese government to obtain information about Nvidia's technology and its agreements with the U.S. government. Nvidia's board said in its statement that it does not believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

Trump said last Sunday that he considers Huang "a fine person" who should stay on as CEO of Nvidia.

"I think he probably has an excuse for it. We'll have to hear it," Trump told reporters. "He's done an amazing job for our country."

On Tuesday, the New York Times reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who is also national security adviser, told Trump in May that the U.S. believed Huang was involved with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Trump received the information aboard Air Force One en route to a summit in China, the Times reported. Huang went with the president on that trip.

The Times said it was not the first time Trump had been told about U.S. intelligence on the affair. But the president said this week he was not aware of Huang's affair when Huang joined him for the China summit.

title_zh: 黄仁勋寻求回归英伟达董事会遭遇华盛顿阻力
summary_zh: 英伟达前CEO黄仁勋正尝试在董事会与硅谷盟友支持下重返公司，但面临美国财政部长贝森特的公开抵制及合规调查
article_content_zh:
黄仁勋正在考虑重新担任英伟达首席执行官，几天前，黄仁勋因有报道称他与一名疑似中国间谍及其下属有染而辞职。

英国《金融时报》援引知情人士的话称，黄已经与心腹讨论了这种可能性。一位盟友告诉该报，他们正在组建一个由硅谷高管组成的“作战室”，游说英伟达董事会让他回归，并将努力赢得白宫的支持。这位盟友表示，黄对这一努力表示支持。

埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和 Epic Games 首席执行官蒂姆·斯威尼 (Tim Sweeney) 支持一封公开信，呼吁 Nvidia 董事会“让詹森回归”。周五，英伟达股东 Altimeter Capital 的 Brad Gerstner 和 Atreides Management 的 Gavin Baker 在一封公开信中敦促董事会保留“所有选项，包括黄仁勋的潜在回报”。

英伟达发言人和黄仁勋的发言人均拒绝向英国《金融时报》发表评论。黄仁勋并不持有英伟达的控股权，也不能否决其董事会。

这一推动遭到了华盛顿的反对。美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特 (Scott Bessent) 周日呼吁英伟达进行“重大改组”，并敦促其董事会在公司外部物色新首席执行官。

“我想继续回到英伟达的文化，他们是否通过这些看似非法的销售来增加收入和利润？”据 CNBC 报道，贝森特在福克斯新闻中说道。据 Axios 报道，他表示希望“在未来 10 天内得到董事会和外部顾问的答复”。

贝森特说：“如果这是一家银行，而他们没有遵守这样的规定，货币监理署现在就会介入其中，许多高管将被免职。”英伟达表示，它遵守美国出口法。

贝森特还指责由部长霍华德·卢特尼克领导的商务部没有限制处于丑闻中心的新加坡公司 Megaspeed。贝森特周五对 CNBC 表示：“财政部、战争部、美国贸易代表办公室和国务院几个月来都赞成将 Megaspeed 列入实体名单，但商务部有笔。”据哥伦比亚广播公司新闻报道，卢特尼克已同意于 12 月 10 日在参议院银行委员会作证。

英伟达周二公布了季度收益报告，这是黄仁勋辞职以来的第一份季度收益报告。据 CNBC 报道，临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯 (Colette Kress) 已安排在周三召开全公司范围的会议。据 CNBC 报道，董事会周五表示，尚未聘请猎头公司或“正式聘请任何潜在候选人”来接替黄。英国《金融时报》周五报道称，董事会已与 Arm 首席执行官雷内·哈斯 (Rene Haas) 接洽。

黄周四在被揭露与多名女性有婚外情后辞职，其中一名女性被指控为中国间谍。该公司在一份声明中表示，英伟达执行副总裁兼首席财务官克雷斯将担任临时首席执行官。哈维·琼斯 (Harvey C. Jones) 被任命为董事会主席。

周四开盘时，英伟达股价暴跌 13%。据 Axios 报道，自 10 月底丑闻爆发以来，该公司市值损失超过 1.2 万亿美元。

董事会在声明中感谢黄先生“对公司做出的不可估量的贡献”。这家芯片制造商处于全球人工智能经济的中心，并与美国政府签订了多项协议。黄仁勋于 1993 年创立了 Nvidia，带领该公司经历了人工智能热潮，使其成为世界上最有价值的上市公司之一。

上周日，英伟达董事会表示，正在对黄被一名涉嫌中国间谍的目标展开调查，黄与该间谍有染。

黄在给英伟达员工的电子邮件中承认了此事，并表示正在配合调查。有报道称，科技公司 Megaspeed 前高管 Alice Huang（无亲属关系）就是与他发生关系的女性。

article_content:
Unsurprisingly, following the scandal involving now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, Congress is looking to further restrict exports of AI chips. Both Democrats and Republicans have voiced support for various measures and bills that would tighten rules and have demanded that Huang and other Nvidia leaders testify before Congress.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has already said that Huang and the Trump administration need to answer to Congress. Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott has also sent letters to both Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick calling on them to publicly testify to the committee.

Bills such as the Remote Access Security Act, first introduced in the House in April 2025 but stalled in the Senate, are receiving renewed interest. While that specific bill might not become law, House Speaker Mike Johnson has said there is “growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China,” according to Reuters. Johnson has also said that he personally supports efforts to restrict China’s access to powerful AI chips from companies like Nvidia.

不出所料，在涉及英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋和一名涉嫌中国间谍的丑闻之后，国会正在寻求进一步限制人工智能芯片的出口。民主党和共和党都表示支持各种收紧规则的措施和法案，并要求黄仁勋和其他英伟达领导人在国会作证。

参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默已经表示，黄和特朗普政府需要向国会负责。参议院银行委员会主席蒂姆·斯科特也致函黄和商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克，呼吁他们公开向委员会作证。

《远程访问安全法案》等法案于 2025 年 4 月首次在众议院提出，但在参议院陷入停滞，如今又重新受到关注。据路透社报道，虽然这项具体法案可能不会成为法律，但众议院议长迈克·约翰逊表示，“国会在限制对中国的芯片出口方面达成了越来越多的共识”。约翰逊还表示，他个人支持限制中国获得英伟达等公司强大的人工智能芯片的努力。

NVIDIA (NVDA) picked up a new China headache on Friday, October 16, though not one that touches its guidance. Taiwan plans to add AI servers and advanced semiconductors to its export control list, and shipping them to China without a license would become a crime under the island's Foreign Trade Act, Bloomberg reported, citing an interview with Taiwan's economy minister.

Taiwan tied the move to commitments in this year's trade deal with Washington. No start date has been set.

Right now, an unlicensed AI chip shipment to China isn't a crime in Taiwan on its own. That gap showed up in August, when prosecutors indicted nine people over 74 Nvidia B300 servers that allegedly reached Chinese buyers. They had to rely on breach of trust and document forgery charges. Two people from Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ)'s Taiwan unit were among them (the company wasn't charged).

In the US, prosecutors charged Super Micro co-founder Wally Liaw in March over about $2.5 billion of Nvidia servers allegedly routed to China.

China (including Hong Kong) revenue fell from $5.53 billion in the January 2025 quarter to $2.77 billion by July 2025, about 6% of the total.

Singapore is the line worth a second look. It hit $10.16 billion in the July 2025 quarter, about 22% of revenue and up 151% in five quarters, while total revenue rose 79%. Those figures were based on customer billing addresses, though. Starting with the October 2025 quarter, Nvidia switched to customer headquarters and recast prior periods. That means Singapore's disappearance and the apparent 67% jump in US revenue compare two different bases. Like for like, China revenue fell 63% from a year earlier to $2.97 billion, while US revenue roughly doubled to $39.18 billion.

Today, Nvidia's outlook assumes no China data center compute revenue at all, and H200 sales to China were under 1% of data center revenue last quarter.

Nvidia stock trades at about 18x forward earnings, near the 17.5x low on TIKR's chart since late 2023 and about 41% below the 30x average.

That discount reflects more than China (this week's CoreWeave debt scare hit every AI name). Still, a law aimed at gray-market shipments doesn't ask investors to write off revenue Nvidia already left out of its guidance.

Super Micro faces the most visible compliance scrutiny, given the cases involving people tied to the company (it wasn't charged in either one, and neither was Nvidia, though prosecutors allege an Nvidia distribution manager in Taiwan cleared the sale). Revenue reached $39.06 billion over the last four quarters, up 78% from $21.98 billion the four before, so there's far more volume moving through its channel to police.

Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM:NYSE) already follows US rules on advanced chips, so its direct hit is compliance work. AMD (AMD:NASDAQ) gets covered too, since its top AI chips face the same US limits.

For Nvidia, Taiwan is closing a door the company's guidance already treats as shut. Once the rules take effect, unlicensed exporters will face criminal charges for the first time. That makes compliance at assemblers and distributors, Super Micro included, the thing to watch. Taiwan still hasn't set a start date.

summary_en: Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs plans to add AI servers and advanced semiconductors to its export control list, making unlicensed shipments to mainland China a criminal offense under the Foreign Trade Act. NVIDIA (NVDA) picked up a new China headache on Friday, October 16, though not one that touches its guidance. Taiwan plans to add AI servers and advanced semiconductors to its export control list, and shipping them to China without a license would become a crime under the island's Foreign Trade Act, Bloomberg reported, citing an interview with Taiwan's economy minister.

Taiwan tied the move to commitments in this year's trade deal with Washington. No start date has been set.

Right now, an unlicensed AI chip shipment to China isn't a crime in Taiwan on its own. That gap showed up in August, when prosecutors indicted nine people over 74 Nvidia B300 servers that allegedly reached Chinese buyers. They had to rely on breach of trust and document forgery charges. Two people from Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ)'s Taiwan unit were among them (the company wasn't charged).

In the US, prosecutors charged Super Micro co-founder Wally Liaw in March over about $2.5 billion of Nvidia servers allegedly routed to China.

China (including Hong Kong) revenue fell from $5.53 billion in the January 2025 quarter to $2.77 billion by July 2025, about 6% of the total.

Singapore is the line worth a second look. It hit $10.16 billion in the July 2025 quarter, about 22% of revenue and up 151% in five quarters, while total revenue rose 79%. Those figures were based on customer billing addresses, though. Starting with the October 2025 quarter, Nvidia switched to customer headquarters and recast prior periods. That means Singapore's disappearance and the apparent 67% jump in US revenue compare two different bases. Like for like, China revenue fell 63% from a year earlier to $2.97 billion, while US revenue roughly doubled to $39.18 billion.

Today, Nvidia's outlook assumes no China data center compute revenue at all, and H200 sales to China were under 1% of data center revenue last quarter.

Nvidia stock trades at about 18x forward earnings, near the 17.5x low on TIKR's chart since late 2023 and about 41% below the 30x average.

That discount reflects more than China (this week's CoreWeave debt scare hit every AI name). Still, a law aimed at gray-market shipments doesn't ask investors to write off revenue Nvidia already left out of its guidance.

Super Micro faces the most visible compliance scrutiny, given the cases involving people tied to the company (it wasn't charged in either one, and neither was Nvidia, though prosecutors allege an Nvidia distribution manager in Taiwan cleared the sale). Revenue reached $39.06 billion over the last four quarters, up 78% from $21.98 billion the four before, so there's far more volume moving through its channel to police.

Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM:NYSE) already follows US rules on advanced chips, so its direct hit is compliance work. AMD (AMD:NASDAQ) gets covered too, since its top AI chips face the same US limits.

For Nvidia, Taiwan is closing a door the company's guidance already treats as shut. Once the rules take effect, unlicensed exporters will face criminal charges for the first time. That makes compliance at assemblers and distributors, Super Micro included, the thing to watch. Taiwan still hasn't set a start date.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 台湾地区经济部宣布计划将AI服务器与先进制程半导体列入出口管制清单，凡未获授权擅自出口至中国大陆的行为将受《外贸法》刑罚制裁。此举旨在响应与华盛顿达成的双边贸易安全承诺，以弥补当前仅能依靠背信或伪造文书起诉此类走私行为的法律漏洞。

NVIDIA 和台湾新芯片法：真正的风险在于 Super Micro Gian Estrada 2026 年 10 月 16 日 3 分钟阅读 NVDA -3.12% SMCI -2.55% 交易披露 上述按钮链接至 Coinbase。雅虎财经不是经纪自营商或投资顾问，不提供证券或加密货币出售或促进交易。 Coinbase 会为通过此链接产生的某些活动向我们付费。显示的价格仅供参考。

10 月 16 日星期五，英伟达 (NVDA) 在中国遇到了新的难题，但并未触及其指引。彭博社援引台湾经济部长的采访报道称，台湾计划将人工智能服务器和先进半导体纳入其出口管制清单，根据该岛的《对外贸易法》，未经许可将其运往中国将构成犯罪。

台湾此举与今年与华盛顿的贸易协议中的承诺挂钩。尚未设定开始日期。

目前，在台湾，未经许可向中国大陆运送人工智能芯片本身并不构成犯罪。这一差距在 8 月份就显现出来了，当时检察官起诉了 74 台 Nvidia B300 服务器上的 9 人，这些服务器据称已到达中国买家手中。他们不得不依靠违反信任和伪造文件的指控。其中有两名来自超微电脑（SMCI：纳斯达克）台湾子公司的人员（该公司没有受到指控）。

在美国，检察官于 3 月份指控 Super Micro 联合​​创始人 Wally Liaw 涉嫌将价值约 25 亿美元的 Nvidia 服务器运往中国。

中国（包括香港）收入从2025年1月季度的55.3亿美元下降至2025年7月的27.7亿美元，约占总收入的6%。

新加坡是值得再看一眼的线路。 2025 年 7 月季度的营收达到 101.6 亿美元，约占收入的 22%，五个季度增长了 151%，而总收入增长了 79%。不过，这些数字是基于客户账单地址的。从 2025 年 10 月季度开始，英伟达转向客户总部并重新制定了前期数据。这意味着新加坡的消失和美国收入明显增长 67% 是两个不同的基础进行比较的。同样，中国的收入同比下降 63% 至 29.7 亿美元，而美国的收入大约翻了一番，达到 391.8 亿美元。

如今，Nvidia 的前景假设根本没有中国数据中心计算收入，并且上季度对中国的 H200 销售额不到数据中心收入的 1%。

Nvidia 股票的预期市盈率约为 18 倍，接近 TIKR 图表上自 2023 年底以来的 17.5 倍低点，比 30 倍平均水平低约 41%。

这一折扣反映的不仅仅是中国（本周的 CoreWeave 债务恐慌袭击了每个人工智能公司）。尽管如此，一项针对灰色市场出货量的法律并没有要求投资者冲销英伟达已经排除在其指导之外的收入。

考虑到这些案件涉及与该公司有关的人员，超微面临着最明显的合规审查（这两起案件中超微都没有受到指控，英伟达也没有受到指控，尽管检察官声称英伟达在台湾的分销经理批准了这笔交易）。过去四个季度的收入达到 390.6 亿美元，比前四个季度的 219.8 亿美元增长了 78%，因此通过其渠道流向警方的交易量要大得多。

台积电（TSM：NYSE）已经遵循美国对先进芯片的规定，因此其直接打击是合规工作。 AMD（AMD：纳斯达克）也受到了保护，因为其顶级人工智能芯片也面临着同样的美国限制。

对于英伟达来说，台湾正在关闭一扇门，该公司的指导方针已经将其视为关闭。一旦规则生效，无证出口商将首次面临刑事指控。这使得包括超微在内的组装商和分销商的合规性成为值得关注的事情。台湾尚未确定开始日期。

title: Sources: Howard Lutnick is expected to join Trump on Air Force One to China this week, after clashing with Scott Bessent and others over Nvidia chip curbs (Ashley Gold/Semafor)
title_en: Sources: Howard Lutnick is expected to join Trump on Air Force One to China this week, after clashing with Scott Bessent and others over Nvidia chip curbs (Ashley Gold/Semafor)

inline_images.caption: Jonathan Drake/Reuters
inline_images.alt: Jonathan Drake/Reuters

author: Semafor
article_content:
Howard Lutnick is expected to travel on Air Force One with the president to China this week as the commerce secretary fights to regain his footing after clashing with Trump officials over Nvidia and China chip controls, according to people familiar with the matter.

President Donald Trump is scheduled to arrive in China on Wednesday to meet with Chinaâs leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit.

Lutnick has become the target of Washington finger-pointing for slow-walking Commerce Department restrictions on certain AI chip exports to China, as well as his close relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week after admitting to an extramarital affair with an Nvidia customer suspected of being a Chinese spy, and media reports of two affairs with subordinates. The woman, Alice Huang, was an executive at Megaspeed, which the US is investigating for improper chip smuggling into China.

Republicans are accusing Lutnick of defying Trump â and warning his job could be on the line â after reports emerged that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other officials had pushed the commerce secretary to place the Nvidia customer, Megaspeed, on a blacklist of companies that pose national security concerns. Treasury âhas been pushing for this for monthsâ but Commerce âhas the pen,â Bessent told CNBC last week.

They have accused Lutnick of allowing the chipmaker to indirectly sell more advanced chips to China than previously known or allowed under US export control laws, through loopholes he has so far declined to close. Heâs also been criticized for giving Nvidia unfettered access to rule-making that would impact the entire industry.

The White House has said it âmaintains complete confidence in the secretary.â

Lutnick had been expected to attend Semaforâs Silicon Valley & The World convening this week alongside OpenAIâs Sam Altman, Amazonâs Andy Jassy, and hundreds of other CEOs, but will instead be with the president.

And while plans could still change, Lutnickâs inclusion in the trip signals that Trump wants to keep Lutnick around long enough to at least accompany the president to China for his visit with Xi.

âThis guy has nine lives,â a person close to the White House previously told Semafor. âHow many does he have left?â

Shelby Talcott and Eleanor Mueller contributed reporting.

article_content_zh:
霍华德·卢特尼克预计本周将与总统一起乘坐空军一号前往中国，这位商务部长在与特朗普官员就英伟达和中国芯片控制问题发生冲突后，正在努力重新站稳脚跟。

美国总统唐纳德·特朗普定于周三抵达中国，在亚太经合组织峰会期间会见中国领导人习近平和俄罗斯总统普京。

卢特尼克因商务部对某些对华人工智能芯片出口的限制行动缓慢，以及他与英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋的密切关系而成为华盛顿指责的目标。黄仁勋上周承认与一名涉嫌中国间谍的英伟达客户发生婚外情，并与媒体报道了他与下属的两起婚外情，黄仁勋上周辞职。这名女子名叫 Alice Huang，是 Megaspeed 的一名高管，美国正在调查该公司是否存在不当向中国走私芯片的情况。

在有报道称财政部长斯科特·贝森特和其他官员敦促商务部长将英伟达客户 Megaspeed 列入构成国家安全问题的公司黑名单后，共和党人指责卢特尼克藐视特朗普，并警告他的工作可能会受到威胁。贝森特上周对 CNBC 表示，财政部“几个月来一直在推动这一举措”，但商务部“有笔”。

他们指责卢特尼克允许这家芯片制造商间接向中国出售比之前已知或美国出口管制法允许的更先进的芯片，而他迄今为止拒绝堵塞这些漏洞。他还因允许英伟达不受限制地参与可能影响整个行业的规则制定而受到批评。

白宫表示“对国务卿保持完全信任”。

预计卢特尼克将与 OpenAI 的 Sam Altman、亚马逊的 Andy Jassy 以及其他数百名首席执行官一起参加本周举行的 Semafor 硅谷与世界会议，但他将与总统一起出席。

尽管计划仍可能发生变化，但卢特尼克参加此次行程表明，特朗普希望让卢特尼克留下足够长的时间，至少陪伴总统前往中国会见习近平。

“这家伙有九条命，”一位接近白宫的人士此前告诉 Semafor。 “他还剩多少？”

谢尔比·塔尔科特和埃莉诺·穆勒贡献了报道。

Apple's latest tech move is HomeView, a smart-home hub designed to bring a more personalized version of Siri into consumers' homes. The device highlights Apple's continued push to make its AI assistant more useful across its ecosystem — the same broader technology that drew scrutiny in a class-action lawsuit over delayed Siri AI capabilities for iPhones.

Plaintiffs alleged that Apple's marketing created expectations about AI features that weren't available when consumers purchased their phones. Apple agreed to pay $250 million to settle the class-action lawsuit, without admitting wrongdoing. The agreement is subject to judge approval.

Now, as Apple expands its AI ambitions to compete with Amazon's Echo Show and Google's Nest Hub, consumers face a familiar question: Should they pay for another Apple device with its major selling point being AI?

Here's what to know about the new AI-powered tech, the ongoing lawsuit and how to claim your share of the pending settlement before it's too late.

Apple HomeView, which will retail at $299, is a smart home-management device that features a seven-inch Liquid Retina display touchscreen, a built-in speaker and a camera that recognizes individual household members, allowing it to personalize the experience for up to six people. Users can make FaceTime calls, play music, view security camera feeds and control connected devices such as thermostats, lights and smart locks, according to Apple's announcement.

But HomeView's biggest selling point is its integration with Apple Intelligence, the company's AI platform that also powers newer Siri capabilities. Apple's upgraded Siri is designed to do more than respond to basic voice commands. The assistant is expected to understand personal context, provide more conversational responses and use information from apps to help users complete tasks.

For example, users can ask questions that require information from their personal schedules rather than relying solely on general internet knowledge. When paired with a compatible Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, HomeView can draw on information from apps such as iMessage and Calendar to deliver more personalized responses.

"Apple HomeView is designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user," Greg Joswiak, Apple's SVP of worldwide marketing, said in a statement. "It's powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone's information private and secure."

Apple HomeView, releasing on Nov. 13, leverages the same broader technology at the center of Apple's pending $250 million settlement.

While Apple denies all of the allegations made in the class-action lawsuit — customer claims centered on the company's 2024 unveiling of new AI-powered capabilities for Siri, including the ability to understand a user's personal context, recognize what's displayed on their screen and perform more actions across apps.

"Powered by Apple Intelligence, Siri becomes more deeply integrated into the system experience," the company wrote in a June 2024 press release introducing Apple Intelligence. "With richer language-understanding capabilities, Siri is more natural, more contextually relevant and more personal, with the ability to simplify and accelerate everyday tasks."

HomeView is not part of the aforementioned settlement. But the tech giant's broader push to develop Siri into a more capable, personalized AI assistant drives consumer interest in the device in the same way.

However, it's worth noting that to fully leverage HomeView, users will need to connect other Apple devices for a more personalized feel.

According to the court-filed motion for preliminary approval, filed on May 5, Apple's $250 million settlement agreement establishes a fund to compensate eligible U.S. consumers who have purchased an eligible device between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, for personal or business use rather than resale.

Eligible devices include the iPhone 16, iPhone 16e, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max, iPhone 15 Pro, and iPhone 15 Pro Max — of which there are approximately 37 million.

Consumers who submit valid claims by Dec. 21, 2026 may receive $25 per device, with payments potentially reaching $95 depending on the number of valid claims and other settlement costs, according to the official settlement website.

Some consumers may have received a settlement notice by email or in the mail containing a claim identification number and PIN. If you did not receive a notice, you can still file a claim by selecting, "I DO NOT have a Claim ID and PIN, but I would like to file a claim online" on the form.

summary_zh: 苹果正加速开发智能眼镜，计划在开发者大会上亮相，重点强化Siri AI与第三方iPhone应用的深度集成，预计于2027年年底前正式交付市场

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 苹果公司已启动智能眼镜研发计划，旨在通过WWDC发布该硬件，并设定2027年为商业出货节点。该项目核心战略在于构建开放生态，利用Siri AI作为中枢，实现第三方iPhone应用在空间计算环境下的无缝流转与深度集成。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Apple is accelerating the development of smart glasses, aiming for a debut at WWDC with a scheduled commercial release by the end of 2027. The core strategy hinges on leveraging Siri AI as the operational hub to enable seamless integration and execution of third-party iPhone applications within a spatial computing environment.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此举标志着苹果将AR/VR研发策略从Vision Pro的高端试水转向轻量化大众市场，试图绕过纯自研内容的产能陷阱。通过引入iPhone存量生态作为应用载体，苹果意在确立空间计算设备在AI Agent时代的交互标准，从而实现对底层算力调度的深度垄断。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This move signals a pivot from high-end headset testing to mass-market AR eyewear, strategically bypassing the self-developed content trap. By porting the existing iPhone ecosystem into a spatial interface, Apple aims to define the interaction standards for AI Agents, effectively monopolizing control over underlying spatial compute resources.

Apple 的最新技术举措是 HomeView，这是一个智能家居中心，旨在将更加个性化的 Siri 版本带入消费者的家中。该设备突显了苹果公司不断努力使其人工智能助手在整个生态系统中更加有用——同样的更广泛的技术在因 iPhone 延迟推出 Siri 人工智能功能而引发的集体诉讼中受到了密切关注。

现在，随着苹果扩大其人工智能野心，与亚马逊的 Echo Show 和谷歌的 Nest Hub 竞争，消费者面临着一个熟悉的问题：他们是否应该为另一款以人工智能为主要卖点的苹果设备付费？

以下是关于人工智能驱动的新技术、正在进行的诉讼以及如何在为时已晚之前索取待决和解中的份额的信息。

Apple HomeView 的零售价为 299 美元，是一款智能家庭管理设备，配备 7 英寸 Liquid Retina 显示屏触摸屏、内置扬声器和可识别家庭成员的摄像头，最多可为 6 人提供个性化体验。根据苹果公司的公告，用户可以进行 FaceTime 通话、播放音乐、查看安全摄像头信息以及控制恒温器、灯光和智能锁等连接设备。

但 HomeView 的最大卖点是它与 Apple Intelligence 的集成，Apple Intelligence 是该公司的人工智能平台，也支持更新的 Siri 功能。苹果升级后的 Siri 的设计目的不仅仅是响应基本的语音命令。助理预计能够了解个人背景，提供更多对话式响应，并使用应用程序中的信息来帮助用户完成任务。

例如，用户可以提出需要个人日程信息的问题，而不是仅仅依赖一般的互联网知识。当与支持 Apple Intelligence 的兼容 iPhone 或 iPad 配对时，HomeView 可以利用 iMessage 和日历等应用程序中的信息来提供更加个性化的响应。

苹果全球营销高级副总裁格雷格·乔斯维亚克 (Greg Joswiak) 在一份声明中表示：“Apple HomeView 的设计初衷是让家里的每个人都能共享，但每个用户都感觉完全个性化。” “它由以 Siri AI 为核心的 Apple Intelligence 提供支持，利用 iPhone 中的个人背景来帮助您找到所需内容并完成更多工作，同时保持每个人信息的私密性和安全性。”

Apple HomeView 于 11 月 13 日发布，在 Apple 悬而未决的 2.5 亿美元和解协议中利用了同样更广泛的技术。

尽管苹果否认了集体诉讼中提出的所有指控，但客户的索赔主要集中在该公司 2024 年推出的 Siri 人工智能新功能上，包括了解用户的个人背景、识别屏幕上显示的内容以及跨应用程序执行更多操作的能力。

该公司在 2024 年 6 月介绍 Apple Intelligence 的新闻稿中写道：“在 Apple Intelligence 的支持下，Siri 更加深入地融入了系统体验。” “凭借更丰富的语言理解能力，Siri 变得更自然、更符合情境、更个性化，能够简化和加速日常任务。”

HomeView 不属于上述和解的一部分。但这家科技巨头更广泛地推动将 Siri 开发为功能更强大、个性化的人工智能助手，这也同样激发了消费者对该设备的兴趣。

然而，值得注意的是，要充分利用 HomeView，用户将需要连接其他 Apple 设备以获得更个性化的感觉。

根据 5 月 5 日向法院提交的初步批准动议，苹果公司 2.5 亿美元的和解协议设立了一项基金，用于补偿在 2024 年 6 月 10 日至 2025 年 3 月 29 日期间购买了符合条件的设备用于个人或商业用途而不是转售的符合条件的美国消费者。

title: Investigation: Howard Lutnick pushed to narrow chip curbs affecting a client of his former firm Cantor Fitzgerald whose Malaysia data center may serve Tencent (New York Times)
title_en: Investigation: Howard Lutnick pushed to narrow chip curbs affecting a client of his former firm Cantor Fitzgerald whose Malaysia data center may serve Tencent (New York Times)

author: New York Times
article_content:
In Malaysia’s lush southern peninsula, a data center known as A201 is set to open next year, packed with hundreds of millions of dollars in Nvidia’s most advanced artificial intelligence servers.

The data center plans to supply this computing power to a Chinese tech giant. The setup is legal and profitable. It will also sidestep U.S. rules that ban sales of the most advanced A.I. chips directly to Chinese firms.

The company operating the data center is a client of Cantor Fitzgerald, the financial services firm formerly led by Howard Lutnick, the commerce secretary, who handed off leadership of it to his sons. Mr. Lutnick is now writing the rules that would have a substantial effect on the data center’s business.

Mr. Lutnick has been seen as a force slowing rules that would clamp down on the sale of Nvidia chips to data centers like A201, which sit outside China but provide A.I. computing power to Chinese firms.

The Trump administration, concerned about ceding the country’s advantage in A.I., bans the sale of cutting-edge chips to China. But it has been embroiled in an internal debate for much of the past two years over how far to go in limiting chip sales to data centers in Southeast Asia. On one side of the debate are China hawks, who see the data centers as a way for Beijing to do an end run around the chip sales ban. On the other are officials, most prominently Mr. Lutnick, who are pushing against going too far in limiting the ability of U.S. companies like Nvidia to sell their products in Asia.

Recently, Mr. Lutnick has been advocating a less stringent version of those controls under consideration, which could cut back on Nvidia’s business by giving the U.S. government more oversight of chip sales to international data centers. It is the latest example of Mr. Lutnick’s soft touch on chip regulation, which has prompted criticism from lawmakers and others in the administration.

Cantor Fitzgerald has had business dealings with several data center companies in Southeast Asia that cater to Chinese clients, and could be affected by the regulations Mr. Lutnick is drafting, a review by The New York Times has found.

Cantor Fitzgerald served as a designated sales agent for an equity offering of up to $1 billion this year by Bitdeer, the Singaporean firm that will operate data center A201, in addition to having other financial ties to various global data center businesses. The relationship between the two companies began as early as 2024, when Cantor Fitzgerald helped Bitdeer arrange a stock offering of up to $250 million.

Mr. Lutnick steered Cantor Fitzgerald for decades, before recusing himself when he joined the Trump administration last year. The Commerce Department says Mr. Lutnick has complied with all ethics agreements, and his former business is now run by his sons.

These dealings are just a tiny portion of Cantor’s business, which stretches from investment banking and trading to real estate. Other investment banks have similar partnerships, and there is no evidence that Cantor’s investments influenced Mr. Lutnick’s deliberations.

But the overlapping relationships are the latest indication of the potential conflicts that exist given Mr. Lutnick’s role in shaping rules around U.S. technology exports. And they demonstrate how the U.S. ban on selling chips directly to China has led to an explosion of data centers in Southeast Asia aimed at Chinese customers. It is now up to Mr. Lutnick to decide whether to tighten the rules in ways that would cut off this avenue.

In the administration, Mr. Lutnick has been seen as one of Nvidia’s strongest champions.

His department has been increasingly criticized in recent months for giving Nvidia unusual access to rule-making and investigations, and standing in the way of sanctions on Nvidia’s customers.

The issue has been thrust into the spotlight in recent weeks with the scandal over the Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s affair with a woman the U.S. government deemed to be a Chinese intelligence asset.

The woman, Alice Huang, had led Megaspeed, a firm that set up data centers in Southeast Asia to serve Chinese companies. The U.S. government is also investigating Megaspeed for illegally smuggling chips into China.

The United States in late 2022 started banning exports of Nvidia’s advanced chips directly to China, out of concern the chips could help Beijing crack American encryption and design new weapons.

The arrangement is viewed by many in Washington as a harmful loophole. While some argue that the sales help U.S. leadership in technology, many in the administration have argued for clamping down, and Congress is considering a bipartisan bill to do so.

In its final weeks, the Biden administration issued global rules to restrict the ability of Chinese companies to remotely access U.S. chips. But President Trump revoked those rules when he came into office, arguing that they stifled American business and innovation.

Trump officials said they would introduce a new rule to replace the Biden ones. But they have struggled to reconcile competing views in the administration about how aggressive the rules should be.

Mr. Lutnick has been described as delaying or deferring these technology controls at several points in the past year, arguing that they could affect companies like Nvidia, or U.S. trade relations with China and other countries.

People familiar with the discussions say the Commerce Department has pushed for a more scaled-back version of the rule. The department has proposed applying regulations to a handful of countries — Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Brazil, South Africa and Norway. Others in the administration have wanted global coverage.

The proposal was first reported by The Information.

The Commerce Department proposal would also apply only to future shipments of advanced chips, exempting data centers already filled with American technology. Companies would need to notify the government if Chinese customers use their data centers to train A.I. models. But they would not automatically need to obtain a license.

The Commerce Department had also argued for the rules to kick in when companies are using a larger amount of computing power, meaning fewer activities by Chinese companies would be regulated.

Chris McGuire, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations and a former Biden administration official, predicted that Chinese companies would find ways to sidestep the more narrow controls the Commerce Department is proposing.

“If you’re only restricting remote access to data centers in certain countries, then China will just rent from the data centers outside those countries,” he said.

Nvidia had been one of Cantor’s largest stock positions early last year, but last fall, the firm began steadily selling off shares. Cantor holds those shares on behalf of clients, not as part of its proprietary investment portfolio.

Still, Cantor Fitzgerald continued to help arrange billions of dollars of financing for industries ranging from data centers to cryptocurrency that depend on a steady supply of computing from Nvidia.

That includes Bitdeer, which is building out the Malaysian data center it expects to generate $1.7 billion in revenue over five years, according to a company statement.

That data center will likely serve Tencent, a Chinese internet giant that would be able to gain access to Nvidia’s most advanced A.I. servers, according to a person with knowledge of the arrangement. Bitdeer is part of Nvidia’s partner network, a program for companies that work closely with the chipmaker.

Bitdeer hosts a Chinese language website that lets customers rent A.I. chips and gain access to Chinese open source A.I. models through data centers in Malaysia, Canada and elsewhere. The Johor facility is one of five data centers the company plans to open in Malaysia in the coming years, according to filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Cantor holds a stake in Bitdeer through its investment in Tether, the crypto company. It is far from the only American financial heavyweight investing in overseas data centers. Bain Capital, Citadel and Blackstone have all poured money into A.I. computing clusters across the region.

Cantor has worked with other Nvidia partners globally, including IREN, an Australian cloud computing company, and Lancium, a Texas data center developer.

A Commerce Department spokeswoman said that Mr. Lutnick makes policy decisions based on the best interests of the United States. He does not discuss department matters with his sons, nor do they discuss Cantor Fitzgerald business with him, she added.

Cantor Fitzgerald declined to comment. Bitdeer did not reply to a request for comment.

Mr. Lutnick, as of October 2025, transferred his remaining ownership stake in Cantor to his family. Before that, he had been given what the White House had called a “limited waiver” that allowed him to participate in certain decisions that could have “a direct and predictable effect on Cantor Fitzgerald,” exempting him from a federal criminal law that would otherwise have required him to entirely recuse himself from these discussions.

Even after Mr. Lutnick finished transferring his ownership stake to his sons late last year, he still had to abide by an ethics rule prohibiting federal employees from using their public office for their private gain or the gain of friends and relatives.

The Times reported last year that Mr. Lutnick was promoting data center projects that worked with his family firms. Senator Elizabeth Warren, Democrat of Massachusetts, and two dozen other Democratic lawmakers called for an investigation.

Maggie Haberman and Eric Lipton contributed reporting.

title_zh: 美商务部长卢特尼克涉嫌利用职务推迟芯片出口监管
summary_zh: 美国商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克被指在职期间干预对华AI芯片出口限制，旨在维护其前东家Cantor Fitzgerald关联的数据中心客户利益
article_content_zh:
在马来西亚郁郁葱葱的南部半岛，一个名为 A201 的数据中心将于明年开业，其中配备了价值数亿美元的 Nvidia 最先进的人工智能服务器。

该数据中心计划向一家中国科技巨头提供这种计算能力。该设置是合法且有利可图的。它还将避开美国禁止销售最先进人工智能的规定。直接向中国企业提供芯片。

运营该数据中心的公司是 Cantor Fitzgerald 的客户，这家金融服务公司以前由商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克 (Howard Lutnick) 领导，后来他将其领导权移交给了他的儿子们。卢特尼克先生现在正在编写将对数据中心业务产生重大影响的规则。

卢特尼克被视为减缓规则的力量，这些规则将限制向 A201 等数据中心出售 Nvidia 芯片，这些数据中心位于中国境外，但提供人工智能服务。中国企业的计算能力。

特朗普政府担心失去美国在人工智能领域的优势，禁止向中国出售尖端芯片。但过去两年的大部分时间里，该公司一直陷入内部争论，争论的焦点是在多大程度上限制对东南亚数据中心的芯片销售。这场辩论的一方是对华鹰派，他们认为数据中心是北京绕过芯片销售禁令的一种方式。另一方是官员，其中最著名的是卢特尼克先生，他们反对过度限制英伟达等美国公司在亚洲销售产品的能力。

最近，卢特尼克一直主张在考虑中采取不太严格的控制措施，这可能会让美国政府对国际数据中心的芯片销售进行更多监督，从而削减英伟达的业务。这是卢特尼克在芯片监管方面软弱态度的最新例子，这引发了立法者和政府其他人的批评。

《纽约时报》的一篇评论发现，坎托·菲茨杰拉德与东南亚的几家为中国客户提供服务的数据中心公司有业务往来，可能会受到卢特尼克正在起草的法规的影响。

Cantor Fitzgerald 担任 Bitdeer 今年高达 10 亿美元股票发行的指定销售代理，Bitdeer 是一家新加坡公司，将运营数据中心 A201，此外还与多个全球数据中心业务有其他财务联系。两家公司之间的关系早在 2024 年就开始了，当时 Cantor Fitzgerald 帮助 Bitdeer 安排了高达 2.5 亿美元的股票发行。

卢特尼克领导了康托·菲茨杰拉德数十年，去年加入特朗普政府后，他自己回避了。美国商务部表示，卢特尼克先生遵守了所有道德协议，他以前的企业现在由他的儿子们经营。

这些交易只是坎托业务的一小部分，其业务范围从投资银行和贸易到房地产。其他投资银行也有类似的合作伙伴关系，没有证据表明坎托的投资影响了卢特尼克的审议。

但考虑到卢特尼克在制定美国技术出口规则方面的作用，这种重叠的关系是潜在冲突的最新迹象。它们还展示了美国禁止直接向中国出售芯片如何导致东南亚针对中国客户的数据中心激增。现在由卢特尼克决定是否以切断这一途径的方式收紧规则。

在政府中，卢特尼克被视为英伟达最强有力的支持者之一。

近几个月来，他的部门因给予英伟达不同寻常的规则制定和调查权限以及阻碍对英伟达客户的制裁而受到越来越多的批评。

最近几周，随着英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋与一名被美国政府视为中国情报人员的女性发生婚外情的丑闻，这个问题成为人们关注的焦点。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 卢特尼克的政策立场凸显了美国在芯片围堵策略中遭遇的内源性掣肘，即华尔街资本通过深度嵌入全球算力基础设施供应端，在合规监管与跨境盈利之间形成博弈。此举不仅挑战了出口管制的统一性，亦预示着美国针对东南亚算力中转站的管控逻辑将进入由资本利益驱动的行政阻滞周期。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Lutnick's stance exposes internal contradictions in U.S. chip containment strategies, where financial capital deeply embedded in global compute infrastructure exerts pressure on regulatory outcomes. This situation signals a period of administrative gridlock where the desire for rigid export controls is undermined by the cross-border revenue imperatives of the very entities navigating those regulations.

title: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 doesn't generate images, it paints them
title_en: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 doesn't generate images, it paints them

author: THE DECODER
article_content:
Anthropic's new language model Claude Fable 5.2 can create complex and even photorealistic paintings by using code to place hundreds of thousands of individual brushstrokes on a virtual canvas.

Current image models like Midjourney typically use diffusion, which gradually refines a noisy image into a clear result. Fable 5.2 takes a different approach by simulating the physical painting process, including bristle texture, how the paint goes on, and mistakes it then has to paint over.

Developer Jake Eaton showed on X what the approach can do. Eaton works at Anthropic, where he regularly contributes to research on language model values, safety mechanisms, and AI agent behavior.Ad

When he asked Fable 5.2 to create a painting as hard to distinguish from a photograph as possible, the model generated an image of a shopping cart in a parking garage using roughly 700,000 simulated brushstrokes.Ad

According to Eaton, Claude works without an external image model and without pre-rendered or traced source images. Each piece is a Python program of 1,000 to 2,000 lines that drives a simulated paint engine. The approach resembles agentic image editing, where language models pick tools and evaluate results.

Earlier attempts with the sibling model Opus 5.5 drew criticism for merely imitating existing art. Eaton responded by having Fable 5.2 develop its own artist personas with fictional backstories and consistent styles. The model needs several thousand brushstrokes per painting, and Eaton redirects them with comments.Ad

Anthropic engineer Michael Graczyk shared a chat log and video of an experiment in which he asked Fable 5.2 to paint a bird at sunrise. The model could only use code to simulate the physics of bristles, wet paint, and canvas texture. It had to output every brushstroke manually as its own coordinate line, with no way to undo strokes once placed. That's what sets this method apart from AI-generated videos, where models like Flux 3 generate image sequences and their temporal consistency directly.

The resulting 21-second video uses a counter to track how the painting takes shape from exactly 111 strokes on a blank canvas. For the first stroke, the model output the color code #30346a, a width of 90 pixels, and five slightly wobbling waypoints. Fable 5.2 said it added the roughly seven-pixel wobble on purpose because a human arm doesn't draw a perfectly straight line either.Ad

Between passes, the model looked at the canvas and reacted to its own mistakes like a real painter would. When the bird's back came out too thin and scraggly, the AI laid a bolder stroke over it, so the stray bristle marks along the edges now look like ruffled feathers.Ad

In a second, 280-stroke piece showing two people painting at dusk, a late lighting effect accidentally smeared paint tubes and a cup on the table. Claude repainted those objects after the fact. The model also had both figures paint with their outer hands so their inner shoulders could touch, just as the prompt requested.

Fable 5.2's ability to plan step by step and self-correct under physical constraints isn't limited to virtual canvases. According to Anthropic, the model is built for extremely demanding long-horizon technical tasks, as is Mythos 5.2, a version designed for verified security and biology researchers.

In internal tests, Fable 5.2 solved two open problems in black hole physics, designed three working electronic devices with circuit board manufacturer Diode, and used more than 1,000 sub-agents to program its own laptop operating system in eight days.

AI researcher Aris Zhu tested how the model performs with real robotic arms. He pitted Fable 5.2 against OpenAI's competing model GPT-6 Astra, with each using a physical robot arm to paint Van Gogh's "The Starry Night." Anthropic reports a score of 64.9 percent for Fable 5.2 on its internal RoboDojo Sim benchmark, compared with 29.8 percent for GPT-6 Astra.

Zhu's real-world comparison still shows limits in fine motor control. Astra painted faster, and so far only OpenAI's model has managed to stand a domino on end. It did so by slowly loosening its gripper to use gravity as a pivot point.

title_zh: Anthropic推出Claude Fable 5.2：重构代码绘图逻辑
summary_zh: Anthropic发布Claude Fable 5.2模型，通过执行数千行Python代码模拟物理笔触生成写实画作
article_content_zh:
Anthropic 的新语言模型 Claude Fable 5.2 可以通过使用代码在虚拟画布上放置数十万个单独的笔触来创建复杂甚至逼真的绘画。

当前的图像模型（例如 Midjourney）通常使用扩散，逐渐将噪声图像细化为清晰的结果。 《神鬼寓言 5.2》采用了不同的方法，通过模拟物理绘画过程，包括刷毛纹理、绘画如何进行以及必须重新绘画的错误。

开发人员 Jake Eaton 在 X 上展示了该方法的用途。 Eaton 在 Anthropic 工作，定期为语言模型值、安全机制和 AI 代理行为的研究做出贡献。

当他要求《神鬼寓言 5.2》创作一幅尽可能难以与照片区分的绘画时，模型使用大约 700,000 笔模拟笔触生成了停车场中购物车的图像。

根据伊顿的说法，克劳德的工作没有外部图像模型，也没有预渲染或跟踪源图像。每一部分都是一个由 1,000 到 2,000 行组成的 Python 程序，用于驱动模拟绘画引擎。该方法类似于代理图像编辑，其中语言模型选择工具并评估结果。

早期对兄弟型号 Opus 5.5 的尝试因仅仅模仿现有艺术而受到批评。伊顿的回应是让神鬼寓言 5.2 开发自己的艺术家角色，具有虚构的背景故事和一致的风格。该模型每幅画需要数千笔触，伊顿通过评论重定向它们。

人类工程师 Michael Graczyk 分享了一段聊天记录和一个实验视频，其中他要求《神鬼寓言 5.2》在日出时画一只鸟。该模型只能使用代码来模拟刷毛、湿油漆和画布纹理的物理特性。它必须手动将每个笔触输出为自己的坐标线，一旦放置就无法撤消笔触。这就是该方法与 AI 生成视频的区别所在，在 AI 生成视频中，Flux 3 等模型直接生成图像序列及其时间一致性。

由此产生的 21 秒视频使用计数器来跟踪这幅画是如何通过空白画布上的 111 笔画形成的。对于第一个笔画，模型输出颜色代码#30346a、宽度为 90 像素和五个稍微摆动的路点。 《神鬼寓言 5.2》表示，它故意添加了大约七像素的摆动，因为人的手臂也无法画出完美的直线。

在两次传递之间，模型会像真正的画家一样看着画布并对自己的错误做出反应。当鸟的背部变得太薄且参差不齐时，人工智能会在它上面进行更大胆的描边，因此边缘上的杂散鬃毛痕迹现在看起来像皱褶的羽毛。

在第二幅 280 笔的作品中，两个人在黄昏时作画，后期的灯光效果意外地弄脏了桌子上的油漆管和杯子。事后克劳德重新粉刷了这些物体。正如提示所要求的那样，模型还用外侧的手绘制两个人物，以便内侧的肩膀可以接触。

《神鬼寓言 5.2》在物理限制下逐步计划和自我修正的能力并不局限于虚拟画布。据 Anthropic 称，该模型是为极其苛刻的长期技术任务而构建的，Mythos 5.2 也是如此，该版本是为经过验证的安全和生物学研究人员设计的。

在内部测试中，Fable 5.2解决了黑洞物理中的两个悬而未决的问题，与电路板制造商Diode一起设计了三个工作电子设备，并使用1000多个子代理在八天内编程了自己的笔记本电脑操作系统。

人工智能研究员 Aris Zhu 测试了该模型在真实机械臂上的表现。他将《神鬼寓言 5.2》与 OpenAI 的竞争模型 GPT-6 Astra 进行比较，每个模型都使用物理机器人手臂来绘制梵高的《星夜》。 Anthropic 报告称，《神鬼寓言 5.2》在其内部 RoboDojo Sim 基准测试中的得分为 64.9%，而 GPT-6 Astra 的得分为 29.8%。

朱的现实世界比较仍然显示出精细运动控制的局限性。 Astra 的绘制速度更快，到目前为止，只有 OpenAI 的模型能够将多米诺骨牌竖立起来。它通过缓慢松开夹具以利用重力作为枢轴点来做到这一点。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Anthropic研发人员Jake Eaton披露了Claude Fable 5.2的新型绘图机制，该模型摒弃了传统扩散模型（Diffusion）的噪声去噪路径，转而通过生成1000至2000行的Python代码指令，驱动虚拟引擎模拟真实笔触、纹理及重叠覆盖过程。模型在创作过程中通过自主评估绘画反馈进行动态纠错，其生成的图像由数十万个坐标点定义的独立笔触构成，实现了对物理绘画流程的程序化模拟。

author: The Verge AI
article_content:
On October 29th, The New York Times reported that Nvidia co-founder and showman CEO Jensen Huang appeared to be the target of a Chinese spy plot. Any major tech CEO potentially being compromised by the Chinese government is concerning — especially Jensen Huang. “If you could draw the network diagram of the entire US AI ecosystem, Nvidia would be at the center of that,” Kyle Chan, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution’s John L. Thornton China Center, previously told The Verge. “If you could draw the diagram of the entire Nvidia ecosystem, a single man is standing at the heart of all of that.”

The Times reported that Jensen Huang had developed a “close relationship” with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. Alice Huang had been on the American government’s radar for some time, perhaps as early as 2024. Her company was investigated by the US Commerce Department over suspicions it was illegally smuggling Nvidia’s AI chips into China in violation of US government trade restrictions. Singapore authorities confiscated her passport back in June of 2025, eventually barring her from the country, after she reportedly gave “inaccurate information” to police. And perhaps more concerningly, some US officials believed she was passing information, possibly about Nvidia’s designs or the White House’s deliberations over trade restrictions, directly back to Beijing.

This made her relationship with Jensen Huang concerning for multiple reasons. Nvidia’s chips are considered crucial to America’s AI superiority and a matter of national security by the White House. The government has restricted the sale of Nvidia’s most advanced chips to China since the Biden administration. But Jensen Huang has routinely pushed to loosen those trade restrictions. Meanwhile, he had gotten quite cozy with President Trump, once even putting him on speakerphone on-stage at the All-In Summit.

Then last week, things escalated quickly.

On Friday, November 6th, the Times reported that Alice Huang was specifically recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia’s CEO. Though, there is some disagreement among US intelligence officials over the strength of evidence tying Alice Huang to Beijing. While the paper did not confirm it at the time, rumors suggested the “close relationship” between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang was romantic in nature.

On Sunday, November 8th, Jensen Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair, but did not name the Megaspeed exec and alleged Chinese spy specifically. Nvidia’s board announced that it was launching an investigation into its CEO shortly after.

Many believed that Jensen Huang would survive the scandal. His company’s importance to America’s booming AI industry and his crucial role at the company seemed to make him nearly untouchable. He was, after all, the only CEO the company had ever known with no clear and obvious succession plan in place, and he sat atop an unusual corporate structure with around 60 direct reports. (These numbers are slightly outdated, but according to the Harvard Business Review, 10 to 20 is far more common among Fortune 500 companies, and Tim Cook reportedly had 17 in 2015, which was deemed “a lot” by Business Insider.)

Then on Wednesday, November 11th, The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang had a second affair — this one with one of his direct reports, Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care. Whether that was the last straw or if they were afraid it would be merely the tip of the iceberg, the board was ready to push Jensen Huang out, according to reports circulating that evening. According to Bloomberg, he had accepted his fate Wednesday evening reportedly looking “broken and shattered” and telling people, “I’m a piece of shit.”

On Thursday, November 12th, Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO of Nvidia.

CFO Colette Kress was immediately named interim CEO, and acknowledged to employees that this has been an “extraordinarily difficult period.” Harvey Jones was also named the first board chair in the company’s history, already signaling there would be some changes to the corporate structure. In a memo to employees, Jones said the company would “search for a permanent successor looking at both internal and external candidates.”

But the destabilizing impact was immediate. Nvidia’s stock closed at an all-time high of $239.24 on October 6th. It closed at $162.85 on November 13th. It’s hard to overstate the importance of Nvidia to the US’s AI arms race with China, and the industry in general. The company has invested $99 billion in various AI labs, startups, and neo clouds. Plus has announced plans to mobilize over $500 billion in financing for building out AI data centers and other infrastructure.

Even before Jensen Huang had resigned, Nvidia was already facing a shareholder lawsuit claiming the company had deceived investors. Jensen Huang and the company’s spokespeople insisted that the relationship with Alice Huang and Megaspeed was “completely normal and not unusual.” Only days later, Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair that raised “national security concerns” without naming anyone specifically. According to Reuters, Jensen Huang misled several Nvidia leaders, “including general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld” about the nature of his relationship with Alice Huang.

Many in the AI industry and Silicon Valley jumped to Jensen Huang’s defense. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney called it a “sad day for NVIDIA, developers, America, and all humanity,” in a particularly hyperbolic post. Elon Musk said on X that it would “be an honor” to hire Jensen Huang. Many of Nvidia’s employees even voiced their support to “bring back THE boss,” on an internal post.

Some even speculated that Jensen Huang was the victim of a vast conspiracy, whether that was a coup by some faction within Nvidia, or perhaps the goal of China all along had simply been to chase him from the CEO chair.

By Thursday night, Reuters reported a third affair, this one also with an Nvidia employee, though no further information has emerged.

First and foremost for Nvidia, it must find a new CEO. It’s possible that Kress eventually ceases to be “interim” CEO, but other names, including Apple’s hardware chief Johny Srouji, have also been rumored. (Donald Trump believes they should hire Tim Cook, but to call that unlikely would be an understatement.)

It’s also possible that Nvidia will undergo a dramatic reorganization. Whoever takes over as CEO is unlikely to keep the 60 direct reports of Jensen Huang. With a first-ever board chair in Jones, it’s also possible that the board of directors will play a larger role in the company going forward.

The board’s investigation into Jensen Huang that began on November 8th is ongoing. The scandal is likely to drag on for some time. With the possibility that Jensen Huang will have to testify before Congress, the company may choose to be proactive about disclosing any additional information publicly.

The incoming Democratic majority is expected to come down harder on Silicon Valley than the current Republican Congress. While it’s unclear just how far the new House and Senate will go in trying to rein in the tech industry and its billionaire leaders, it’s possible it will try to make an example of Nvidia as an early act of strength. If Nvidia is found to have been turning a blind eye to companies like Megaspeed, which are suspected of funneling advanced chips to China, it could face civil or criminal penalties. And it seems increasingly likely that stricter trade restrictions will be implemented on Nvidia’s chips, which could increase tensions with China in an already costly trade war.

There is a possibility that Jensen Huang could face criminal charges. In May, he claimed that Nvidia had “zero percent” market share in China due to stringent export restrictions. But shortly after, Culper Research published a report claiming that in reality over 20 percent of the company’s 2026 compute revenue was from China, though that number has not been independently verified. The report cited “illegal GPU diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries” as the primary source of those revenues. Among the largest of those intermediaries, according to Culper Research, was Megaspeed, which Nvidia repeatedly vouched for to the US government.

If proof is established that the CEO was knowingly helping Megaspeed or any other companies to illegally divert restricted chips to China, he could face criminal charges. And, as The Verge’s Elizabeth Lopatto put it, “under a functioning legal system, [he] could actually go to jail.”

There is the chance that members of the current administration are also tied up in this scandal, as it’s unclear how much the White House knew and when.

Considering Nvidia’s sizable investments, borrowing to build data centers, and the importance of its hardware, there are tons of open questions about how this impacts not just the AI industry, but the American economy as a whole. Nvidia is essentially propping up a large part of the tech industry and, if money stops flowing out of its coffers, it could drag a lot of other companies down with it.

There are also open questions about how this impacts the American public’s perception of the AI industry. The new Democratic majority was elected in part by campaigning against AI companies and the explosion of data center buildout across the country. That one of its more prominent CEOs is now embroiled in a spying scandal and multiple extramarital affairs probably isn’t going to endear the industry to the public.

* Megaspeed is just one of multiple companies that Nvidia has been approved to sell chips with suspicious offices. The New York Times described New Matrix’s headquarters as “a hollow gray shell with wires dangling from the ceiling where lights should be.”

* Jensen Huang’s connections to Super Micro are also under scrutiny. Earlier this year, one of its founders, an employee, and a contractor for the company were indicted by the Justice Department for conspiring to violate American export controls and divert Nvidia chips to China.

* While a lot has changed, it’s still worth reading the Times’ first big report from October 29th that lays the groundwork for the eventual deluge of international intrigue and infidelity that ultimately led to Jensen Huang’s downfall.

* The New York Times paints a fascinating portrait of Alice Huang who now finds herself at the center of an international espionage scandal.

* The Decoder interview with Kyle Chan, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution’s John L. Thornton China Center, digs into what China hoped to get out of Jensen Huang.

article_content_zh:
10 月 29 日，《纽约时报》报道称，英伟达联合创始人兼 CEO 黄仁勋似乎成为中国间谍阴谋的目标。任何可能受到中国政府损害的主要科技公司首席执行官都值得担忧——尤其是黄仁勋。 “如果你能画出整个美国人工智能生态系统的网络图，那么英伟达将处于其中的中心，”布鲁金斯学会约翰·L·桑顿中国中心的外交政策研究员凯尔·陈 (Kyle Chan) 此前告诉 The Verge。 “如果你能画出整个 Nvidia 生态系统的图表，就会发现有一个人站在这一切的核心。”

据《泰晤士报》报道，黄仁勋与新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的高管 Alice Huang（无亲属关系）建立了“密切关系”。 Alice Huang 早在 2024 年就已经受到美国政府的关注。她的公司因涉嫌违反美国政府贸易限制，将 Nvidia 的人工智能芯片非法走私到中国而受到美国商务部的调查。据报道，在她向警方提供“不准确信息”后，新加坡当局于 2025 年 6 月没收了她的护照，最终禁止她入境。也许更令人担忧的是，一些美国官员认为她正在将信息直接传回北京，这些信息可能涉及英伟达的设计或白宫对贸易限制的审议。

这让她与黄仁勋的关系因多种原因而令人担忧。白宫认为英伟达的芯片对美国的人工智能优势至关重要，而且事关国家安全。自拜登政府以来，政府一直限制英伟达最先进的芯片向中国销售。但黄仁勋经常推动放松这些贸易限制。与此同时，他与特朗普总统关系非常融洽，甚至有一次在全押峰会的舞台上让他打开免提电话。

然后上周，事情迅速升级。

11 月 6 日星期五，《泰晤士报》报道称，爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 被中国国家安全部专门招募来监视英伟达首席执行官。不过，美国情报官员对于将爱丽丝·黄与北京联系起来的证据的强度存在一些分歧。虽然该报当时没有证实这一点，但有传言称黄仁勋和黄爱丽之间的“亲密关系”本质上是浪漫的。

11 月 8 日星期日，黄仁勋承认自己有婚外情，但没有具体点名 Megaspeed 高管和被指控的中国间谍。不久后，英伟达董事会宣布对其首席执行官展开调查。

许多人相信黄仁勋会在丑闻中幸存下来。他的公司对美国蓬勃发展的人工智能行业的重要性以及他在公司中的关键作用似乎使他几乎不可撼动。毕竟，他是公司有史以来唯一一位没有制定清晰明确的继任计划的首席执行官，而且他领导着一个不寻常的公司结构，有大约 60 名直接下属。 （这些数字有点过时，但根据《哈佛商业评论》，财富 500 强公司中 10 到 20 个的情况更为常见，据报道，蒂姆·库克在 2015 年有 17 个，《商业内幕》认为这个数字“很多”。）

然后在 11 月 11 日星期三，《纽约时报》报道称黄仁勋有第二段恋情——这一次是与他的直接下属之一、英伟达医疗保健副总裁金伯利·鲍威尔 (Kimberly Powell) 发生的。据当晚流传的报道称，无论这是最后一根稻草，还是担心这只是冰山一角，董事会已经准备好将黄仁勋赶下台。据彭博社报道，周三晚上，他接受了自己的命运，据报道，他看上去“心碎且破碎”，并告诉人们，“我是一坨屎”。

11 月 12 日星期四，英伟达宣布黄仁勋辞去英伟达首席执行官职务。

首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯立即被任命为临时首席执行官，并向员工承认这是一个“异常困难的时期”。哈维·琼斯还被任命为公司历史上第一位董事会主席，这已经表明公司结构将会发生一些变化。琼斯在给员工的一份备忘录中表示，公司将“同时考虑内部和外部候选人，寻找永久继任者”。

但破坏稳定的影响是立竿见影的。 10 月 6 日，英伟达股价收于 239.24 美元的历史新高。 11 月 13 日收盘价为 162.85 美元。英伟达对于美国与中国的人工智能军备竞赛以及整个行业的重要性怎么强调都不为过。该公司已向各种人工智能实验室、初创公司和 Neo 云投资了 990 亿美元。 Plus宣布计划筹集超过5000亿美元的资金用于建设人工智能数据中心和其他基础设施。

甚至在黄仁勋辞职之前，英伟达就已经面临股东诉讼，指控该公司欺骗投资者。黄仁勋和该公司发言人坚称，与 Alice Huang 和 Megaspeed 的关系“完全正常，并不罕见”。几天后，黄仁勋承认了引发“国家安全担忧”的婚外情，但没有具体点名任何人。据路透社报道，黄仁勋在他与黄仁勋关系的性质上误导了几位英伟达领导人，“包括总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特和首席营销官艾莉森·瓦贡菲尔德”。

人工智能行业和硅谷的许多人都站出来为黄仁勋辩护。 Epic Games 首席执行官 Tim Sweeney 在一篇特别夸张的帖子中称这是“对 NVIDIA、开发者、美国和全人类来说悲伤的一天”。埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 在 X 上表示，聘用黄仁勋将是“一种荣幸”。英伟达的许多员工甚至在内部帖子中表示支持“让老板回来”。

甚至有人猜测，黄仁勋是一个巨大阴谋的受害者，无论是英伟达内部某个派系的政变，还是中国一直以来的目标只是将他赶下CEO宝座。

title: Inside the first AI Music Awards in Los Angeles, featuring AI announcers, lip-syncing, and human stand-ins, as the ceremony was mired in technical issues (Corbin Bolies/Variety)
title_en: Inside the first AI Music Awards in Los Angeles, featuring AI announcers, lip-syncing, and human stand-ins, as the ceremony was mired in technical issues (Corbin Bolies/Variety)

inline_images.caption: The Sonic Intelligence Academy
inline_images.alt: The Sonic Intelligence Academy

author: Variety
article_content:
I knew things were a little off when the first thing I heard on my walk to the AI Music Awards was “the winner…” followed by the sweet voice of Kelly Clarkson.

To qualify for the awards, artists needed to register their tracks to SIQA’s “Verified Registry,” which denotes whether the song was fully AI-generated, made with the assistance of AI or featured a cloned human voice to lead the tune (what the group calls a “human + AI hybrid”).

Registered artists then nominate their peers in the 25 categories up for consideration — everything from “AI Song of the Year” to “Best AI Pop Song” to “Best AI Comedic Song” — and then vote on the winners. One of those nominees was Xania Monet, the AI persona of Telisha “Nikki” Jones, who a day earlier won the AI Album of the Year category at SIQA’s inaugural summit and who would eventually go on to win both artist and song of the year, three out of four of the awards’ top categories. (The fourth, producer of the year, went to “DJ Shawn Q.”)

The Sonic Intelligence Academy is the brainchild of software engineer Timirah “TJ” James and her sister Mia James. Since its January launch, it has worked to establish an awards program to counter the mainstream music industry’s aversion to AI. The group believes there needs to be infrastructure that supports those using AI to create music, rather than dismissing its existence, and it hopes to be an AI counterpart to the longstanding Recording Academy that governs the Grammy Awards. It advocates for artists to publicly associate themselves with their AI-powered work, eager to highlight the humans who helped create the product.

It’s a noble, if surprising, decision to embrace its role as counterculture when AI artists continue to pursue a Billboard charting position. Some of its methods are a little overt, perhaps intentionally: After some in the industry spurned the idea of AI-generated music charting on Billboard’s industry-standard charts, the group used a week in January ahead of the Grammys to launch its own charts exclusively for AI music. The Mayan is a 12-minute walk from the Crypto.com Arena, the Grammys’ longtime home.

The moves are not subtle, but subtlety is not the organization’s goal. The group and awards’ existence alone reflects those in the AI music space trying to move past the thorny legal questions surrounding AI music, which have led to lawsuits by artists and record labels against generators like Suno and Udio over copyright infringement, and into a realm of relevance within the genres they’re trying to embody.

It is, in a word, new, and new things mean kinks to work out.

The first kink I noticed was when, as I arrived 30 minutes before the red carpet was set to begin, the doors to the venue were locked. I had to pull on each door before someone opened one, which led me to the check-in stand (bypassing any form of security, which didn’t seem to exist). I entered the foyer and arrived at the makeshift red carpet, where about 12, mostly independent media ventures set up cameras to interview the various nominees, presenters, and VIPs who’d grace the roughly 7-foot-long red carpet in front of one of the two step-and-repeat backdrops. A spokesperson told me 29 media outlets had signed up to cover the event, but that some couldn’t make it because of the sudden flight ground-stop issued by the Federal Aviation Administration around 12:30 p.m. PT. Whether human or AI, aviation afflictions come for us all.

The guests gracing the red carpet were not screens rolled out displaying AI avatars, contrary to a reasonable assumption. Instead, the human creators behind the digital faces strutted the carpet in their Sunday best, treating the night less as music’s biggest night and more as the biggest night for their music. Sequined dresses and colorful blazers strolled through, stopping to speak with outlets like Reuters to the fiery red mohawk-sporting, sequin-wearing host of “The Iconic Punk Oz” Oz Powers to, tucked against a wall and steps from the red carpet, an effective AI red carpet correspondent housed inside a tall, white faux-stone vessel. The contraption was developed by the event’s top sponsor, Deepgram, an AI startup specializing in text-to-speech agents.

The device, which knew the artists and pressed them about the event, struck in me a slight fear about whether people might opt for robot reporters instead of humans, though that fear subsided when I realized this device could not appear on the red carpet because it could not move. The creators seemed more eager to speak to the physical reporters anyway, with some of them emphasizing the human elements of their AI work. Fredro Starr, one half of the rap group Onyx, spent much of the carpet touting the human vocals that made up his AI-beat-laden record “It All Started in Brooklyn,” which he claimed was the first AI album on vinyl.

“You can’t replace [humans],” Starr told me, using the carpet to debut his new moniker, “Mad AI.” “The feeling that you get was what we bring with the spirit of hip-hop. So vocally, you can hear that, but the AI just took it to another level.”

Inside the theater, SIQA tried to bring a party-like feel to the function. A bar at the back of the venue —at a charge — kept well drinks flowing, and the bar top was littered with copies of a sponsored version of the newspaper “Rolling Out” featuring interviews with many of the nominees and James, the SIQA founder. One of those featured, Xania Monet founder Jones, sparked a wave of controversy last year when some of her Monet songs hit some of Billboard’s genre charts, leading to an interview with CBS’s Gayle King and to Kehlani slamming a $3 million record deal Jones received. As she waited for a drink by the bar ahead of the event’s start, Jones told me she wasn’t worried about the AI of it all overshadowing the pursuit of legitimacy within the greater music industry.

“AI is just a tool,” she said. “It just emphasizes what we do. I just feel like we should all be one.”

But despite that lofty goal, the kinks kept rearing their heads.

The event started about 30 minutes past its 6:15 p.m. start time, skipping a planned opening video montage for a dance break performed and choreographed by actor Giovanni Wilson with eight dancers to a seemingly AI-produced song that described — in literal terms — how we were at the inaugural AI music awards. The delay forced the show to skip introducing the nominees for the first half of the awards and instead have presenters just state the winner, robbing some attendees of hearing their names called for what felt like one of their biggest achievements.

The event was hosted by Wilson and podcast host Lana Hout, one half of the podcasting duo the “AI Chicks,” with a three-member house band of real people playing guitar, bass, keys and drums, soundtracking much of the night. The two hosts shared the only two microphones apparently available throughout the night, with a teleprompter loaded with the Claude-generated run-of-show, but they often seemed lost about what category, presenter, performance or commercial break was next.

At one point, Hout and Wilson were confused over whether they would cut to commercial or bring out the two presenters for best AI country artist. They then brought out the two country award presenters, only for Hout to walk back out mid-introduction to interrupt and say that, actually, they would go to commercial break. The award was eventually presented 13 minutes later with a different presenter.

Oftentimes, the use of AI seemed to hover over some of the technical hiccups. Deepgram was meant to power an AI voice that introduced the night’s presenters and nominees, but it often didn’t work and, when it did, talked over many of the presenters. Deepgram also had a commercial that played throughout the evening, but it would sometimes play at random moments even when a commercial break wasn’t called. The Deepgram team sat on the couch to my left, and when I looked over to see their reaction to the madness, one member had her head in her hands.

Early in the night, Wilson tried to introduce a trailer for his latest acting gig, the Terrance Howard-led film “A Good Hand Wasted” that he said used AI to help finish the project, but none of Wilson’s cues seemed to get it to play. Once it finally did, the screen only played a portion of the trailer before Howard’s face even appeared.

“So, ugh,” he said, before raising his hand to summon the audience’s applause.

The teleprompter was not much help, often shifting rapidly as presenters were speaking. The chaos led Wilson, who spent much of the night trying to maintain some decorum throughout the frustration, to joke they were “dealing with a prompter that has Tourette’s.”

Some of the greatest energy came from the evening’s nearly 10 performances, all of which made the cut despite the event running nearly 40 minutes behind schedule the entire night.

There had been some speculation over how, exactly, songs produced with AI and presented by AI avatars would play on stage. It turns out, through the power of lip-syncing and acting. Some acts, like country artist Ava Bentley and R&B artist EJ Rogers, lip-synced their entire performance, while others relied on hired performers who did even that for them. For “Chaisen Hale,” a project that features a video of an AI-generated boy with AI-generated vocals, a human lookalike singer named John Victor, 14, was brought out to lip-sync to the track. Attendees — including one duo, for some reason, dressed as Frankenstein and his bride — were generally riveted.

Nearly all of the performances were backed by the live band and dancers, who were provided to the artists for free by SIQA. Many who produce music with AI say they did so because they could not afford the studio musicians and resources required to bring their tracks to life, which made the reliance on the house band feel more like an opportunity to live out their dreams without the cost often paid by traditional artists who hire such musicians to produce their work.

Some of the only actual live vocals came from a rapper named GodFellow and Grammy-winning singers Eric Bellinger and Candace Wakefield, the latter of whom made a point to note the “hiccups” throughout the night and that she was singing live as she performed a song by AI artist “Aria Blue.” The performances captured much of what remained in the crowd, which grew smaller and smaller as the night progressed.

James, the SIQA founder, acknowledged the “technical difficulties” ahead of presenting Jones with her awards, but she promised those would be resolved ahead of next year’s ceremony.

“Because there will be a next year because this is the new music industry,” she told the crowd around 9:45 p.m., just as it was hitting its hard end time. ”SIQA has created the infrastructure for that industry and for all the artists coming up in that industry.”

And for many of the people in the room, that’s all they wanted. One artist, Sheena Taylor, accepted her award for best AI gospel song for a track called “I Denounce You, Satan,” by acknowledging the intense traumas she endured that led to a religious discovery. Another artist named Ramona Höffel, a 56-year-old woman who spends her days helping disabled people, flew in from Switzerland to represent her AI persona “Vireya” on her first-ever red carpet. (When I addressed her by her given name, she snapped at me.)

“I have a lot of ideas and wishes, and for a long time I paint, then I write, and that’s not enough,” she said, visibly nervous to be the first person to walk the red carpet. “The music gives me room to all this bring outside of my brain.”

I thought about Höffel’s words as I left the venue just after 10 p.m., well past the event’s scheduled 9:30 end, and into the downtown rain. To my right was a line forming to get into the venue for “Club 2010s” night, now delayed due to the prolonged awards show. It’s unclear whether AI music will generate an enduring monoculture in the way the music from the 2010s has, particularly as the larger music industry has mostly ostracized it. But it’s left people like Höffel feeling stronger, which is all someone like 2011 chart-topper Kelly Clarkson could ask for.

article_content_zh:
当我在走向人工智能音乐奖的路上听到的第一句话是“获胜者……”，然后是凯莉·克拉克森甜美的声音时，我知道事情有点不对劲。

为了获得奖项资格，艺术家需要将他们的曲目注册到 SIQA 的“验证注册表”，这表明歌曲是否完全由人工智能生成、在人工智能的帮助下制作，或者以克隆人的声音来主导曲调（该组织称之为“人类 + 人工智能混合体”）。

然后，注册艺术家在 25 个类别中提名他们的同行以供考虑——从“年度人工智能歌曲”到“最佳人工智能流行歌曲”再到“最佳人工智能喜剧歌曲”——然后投票选出获胜者。其中一位提名者是 Xania Monet，她是 Telisha “Nikki” Jones 的人工智能角色，一天前，她在 SIQA 首届峰会上赢得了年度人工智能专辑类别，并最终赢得了年度艺术家和年度歌曲，这是该奖项四个顶级类别中的三项。 （第四位，年度制作人，颁给了“DJ Shawn Q”。）

声波智能学院是软件工程师蒂米拉·“TJ”·詹姆斯和她的妹妹米娅·詹姆斯的创意。自一月份推出以来，它一直致力于建立一个奖项计划，以应对主流音乐行业对人工智能的厌恶。该组织认为，需要有基础设施来支持那些使用人工智能创作音乐的人，而不是忽视它的存在，并且它希望成为管理格莱美奖的长期录音学院的人工智能对手。它提倡艺术家公开将自己与人工智能驱动的作品联系起来，渴望突出帮助创造该产品的人类。

当人工智能艺术家继续追求广告牌排行榜的位置时，接受其反主流文化的角色是一个崇高但令人惊讶的决定。它的一些方法有点公开，也许是故意的：在一些业内人士拒绝在公告牌行业标准排行榜上人工智能生成音乐排行榜的想法之后，该组织利用一月份格莱美颁奖典礼前一周的时间推出了自己的专门针对人工智能音乐的排行榜。 Mayan酒店距离格莱美奖的长期所在地Crypto.com Arena体育场有12分钟步行路程。

这些举动并不微妙，但微妙并不是该组织的目标。该团体和奖项的存在本身就反映了人工智能音乐领域的人们试图摆脱围绕人工智能音乐的棘手法律问题，这些问题导致艺术家和唱片公司因侵犯版权而对 Suno 和 Udio 等生成器提起诉讼，并进入他们试图体现的流派的相关领域。

简而言之，新事物意味着需要解决的问题。

我注意到的第一个问题是，当我在红地毯开始前 30 分钟到达时，会场的门被锁上了。在有人打开一扇门之前，我必须拉上每一扇门，这将我带到办理登机手续的柜台（绕过任何形式的安检，而安检似乎并不存在）。我走进门厅，来到临时红地毯上，大约 12 家主要是独立的媒体企业架起了摄像机，采访各个提名者、主持人和贵宾，他们在两个步进重复背景之一前为大约 7 英尺长的红地毯增光添彩。一位发言人告诉我，已有 29 家媒体报名报道此次活动，但由于美国联邦航空管理局在中午 12 点 30 分左右突然发布航班地面停止令，一些媒体未能参加。 PT。无论是人类还是人工智能，航空苦难都会降临到我们所有人身上。

与合理的假设相反，走上红地毯的客人并不是显示人工智能头像的屏幕。相反，数字面孔背后的人类创造者以他们周日最好的姿态在地毯上昂首阔步，将这个夜晚视为音乐最盛大的夜晚，而更多地将其视为他们音乐最盛大的夜晚。亮片连衣裙和色彩缤纷的西装外套漫步其中，停下来与路透社等媒体交谈，与《标志性朋克绿野仙踪》中火红的莫霍克发型、穿着亮片的主持人奥兹·鲍尔斯 (Oz Powers) 交谈，他靠在墙边，距离红地毯几步之遥，是一位高效的人工智能红毯记者，住在一个高大的白色人造石容器内。该装置是由该活动的顶级赞助商 Deepgram 开发的，Deepgram 是一家专门从事文本转语音代理的人工智能初创公司。

这个设备认识艺术家，并向他们询问有关这一事件的信息，这让我有点担心人们是否会选择机器人记者而不是人类，尽管当我意识到这个设备因为无法移动而不能出现在红地毯上时，这种恐惧就消退了。无论如何，创作者似乎更渴望与现场记者交谈，其中一些人强调了人工智能工作中的人为因素。说唱乐队 Onyx 的成员弗雷德罗·斯塔尔 (Fredro Starr) 在地毯上花了很多时间来宣传人类的声音，这些声音构成了他的人工智能节拍唱片《一切都始于布鲁克林》，他声称这是第一张人工智能黑胶唱片专辑。

“你无法取代（人类），”斯塔尔告诉我，他在地毯上首次展示了他的新绰号“疯狂人工智能”。 “你得到的感觉就是我们用嘻哈精神带来的。所以从声音上来说，你可以听到，但人工智能只是将它提升到了另一个水平。”

在剧院内，SIQA 试图为活动带来一种派对般的感觉。会场后面的一个收费酒吧让饮料畅通无阻，酒吧顶部散落着赞助版的《Rolling Out》报纸，其中采访了许多提名者和 SIQA 创始人詹姆斯。其中一位特色人物是 Xania Monet 创始人琼斯，去年她的一些莫奈歌曲登上了 Billboard 的一些流派排行榜，引发了一场争议，导致哥伦比亚广播公司盖尔·金 (Gayle King) 接受采访，凯拉尼 (Kehlani) 猛烈抨击了琼斯收到的 300 万美元唱片合约。活动开始前，当她在酒吧等待喝一杯时，琼斯告诉我，她并不担心人工智能会掩盖整个音乐行业对合法性的追求。

“人工智能只是一个工具，”她说。 “它只是强调我们所做的事情。我只是觉得我们都应该成为一体。”

尽管目标如此崇高，但那些怪癖却不断抬头。
