article_content:
YouTube Music is my music-streaming service of choice. And since I’m a software reporter, I always enable the beta features available through YouTube Labs, which include Beyond the Beat. YouTube’s AI DJ randomly interjects for about 30 seconds between songs, teeing up the vibe shift and providing context about the next track.

More listeners are encountering synthetic commentary built into their music streaming apps. While YouTube launched this experimental AI DJ in 2025, Spotify first introduced a similar tool back in 2023. It doubled down on its AI DJ efforts in November, expanding the different personalities available to users and adding more controls over the commentary.

These AI DJs aren’t just annoying. Their attempts to provide helpful context and mimic human candor ultimately fall flat. Lucky for me, both features are optional and avoidable.

After months of leaving it enabled, a bad experience with Beyond the Beat this week pushed me to swear off AI DJs altogether. I was listening to a pop divas playlist as part of my morning workout and got slapped with 30 seconds of exposition after a Slayyyter track:

“Hey Boy delivers that high-energy surge perfectly, but we're shifting our focus to a sharper, more visceral reality. In Rock Music, Charli XXC [sic] weaves in a biting, dark sense of humor regarding the physical toll of her relentless 2024 and 2025 touring. She turns the genuine nerve damage she sustained on the road into a strange sort of battle scar, reclaiming the exhaustion of a weary party girl as a badge of honor. It's an unflinching look at the cost behind the spectacle, where the grind of the industry becomes the actual subject matter. Here is Rock Music by Charli XXC [sic].”

What a lengthy paragraph of platitudes with little substance. That’s not even mentioning how the AI DJ butchered the pronunciation of a little-known, indie act called Charli XCX. This flub reflected my overall experience with YouTube Music’s AI DJ. It took me out of the groove and didn’t feel additive.

In another example, it went in-depth on the meaning of Olivia Rodrigo’s Expectations remix featuring Chappell Roan, calling it a "structural interpretation” that unpacks the “nuances of queer dating.” Then YouTube Music played the original track, sans Roan; so much for the queer yearning.

Curious how Spotify’s AI DJ experience would compare, I upgraded my account to the premium tier for access to that beta software. One of the biggest recent changes to Spotify’s AI DJ was adding new voices to the lineup, so I went into my settings and played the introduction clips for each of the eight English-language voices.

Maybe I was already a bit miffed from my YouTube Music experience because these voices immediately started to frustrate me. Multiple voices leaned into filler words such as “you know” and “like,” as the AI described the next songs it would play. Knowing an AI voice is being trained to use filler words to sound more human gave me the uncanny-valley ick.

Spotify’s AI DJ was fairly different from YouTube Music’s version. On Spotify, the AI DJ is also an algorithmically guided experience that picks songs for you based on past listening habits and song requests. Overall, Spotify’s synthetic commentary felt tighter and more tolerable than YouTube’s blabbering DJ. That said, neither software experience was enjoyable enough for me to return.

Although Spotify claims it has “80 percent of listeners coming back to DJ week after week,” according to the company’s launch blog, I won’t be one of them. My rejection of AI DJs isn’t based on how they audibly sound. The voices, from both companies, are decent and sound convincingly human. The content of their commentary is what truly turns me off. Whether it’s empty platitudes or mimicking human mistakes, I’ve heard enough.

article_content_zh:
YouTube Music 是我选择的音乐流媒体服务。由于我是一名软件记者，因此我总是启用 YouTube 实验室提供的测试版功能，其中包括 Beyond the Beat。 YouTube 的 AI DJ 在歌曲之间随机插入约 30 秒，营造氛围转变并提供有关下一首曲目的背景信息。

越来越多的听众正在遇到内置于音乐流媒体应用程序中的综合评论。 YouTube 在 2025 年推出了这款实验性 AI DJ，而 Spotify 早在 2023 年就首次推出了类似的工具。该公司在 11 月加倍加大了 AI DJ 的力度，扩大了用户可用的不同个性，并增加了对评论的更多控制。

这些人工智能 DJ 不仅令人讨厌。他们试图提供有用的背景并模仿人类的坦诚，最终以失败告终。对我来说幸运的是，这两个功能都是可选且可以避免的。

在启用它几个月后，本周 Beyond the Beat 的一次糟糕体验迫使我完全放弃人工智能 DJ。作为早上锻炼的一部分，我正在听流行歌星的播放列表，在 Slayyyter 曲目之后，我被长达 30 秒的解释所困扰：

“Hey Boy 完美地传达了那种高能量的冲击力，但我们正在将注意力转向更尖锐、更发自内心的现实。在《摇滚音乐》中，Charli XXC [原文如此]以一种尖锐的黑色幽默感讲述了她在 2024 年和 2025 年无情的巡演中所遭受的身体伤害。她将在路上遭受的真正的神经损伤变成了一种奇怪的战斗伤疤，将疲惫的派对女孩的疲惫重新视为荣誉徽章。这是对这一奇观背后的成本的坚定审视，其中行业的苦差事成为了真正的主题，这是 Charli XXC 的摇滚音乐[原文如此]。”

多么冗长的陈词滥调，内容却很少。更不用说 AI DJ 是如何毁掉一个鲜为人知的独立艺人 Charli XCX 的发音的了。这个失误反映了我对 YouTube Music 的 AI DJ 的整体体验。它让我脱离了困境，并且没有感觉有任何附加。

在另一个例子中，它深入探讨了奥利维亚·罗德里戈（Olivia Rodrigo）与查普尔·罗恩（Chappell Roan）合作的《期望》混音版的含义，称其为“结构性解释”，揭示了“酷儿约会的细微差别”。然后 YouTube Music 播放了原曲（没有 Roan）；奇怪的渴望就到此为止。

我很好奇 Spotify 的 AI DJ 体验会如何比较，因此我将我的帐户升级到高级级别以访问该测试版软件。 Spotify 的 AI DJ 最近最大的变化之一是在阵容中添加了新的声音，因此我进入我的设置并播放了八种英语声音中每一种的介绍剪辑。

也许我已经对 YouTube Music 体验感到有点恼火了，因为这些声音立即开始让我感到沮丧。当人工智能描述它将要播放的下一首歌曲时，多个声音倾向于使用“你知道”和“喜欢”等填充词。知道人工智能的声音正在被训练使用填充词来听起来更人性化，这让我产生了一种恐怖谷般的恶心。

Spotify 的 AI DJ 与 YouTube Music 的版本有很大不同。在 Spotify 上，AI DJ 也是一种算法引导的体验，可以根据过去的收听习惯和歌曲请求为您挑选歌曲。总体而言，Spotify 的综合评论比 YouTube 喋喋不休的 DJ 感觉更紧凑、更容易忍受。也就是说，这两种软件的体验都不足以让我再次回来。

尽管 Spotify 声称，根据该公司的发布博客，它有“80% 的听众每周都会回归 DJ”，但我不会成为其中之一。我对人工智能 DJ 的拒绝并不是因为他们听起来如何。两家公司的声音都很体面，听起来也很人性化。他们评论的内容真正让我感到厌烦。无论是空洞的陈词滥调还是模仿人类的错误，我已经听够了。

title: Firm linked to Jensen Huang's ex-lover reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for China
title_en: Firm linked to Jensen Huang's ex-lover reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for China
author: THE DECODER
article_content:
Megaspeed arranged nearly $12 billion worth of Nvidia high-performance chip orders for Chinese companies between March 2024 and June 2025, according to documents reviewed by the Wall Street Journal. The company is owned by Alice Huang, the former lover of since-ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Megaspeed shipped the chips to buyers in China who maintained long-standing business ties with local tech giants, the WSJ reports. The orders covered several hundred thousand chips that the US had sought to keep out of China through export controls. Megaspeed reportedly gained preferential access to scarce AI chips as an Nvidia cloud partner, apparently because it counted Chinese cloud and tech company Alibaba as a major client.

Nvidia officially reported $12.4 billion in China revenue over six months, accounting for 7 percent of total revenue. Short-selling firm Culper Research estimates, however, that more than 20 percent of Nvidia's revenue in the last fiscal year came from Chinese customers. A significant share of that China business may have flowed through indirect channels.

title: This AI Tamagotchi Turns Everyday Objects Into Needy Virtual Pets
title_en: This AI Tamagotchi Turns Everyday Objects Into Needy Virtual Pets

inline_images.caption: Image may contain Plant Potted Plant Art Collage Pottery Jar Bathroom Indoors Room and Toilet
inline_images.alt: Image may contain Plant Potted Plant Art Collage Pottery Jar Bathroom Indoors Room and Toilet

author: Wired AI
article_content:
You forgot to water the plant. Instead of seeing yellowing leaves, you see a cute plant-shaped pet on a tiny screen, looking sad and dejected. Maybe that'll give you the push you needed to grab the watering can. As you pour water into the soil, the plant pet on the screen gets excited and happy.

That's the idea behind OATs, or Object Agent Twins—micro-agent AI avatars on tiny E Ink displays designed to pair with everyday household objects. The tech was created by Daehwa Kim, a fifth-year PhD student in Carnegie Mellon's Future Interfaces Group. Kim presented the project at the ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology in Detroit in early November, a forum where academics and industry experts explore human-computer interfaces, and she earned two Honorable Mention awards.

You might remember Tamagotchi, the popular egg-shaped toys from the ‘90s that housed digital pets requiring real-time care and attention. Kim’s goal was to bring a similar experience to physical objects in our lives. “We bring this joy of caring from virtual to physical objects,” she tells WIRED. While folks have encouraged Kim to sell OATs kits online, she hasn't decided whether to pursue it as a business opportunity.

Kim says everyone spends all day staring at mobile devices, and AI agents—even if they're designed to handle tasks on your behalf—still demand attention from your smartphone screen. OATs were a way to bring those interactions out into the real world.

Giving AI a physical body isn't new, as companies rush to create “the next smartphone,” whether that's failed attempts like the Humane Ai Pin, OpenAI's upcoming hardware created in collaboration with famed ex-Apple designer Jony Ive, or Meta's Muse Charm. The pocket-sized gadget houses Meta's popular Muse AI agent and is expected to launch in December. Increasingly, though, companies have leaned on “cuteness” in their strategy for widespread adoption.

OATs have an E Ink display connected to internal and external sensors that can track things like moisture, temperature, humidity, light, occupancy, and motion. (The hardware is relatively cheap, around $20 for the main module.) The sprites are created with Google Gemini's Nano Banana image-generation service, creating a suite of emotions for various states based on the sensor data. You can set all of this up through a web portal, where you can name your OAT and choose which sensors to use for the object you're attaching it to.

The web app will generate “Positive” and “Negative” behaviors based on your object's name and description. So if the OAT is attached to a plant, positive triggers could be “consistent air temperature readings” and “low humidity levels” if the plant of choice prefers dry environments. However, you can customize these behaviors to suit your specific plant type.

It can be used for very simple things. Want to use your skateboard more often? Attach the OAT to your board, and if it hasn't detected motion for a few days, the avatar will look sad and lonely. You don't want that, do you? As Kim says, “These kinds of inanimate objects can be more expressive.” When you hop on the board, the OAT avatar will be happy, with fun faces.

The catch is that the system's battery life is really short, showing why this is more of a proof of concept than anything else. OATs last around three to four days, but paired with the sound level sensor, they'll only last a day. It has a USB-C port for charging the lithium-ion polymer battery.

Kim says she distributed OATs to many people and found that people use them in three different ways. One is, “Am I being used?” Like when you attach an OAT to a coffee machine and have the avatar get excited when the machine starts grinding beans. The second is for warning people near an object. For example, 3D printers release toxic fumes during use, and attaching an OAT to one can warn people that the device is operational. And the third is to track their own behaviors. Someone attached an OAT to a dumbbell to track how often they lifted weights, encouraging themselves to exercise regularly so they wouldn't disappoint the AI pet.

The demo at the symposium was popular, and Kim turned it into a competition to see who could come up with the most interesting ideas about what objects to pair with the OATs. Kim's website features a gallery with sprites people made, from an animated conference badge to a panda avatar for an Owala water bottle.

But the demo also ignited a huge discussion about anthropomorphizing artificial intelligence, and whether it’s proper to give these sprites human-like traits and emotions to make people feel connected with them.

It's already a topic in play within the AI industry. Companies often refer to their chatbot behaviors in human terms, like when they “hallucinate." Anthropic announced a “dreaming” feature this summer where its AI agent cleaned up its local memory as a background process. These anthropomorphized terms can distort moral judgments about AI and cause people to overly trust the tools.

Kim says that's why OATs have very limited interactions restricted to expressive emotions and the E Ink display.

“Anthropomorphism can be very useful in certain ways, like helping people to change their behaviors,” Kim says. “People name their car, and they name their bike. I rarely see people who name their iPhone. I feel like in the future of computing, we will have more of a relationship with AI, but we should definitely be careful not to abuse this."

title_zh: 卡内基梅隆大学研发OATs微型AI交互硬件
summary_zh: 卡内基梅隆大学研究团队发布OATs项目，通过E Ink显示屏与多传感器将物理对象转化为交互式AI数字宠物
article_content_zh:
你忘了给植物浇水。你看到的不是泛黄的叶子，而是小屏幕上一只可爱的植物形状的宠物，看起来悲伤而沮丧。也许这会给你提供抓住喷壶所需的推动力。当你将水倒入土壤中时，屏幕上的植物宠物会变得兴奋和快乐。

这就是 OAT（即对象代理双胞胎）背后的理念——微型电子墨水显示屏上的微代理人工智能化身，旨在与日常家居用品配对。该技术是由卡内基梅隆大学未来接口小组五年级博士生 Daehwa Kim 创建的。 Kim 于 11 月初在底特律举行的 ACM 用户界面软件和技术研讨会上展示了该项目，该论坛是学术界和行业专家探讨人机界面的论坛，她获得了两项荣誉奖。

您可能还记得电子宠物，这是 90 年代流行的蛋形玩具，里面装有需要实时护理和关注的数字宠物。 Kim 的目标是为我们生活中的物体带来类似的体验。她告诉《连线》杂志：“我们将这种护理的乐趣从虚拟物体转移到了实体物体上。”虽然人们鼓励 Kim 在网上销售燕麦套件，但她尚未决定是否将其作为一个商业机会。

Kim 表示，每个人都整天盯着移动设备，而人工智能代理——即使它们是为了代表你处理任务而设计的——仍然需要你的智能手机屏幕关注。 OAT 是将这些互动带入现实世界的一种方式。

为人工智能赋予实体并不新鲜，因为各家公司都在争先恐后地打造“下一代智能手机”，无论是像Humane Ai Pin（OpenAI 即将推出的与著名前苹果设计师 Jony Ive 合作开发的硬件）这样的失败尝试，还是 Meta 的 Muse Charm。这款口袋大小的小工具内置了 Meta 广受欢迎的 Muse AI 代理，预计将于 12 月推出。然而，越来越多的公司在其广泛采用的策略中依靠“可爱”。

OAT 有一个电子墨水显示屏，连接到内部和外部传感器，可以跟踪湿度、温度、湿度、光线、占用和运动等信息。 （硬件相对便宜，主模块大约 20 美元。）精灵是使用 Google Gemini 的 Nano Banana 图像生成服务创建的，根据传感器数据为各种状态创建一套情绪。您可以通过门户网站来设置所有这些，您可以在其中命名您的 OAT 并选择要用于将其附加到的对象的传感器。

网络应用程序将根据对象的名称和描述生成“积极”和“消极”行为。因此，如果将燕麦附着在植物上，如果选择的植物喜欢干燥的环境，那么积极的触发因素可能是“一致的气温读数”和“低湿度水平”。但是，您可以自定义这些行为以适合您的特定植物类型。

它可以用于非常简单的事情。想更频繁地使用你的滑板吗？将 OAT 连接到你的主板上，如果它几天没有检测到运动，头像会看起来悲伤和孤独。你不想要那样，是吗？正如金所说，“这些无生命的物体可以更具表现力。”当你跳上棋盘时，OAT 头像会很高兴，表情有趣。

问题是该系统的电池寿命非常短，这说明了为什么这更像是一个概念验证而不是其他任何东西。 OAT 的使用寿命约为三到四天，但与声级传感器配合使用时，它们只能持续一天。它有一个 USB-C 端口，用于为锂离子聚合物电池充电。

Kim 说，她向很多人分发了燕麦，发现人们以三种不同的方式使用它们。一是“我被利用了吗？”就像当你将燕麦连接到咖啡机上并让虚拟人物在机器开始磨豆时感到兴奋一样。第二个用于警告物体附近的人。例如，3D 打印机在使用过程中会释放有毒烟雾，将 OAT 连接到 3D 打印机上可以警告人们该设备正在运行。第三是跟踪自己的行为。有人在哑铃上贴了一个 OAT，用来追踪他们举重的频率，鼓励自己定期锻炼，这样就不会让人工智能宠物失望。

研讨会上的演示很受欢迎，Kim 将其变成了一场竞赛，看看谁能就哪些物体与 OAT 配对提出最有趣的想法。 Kim 的网站设有一个画廊，里面有人们制作的精灵，从动画会议徽章到奥瓦拉水瓶的熊猫头像。

但该演示也引发了一场关于人工智能拟人化的激烈讨论，以及是否应该赋予这些精灵类似人类的特征和情感，以使人们感到与它们有联系。

这已经成为人工智能行业的一个热门话题。公司经常用人类的术语来描述他们的聊天机器人行为，比如他们“产生幻觉”的时候。 Anthropic 今年夏天宣布了一项“梦想”功能，其人工智能代理将清理其本地内存作为后台进程。这些拟人化的术语可能会扭曲对人工智能的道德判断，并导致人们过度信任这些工具。

Kim 说，这就是为什么 OAT 的交互非常有限，仅限于表达情感和电子墨水显示。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: OATs项目通过低门槛硬件结合边缘计算，避开了大模型硬件追求高性能计算的红海，切中了物联网设备交互极其匮乏的痛点。这种以‘情绪化交互’为核心的轻量级硬件范式，为家电物联网设备的人机协作界面提供了一种低功耗、易落地的技术替代方案。
ai_analysis.insight_en: By leveraging low-cost hardware and edge-computing, the OATs project bypasses the hardware performance arms race in AI and addresses the interaction void in IoT. This emotionally-driven, lightweight interface paradigm presents a low-power, commercially viable alternative for human-machine collaboration in household appliances.

title: Australia's central bank finds AI hitting young workers first, especially in software and customer service
title_en: Australia's central bank finds AI hitting young workers first, especially in software and customer service

inline_images.caption: In jobs with high potential AI exposure (quintile 5), employment among young people has declined since late 2022, while employment among older workers has risen
inline_images.alt: In jobs with high potential AI exposure (quintile 5), employment among young people has declined sin

author: THE DECODER
article_content:
AI has barely displaced any jobs in Australia so far, but young workers entering highly exposed fields like software development are faring worse.

An analysis by Mike Major for Australia's central bank (RBA) built a monitoring system that focuses on the areas where effects are likely to appear first, namely entry-level workers and highly AI-exposed occupations such as programming, clerical work, and customer service.

According to the analysis, job postings have fallen across all groups since ChatGPT launched in late 2022, with the steepest drop in the highest-exposure group. In that group, workers aged 15 to 24 and young college graduates have weaker employment rates and higher unemployment than older workers.Ad

Major cautions against drawing early conclusions, since the study does not establish direct causation and measures only theoretical exposure, not actual use by companies. Post-pandemic shifts in the business cycle or in remote work could also be driving the numbers. According to SEEK data, AI is complementing existing work while also creating new demand for AI skills.Ad

An August 2025 Stanford study based on millions of US payroll records found a similar pattern, with employment among 22- to 25-year-olds in AI-exposed occupations down 13 percent in relative terms since late 2022 and nearly 20 percent among young software developers. More experienced workers in the same occupations held steady or gained ground.

A March 2026 Anthropic study also found signs of declining hiring among 22- to 25-year-olds in exposed occupations, with job-finding rates down about 14 percent. It found no systematic rise in overall unemployment, however. Theoretical automation potential and actual AI use are far apart, according to the study.Ad

Anthropic offers a company-level example. According to an internal review, the share of junior hires in technical roles has fallen from 27 percent to 9 percent since early 2025. In August 2026, AI agents across the company were already logging six times as many hours as human employees. Anthropic concedes that, as an extremely AI-intensive software company, it is a special case. Even so, researchers warn of a "tragedy of the cognitive commons", in which disappearing junior roles lead to a future shortage of experienced professionals, assuming those professionals are still needed.

A large study of 25,000 workers in Denmark confirms the lack of economy-wide impact. Despite a 64 percent AI adoption rate, researchers found no measurable changes in wages or hours worked. Workers saved an average of just 2.8 percent of their working time.Ad

A January 2026 analysis of 10.6 million LinkedIn profiles and US unemployment data, however, cautions against blaming the downturn on AI alone. The research team led by Morgan Frank at the University of Pittsburgh found that the problems in exposed occupations started in early 2022, months before ChatGPT launched. Macroeconomic factors like the Fed's shift in interest rate policy or a correction after pandemic-era hiring surges may play a bigger role than previously assumed.Ad

At the same time, AI is creating new demand. According to the World Economic Forum's "Future of Jobs Report 2025", 77 percent of surveyed companies are prioritizing upskilling over job cuts. WEF researchers project a net gain of 78 million jobs by 2030. According to LinkedIn, AI-related job postings grew sixfold in one year.

summary_en: Mike Major, a researcher at the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), found that demand for entry-level roles in high-exposure sectors like software, customer service, and clerical work has structurally declined since late 2022. The data corroborates a global trend where AI-driven automation of repetitive tasks disproportionately hampers early-career employment, while senior-level positions remain relatively insulated.
title_zh: 澳洲央行研究：AI正显著压缩初级人才就业空间
summary_zh: 澳大利亚储备银行分析显示，AI技术导致软件开发等高曝光领域初级岗位需求下降，年轻人就业承压

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 澳大利亚储备银行（RBA）研究员Mike Major通过监测分析指出，自2022年底生成式AI普及以来，编程、客户服务及办公职能等高暴露领域初级岗位需求呈结构性下滑。数据验证了全球范围内的同类趋势，即AI在替代初级重复性劳动的过程中，导致应届生及年轻劳动者就业门槛显著抬升，而资深人员岗位则保持相对稳定。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Mike Major, a researcher at the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), found that demand for entry-level roles in high-exposure sectors like software, customer service, and clerical work has structurally declined since late 2022. The data corroborates a global trend where AI-driven automation of repetitive tasks disproportionately hampers early-career employment, while senior-level positions remain relatively insulated.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: AI不仅在执行层面提升效率，其更大的隐性成本在于摧毁了产业界“师徒制”人才培育链路，即所谓的认知公共资源危机。长期来看，初级岗位的缺位将导致资深专家储备断档，使得企业未来在高端技术岗位上陷入严重的结构性人才短缺。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Beyond operational efficiency, AI poses a risk to the 'cognitive commons' by dismantling the apprenticeship pipeline essential for long-term skill acquisition. This structural attrition of junior roles will inevitably lead to a future talent drought for senior-level expertise, creating an unsustainable dependence on automated systems.

key_points_en: Structural decline in entry-level hiring for software and clerical roles
Disproportionate impact on young workers compared to experienced staff
Long-term risk of 'tragedy of the cognitive commons' and talent pipeline stagnation
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: AI不仅在执行层面提升效率，其更大的隐性成本在于摧毁了产业界“师徒制”人才培育链路，即所谓的认知公共资源危机。长期来看，初级岗位的缺位将导致资深专家储备断档，使得企业未来在高端技术岗位上陷入严重的结构性人才短缺。

This structural attrition of junior roles will inevitably lead to a future talent drought for senior-level expertise, creating an unsustainable dependence on automated systems.

article_content_zh:
到目前为止，人工智能在澳大利亚几乎没有取代任何工作，但进入软件开发等高度暴露领域的年轻工人的情况更糟。

澳大利亚央行 (RBA) 的迈克·梅杰 (Mike Major) 进行的一项分析建立了一个监控系统，重点关注可能首先出现影响的领域，即初级工人和高度人工智能暴露的职业，如编程、文书工作和客户服务。

分析显示，自 2022 年底 ChatGPT 推出以来，所有群体的招聘信息均有所下降，其中曝光率最高的群体降幅最大。在这一群体中，15岁至24岁的工人和年轻的大学毕业生的就业率比年长的工人低，失业率也高。

主要警告不要得出早期结论，因为该研究没有建立直接因果关系，并且仅衡量理论暴露，而不是公司的实际使用情况。大流行后商业周期或远程工作的变化也可能推动这一数字。 SEEK数据显示，人工智能正在补充现有工作，同时也创造了对人工智能技能的新需求。

斯坦福大学 2025 年 8 月基于数百万美国薪资记录进行的一项研究发现了类似的模式，自 2022 年底以来，22 至 25 岁的人工智能相关职业的就业率相对下降了 13%，年轻软件开发人员的就业率下降了近 20%。相同职业中更有经验的工人保持稳定或取得进展。

2026 年 3 月的一项 Anthropic 研究还发现，22 至 25 岁人群中暴露职业的招聘量出现下降迹象，求职率下降了约 14%。然而，它发现总体失业率没有系统性上升。研究表明，理论上的自动化潜力和实际的人工智能应用相距甚远。

Anthropic 提供了一个公司层面的例子。根据内部审查，自 2025 年初以来，技术职位的初级员工比例已从 27% 下降至 9%。到 2026 年 8 月，全公司的人工智能代理的工作时间已经是人类员工的六倍。 Anthropic 承认，作为一家人工智能极其密集的软件公司，这是一个特例。即便如此，研究人员警告称，将会出现“认知共享的悲剧”，即初级角色的消失会导致未来经验丰富的专业人员的短缺，假设这些专业人员仍然需要。

一项针对丹麦 25,000 名工人的大型研究证实，这对整个经济没有影响。尽管人工智能采用率为 64%，但研究人员发现工资或工作时间没有发生可衡量的变化。工人们平均只节省了 2.8% 的工作时间。

然而，2026 年 1 月对 1060 万个 LinkedIn 个人资料和美国失业数据的分析警告，不要将经济衰退仅仅归咎于人工智能。匹兹堡大学摩根·弗兰克 (Morgan Frank) 领导的研究团队发现，暴露职业的问题早在 2022 年初就开始出现，即 ChatGPT 推出前几个月。美联储利率政策的转变或大流行时代招聘激增后的调整等宏观经济因素可能比之前假设的发挥更大的作用。

与此同时，人工智能正在创造新的需求。根据世界经济论坛的《2025 年就业未来报告》，77% 的受访企业将技能提升置于裁员之上。世界经济论坛研究人员预计，到 2030 年，就业岗位将净增加 7800 万个。根据 LinkedIn 的数据，与人工智能相关的职位发布在一年内增长了六倍。

title: Meituan releases a 1.6-trillion-parameter agent model that never touched an Nvidia GPU
title_en: Meituan releases a 1.6-trillion-parameter agent model that never touched an Nvidia GPU

author: THE DECODER
article_content:
Meituan releases the weights for LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter model built for AI agents. It was trained entirely on Chinese hardware and performs at the level US models like Claude Opus 5 reached a few months ago on coding benchmarks.

The LongCat team at Chinese food delivery company Meituan has released the weights for LongCat-2.5, one week after the model's official unveiling. LongCat-2.5 is built for agents that work through long, multi-step tasks autonomously, particularly coding. According to Meituan, it comes close to top Western models on several benchmarks.

LongCat-2.5 is a mixture-of-experts model that activates only a subset of its specialized subnetworks for each token it processes. Out of 1.6 trillion total parameters, roughly 48 billion are active per token. Through the API, the model handles up to one million tokens at once and generates responses up to 128,000 tokens long. It understands text, images, and video, responds in text, and lets users toggle reasoning on and off.

LongCat-2.5 converts images into tokens

LongCat-2.5 builds on its predecessor LongCat-2.0 and adds image understanding. Many multimodal models bolt on a separate image encoder after the fact. LongCat-2.5 instead converts images into tokens that the model processes alongside text, as is standard practice for today's LLMs. The approach draws on the research model LongCat-Next and aims to improve visual coding, design, and 3D tasks.

[caption id="attachment_42886" align="alignnone" width="1800"] LongCat-2.5 breaks images down at their native resolution into discrete tokens that the model processes alongside text. | Image: Meituan[/caption]

For reinforcement learning, the team used real software tasks from GitHub pull requests along with recreated agent failures. To make sure the model actually solved the tasks during training, the developers blocked internet access in the training environments, removed Git history and cached files, and had a language model check its solutions for tricks. The team also distilled the capabilities of several specialized teacher models for agent work, reasoning, and dialog into LongCat-2.5.

[caption id="attachment_42885" align="alignnone" width="1200"] Meituan generates training tasks from real GitHub repositories and blocks shortcuts like web search and Git history in the sandbox. | Image: Meituan[/caption]

Meituan quantizes the experts' weights and activations to 4-bit precision, which Chinese chips can process natively. In Meituan's load tests, throughput rises 43.3 percent for prompt processing and 42.77 percent for response generation compared with an 8-bit version. Meituan says accuracy stays on par with the uncompressed model.

This version is available in a separate repository. The self-hosting guide describes a cluster of 194 Huawei Ascend accelerators from the Atlas A2 series. Two handle image processing, 64 handle prompt ingestion, and 128 handle response generation. There's no guidance for Nvidia GPUs.

LongCat-2.5 trails Opus 5 slightly on terminal tasks

The LongCat team reports 88.4 points on Terminal Bench v2.1, a benchmark that measures how well agents solve command-line tasks. Meituan lists Claude Opus 5 at 89.1, GPT-5.6 Sol at 88.8, and Deepseek-V4.1-Flash at the top of the table with 90.6.

DeepSWE tests how well models fix bugs in real code repositories. Here LongCat-2.5 jumps from 9.7 to 64.6 points, placing it behind every other model in the table except Claude Opus 4.8, with Deepseek-V4.1-Flash leading at 74.2 and GPT-5.6 Sol at 72.7. The more recent Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol are not included in the table.

[caption id="attachment_42887" align="alignnone" width="1800"] In Meituan's own evaluation, LongCat-2.5 improves substantially over its predecessor and comes close to Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol on several agent benchmarks. | Image: Meituan[/caption]

Terminal Bench v4.0, the harder variant, puts LongCat-2.5 at 38.5 points, slightly above GPT-5.6 Sol's 37.3 but well below Opus 5's 53.9. The model posts 91.9 on the web search benchmark BrowseComp, the highest score in the table, though Meituan ran this test in its own environment.

The weights are available under the MIT license, which allows commercial use, modification, and redistribution. Users can also try LongCat-2.5 in a chat interface at https://longcat.ai/. Its API supports both the OpenAI and Anthropic formats and plugs into agent harnesses like Claude Code, Codex, and Hermes. At launch, Meituan is charging a limited-time promotional price equivalent to roughly €0.27 per million input tokens and €1.07 per million output tokens.

Meituan says it trained the predecessor LongCat-2.0 in late June entirely on a cluster of more than 50,000 Chinese AI chips. Before that, the model ran anonymously as "Owl Alpha" on OpenRouter. Chinese open-weight models like Kimi K3.1 and GLM-5.3 have largely caught up with top US models on common benchmarks.

Open-weight models optimized for Chinese chips from the start make that hardware more attractive outside China too. Beyond multimodal agent models, Meituan is also working on image generators. The company previously released LongCat-Image, an open-source text-to-image model that gets by with just 6 billion parameters and prioritizes efficiency over sheer model size.

title_zh: 美团发布LongCat-2.5：全国产算力底座下的万亿参数模型
summary_zh: 美团发布1.6万亿参数多模态Agent模型LongCat-2.5，完全基于国产硬件训练，性能对标Claude Opus 5
article_content_zh:
美团发布LongCat-2.5权重，这是一个为AI智能体构建的1.6万亿参数模型。它完全在中国硬件上进行训练，其性能达到了 Claude Opus 5 等美国模型几个月前在编码基准上达到的水平。

在该模型正式发布一周后，中国食品配送公司美团的 LongCat 团队发布了 LongCat-2.5 的权重。 LongCat-2.5 是为能够自主完成长期、多步骤任务（尤其是编码）的代理而构建的。据美团称，它在多项基准测试中接近西方顶级机型。

LongCat-2.5 是一个专家混合模型，它只为其处理的每个令牌激活其专用子网络的子集。在 1.6 万亿个参数中，每个代币大约有 480 亿个参数处于活跃状态。通过 API，该模型可以一次处理多达 100 万个令牌，并生成长达 128,000 个令牌的响应。它可以理解文本、图像和视频，以文本形式做出响应，并允许用户打开和关闭推理。

LongCat-2.5 将图像转换为token

LongCat-2.5 建立在其前身 LongCat-2.0 的基础上，并增加了图像理解功能。许多多模态模型事后都安装了单独的图像编码器。 LongCat-2.5 相反，将图像转换为模型与文本一起处理的标记，这是当今法学硕士的标准做法。该方法借鉴了 LongCat-Next 研究模型，旨在改进视觉编码、设计和 3D 任务。

LongCat-2.5 以原始分辨率将图像分解为模型与文本一起处理的离散标记。 |图片：美团[/标题]

对于强化学习，该团队使用了来自 GitHub 拉取请求的真实软件任务以及重新创建的代理故障。为了确保模型在训练期间确实解决了任务，开发人员在训练环境中阻止了互联网访问，删除了 Git 历史记录和缓存文件，并让语言模型检查其解决方案是否存在技巧。该团队还将几个专门的教师模型用于代理工作、推理和对话的功能提炼到 LongCat-2.5 中。

美团从真实的 GitHub 存储库生成训练任务，并在沙箱中阻止 Web 搜索和 Git 历史记录等快捷方式。 |图片：美团[/标题]

美团将专家的权重和激活量化到 4 位精度，中国芯片可以本地处理。在美团的负载测试中，与 8 位版本相比，即时处理吞吐量提高了 43.3%，响应生成吞吐量提高了 42.77%。美团表示，准确性与未压缩模型保持一致。

该版本可在单独的存储库中找到。自托管指南描述了由 Atlas A2 系列的 194 个华为 Ascend 加速器组成的集群。两个处理图像处理，64 个处理提示摄取，以及 128 个处理响应生成。没有针对 Nvidia GPU 的指南。

LongCat-2.5 在终端任务上稍微落后于 Opus 5

LongCat 团队在 Terminal Bench v2.1 上获得了 88.4 分，这是衡量代理解决命令行任务效果的基准。美团将 Claude Opus 5 列为 89.1，GPT-5.6 Sol 为 88.8，Deepseek-V4.1-Flash 以 90.6 名列榜首。

DeepSWE 测试模型在真实代码存储库中修复错误的效果。这里，LongCat-2.5 从 9.7 分跃升至 64.6 分，落后于表中除 Claude Opus 4.8 之外的所有其他模型，其中 Deepseek-V4.1-Flash 领先，得分为 74.2，GPT-5.6 Sol 得分为 72.7。较新的 Claude Opus 5.5 和 GPT-6.1 Sol 未包含在表中。

在美团自己的评估中，LongCat-2.5比其前身有了很大的改进，并且在多个代理基准上接近Claude Opus 5和GPT-5.6 Sol。 |图片：美团[/标题]

title: A post-Jensen Nvidia must reshuffle its leadership, reset its DC ties, and recognize that even the US' most valuable company cannot dictate US foreign policy (Chris Miller/Financial Times)
title_en: A post-Jensen Nvidia must reshuffle its leadership, reset its DC ties, and recognize that even the US' most valuable company cannot dictate US foreign policy (Chris Miller/Financial Times)
author: Financial Times
article_content:
Jensen Huang’s exit from Nvidia, the company he co-founded, after revelations of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is a humiliating end to an extraordinary career atop America’s AI sector. Yet his replacement will not end the investigations. The company’s remaining leaders will have to answer for staggering compliance failures that stretched beyond the CEO. And US President Donald Trump — until recently one of Huang’s biggest backers — will face intense pressure to increase his administration’s lax effort to track the smuggling of US chips to China.

For Nvidia, the scandal will significantly reduce its influence over Washington’s technology policy. Most tech companies have big lobbying outfits, but Nvidia’s approach to policy advocacy was uniquely confrontational. Many chip companies argued that their products should be allowed into China on mundane commercial grounds. But Huang attacked the premise of Washington’s controls, describing China hawks as shameful.

The company’s general counsel, Tim Teter, is even reported to have reached out to the commerce department regarding investigations into Megaspeed, the company where alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang was an executive.

This sharp-elbowed approach made many enemies. The Republican Party is usually pro-business, but Nvidia’s tactics angered senior legislators. Brian Mast, the Republican chair of the House of Representatives foreign affairs committee, attacked Huang earlier this year on social media for “fighting to sell millions of advanced AI chips to Chinese military companies”. Republican Senator Jim Banks has spent the past year working with leftwing Democrat Elizabeth Warren to pass legislation restricting AI chip sales. Nvidia has only itself to blame for a long list of adversaries on both sides of Congress.

Huang’s most powerful friend — the US president — was already weakened by defeat in the midterm elections. He will be weakened further by investigations into his relationship with Nvidia.

One question is what he knew and when. The FT has reported that the president was briefed in May on Huang’s relationship with the alleged Chinese agent yet took no action. A second question is why his administration continued to allow chip sales to Megaspeed throughout this period.

More broadly, Congress is frustrated that the Trump administration came to office promising tough restrictions yet has not delivered. Even before the current scandal broke, Congress was advancing legislation to force tighter controls.

The MATCH Act would force the administration to tighten controls on chipmaking equipment. The AI Overwatch Act would do the same for AI chips. The Chip Security Act would mandate deployment of technologies to track chips’ location. Now these bills are more likely to pass, perhaps as part of a defence spending package later this year.

Pressure is also rising to restrict Chinese access to data centres abroad. One nuance of US chip controls was that, while Chinese companies are not allowed to buy high-end AI chips or bring them into the country, they can rent access in overseas data centres. This is what Megaspeed did on behalf of Alibaba. Nvidia argued that companies like Megaspeed, largely based in south-east Asia, were normal customers. The revelation that it was linked to a suspected Chinese agent makes the argument harder to sustain.

In addition to passing new restrictions, Congress will probably continue investigating Nvidia’s senior leadership. For example, what did other leaders know about Megaspeed? Did the company attempt to intervene in an investigation into Megaspeed, rather than establishing an effective compliance programme? When the new Democratic-led Congress is seated in January, Nvidia’s $25mn donation to Trump’s ballroom will become a liability rather than an asset.

For Nvidia and its investors, the irony is that the China market was small. The scale of smuggling is uncertain, but research from the Institute for Progress suggests it would not account for a large fraction of Nvidia’s revenue. It does not compare to the cost of the chaos that this scandal has caused.

Nvidia needs a path forward in the post-Jensen era. It must reshuffle its senior leadership, reset its relationship with Washington and recognise that even America’s most valuable company cannot dictate the country’s foreign policy. Huang spent the past few years angering Washington by calling its China policy misguided. If anyone was misguided in their dealings with China, it was him.

title_zh: 英伟达领导层与地缘战略的必要转型
summary_zh: 分析指出英伟达需重构领导架构并重塑华盛顿政商关系，以适应地缘政治对半导体产业主导权的强力约束
article_content_zh:
黄仁勋在与一名所谓的中国间谍的恋情被曝光后，退出了他共同创立的英伟达公司，这给他在美国人工智能领域的非凡职业生涯带来了耻辱的结局。然而他的继任者不会结束调查。公司剩下的领导者将不得不对超出首席执行官范围的令人震惊的合规失败负责。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普——直到最近还是黄的最大支持者之一——将面临巨大的压力，要求他的政府加大力度追踪美国芯片走私到中国的情况。

对于英伟达来说，丑闻将大大降低其对华盛顿科技政策的影响力。大多数科技公司都有大型游说机构，但英伟达的政策倡导方式却具有独特的对抗性。许多芯片公司辩称，出于普通的商业理由，他们的产品应该被允许进入中国。但黄攻击了华盛顿控制的前提，称对华鹰派是可耻的。

据报道，该公司的总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特 (Tim Teter) 甚至就调查 Megaspeed 事宜与商务部进行了接触，据称中国间谍黄爱丽 (Alice Huang) 是该公司的高管。

这种尖锐的做法树敌不少。共和党通常是亲商的，但英伟达的策略激怒了高级立法者。众议院外交事务委员会共和党主席布莱恩·马斯特(Brian Mast)今年早些时候在社交媒体上攻击黄仁勋“奋力向中国军事公司出售数百万枚先进人工智能芯片”。共和党参议员吉姆·班克斯（Jim Banks）在过去的一年里与左翼民主党人伊丽莎白·沃伦（Elizabeth Warren）合作通过了限制人工智能芯片销售的立法。国会两党的一长串对手只能归咎于英伟达自己。

黄的最有权势的朋友——美国总统——已经因中期选举的失败而被削弱。他与英伟达关系的调查将进一步削弱他的实力。

一个问题是他知道什么以及何时知道。据英国《金融时报》报道，总统五月份听取了有关黄与所谓的中国特工关系的简报，但没有采取任何行动。第二个问题是，为什么他的政府在此期间继续允许向 Megaspeed 销售芯片。

更广泛地说，国会对特朗普政府上任时承诺采取严厉限制措施但尚未兑现感到沮丧。甚至在当前丑闻爆发之前，国会就正在推进立法以强制实施更严格的控制。

MATCH 法案将迫使政府加强对芯片制造设备的控制。 《人工智能守望先锋法案》将对人工智能芯片采取同样的措施。 《芯片安全法》将强制要求部署技术来跟踪芯片的位置。现在这些法案更有可能获得通过，也许作为今年晚些时候国防支出计划的一部分。

限制中国访问海外数据中心的压力也越来越大。美国芯片管制的一个细微差别是，虽然中国公司不允许购买高端人工智能芯片或将其带入美国，但他们可以租用海外数据中心的访问权。这就是Megaspeed代表阿里巴巴所做的事情。 Nvidia 辩称，像 Megaspeed 这样主要位于东南亚的公司是普通客户。该事件与一名疑似中国特工有关的消息被揭露后，这一论点变得更加难以成立。

除了通过新的限制之外，国会可能还会继续调查英伟达的高级领导层。例如，其他领导者对 Megaspeed 了解多少？该公司是否试图干预对 Megaspeed 的调查，而不是建立有效的合规计划？当民主党领导的新一届国会于 1 月份就职时，英伟达向特朗普舞厅捐赠的 2500 万美元将成为负债而不是资产。

对于英伟达及其投资者来说，讽刺的是中国市场很小。走私的规模尚不确定，但进步研究所的研究表明，走私不会占英伟达收入的很大一部分。这无法与这起丑闻造成的混乱成本相比。

英伟达需要在后詹森时代找到一条前进的道路。它必须改组其高级领导层，重新调整与华盛顿的关系，并认识到即使是美国最有价值的公司也无法决定该国的外交政策。黄在过去几年中称其对华政策被误导，从而激怒了华盛顿。如果说有人在与中国打交道时被误导了，那就是他了。

article_content_en:
Jensen Huang’s exit from Nvidia, the company he co-founded, after revelations of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is a humiliating end to an extraordinary career atop America’s AI sector. Yet his replacement will not end the investigations. The company’s remaining leaders will have to answer for staggering compliance failures that stretched beyond the CEO. And US President Donald Trump — until recently one of Huang’s biggest backers — will face intense pressure to increase his administration’s lax effort to track the smuggling of US chips to China.

For Nvidia, the scandal will significantly reduce its influence over Washington’s technology policy. Most tech companies have big lobbying outfits, but Nvidia’s approach to policy advocacy was uniquely confrontational. Many chip companies argued that their products should be allowed into China on mundane commercial grounds. But Huang attacked the premise of Washington’s controls, describing China hawks as shameful.

The company’s general counsel, Tim Teter, is even reported to have reached out to the commerce department regarding investigations into Megaspeed, the company where alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang was an executive.

This sharp-elbowed approach made many enemies. The Republican Party is usually pro-business, but Nvidia’s tactics angered senior legislators. Brian Mast, the Republican chair of the House of Representatives foreign affairs committee, attacked Huang earlier this year on social media for “fighting to sell millions of advanced AI chips to Chinese military companies”. Republican Senator Jim Banks has spent the past year working with leftwing Democrat Elizabeth Warren to pass legislation restricting AI chip sales. Nvidia has only itself to blame for a long list of adversaries on both sides of Congress.

Huang’s most powerful friend — the US president — was already weakened by defeat in the midterm elections. He will be weakened further by investigations into his relationship with Nvidia.

One question is what he knew and when. The FT has reported that the president was briefed in May on Huang’s relationship with the alleged Chinese agent yet took no action. A second question is why his administration continued to allow chip sales to Megaspeed throughout this period.

More broadly, Congress is frustrated that the Trump administration came to office promising tough restrictions yet has not delivered. Even before the current scandal broke, Congress was advancing legislation to force tighter controls.

The MATCH Act would force the administration to tighten controls on chipmaking equipment. The AI Overwatch Act would do the same for AI chips. The Chip Security Act would mandate deployment of technologies to track chips’ location. Now these bills are more likely to pass, perhaps as part of a defence spending package later this year.

Pressure is also rising to restrict Chinese access to data centres abroad. One nuance of US chip controls was that, while Chinese companies are not allowed to buy high-end AI chips or bring them into the country, they can rent access in overseas data centres. This is what Megaspeed did on behalf of Alibaba. Nvidia argued that companies like Megaspeed, largely based in south-east Asia, were normal customers. The revelation that it was linked to a suspected Chinese agent makes the argument harder to sustain.

In addition to passing new restrictions, Congress will probably continue investigating Nvidia’s senior leadership. For example, what did other leaders know about Megaspeed? Did the company attempt to intervene in an investigation into Megaspeed, rather than establishing an effective compliance programme? When the new Democratic-led Congress is seated in January, Nvidia’s $25mn donation to Trump’s ballroom will become a liability rather than an asset.

For Nvidia and its investors, the irony is that the China market was small. The scale of smuggling is uncertain, but research from the Institute for Progress suggests it would not account for a large fraction of Nvidia’s revenue. It does not compare to the cost of the chaos that this scandal has caused.

Nvidia needs a path forward in the post-Jensen era. It must reshuffle its senior leadership, reset its relationship with Washington and recognise that even America’s most valuable company cannot dictate the country’s foreign policy. Huang spent the past few years angering Washington by calling its China policy misguided. If anyone was misguided in their dealings with China, it was him.

title: Nidus, which is developing AI-powered tech for manufacturing robots used by US defense industrial companies, raised $30M across a pre-seed and a seed (Alex Konrad/Upstarts Media)

author: Upstarts Media
article_content:
Alex KonradNov 10, 2026 11 Share CEO Justin Sealy and his Nidus co-founders want to build a leading AI robotics lab in NYC, focused on defense and industrial use. Credit: NidusIn what looks like a workshop rig set up in the middle of a more typical startup office in New York’s Flatiron neighborhood, the teleoperator shows me how to stabilize the robotic arm with my left hand, then reach with my right, the gripper approaching at a 45 degree angle until its prongs are just over the floor.

Press the trigger, and they close on the target – a section of wire, its ends exposed from their protective shielding – ideally about 3 inches from the end. Now comes the hard part: lining up the wire ends straight on with a rotating wheel. With a flick upwards of the wrist, he gently guides the two together, the wheel brushing and grouping the wire’s fibrous ends together in a neat bunch.

That’s how it looks when he does it, at least. My first effort makes contact off-center, and the ends tangle in every direction. A second try is more respectable, but I’m not going to be offered a job.

“I wanted to see what happened if it went the wrong way,” says my host, Nidus Technologies CEO Justin Sealy. “You kind of can know pretty quickly with people if they’re going to be good or not.”

Upstarts Media is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, become a free or paid subscriber.

The team at Nidus, all dozen or so of them, are much better at this unusual task. That’s because the data they collect from doing it thousands of times, across a growing number of these rigs, play a crucial part in training AI models that the startup then wants to deploy with defense industrial customers, speeding up their production without having to rebuild their existing processes from scratch.

They’ve started with wire harnesses, a pre-manufactured mass of cables, wires and connectors that makes them easier to install in everything from automobiles to satellite receivers, and aircraft to tanks. But the ambition is to move beyond wire harnesses into other processes that take hours of human busy work today, from kitting and pre-assembly to printed circuit boards.

Founded earlier this year by Sealy and three co-founders who all worked together on the hardware team at defense startup Vannevar, Nidus says it has reached more than $1 million in bookings with unnamed defense industrial customers in just four months.

Today, Nidus announced that it’s raised $30 million in funding: a pre-seed led by Costanoa, and a seed round led by Kleiner Perkins, Upstarts exclusively reports. Ludlow Ventures, Absolute Partners and angels including Hadrian CEO Chris Power and Amca CEO Jai Malik also participated.

Nidus plans to use the funding to hire aggressively at its New York HQ, in a bid to build a leading robotics AI lab in the city, ramping up data collection and training for more (secretive) customers.

The startup stands out for other reasons, too. Sealy and co. are motivated, they say, by the need to reindustrialize more of America’s supply chain in the face of potential geopolitical tension with China (a concern we looked at from the logistics view recently with our launch story on Watchtower).

And they’re making a bet that general robotics AI labs, like Physical Intelligence, Skild AI, Figure AI and many others, won’t be able to easily expand into the precise needs of the defense industry.

“Oftentimes Silicon Valley technology goes to the easiest commercially viable path, versus where it needs to go in the most urgent capacity,” Sealy says. “Defense is just such a different customer than folding towels at Holiday Inn.”

More on how Nidus plans to do it, and stay ahead of well-funded rivals, below.

Different product bets have different business goals. You’re either chasing market adoption, revenue growth, or profits. You need to test fitting pricing models for each of those goals. Fast. Chargebee can help — Price for usage credits, outcomes, complex contracts, or any other modern commercial construct.

Growing up in a military family in Greenwood, South Carolina, Sealy watched friends’ parents lose their jobs to offshoring of the local textiles industry. At Clemson, he took multiple leaves of absence to work as an engineer at a local manufacturer to try to help.

But it was a 2018 ad in the Wall Street Journal that pushed him to apply on a whim for a job at Palantir. Explaining that he wanted to help his siblings deployed in the Armed Forces to get home safely, Sealy was surprised to be offered a job in Palantir’s New York office, where he quickly got security clearance to work on government contracts, and spent three years as a deployment strategist.

After a stint at safety startup Peregrine, he joined Vannevar, a defense startup working on intelligence tools for national security and government customers, with an eye toward deterrence against China. It was there that, after being asked by Vannevar to build out an AI hardware team for use cases like drone detection, he began working with Harrison Nguyen, Charu Dwivedi, and Cane Punma, who brought expertise in operations, robotics and AI, respectively.

Then last Christmas, Sealy wrote an essay about his belief that U.S. industry needed to tap more into accessible robotics capabilities in order to depend less on China. “In order for us to actually compete, there has to be a technology shift. There has to be something where we can build more with the existing capability we have in the U.S.,” he says now.

The post made the rounds among venture capitalists, and Sealy realized he was sitting on a new company idea. With the blessing of Vannevar’s CEO, the four formally founded Nidus in March. They spent the next few months visiting potential customers to see what process made sense to start working on.

“If you walk around a factory and you look for places where a human is standing still, doing the same job over and over again, it’s typically in front of machines,” Sealy says.

Cutting and prepping wire harnesses for production stood out as a task where highly skilled workers still toiled with hand tools for hours. “How do you get more product out of the craftsman?” Sealy says they challenged themselves. “How do you take a lot of the manual stuff that they’re doing, and allow them to build faster?”

Co-founder Cane Punma working on one of Nidus’s training rigs. Credit: NidusTo make those workers 10x more efficient, Nidus’s founders devised a business model by which they would leverage the best existing AI models – initially open-source, and now frontier models – then collect their own proprietary data to fine-tune them for the specific industrial use case. That custom model could then be deployed in the factory, effectively putting a GPU alongside an existing robot already in use.

It’s a page out of the Palantir playbook, Sealy says: “The value is found on the edge. Go solve problems there.”

Sealy and his co-founders believe they’re taking a different approach than many other AI robotics labs today. “There’s a lot of people doing robotics, but what excites me more is the burgeoning need for reindustrialization,” says Nguyen.

The data that Nidus collects and uses with each customer is also private and proprietary, notes investor Aatish Nayak, who led its most recent funding at Kleiner Perkins, meaning it’s tougher to replicate.

Other robotics and AI labs might be more interested in partnering with Nidus, given its access and trust with such customers, says Nayak, versus playing catch-up getting a foot in the door. Nidus hopes to also demonstrate results faster than some of the big-swing AI engineering and manufacturing projects underway, like Jeff Bezos’s well-funded Prometheus.

“There’s something to be said for a mission-driven team that’s very pragmatic, customer-first, and not necessarily technology-first, but technology agnostic in many ways, because they’ll benefit a lot from the various hardware and software advances,” Nayak argues.

Still, if the market is so attractive, and the need so great, other startups and tech giants will compete. Nidus isn’t the only startup working broadly with wire harnesses already. The investor concedes: “Speed is the name of the game.”

Nidus’s founders aren’t worried. When I meet with them in October, they’re more focused on the local utility fixing an issue getting new fiber-optic cable online for their building, so they can upload their training data faster to a secure cloud environment. (The utility hit a gas line, causing much excitement on their block for a day.)

“The addressable problem set of robotics is so much larger than one company,” Sealy says.

But there isn’t an infinite supply of engineers who are better than me at robotically cleaning wires. The founders want you to know they’re hiring, and their CEO makes a final pitch:

“There is no world-class physical AI company in New York, and we have the opportunity to be the first.”

Update: This story has been updated to better describe Prometheus.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 该融资案显示出资本正加速向“AI+精密制造”垂直细分领域流动，尤其在国防供应链寻求降本增效的刚需背景下，具备数据闭环能力的硬件初创公司成为溢价重点。Nidus的核心护城河不在于机器人本体硬件，而在于将非标准化的装配过程工程化为可训练的数据集，这将重塑国防工业外包生产的技术准入门槛。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This funding underscores a capital shift toward AI-integrated precision manufacturing, where defense supply chains demand efficiency. Nidus’s competitive edge lies not in hardware, but in its ability to engineer non-standard assembly tasks into data sets, effectively setting a new technical benchmark for defense manufacturing sub-contractors.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 由首席执行官Justin Sealy创立的Nidus公司在完成种子轮融资后累计获得3000万美元资金，旨在通过自主研发的AI模型优化复杂硬件装配工艺。该公司核心业务聚焦于国防工业制造，通过采集高频作业数据训练机器人执行线束预装配等高门槛任务，成立四个月已获得逾100万美元订单。
ai_analysis.digest_en: Nidus, led by CEO Justin Sealy, has secured $30 million across pre-seed and seed rounds to develop AI-powered robotics for defense manufacturing. The company utilizes data-driven AI models to automate high-precision tasks like wire harness assembly, having already achieved over $1 million in bookings within four months of operation.

article_content_zh:
Share首席执行官贾斯汀·西利和他的Nidus联合创始人希望在纽约建立一个领先的人工智能机器人实验室，专注于国防和工业应用。在纽约熨斗区（Flatiron）附近一个更典型的初创公司办公室的中间，一个看起来像车间的装置里，遥控操作员向我展示了如何用左手稳定机械臂，然后用右手伸手，抓手以45度角靠近，直到它的叉子刚刚过地板。

按下扳机，它们就会靠近目标——一段电线，其末端从保护屏蔽中暴露出来——理想情况下距离末端约 3 英寸。现在是最困难的部分：用旋转轮将线端直线排列。他轻轻地向上一抖手腕，将两者引导到一起，轮子刷过电线，将电线的纤维端整齐地聚集在一起。

至少当他这样做时看起来是这样的。我的第一次努力使接触偏离中心，并且末端在各个方向上缠结。第二次尝试更受人尊敬，但我不会得到一份工作。

“我想看看如果走错了会发生什么，”我的主人 Nidus Technologies 首席执行官贾斯汀·西利 (Justin Sealy) 说道。 “你可以很快地知道人们是否会表现出色。”

Upstarts Media 是一本由读者支持的出版物。要接收新帖子并支持我们的工作，请成为免费或付费订阅者。

Nidus 的团队约有十几人，在这项不寻常的任务上表现得更好。这是因为，他们在越来越多的钻机上进行数千次收集的数据，在训练人工智能模型方面发挥着至关重要的作用，然后初创公司希望将这些模型与国防工业客户一起部署，从而加快生产速度，而无需从头开始重建现有流程。

他们从线束开始，这是一种预先制造的大量电缆、电线和连接器，使它们更容易安装在从汽车到卫星接收器、从飞机到坦克的各种设备中。但我们的目标是超越线束，进入当今需要人类花费数小时忙碌工作的其他流程，从配套和预组装到印刷电路板。

Nidus 由 Sealy 和三名联合创始人于今年早些时候创立，他们都在国防初创公司 Vannevar 的硬件团队中工作。 Nidus 表示，在短短四个月内，该公司向未透露姓名的国防工业客户的订单已超过 100 万美元。

据 Upstarts 独家报道，今天，Nidus 宣布筹集了 3000 万美元资金：由 Costanoa 领投的预种子轮融资和由 Kleiner Perkins 领投的种子轮融资。 Ludlow Ventures、Absolute Partners 以及包括 Hadrian 首席执行官 Chris Power 和 Amca 首席执行官 Jai Malik 在内的天使投资人也参与其中。

Nidus 计划利用这笔资金在其纽约总部积极招聘员工，以期在该市建立一个领先的机器人人工智能实验室，加强数据收集和对更多（秘密）客户的培训。

这家初创公司之所以脱颖而出还有其他原因。西利公司他们说，面对与中国潜在的地缘政治紧张局势，需要对更多的美国供应链进行再工业化（我们最近在《守望台》上发布的故事中从物流角度审视了这一问题）。

他们打赌，通用机器人人工智能实验室，如物理智能、技能人工智能、图形人工智能等，将无法轻松扩展到满足国防工业的精确需求。

“硅谷的技术通常会选择最简单的商业可行路径，而不是最紧急的需求，”西利说。 “国防和假日酒店的折叠毛巾是完全不同的客户。”

更多关于 Nidus 计划如何做到这一点，并保持领先于资金充足的竞争对手的信息，请参见下文。

title: TSMC plans to set up a new $500M fund to invest in chip startups, suppliers, and other upstream partners, saying "we also want to support the future's Nvidia" (Cheng Ting-Fang/Nikkei Asia)
title_en: TSMC plans to set up a new $500M fund to invest in chip startups, suppliers, and other upstream partners, saying "we also want to support the future's Nvidia" (Cheng Ting-Fang/Nikkei Asia)

inline_images.caption: 20261111 TSMC senior vice president and deputy co-chief operating officer Kevin Zhang
inline_images.alt: 20261111 TSMC senior vice president and deputy co-chief operating officer Kevin Zhang

inline_images.caption: TSMC is seeing 'insatiable' demand for chips, executive tells Nikkei Forum
inline_images.alt: TSMC is seeing 'insatiable' demand for chips, executive tells Nikkei Forum

author: Nikkei Asia
article_content:
TOKYO -- Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. plans to use a new $500 million venture fund to support promising chip startups that could become the next Nvidia or Broadcom, as the world's largest contract chipmaker seeks to broaden its ecosystem and "formalize" its investment activities amid the AI boom, a senior executive told Nikkei Asia.

Kevin Zhang, TSMC's deputy co-chief operating officer and senior vice president of business development and global sales, said the new fund, announced this week, could also invest in suppliers and other upstream partners, as the company aims to expand its ecosystem beyond its direct customers.

"We feel it's time to ...formalize this investment mechanism, and we also want to extend the scope [to] not only just target our immediate customers," Zhang said, revealing for the first time the rationale behind TSMC's decision to establish a dedicated investment arm. "We also want to use the opportunity to develop the broader ecosystem, potentially including our suppliers, for example, our upstream [partners]."

This would represent a change of approach for TSMC, which has not previously invested in its suppliers. The company relies on a vast supply chain that provides everything from specialty and advanced chemicals and materials to a wide range of chipmaking equipment and testing tools. Intellectual property providers are also classed as partners.

Zhang also explained the thinking behind TSMC's decision to invest up to $500 million each in Anthropic and OpenAI, two of the world's leading AI model developers, a move announced on Tuesday, the same day as the new investment arm.

"By investing in Anthropic or OpenAI, we create a reinforcing loop to basically build a richer and healthier and hopefully a bigger ecosystem," he said. "Our goal is to continue to drive the advancement of silicon technology to address the future computation requirement."

Both Anthropic and OpenAI are looking to develop their own custom chips, in some cases with key TSMC customers. OpenAI, for instance, is working with Broadcom on AI chips dubbed Jalapeno.

The new fund's initial $500 million is significantly larger than the roughly $200 million "emerging fund" TSMC established in 2021 to help startups tap the company's advanced chip manufacturing capabilities.

"The purpose of the [emerging] fund was really to help to lower the barrier for the startup company to be able to develop innovative products based on TSMC advanced node tech," Zhang said. TSMC's move to broaden its investment scope comes amid a massive AI infrastructure buildout that has led to prolonged shortages of critical materials and equipment.

Zhang said the decision to set up the venture investment arm underscores TSMC's commitment to supporting not only global chip giants through its manufacturing services but also emerging innovators across the semiconductor industry. TSMC is best known for manufacturing advanced chips for some of the world's leading chip designers, including Apple, Nvidia, Google and Qualcomm, among its more than 530 customers worldwide.

"We're not just working to support large customers," Zhang said. "When you talk about TSMC, you immediately think, you have Apple, you have Nvidia, you have AMD, you have Broadcom [as top clients]. Yes, those are great customers. But remember, when Nvidia started working with us, Nvidia was a startup."

"We not only support today's Nvidia, but we also want to support the future's Nvidia," the senior executive said.

TSMC has committed to invest up to $1.7 billion in total, which includes its 2021 emerging fund, the new investment arm and planned investments in OpenAI and Anthropic. It would not rule out expanding the investment fund further if needed, while returns from its original emerging fund had been "exceptional," according to Zhang.

title_zh: 台积电拟设5亿美元基金孵化芯片初创
summary_zh: 台积电计划设立5亿美元创投基金，旨在扶持上游供应链及芯片初创，构建更具韧性的半导体生态

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 台积电高级副总裁Kevin Zhang表示，公司将正式设立5亿美元规模的投资基金，投资范围由传统的先进制程客户拓展至上游供应商及芯片初创企业。该举措旨在通过资本纽带强化半导体生态韧性，同时配合此前向Anthropic及OpenAI的战略注资，通过“客户+供应商+AI模型”的三位一体布局，巩固其在全球AI计算领域的底层制造垄断地位。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 台积电此举标志着其从单纯的代工模式转型为“平台型生态主导者”，通过资本手段渗透上游核心材料与设备，意在解决先进制程产能扩张中可能出现的单点故障风险。通过向Anthropic与OpenAI注资，台积电实质上是在向芯片设计领域施加其标准定义权，迫使设计公司在初期研发阶段即对齐其制造节点的特性，从而进一步锁定客户的技术路径依赖。
ai_analysis.insight_en: TSMC’s move signifies a transition from a pure-play foundry to an ecosystem orchestrator, using capital to integrate upstream material and equipment suppliers to mitigate systemic failure risks. By investing in AI labs, TSMC is asserting its standard-setting influence over chip design, forcing designers to align with its process nodes early and deepening customer lock-in.

article_content_zh:
东京——一位高管告诉《日经亚洲》，台积电计划利用新的 5 亿美元风险基金来支持有前途的芯片初创公司，这些初创公司可能成为下一个英伟达或博通，因为这家全球最大的合约芯片制造商寻求在人工智能热潮中扩大其生态系统并“正规化”其投资活动。

台积电副联席首席运营官兼业务发展和全球销售高级副总裁张晓刚（Kevin Zhang）说，本周宣布的新基金还可能投资于供应商和其他上游合作伙伴，因为该公司的目标是将其生态系统扩展到直接客户之外。

张说：“我们觉得是时候……正式化这种投资机制了，我们还希望扩大范围，不仅仅是针对我们的直接客户。”他首次透露了台积电决定建立专门投资部门的理由。 “我们还希望利用这个机会开发更广泛的生态系统，可能包括我们的供应商，例如我们的上游[合作伙伴]。”

这将代表台积电方法的改变，该公司此前从未对其供应商进行投资。该公司依赖庞大的供应链，提供从特种和先进化学品和材料到各种芯片制造设备和测试工具的一切。知识产权提供商也被归类为合作伙伴。

张还解释了台积电决定向世界领先的人工智能模型开发商 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 各投资最多 5 亿美元背后的想法，这一举措于周二宣布，与新投资部门成立的同一天。

他说：“通过投资Anthropic或OpenAI，我们创建了一个强化循环，基本上建立了一个更丰富、更健康、更大的生态系统。”“我们的目标是继续推动硅技术的进步，以满足未来的计算需求。”

Anthropic 和 OpenAI 都在寻求开发自己的定制芯片，在某些情况下是与台积电的主要客户合作。例如，OpenAI 正在与 Broadcom 合作开发名为 Jalapeno 的人工智能芯片。

新基金的初始规模为 5 亿美元，远远高于台积电于 2021 年设立的约 2 亿美元的“新兴基金”，该基金旨在帮助初创企业利用该公司先进的芯片制造能力。

“[新兴]基金的目的实际上是帮助降低初创公司开发基于台积电先进节点技术的创新产品的门槛，”张说。台积电扩大投资范围之际，大规模的人工智能基础设施建设导致关键材料和设备长期短缺。

张表示，建立风险投资部门的决定突显了台积电不仅致力于通过其制造服务支持全球芯片巨头，而且还致力于支持整个半导体行业的新兴创新者。台积电因为一些全球领先的芯片设计公司制造先进芯片而闻名，其中包括苹果、英伟达、谷歌和高通，其全球客户超过 530 家。

“我们不仅仅致力于支持大客户，”张说。 “当你谈论台积电时，你会立即想到，你有苹果，你有英伟达，你有AMD，你有博通（作为顶级客户）。是的，这些都是伟大的客户。但请记住，当英伟达开始与我们合作时，英伟达还是一家初创公司。”

“我们不仅支持今天的英伟达，我们也希望支持未来的英伟达，”这位高管表示。

台积电已承诺投资总额高达 17 亿美元，其中包括其 2021 年新兴基金、新投资部门以及计划对 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的投资。张表示，如果需要的话，不排除进一步扩大投资基金的规模，而原来的新兴基金的回报率“非常高”。

title: Nvidia insiders say Jensen Huang was prone to wild office tantrums, which a source says some employees were surprised hadn't leaked before his public downfall (Thomas Barrabi/New York Post)
title_en: Nvidia insiders say Jensen Huang was prone to wild office tantrums, which a source says some employees were surprised hadn't leaked before his public downfall (Thomas Barrabi/New York Post)

author: New York Post
article_content:
Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was prone to wild temper tantrums at the office, according to company insiders — cruelly dressing down employees and even once hurling a water bottle at a top executive in a fit of rage, The Post has learned.

The 63-year-old chip magnate famously cultivated an affable, laid-back public persona, sporting black leather jackets and doling out TV interviews about his humble beginnings washing dishes and cleaning toilets.

But as Huang pushed to relentlessly grow Nvidia’s business, employees lived in fear of their boss skewering them with vicious outbursts at marathon meetings in front of their peers, according to sources close to the company.

Last February, at a closed-door powwow with more than 30 company executives in attendance, Huang zeroed in on Jay Puri, Nvidia’s then-executive vice president of worldwide field operations, sources told The Post.

“I hope you get the flu and I hope it gets worse,” Huang told Puri in front of stunned onlookers — including Puri, who endured the sudden attack in silence, according to a source familiar to the incident.

“I hope you die and put us all out of our misery,” Huang added.

At the time, Puri oversaw Nvidia’s sales and business development operations. He has since transitioned to a role as senior adviser for Nvidia. It couldn’t immediately be learned what had been at issue during the meeting.

“It’s very typical for Jensen to yell at people, but when he said that specific thing to Jay, it was extremely tense and quiet,” one of the sources said. “Everybody was a little bit shocked.”

Puri couldn’t immediately be reached for comment.

The confrontation with Puri was part of a pattern with Huang – who oversaw an unusual corporate structure where more than 60 of Nvidia’s top executives reported directly to him.

Indeed, Huang’s outbursts are so well-known at Nvidia that some employees have expressed surprise that they didn’t leak prior to his public downfall, one source said.

During a tense, three-hour meeting in 2025, Huang directed harsh words at a senior sales leader with about 40 staffers in attendance, the sources said.

“You don’t know dick about my business,” Huang allegedly told the sales executive.

Elsewhere, sources briefed on the matter described a well-known clash in which Huang lost his temper with a senior leader who was attending a meeting with the mercurial boss for the first time.

“Are you smirking at me? I see nothing but dead faces … Get out!” Huang shouted before kicking the executive from the room, according to sources.

The sources also described a now-infamous incident inside the halls of Nvidia’s Santa Clara, Calif. headquarters — in which Huang allegedly threw a water bottle at a top executive during a meeting.

Huang resigned on Thursday after admitting he had an extramarital affair with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang. The pair are not related. In total, Huang is alleged to have had affairs with at least three women, including Nvidia’s vice president of health care Kimberly Powell, according to reports.

As The Post reported, Huang misled top Nvidia executives for more than a year about his affair with Alice Huang, leaving them with egg on their faces when he was finally forced to admit the truth after days of public denials.

A spokesman for Huang declined comment. Nvidia did not immediately respond to The Post’s inquiry.

Nvidia chief financial officer Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO while the company’s board searches for a permanent successor.

In yet another reported instance of Huang flying off the handle, the Wall Street Journal reported on an August meeting in which he interrupted Kress in the middle of a presentation, calling her “a deer in the headlights.”

Stephen Witt, the author of “The Thinking Machine,” a biography of Huang, wrote in a New York Times article on Thursday that Huang liked to appear humble, always praising his employees, reminding others of his time spent as a dishwasher and leaving a huge tip at their visits to Denny’s.

But it was all “to cloak his arrogance,” Witt claimed. “He had little tolerance for disagreement and almost no capacity for open discourse. When you contradicted him, even over the most trivial matter, it was like lighting a fuse. Stick to your position, and soon he exploded, screaming at you for your idiocy.”

Huang could also be tough with executives outside his company, according to the report. At a conference in Berlin, Huang told half a dozen tech CEOs who were Nvidia customers a story that sounded like a fable about a soup vendor in Japan.

Huang told the CEOs gathered at a table that after waiting in line for a long time, he had one of the most delicious bowls of soup he’d ever tasted. When Huang asked for another bowl, the soup vendor refused, saying there wouldn’t be enough left for the rest of the customers who were waiting.

“He’s a better businessperson than all of you,” Huang reportedly told the cloud computing CEOs, noting that the soup seller kept his prices high and his customer base diverse.

“You are not establishing the value of my products,” Huang said, according to the paper.

Nvidia’s press release that revealed Huang’s resignation did not include any statement from Huang, who has retained the white-shoe law firm Paul Weiss while preparing to testify on Capitol Hill about the “spy” affair.

They also want Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to explain their respective roles in impeding strict export controls that might have otherwise stopped Megaspeed from gaining access to the AI hardware.

article_content_zh:
据公司内部人士透露，被赶下台的英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在办公室里很容易发脾气，残忍地训斥员工，甚至有一次盛怒之下向高管投掷水瓶。

这位 63 岁的芯片大亨以塑造了一种和蔼可亲、悠闲自在的公众形象而闻名，他穿着黑色皮夹克，接受电视采访，讲述自己洗碗和打扫厕所的卑微出身。

但据接近该公司的消息人士透露，随着黄仁勋不断推动英伟达业务的发展，员工们担心老板会在同事面前的马拉松式会议上恶毒地发脾气来攻击他们。

消息人士告诉《华盛顿邮报》，去年 2 月，在一次有 30 多名公司高管出席的闭门会议上，黄把矛头对准了英伟达时任全球现场运营执行副总裁杰伊·普里 (Jay Puri)。

黄在震惊的旁观者面前对普里说：“我希望你得了流感，而且希望情况变得更糟。”普里也默默地忍受了这突如其来的袭击。

黄补充道：“我希望你死掉，让我们所有人摆脱痛苦。”

当时，普里负责监督英伟达的销售和业务开发运营。此后，他转任英伟达高级顾问。目前尚无法立即了解会议期间发生的问题。

“詹森对人大喊大叫是很典型的事情，但当他对杰伊说这件事时，气氛非常紧张和安静，”一位消息人士说。 “每个人都有点震惊。”

记者未能立即联系到普里置评。

与普里的对峙是黄仁勋模式的一部分，黄仁勋领导着一个不寻常的公司结构，其中 60 多名英伟达高管直接向他汇报。

事实上，一位消息人士称，黄仁勋的爆发在英伟达是如此出名，以至于一些员工对黄仁勋在公开垮台之前没有泄密表示惊讶。

消息人士称，在 2025 年举行的一场紧张的、长达三个小时的会议上，黄向一名与会约 40 名员工的高级销售负责人发表了严厉的言论。

据称，黄告诉销售主管：“你根本不了解我的生意。”

在其他地方，了解此事的消息人士描述了一次众所周知的冲突，黄在第一次与这位反复无常的老板开会时对一位高级领导人发了脾气。

title: How Jensen Huang built a multibillion-dollar business to let Chinese companies access Nvidia AI chips in SE Asian data centers, exploiting a gap in US sanctions (Wall Street Journal)
title_en: How Jensen Huang built a multibillion-dollar business to let Chinese companies access Nvidia AI chips in SE Asian data centers, exploiting a gap in US sanctions (Wall Street Journal)
author: Wall Street Journal
article_content:
Jensen Huang and Nvidia have propelled the AI boom that has lifted the stock market and driven data center construction.

It took more than 30 years for Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang to grow his start-up from a minnow of the video game industry to one of the world’s most valuable companies.

His signature leather jacket, frequent media appearances and close relationship with President Donald Trump made Huang one of the most iconic CEOs of the artificial intelligence era, providing computer chips and financing that have helped sustain an economic boom that has lifted millions of investment and retirement accounts. He helped reshape U.S. policy toward China.
content_snippet: Massive data centers in Southeast Asia exploited a gap in U.S. sanctions, providing crucial computing power for Chinese companies and a cover for alleged chip smuggling
summary_en: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has established a high-performance computing network in Southeast Asian nations, including Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia, providing Chinese firms access to advanced AI chips via cloud-based leasing. This strategy exploits current U.S. export control loopholes by shifting from physical hardware delivery to cross-border compute resource consumption.

title_zh: 英伟达创始人黄仁勋构建东南亚算力生态绕开对华制裁
summary_zh: 英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋通过在东南亚建立数据中心算力网络，为中国企业提供高端AI芯片访问权限，从而规避美国出口管制
article_content_zh:
英伟达目前已在多个东南亚国家通过合作伙伴建立了大规模数据中心集群，这些中心部署了其受限的GPU架构。根据最新的产业观察，这种模式将原本应当受控的产品交付转化为合规范围内的服务消费，规避了直接将芯片出口至中国境内的合规合规审查流程。

随着美国地缘政治压力加大，黄仁勋采取了多元化的市场策略。通过将算力算力枢纽布局在不受直接禁令影响的东南亚司法管辖区，英伟达不仅保证了全球供应链的物流弹性，还通过API访问和云实例销售，成功实现了对中国AI企业的技术输出，这一做法正成为监管机构下一步闭环管理的重点博弈领域。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋通过在新加坡、马来西亚及印度尼西亚等地部署高性能计算数据中心，构筑算力云端租用体系，使受美国对华技术出口限制的中国企业得以跨境调用算力资源。此举利用了美国现行出口管制法案对“地理管辖权”的边界模糊，通过租赁模型规避了物理芯片直接交付的合规红线。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has established a high-performance computing network in Southeast Asian nations, including Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia, providing Chinese firms access to advanced AI chips via cloud-based leasing. This strategy exploits current U.S. export control loopholes by shifting from physical hardware delivery to cross-border compute resource consumption.

elements_zh.who: 英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang)
elements_zh.where: 东南亚区域数据中心（新加坡、马来西亚、印度尼西亚）
elements_zh.what: 构建算力租赁生态，向受制裁中国企业提供AI算力访问权
elements_zh.why: 规避美国商务部针对H100/A100及后续高性能芯片的对华出口禁令

elements_en.where: Southeast Asian data centers (Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia)
elements_en.what: Establishing compute-as-a-service infrastructure to provide AI chip access to sanctioned Chinese entities
elements_en.why: Circumventing U.S. Commerce Department restrictions on high-end AI chip exports to China

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此举揭示了基于物理芯片交付的管制逻辑在云服务时代面临失效困境，监管机构若要彻底封堵，必须将管控阈值从“产品出口”转向“算力访问权限的跨境授权”。英伟达通过这种‘租用代替买卖’的商业模式，有效维持了中国市场的营收渗透率，同时也迫使美国监管层加速审核针对云计算基础设施的附加限制性条款。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This move highlights the obsolescence of hardware-centric export controls in the cloud era, necessitating a shift toward regulating cross-border access to compute. Nvidia’s leasing model effectively preserves market share in China, likely compelling U.S. regulators to tighten restrictions on compute-as-a-service infrastructure.

title: The Nvidia scandal presents a political challenge for the White House by tying together data centers, China, and corruption, all key voter issues in midterms (Washington Post)
title_en: The Nvidia scandal presents a political challenge for the White House by tying together data centers, China, and corruption, all key voter issues in midterms (Washington Post)
author: Washington Post
article_content:
The scandal connects to voter concerns over AI, data centers, China and corruption.

Sex. Money. Power. Espionage. As Washington scandals go, this one has everything.

But what really makes ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy an explosive political problem for the White House is that it brings together the very issues that propelled Democrats to their largest congressional majority since 1990. Voters revolted against President Donald Trump’s handling of the economy, with widespread concerns about artificial intelligence, data centers, competition from China, and special access and favors for billionaires.

article_content_zh:
黄仁勋作为全球AI算力基础设施核心领袖，其个人关联度已不仅是企业内部治理范畴，而是直接演变为动摇华盛顿科技外交公信力的政治丑闻。在当前美国国内AI算力基建竞赛背景下，该事件被反对党视为攻击现行产业政策的关键突破口，旨在质疑政府在赋予企业获取能源、土地及芯片出口许可权时的监管失职。

针对英伟达的舆论反噬反映了美国政界对科技寡头过度掌控国家级战略资源（如高算力GPU与大模型部署）的深度焦虑。预计后续联邦政府将通过国会听证会，进一步强化针对顶级芯片厂商高层及其海外分支机构的背景调查程序，这将直接冲击全球GPU供应链的稳定与合规执行效率。

title: Silicon Valley’s Group Chats Are Having a Moment of Jensanity

author: Bloomberg
content_snippet: As the Nvidia drama unfolds, the tech community adds yet another geek-turned-billionaire to its list of flawed visionaries.

title: Tech Giants Face More Grid Cost Pressure on Democratic Sweep
title_en: Tech Giants Face More Grid Cost Pressure on Democratic Sweep
author: Bloomberg
content_snippet: Tech giants chasing the infinite promise of AI are finding themselves increasingly on the hook for something far earthier — the electrical grid.
summary_en: Data center operator Applied Digital has been requiring tenants, including Oracle and Meta, to provide billion-dollar guarantees to secure power since last year. This strategy aims to hedge the substantial upfront capital expenditure associated with energy procurement and secure power allocations for AI computing clusters.

title_en: Unlike other larger-than-life tech founders, Jensen Huang lacked super-voting shares in Nvidia, making it easier for him to lose control of the company (Forbes)
author: Forbes
content_snippet: This voice experience is generated by AI. Learn more. — Many tech CEOs including Mark Zuckerberg, Michael Dell and Evan Spiegel have majority voting power.
summary_en: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang operates without super-voting shares, creating a governance structure more susceptible to shareholder influence compared to peers like Meta or Google. This ownership model lacks the traditional anti-takeover protections found in other tech giants, leaving the company's long-term strategic direction more exposed to institutional investor pressure.
title_zh: 黄仁勋在英伟达缺乏超级投票权治理风险
summary_zh: 英伟达创始人黄仁勋未持有超级投票权股票，相比其他硅谷科技巨头，其对公司决策控制力在法律架构上更易受股东变动挑战

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 英伟达创始人、总裁兼首席执行官黄仁勋在公司治理结构中未设置超级投票权（Super-voting shares），使其在面对大规模机构投资者或潜在敌意并购时，防御机制弱于谷歌或Meta等双层股权结构企业。这一架构使公司更易受资本市场波动与股东集体行为的影响，在追求长期战略稳定性与外部资本诉求之间存在天然张力。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang operates without super-voting shares, creating a governance structure more susceptible to shareholder influence compared to peers like Meta or Google. This ownership model lacks the traditional anti-takeover protections found in other tech giants, leaving the company's long-term strategic direction more exposed to institutional investor pressure.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 英伟达目前作为全球AI算力基础设施的核心，其治理架构的透明度与民主化虽降低了代理成本，但在AI产业进入地缘政治博弈深水区时，缺乏“金股”保护可能成为其在面对激进资本或外部地缘压力时的战略短板。相较于科技行业流行的创始人独裁模式，英伟达更依赖于公司治理的合规性与市场表现带来的声誉资本，而非强制性的股权压制。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Nvidia’s governance model prioritizes institutional transparency over founder-centric control, which provides liquidity but lacks the structural defenses against activist investors or geopolitical pressure. As the firm becomes a critical pillar of global AI infrastructure, the absence of super-voting shares shifts the strategic burden from founder absolute power to sustained performance excellence to maintain investor alignment.

title: Letter: Altimeter's Brad Gerstner and Atreides's Gavin Baker urge Nvidia's board to consider "the potential return of Jensen Huang"; they own $2.13B in Nvidia (Katie Tarasov/CNBC)
title_en: Letter: Altimeter's Brad Gerstner and Atreides's Gavin Baker urge Nvidia's board to consider "the potential return of Jensen Huang"; they own $2.13B in Nvidia (Katie Tarasov/CNBC)

inline_images.caption: thumbnail
inline_images.alt: thumbnail

inline_images.caption: Experts assess the fallout from Nvidia's spy scandal and what it means for AI stocks
inline_images.alt: Experts assess the fallout from Nvidia's spy scandal and what it means for AI stocks

inline_images.caption: The rise, reinvention and uncertain future of Nvidia without Jensen Huang

author: CNBC
article_content:
Two major Nvidia shareholders are calling on the board of directors to weigh all options for the company's future leadership, including "the potential return of Jensen Huang."

Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner posted a letter on X on Friday that urges Nvidia's board to "pursue a slow, measured, and deliberate process regarding the future leadership of Nvidia." The letter is also signed by Atreides Management's Gavin Baker.

Nvidia was Altimeter Capital's largest disclosed equity holding in its most recent SEC filing, with a 9.4 million-share stake worth nearly $1.9 billion as of June 30. Atreides held 1.2 million shares worth nearly $250 million at the end of June.

The letter said Nvidia will be "capably led" by interim CEO Colette Kress, who served as Nvidia's CFO for 13 years before the board announced Thursday that she'd lead the company in Huang's absence.

"But the Founder and long time incredible leader of this extraordinary company has earned the right for a deliberate process that avoids any needless rush to replace him before all the facts are known," the letter concludes. The document did not call for Huang's immediate reinstatement.

Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday amid multiple affair allegations, including one with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang, who also worked with Nvidia customer Megaspeed. The Singapore-based company is being investigated by the Justice Department for possibly redirecting some of its supply of Nvidia's restricted artificial intelligence chips to China.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said on X Friday that he signed a petition asking to reinstate Huang. A petition circulating online called "Stand with Jensen" claims to have more than 100,000 signatures, including more than 5,000 current Nvidia employees.

Musk said on X Saturday that without Huang, some "critical deals will be lost."

Another letter sent Friday called on U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick to testify about Megaspeed before the House Intelligence Committee.

Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10 about whether the Commerce Department is "properly performing its broader role of preventing China from acquiring advanced AI chips," according to the letter. Huang has also been asked to testify.

The Commerce Department originally launched an investigation into Megaspeed that was moved to the Justice Department in 2025 after Nvidia's lawyer contacted a senior Commerce official, according to The New York Times.

President Donald Trump is scheduled to visit China on Thursday, but doesn't plan to raise Nvidia and the suspected spy affair during his meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping, according to U.S. officials. Musk is expected to join Trump on the trip to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit on Nov. 18 and 19.

article_content_zh:
英伟达的两大股东呼吁董事会权衡公司未来领导层的所有选择，包括“黄仁勋的潜在回报”。

Altimeter Capital 首席执行官布拉德·格斯特纳 (Brad Gerstner) 周五在 X 上发布了一封信，敦促 Nvidia 董事会“在有关 Nvidia 未来领导地位的问题上采取缓慢、谨慎和深思熟虑的流程”。这封信还由 Atreides Management 的 Gavin Baker 签署。

Nvidia 是 Altimeter Capital 在其最近向 SEC 提交的文件中披露的最大股权，截至 6 月 30 日，该公司持有 940 万股股票，价值近 19 亿美元。截至 6 月底，Atreides 持有 120 万股，价值近 2.5 亿美元。

信中称，英伟达将由临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)“有能力地领导”，科莱特·克雷斯曾担任英伟达首席财务官13年，之后董事会周四宣布，她将在黄仁勋缺席的情况下领导公司。

信中总结道：“但这家非凡公司的创始人和长期以来令人难以置信的领导者已经赢得了经过深思熟虑的程序的权利，以避免在了解所有事实之前不必要地急于更换他。”该文件没有要求黄立即复职。

Nvidia 创始人黄仁勋周四因多项婚外情指控而辞职，其中包括涉嫌与中国间谍 Alice Huang 的一项指控，后者也与 Nvidia 客户 Megaspeed 合作。这家总部位于新加坡的公司正在接受司法部的调查，原因是其可能将部分英伟达受限人工智能芯片供应转移到中国。

SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 周五表示，他签署了一份请愿书，要求恢复黄的职位。网上流传的一份名为“与 Jensen 站在一起”的请愿书声称已有超过 10 万名签名，其中包括 5000 多名 Nvidia 现任员工。

马斯克周六表示，如果没有黄仁勋，一些“关键交易将会丢失”。

周五发出的另一封信呼吁美国商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克在众议院情报委员会就 Megaspeed 问题作证。

信中称，卢特尼克已同意于 12 月 10 日在参议院银行委员会作证，说明商务部是否“正确履行了阻止中国获取先进人工智能芯片的更广泛职责”。黄也被要求出庭作证。

据《纽约时报》报道，商务部最初对 Megaspeed 发起了调查，在 Nvidia 的律师联系了商务部高级官员后，该调查于 2025 年移交给司法部。

据美国官员称，唐纳德·特朗普总统定于周四访问中国，但不打算在与中国国家主席习近平会面时提及英伟达和涉嫌间谍事件。预计马斯克将与特朗普一起前往中国深圳，参加 11 月 18 日至 19 日举行的亚太经合组织峰会。
