title: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back to Life After a 24-Hour Outage
title_en: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back to Life After a 24-Hour Outage
author: Wired AI
article_content:
Sorry, Margaret, your email is working again.

After a widespread outage shut down Microsoft 365 services for businesses, governments, and tens of millions of other users around the world, the essential cloud services are now (mostly) back online, according to the company’s status page.

The outage debacle began around lunchtime on the East Coast on Thursday, with users reporting Outlook outages to the service-tracking website Downdetector just after 12 pm ET. Within the hour, Microsoft said it was investigating reports of an outage that at the time was limited to North America. It quickly spread to impact more than 70 countries around the world.

The full cause of Microsoft’s unprecedented outage remains unknown, but the company repeatedly ruled out a cyberattack as the cause in statements to its status page. It is also ruling out AI or AI agents playing a role in the debacle.

“We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services,” a Microsoft spokesperson says in a statement. “This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.”

The company has promised a “full post-incident report” after it has fully reviewed what went wrong.

As Outlook, Teams, Copilot, and other Microsoft 365 systems come back online, users will likely see their inboxes turn into a mess. “You're probably going to get a lot of notifications when things come back,” says Jonathan Leitschuh, an independent researcher.

Microsoft said it had increased the queue time for emails to 48 hours in an attempt to ensure that every message that people tried to send while its systems were down gets delivered. Leitschuh points out that, even with the bulk of systems restored, users may receive “a flood of notifications a few hours down the pike” as subsystems come back online.

The total impact of the Microsoft outage may never be fully known, but it’s safe to say it’s already significant. Governments from Japan to the United States reported disruptions to a bevy of functions. Airlines reported problems with their ability to communicate with customers. Many law enforcement and emergency services ground to a halt. And hospitals reported widespread interruptions to their operations.

Ultimately, the episode serves as a reminder of the risks involved when the whole world relies on a single company for a critical service. “We're very interdependent on these systems in modern life,” says Leitschuh. Next time, delayed emails may be the least of our worries.

article_content_zh:
抱歉，玛格丽特，您的电子邮件已恢复正常。

根据该公司的状态页面，在大范围的故障关闭了为企业、政府和全球数千万其他用户提供的 Microsoft 365 服务后，基本的云服务现在（大部分）重新上线。

故障灾难始于周四东海岸的午餐时间左右，美国东部时间中午 12 点刚过，用户就向服务跟踪网站 DownDetector 报告了 Outlook 故障。一个小时内，微软表示正在调查当时仅限于北美地区的宕机报告。它迅速蔓延影响全球70多个国家。

微软史无前例的宕机的完整原因尚不清楚，但该公司在其状态页面的声明中一再排除网络攻击的原因。它还排除了人工智能或人工智能代理在这场灾难中发挥作用的可能性。

微软发言人在一份声明中表示：“我们的服务得到了广泛的恢复和稳定。” “这是一个与网络或人工智能/代理无关的技术问题。该事件是由近期网络变更后出现的早期网络容量升级过程中的一个问题引起的。我们已经解决了根本问题，并继续为其余客户和地区恢复服务。”

该公司承诺在全面审查问题原因后提供“完整的事件后报告”。

随着 Outlook、Teams、Copilot 和其他 Microsoft 365 系统重新上线，用户可能会看到他们的收件箱变得一团糟。 “当事情恢复时，你可能会收到很多通知，”独立研究员 Jonathan Leitschuh 说。

微软表示，它已将电子邮件的排队时间延长至 48 小时，以确保人们在系统停机时尝试发送的每条消息都能送达。 Leitschuh 指出，即使大部分系统已恢复，当子系统恢复在线时，用户也可能会“在几个小时内收到大量通知”。

微软宕机的总体影响可能永远无法完全知晓，但可以肯定地说影响已经很严重了。从日本到美国，各国政府均报告称一系列职能受到干扰。航空公司报告称其与客户沟通的能力存在问题。许多执法和紧急服务陷入停滞。医院报告称其运营大范围中断。

最终，这一事件提醒人们，当全世界都依赖一家公司提供关键服务时所涉及的风险。 “在现代生活中，我们非常依赖这些系统，”Leitschuh 说。下次，延迟的电子邮件可能是我们最不用担心的了。

title: OpenAI rebuilt AI shopping from scratch with ChatGPT Wallet
title_en: OpenAI rebuilt AI shopping from scratch with ChatGPT Wallet
author: THE DECODER
article_content:
OpenAI is taking a second shot at AI shopping with ChatGPT Wallet, catching up with rivals like Anthropic, Meta, and xAI, whose agents can already shop online.

To get started, users add their card once. Before every purchase, the system displays the items, the total, and the selected card. Users then approve each payment with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint.Ad

Neither the agent nor the online store ever sees the real card details. Instead, payment partners American Express, Mastercard, and Visa generate a payment token, a stand-in card number with its own security code. According to OpenAI, existing card rewards and the usual bank protections for eligible disputes still apply. OpenAI plans to eventually let users hand purchases off to their agents entirely, within set spending limits, product categories, and timeframes.Ad

According to OpenAI, a purchase starts with the customer describing what they want, after which ChatGPT searches the open web, APIs, or merchant product feeds for options, and the user compares them and picks one. ChatGPT then completes the purchase either by using a browser on the merchant's existing website or through a plugin that supports structured actions such as managing the cart.

Many websites and payment systems still block AI agents as bots or reject their purchases for security reasons. To address that, OpenAI is also releasing a Commerce Partner Playbook. The guide explains how merchants can adjust their firewalls, provide product data, and work with payment providers such as Stripe, Adyen, and Riskified so agent-driven purchases go through.Ad

OpenAI is playing catch-up on payment features for AI agents. Competitors such as Anthropic's Claude Duet, Meta's Muse, and xAI's Grok Bot already have built-in payments and rely in part on single-use cards via Stripe Link. Google and Perplexity also let users buy through their own checkout tools, such as Google Pay and Instant Buy.

title: Banks bar Chinese and Hong Kong investors from Anthropic IPO over US export controls
title_en: Banks bar Chinese and Hong Kong investors from Anthropic IPO over US export controls
author: THE DECODER
article_content:
Investors from mainland China and Hong Kong are being shut out of Anthropic's IPO, according to Bloomberg. Multiple banks have reportedly rejected buy orders from those regions or consider allocations unlikely, with some of the people involved citing ITAR, the US export control rules governing defense-related goods, as the reason. Anthropic declined to comment.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the offering, with 20 other banks involved. The stock is expected to trade on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT after pricing on November 18.

The company's products aren't officially available in China or Hong Kong, and its broader relationship with the country has been defined by confrontation. Anthropic has blocked firms under Chinese control from its AI services and is fighting workarounds that let Chinese companies access Claude Code. It also exposed large-scale distillation attacks by DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax involving some 16 million queries.AdAd

title: Anthropic's Claude for Manufacturing plugs AI directly into factory software to automate industrial workflows
title_en: Anthropic's Claude for Manufacturing plugs AI directly into factory software to automate industrial workflows
author: THE DECODER
article_content:
Anthropic has released Claude for Manufacturing, a plugin giving the AI direct access to industrial software to automate factory workflows. The new solution connects via four universal interfaces to Autodesk Fusion, Oracle NetSuite, Microsoft 365, and Infor. Other systems can be integrated through file exports to Microsoft 365.

With 17 specific skills, the AI drafts quotes from actual inventory, compares suppliers, generates quality reports and design variants, and analyzes sensor data and manuals during machine downtime. Via an added Infor plugin, Claude can also order from backup suppliers when deliveries are delayed and reschedule production—after human approval. All results are linked to original source documents for employee review before reaching customers or suppliers.

The plugin is available to Team and Enterprise customers but doesn't control physical machines yet. For that, Anthropic is separately developing the Model Hardware Standard as a research preview, connecting AI agents to devices like robotic arms and microscopes via standardized drivers. This cuts setup time from weeks or months to hours or minutes but still requires human oversight due to the AI's limited grasp of physical processes.AdAd

title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
title_en: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
author: Ars Technica
article_content:
“SignDrop” exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights.

Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day.

On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System, which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System.

The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions. The exploit uses Windows Defender to open a log file created by a standard user by calling ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature, a legitimate Defender function for processing antivirus signature updates.

By manipulating Windows Object Manager symbolic links, the attacker causes Defender to open the CLFS container in the security context of the antimalware engine. If an associated authentication file is missing, CLFS creates it using Defender’s System privileges. Because CLFS assigns the newly created file the Discretionary Access Control List of the original file, the attacker may gain access to a file created with System privileges, allowing the file-creation operation to be abused as part of a privilege-escalation attack.

Ironically, the vulnerability stems from a security measure Microsoft introduced in October 2025 to prevent attackers from exploiting other vulnerabilities in CLFS.

“If everything is chained correctly, funnily this legit security mitigation can be used against itself and allow an elevation [of] privileges,” Nightmare Eclipse wrote. “Everything is done properly by Microsoft here but the logic allows abuse.”

What makes it funnier is the fact that it can be used against any antimalware engine to bypass their self defense (or tamper protection) mechanism as you can trigger arbitrary file creation in the context of their own antimalware process so from the perspective of their kernel drivers, the file creation request is coming from their own legit process so it passes, this makes this vulnerability unique as it can be used to turn off any antivirus/EDR.

Nightmare Eclipse said the exploit worked against Windows 11 26H2, Windows 11 26H2 Experimental, and Windows Server 2025 Experimental. People can see if their systems are vulnerable by checking the CLFS authentication mode. If it’s in learning mode or enforcement mode, the system is vulnerable, and the PoC supplied in the post should spawn a SYSTEM shell. Nightmare Eclipse has published numerous other Windows zero-days in recent months.

Researcher Will Dormann said in an interview that he has been able to reproduce the exploit and that it works as described, but not on all versions of Windows 11. But there’s a catch, he said.

“The requirements are important in that it seems to require Windows 26H2, and one that has existed for more than 90 days, it seems,” he explained. “That is, you can’t just take a new 26H2 system and install updates and have it work.”

For a system to be vulnerable, Dormann said, the HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CLFS\Authentication\Mode value must be 0 or 1.” Of the many machines Dormann uses, only a single one met this requirement.

Microsoft does staged rollouts of Windows updates, such as 26H2, so it’s not clear how many people have it. You can check by running the “winver” command. In a statement sent after this post went live, Microsoft said it was investigating the writeup and had no evidence the vulnerability was being exploited in the wild. The company also said Defender blocks potential exploitation attempts.

This story was updated to add Microsoft’s comment.

article_content_zh:
“SignDrop”漏洞让本地用户获得全能的系统权限。

Nightmare Eclipse 是一名研究人员的化名，该研究人员一直在公开地与微软发生争执，该公司又发布了另一个 Windows 零日漏洞。

周二，Nightmare Eclipse 披露了 SignDrop，这是一个为本地用户提供某些 Windows 版本的完全系统权限的漏洞。该漏洞存在于通用日志文件系统中，微软将其描述为“在用户模式或内核模式下运行的软件客户端使用的通用日志服务”。通过强制 Windows Defender 等特权进程打开精心设计的 CLFS 容器，具有普通用户权限的攻击者可以滥用特权文件创建来将权限提升到 System.

该攻击利用 CLFS、Windows Defender 和 Windows 文件权限的交互。该漏洞利用 Windows Defender 打开标准用户通过调用 ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature 创建的日志文件，ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature 是用于处理防病毒签名更新的合法 Defender 函数。

通过操纵 Windows 对象管理器符号链接，攻击者使 Defender 在反恶意软件引擎的安全上下文中打开 CLFS 容器。如果关联的身份验证文件丢失，CLFS 将使用 Defender 的系统权限创建它。由于 CLFS 为新创建的文件分配原始文件的自主访问控制列表，因此攻击者可能会获得对使用系统权限创建的文件的访问权限，从而允许文件创建操作被滥用作为权限升级攻击的一部分。

讽刺的是，该漏洞源于微软于 2025 年 10 月推出的一项安全措施，旨在防止攻击者利用 CLFS 中的其他漏洞。

Nightmare Eclipse 写道：“如果一切都正确链接，有趣的是，这种合法的安全缓解措施可以用来对付自身，并允许特权提升。” “微软在这里所做的一切都是正确的，但逻辑允许滥用。”

更有趣的是，它可以用于对抗任何反恶意软件引擎，以绕过其自我防御（或篡改保护）机制，因为您可以在其自己的反恶意软件进程的上下文中触发任意文件创建，因此从其内核驱动程序的角度来看，文件创建请求来自其自己的合法进程，因此它会通过，这使得该漏洞独一无二，因为它可用于关闭任何防病毒/EDR。

Nightmare Eclipse 表示，该漏洞适用于 Windows 11 26H2、Windows 11 26H2 Experimental 和 Windows Server 2025 Experimental。人们可以通过检查 CLFS 身份验证模式来了解自己的系统是否存在漏洞。如果处于学习模式或强制模式，系统很容易受到攻击，并且帖子中提供的 PoC 应该会生成一个 SYSTEM shell。近几个月来，Nightmare Eclipse 发布了许多其他 Windows 零日漏洞。

研究员 Will Dormann 在接受采访时表示，他已经能够重现该漏洞，并且其工作原理与描述的一样，但并非在所有版本的 Windows 11 上都有效。但他说，有一个问题。

“这些要求很重要，因为它似乎需要 Windows 26H2，而且这个版本似乎已经存在了 90 多天，”他解释道。 “也就是说，你不能只采用新的 26H2 系统并安装更新并让它工作。”

Dormann 表示，要使系统容易受到攻击，HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CLFS\Authentication\Mode 值必须为 0 或 1。在多曼使用的众多机器中，只有一台满足这一要求。

微软确实分阶段推出了 Windows 更新，例如 26H2，因此尚不清楚有多少人拥有它。您可以通过运行“winver”命令进行检查。在这篇文章发布后发布的一份声明中，微软表示正在调查该文章，并且没有证据表明该漏洞正在被利用。该公司还表示，Defender 会阻止潜在的利用尝试。

这个故事已更新以添加微软的评论。

title: Jensen Huang and the End of the Founder Fairy Tale
title_en: Jensen Huang and the End of the Founder Fairy Tale
author: Wired AI
article_content:
It was July of 2024, and Jensen Huang was punchy.

I had agreed to travel to Denver, Colorado, to interview the Nvidia CEO at SIGGRAPH, the annual confab of computer graphics PhDs and practitioners. Early that year I’d conducted a lengthy sit-down interview with Huang for a WIRED magazine feature, which apparently went well enough—both for WIRED and for Nvidia’s executive communications team—that I had been asked to interview Huang again at this conference. Another opportunity to grill the CEO of the modern world’s most consequential company? Yes, of course. I began preparing.

What ensued was, in a word, bizarre. During the first prep call for the conference, the type of call-in which PR handlers typically try to coax specific questions out of journalists to prevent an ambush, a youngish, vaguely familiar woman took the lead. This was Madison Huang, Jensen’s daughter. She was clearly intelligent, commanding respect. She told me about the slides Jensen would be presenting on stage at SIGGRAPH and offered suggestions for key moments when I might tee him up to talk about the slides.

Slides? Tee up Jensen? What kind of “interview” was this?

I raised my concerns with both my editors and Nvidia. We agreed that I would ask the questions I intended to ask him, which included questions about the environmental impact of data centers, and that Huang would also be referring to slides. Let’s just say the interview didn’t go smoothly. (It’s on YouTube.) To this day, former and current Nvidia workers sometimes tell me that I “handled” the whole thing well. Huang was domineering, evaded some of my questions, and, immediately after our session concluded, did an impromptu Q&A session with a much more adoring crowd than me. Then I was guided offstage, and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg hopped on, where he and Huang had a lovey-dovey fireside chat.

As a longtime journalist I’m used to occasional adversarial interactions; I really don’t lose sleep over them. This was just a CEO being a CEO. Huang later agreed to meet with me again, in December 2024. But that interview in Denver had underscored for me how much Jensen Huang wanted to control the narrative. Not just wanted to; he assumed he would. And to a large extent he did. Until this week.

Narrative has always been a critical part of Huang’s success. He was not just your average electrical engineering nerd who toiled away on something that would eventually find a product-market fit. By Huang’s own telling, he was an immigrant founder, an underdog, a wife guy who chased (and eventually married) his college sweetheart, a scrappy startup guy who dined at Denny’s in the early days. A visionary who worked Sundays and who didn’t sleep well because he always heard the hoof steps of competitors. A parent who brought his kids into the corporate fold. A man who loved Nvidia so much he tattooed an abstract version of the company logo on his arm.

Huang built the highest-valued publicly traded company in history. That part’s not just fairy tale. It’s true. Now, it’s starting to read more like a Greek tragedy.

Back in January 2024, when I sat down with him for our first-ever in-person meeting, Huang right off the bat talked about the importance of storytelling. Here’s an excerpt:

Jensen Huang: Somebody who I really admire, as a leader and a person, is Shantanu Narayen, the CEO of Adobe. He said he always wanted to be a journalist because he loved telling stories.

WIRED: It seems like an important part of building a business, being able to tell its story effectively.

Yes. Strategy setting is storytelling. Culture building is storytelling.

You’ve said many times you didn’t sell the idea of Nvidia based on a pitch deck.

That’s right. It was really about telling the story.

Of course, even then, Huang was caught up in the crosshairs of the US–China AI war and at the mercy of regulators, as I wrote at the time. After Donald Trump’s reelection that year, Huang once again deployed his storytelling skills and lobbied the Trump administration to loosen export controls, so he could sell some of his company’s chips to China.

Another crucial part of the Huang lore is that he ran a “flat” organization, with a few dozen top executives reporting to him. (This is sometimes reported as being “60” people; insiders have told me at times it’s closer to 35.) Huang once said the structure allowed Nvidia “to adapt a lot more quickly, which we need because our technology is moving so quickly.” Huang was also known to be controlling of all aspects of the business—participating in every significant meeting, seemingly aware of every moving part, and staying in the loop on sourcing, supply chains, and the company’s allocation of chips.

This is where Huang’s cult of leadership, and his Nvidia storytelling, may have come to a stupidly disappointing final chapter. As one former employee put it, Huang can’t simultaneously have had knowledge of every element of Nvidia’s business and then potentially feign ignorance about where the chips may have fallen, both figuratively and literally. His apparent lapses in judgment have now led him to resign from the very company he coaxed into existence and have shattered the mythos of its ever-prescient founder.

It’s certainly not the narrative ending Huang would have chosen, were he still in control.

article_content_zh:
那是 2024 年 7 月，黄仁勋精力充沛。

我同意前往科罗拉多州丹佛市，在 SIGGRAPH（计算机图形学博士和从业者的年度会议）上采访 Nvidia 首席执行官。那年早些时候，我为《连线》杂志的一篇专题文章对黄进行了一次长时间的静坐采访，显然这次采访对《连线》和 Nvidia 的高管沟通团队来说都进展顺利，以至于我被邀请在这次会议上再次采访黄。另一个拷问现代世界最有影响力的公司首席执行官的机会吗？是的当然。我开始准备。

总之，接下来发生的事情很奇怪。在会议的第一次准备电话会议中，公关人员通常试图向记者提出具体问题以防止伏击，在这种电话会议中，一位年轻的、有点熟悉的女性带头。这是詹森的女儿麦迪逊·黄。她显然很聪明，值得尊敬。她告诉我 Jensen 将在 SIGGRAPH 舞台上展示的幻灯片，并为我可能邀请他谈论幻灯片的关键时刻提供建议。

幻灯片？詹森打球吗？这是一次什么样的“采访”？

我向我的编辑和 Nvidia 提出了我的担忧。我们同意我会问我想问他的问题，其中包括有关数据中心对环境影响的问题，黄也会提到幻灯片。只能说面试进行得并不顺利。 （在 YouTube 上。）直到今天，前任和现任 Nvidia 员工有时都会告诉我，我“处理”了整个事情。黄很霸道，回避了我的一些问题，并且在我们的会议结束后立即与比我更崇拜的人群进行了即兴问答。然后我被引导下台，Meta 首席执行官马克·扎克伯格跳上车，他和黄在炉边进行了一场恩爱的谈话。

作为一名资深记者，我习惯了偶尔的敌对互动；我真的不会因为他们而失眠。这就是首席执行官的本质。黄后来同意在 2024 年 12 月再次与我会面。但在丹佛的那次采访向我强调了黄仁勋多么想控制叙事。不只是想要；他以为他会的。在很大程度上他做到了。直到本周。

叙事一直是黄的成功的关键部分。他不仅仅是普通的电气工程书呆子，他们为最终找到适合产品市场的东西而辛勤工作。根据黄自己的说法，他是一位移民创始人，一个失败者，一个追逐（并最终结婚）大学恋人的妻子，一个早期在丹尼餐厅用餐的斗志旺盛的创业者。一个周日工作的有远见的人，因为总是听到竞争对手的马蹄声而睡不好觉。一位将孩子带入公司的父母。一个非常热爱英伟达的人，他在手臂上纹了公司徽标的抽象版本。

黄建立了历史上价值最高的上市公司。这部分不仅仅是童话故事。这是真的。现在，它开始读起来更像是希腊悲剧。

早在 2024 年 1 月，当我与他第一次面对面会面时，黄立即谈到了讲故事的重要性。这是摘录：

黄仁勋：作为领导者和个人，我真正敬佩的人是 Adob​​e 的首席执行官 Shantanu Narayen。他说他一直想成为一名记者，因为他喜欢讲故事。

连线：能够有效地讲述自己的故事似乎是建立企业的重要组成部分。

是的。战略制定就是讲故事。文化建设就是讲故事。

你曾多次说过，你并没有根据宣传材料推销 Nvidia 的想法。

这是正确的。这实际上是为了讲故事。

title: Nearly 70 percent of US agencies use generative AI, and unions are finally catching up with guardrails
title_en: Nearly 70 percent of US agencies use generative AI, and unions are finally catching up with guardrails
author: THE DECODER
article_content:
US public-sector unions are winning more protections against AI surveillance and automation-driven job losses. The issue is growing more urgent as nearly 70 percent of US government agencies already use generative AI, according to an Ernst and Young survey.

The wins are piling up nationwide. After a strike vote in October, IFPTE Local 21 in Oakland secured retraining programs instead of AI-related layoffs. In Pennsylvania, Governor Josh Shapiro guaranteed SEIU Local 668 human oversight during a pilot of OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise. The Transport Workers Union in Ohio won veto power over autonomous vehicles. On top of that, California Governor Gavin Newsom banned AI surveillance software, often called "bossware," along with automated firings in September. New York has protected state employees from AI displacement by law since late 2025.

Employers are pushing automation to cut costs, according to labor researcher Kung Feng at UC Berkeley. Union leaders like Liz Shuler of the AFL-CIO, Lorena Gonzalez, and TWU's John Samuelsen support AI safety systems where they help workers but insist on mandatory human control over every AI application in the workplace, the Guardian reports.AdAd

title: Former OpenAI researcher says he found Nvidia Blackwell fingerprints hidden inside six Chinese AI models
title_en: Former OpenAI researcher says he found Nvidia Blackwell fingerprints hidden inside six Chinese AI models
author: THE DECODER
article_content:
AI researcher Will DePue says a forensic analysis has turned up the first technical evidence that leading Chinese AI labs have access to Nvidia's latest Blackwell hardware despite US export controls. He says senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic have already checked the method.

According to a forensic investigation by Will DePue, Chinese AI companies DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group are using Nvidia's export-controlled Blackwell GPUs. DePue played a key role at OpenAI in building the Sora and Sora 2 video models as well as GPT-4o, o3, and GPT-5 before founding the nonprofit research group Unemployment Labs.

His analysis, he says, provides the first technical evidence of this access. US officials and news outlets had suspected that DeepSeek and Moonshot AI were using Blackwell chips but never published proof. DePue wrote on X that senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic have already independently checked and confirmed his findings. According to DePue, six Chinese models released since April 2026 carry the distinct signature of Nvidia's Blackwell generation, while earlier models such as DeepSeek-V3 and Kimi K2.5 show traces of Nvidia's older Hopper generation.

The evidence comes directly from the published language models. An AI model consists of billions of numerical values called weights. Before training starts, PyTorch, the standard software framework, fills these empty slots with random numbers generated from a starting value called a seed. To distribute this massive amount of data quickly, the GPU splits the work across its individual compute cores. Because different chip models have different core counts, the filling process produces a characteristic pattern, according to the report. Older Hopper chips such as the H100 and H800 use 132 compute cores, while the newer Blackwell chips use exactly 148 or 152 cores depending on the model (B200/B300 or GB200/GB300).

Training then adjusts these values millions of times, but some slots for unused words or symbols keep their initial random values. Even in heavily trained parts of the model, a faint statistical echo of the initial distribution survives, according to DePue. He says he worked the pattern backward and reproduced the results for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi K3 exactly on real Blackwell chips. He has published the verification code on GitHub.

Training runs costing more than half a billion dollars

The analysis maps DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M3 to B200 or B300 chips (148 cores). DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1-Pro, and Ant Group's Ling-3.1-flash show, according to the analysis, the 152-core pattern of Nvidia's liquid-cooled GB200 or GB300 flagship rack systems. DePue says chance can be ruled out statistically and that the method correctly identified all 24 control models with known hardware, including Meta's Llama 3.1 (H100).

[caption id="attachment_42802" align="alignnone" width="1200"] Image: Will DePue / Unemployment Labs[/caption]

DePue's report estimates that the five training runs he examined required about 12,000 Blackwell GPUs combined, as much computing power as roughly 30,000 older H100 chips. Kimi K3 alone required an estimated 4,500 Blackwell processors over about 70 days, and DeepSeek-V4-Pro about 3,000. At a unit price of about $70,000, each of those clusters would cost $200 million to $300 million, and all five systems together more than half a billion dollars.

The findings also align with analysis from Dylan Patel, chief analyst at SemiAnalysis. In an interview with Sequoia Capital, Patel said DeepSeek-V3's model architecture was still specifically tailored for Nvidia's Hopper chips, while DeepSeek-V4's architecture was built for Blackwell GPUs and Huawei's Ascend chips. According to DePue's report, models from other Chinese labs, including Alibaba's Qwen3.8 and those from Zhipu, Tencent, Xiaomi, and StepFun, still show only Hopper signatures, while Meituan's LongCat-2.0 points to Huawei hardware.

The fingerprint doesn't prove a legal violation

Strictly speaking, the method shows only which hardware initialized the weights, though the training itself very likely ran on the same systems. The only other technical explanation would be an AMD MI300X, which is also restricted, artificially throttled so it produces the same pattern. DePue says he ruled out AMD for DeepSeek-V4-Flash using tiny rounding differences between the chips.

The data doesn't reveal where the GPUs are or who owns them, according to the investigation. Because Chinese companies can rent computing capacity at data centers outside China, the report says its technical evidence shows access to Nvidia's top hardware but does not by itself prove physical smuggling or a violation of US export law.

article_content_zh:
人工智能研究员 Will DePue 表示，法医分析已经找到了第一个技术证据，表明尽管美国有出口管制，中国领先的人工智能实验室仍可以使用 Nvidia 最新的 Blackwell 硬件。他说 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的高级研究人员已经检查了该方法。

根据 Will DePue 的取证调查，中国人工智能公司 DeepSeek、Moonshot AI、MiniMax 和 Ant Group 正在使用 Nvidia 受出口管制的 Blackwell GPU。 DePue 在创建非营利研究组织失业实验室之前，在 OpenAI 构建 Sora 和 Sora 2 视频模型以及 GPT-4o、o3 和 GPT-5 方面发挥了关键作用。

他说，他的分析提供了这种访问的第一个技术证据。美国官员和新闻媒体曾怀疑 DeepSeek 和 Moonshot AI 使用 Blackwell 芯片，但从未公布证据。 DePue 在 X 上写道，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的高级研究人员已经独立检查并证实了他的发现。 DePue 表示，自 2026 年 4 月以来发布的六款中国型号带有 Nvidia Blackwell 一代的独特特征，而 DeepSeek-V3 和 Kimi K2.5 等早期型号则显示出 Nvidia 老 Hopper 一代的痕迹。

证据直接来自已发布的语言模型。人工智能模型由数十亿个称为权重的数值组成。在训练开始之前，标准软件框架 PyTorch 会使用从称为种子的起始值生成的随机数来填充这些空槽。为了快速分发如此大量的数据，GPU 将工作分配给各个计算核心。报告称，由于不同的芯片型号具有不同的核心数量，因此填充过程会产生一种特征图案。 H100 和 H800 等较旧的 Hopper 芯片使用 132 个计算核心，而较新的 Blackwell 芯片则使用 148 或 152 个核心，具体取决于型号（B200/B300 或 GB200/GB300）。

然后训练会调整这些值数百万次，但未使用的单词或符号的一些槽位会保留其初始随机值。德普表示，即使在模型训练有素的部分，初始分布的微弱统计回声仍然存在。他说，他对模型进行了反向运算，并在真正的 Blackwell 芯片上准确地重现了 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 和 Kimi K3 的结果。他已在 GitHub 上发布了验证码。

培训费用超过 5 亿美元

该分析将 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 和 MiniMax-M3 映射到 B200 或 B300 芯片（148 个内核）。 DeepSeek-V4-Pro、Kimi K3、Kimi K3.1-Pro和蚂蚁集团的Ling-3.1-flash显示，根据分析，Nvidia液冷GB200或GB300旗舰机架系统的152核心模式。 DePue 表示，统计上可以排除偶然性，并且该方法使用已知硬件正确识别了所有 24 个控制模型，包括 Meta 的 Llama 3.1 (H100)。

图片：Will DePue / 失业实验室[/caption]

DePue 的报告估计，他检查的五次训练总共需要大约 12,000 个 Blackwell GPU，计算能力相当于大约 30,000 个较旧的 H100 芯片。仅 Kimi K3 在大约 70 天内就需要大约 4,500 个 Blackwell 处理器，而 DeepSeek-V4-Pro 则需要大约 3,000 个处理器。以约 7 万美元的单价计算，每个集群的成本为 2 亿至 3 亿美元，所有五个系统总共花费超过 5 亿美元。

研究结果也与 SemiAnalysis 首席分析师迪伦·帕特尔 (Dylan Patel) 的分析相符。 Patel在接受红杉资本采访时表示，DeepSeek-V3的模型架构仍然是专门为Nvidia的Hopper芯片量身定制的，而DeepSeek-V4的架构是为Blackwell GPU和华为的Ascend芯片构建的。根据 DePue 的报告，来自其他中国实验室的模型，包括阿里巴巴的 Qwen3.8 以及来自智浦、腾讯、小米和 StepFun 的模型，仍然只显示 Hopper 签名，而美团的 LongCat-2.0 则指向华为硬件。

指纹并不能证明违法行为

严格来说，该方法仅显示哪个硬件初始化了权重，尽管训练本身很可能在相同的系统上运行。唯一的其他技术解释是 AMD MI300X，它也受到限制，人为节流，因此它会产生相同的模式。 DePue 表示，他利用芯片之间微小的舍入差异排除了 AMD 推出 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 的可能性。

调查显示，这些数据并未透露 GPU 的位置或所有者。由于中国公司可以在中国境外的数据中心租用计算能力，报告称其技术证据显示可以访问英伟达的顶级硬件，但其本身并不能证明存在实体走私或违反美国出口法。

title: Anthropic's IPO is six times oversubscribed and on track to become the largest public offering in history
title_en: Anthropic's IPO is six times oversubscribed and on track to become the largest public offering in history
author: THE DECODER
article_content:
Anthropic is on track for the largest IPO ever, with orders exceeding available shares by a factor of six. That's according to Bloomberg. The Claude developer and its co-founders aim to raise up to $64.4 billion through the public offering and another $26 billion via a private placement, which would surpass even SpaceX's IPO. The target valuation sits at roughly $1.4 trillion, with existing investors getting priority in share allocation.

The company's financials likely fuel much of the demand. Anthropic's annualized revenue climbed to $81 billion by late October, up from $71 billion in September. Nvidia, whose investors have grown more cautious since CEO Jensen Huang was ousted over an alleged espionage scandal, is itself buying $10 billion in Anthropic stock through the private placement. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are managing the Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT, and CEO Dario Amodei will pitch investors alongside JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon in a Friday livestream.

title: Meta's Muse now calls businesses for you, but many companies might just hang up on the AI
title_en: Meta's Muse now calls businesses for you, but many companies might just hang up on the AI
author: THE DECODER
article_content:
Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said the agent, with more than 10 million users, handles tedious calls to cable companies, the DMV, and restaurants, and will soon get a free email address. Google's Gemini, startup Instinct, and xAI's Grok Bot can already place calls as well, while OpenAI's ChatGPT Dots and Anthropic's Claude Duet still cannot.

Many businesses, however, hang up the moment they detect an AI on the line. That problem forced Meta to temporarily test human operators for Muse in September, echoing Google's experience with Duplex, where on launch one in four calls was handled by a human. Synthetic voices keep getting more realistic, making that detection increasingly difficult. Users are drawn to the feature largely because the AI will sit on hold indefinitely and work through complex phone menus without complaint.AdAd

title: OpenAI enters the cybersecurity market with two Daybreak products
title_en: OpenAI enters the cybersecurity market with two Daybreak products
author: THE DECODER
article_content:
OpenAI has launched two security products under its Daybreak brand. The first, Daybreak Red Team, is available in Early Access and uses AI agents to automatically probe web applications for vulnerabilities by analyzing source code and app context to map out attack paths. The tool also verifies reported security flaws from bug bounty programs or code scanners and tests patches. Nancy Wang, head of Cyber-Applied AI, said the tool is designed to deliver penetration testing at the speed of automated continuous scanning while matching the depth of human testers.

The second product, Daybreak Defense Factory, automates the defensive side. AI agents scan a company's codebase for vulnerabilities and generate patches, delivering ready-to-deploy pull requests with fixes and accompanying tests for developer approval. Both products run on OpenAI's latest cyber model, GPT-6 Cyber.

title: Introducing ChatGPT Wallet
title_en: Introducing ChatGPT Wallet
author: OpenAI 官方动态
article_content:
Building trusted agentic payments with networks, banks, and businesses.

1.2B people use ChatGPT each week, and many of them turn to it to research products, compare options, and decide what to buy. With ChatGPT Wallet, we’re now helping people complete purchases, and giving their agents a way to pay that businesses can accept with their existing systems.

To accept payment from ChatGPT Wallet, websites need to ensure agents are not inadvertently blocked, and payment and risk systems need to recognize legitimate purchases made by agents. We’re starting with limited availability to ChatGPT Pro users, so we can learn from real-world use and work with businesses, banks, and payment networks to improve compatibility and reliability.

ChatGPT Wallet gives agents a secure way to pay on a user’s behalf. Users add a card once, then approve each purchase without re-entering their payment details.

Before each purchase, the user reviews the items, total, and selected card, then approves it with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan. Each approval creates a clear record of the purchase the user authorized the agent to make.

After the user approves, the payment network provides a payment token—a substitute for the user’s actual card details—with a card number, security code, and expiration date. The payment is charged to their selected card without ChatGPT Wallet sharing their actual card details with the business or agent.

We’re building agent-led commerce to fit reliably into existing systems. Users keep their card’s existing rewards and protections for eligible disputes with businesses, for example when an item is defective. Banks and networks bring their expertise to evaluating transactions. Users transact directly with businesses, which keep their customer relationships and control over pricing, fulfillment, returns, and customer service.

Over time, we expect users to be able to delegate purchases entirely to their agent by setting clear parameters—such as spending limits, purchase categories, or time periods—and pre-approve those purchases with enhanced safeguards that build on today’s protections, including biometric checks and clear records of authorization.

Agentic commerce is still in its early days. As agents begin to take on more shopping and purchasing tasks, many websites and payment systems are still adapting to this modality. Some sites may unintentionally block purchases through ChatGPT Wallet or other agentic payment products, and we are focused on helping businesses make that transition.

Alongside ChatGPT Wallet, we’re publishing a Commerce Partner Playbook⁠(opens in a new window) with tools and practical guidance to help businesses support customers using agents through their existing websites and systems. It covers making product information available, ensuring agent access, and working with payment and risk providers to reduce unnecessary declines. Businesses can start with the areas most relevant to their customers:

Help customers find accurate product information. Claim your business in ChatGPT and, once verified, update your business details and upload a product feed with current pricing and availability.

Ensure ChatGPT agents can access your website. Configure your CDN or firewall to recognize signed requests using Web Bot Auth and confirm your general site security measures are not inadvertently blocking ChatGPT agents. Browser access does not require a plugin or product feed.

Work with your payments and risk providers to support agent purchases. Wallet’s payment tokens work with existing checkout flows, but risk systems may still flag legitimate purchases made by agents, leading to declines or cancellations. You can work with your providers to understand how they recognize these transactions. We’re also working with fraud prevention partners including Forter, Riskified, Sardine and Signifyd and payment service providers including Adyen, Checkout.com, and Stripe to help their systems recognize legitimate purchases made by agents.

Give agents more ways to work with your business. Build a plugin to let agents check availability, manage carts, or take other actions through your existing systems. Websites can also add WebMCP tools.

key_points_zh: 核心事实：ChatGPT 钱包简介
key_points_en: Key Development: Introducing ChatGPT Wallet

article_content_zh:
与网络、银行和企业建立可信的代理支付。

1.2B 的人每周都会使用 ChatGPT，其中许多人利用它来研究产品、比较选项并决定购买什么。借助 ChatGPT 钱包，我们现在正在帮助人们完成购买，并为他们的代理商提供企业现有系统可以接受的支付方式。

为了接受 ChatGPT 钱包的付款，网站需要确保代理商不会被无意中屏蔽，并且支付和风险系统需要识别代理商的合法购买行为。我们一开始对 ChatGPT Pro 用户的可用性有限，因此我们可以从现实世界的使用中学习，并与企业、银行和支付网络合作，以提高兼容性和可靠性。

ChatGPT 钱包为代理提供了代表用户付款的安全方式。用户添加卡一次，然后批准每次购买，无需重新输入付款详细信息。

每次购买之前，用户都会检查商品、总数和所选卡，然后通过安全检查（例如面容 ID 或指纹扫描）进行批准。每次批准都会创建用户授权代理商进行的购买的清晰记录。

用户批准后，支付网络会提供支付令牌（用户实际卡详细信息的替代品）以及卡号、安全代码和到期日期。付款将从他们选择的卡中扣除，ChatGPT Wallet 不会与企业或代理分享他们的实际卡详细信息。

我们正在构建以代理为主导的商务，以可靠地融入现有系统。用户保留其卡的现有奖励和保护，以应对与企业发生的合格纠纷，例如当商品有缺陷时。银行和网络利用其专业知识来评估交易。用户直接与企业进行交易，企业可以保持客户关系并控制定价、履行、退货和客户服务。

随着时间的推移，我们希望用户能够通过设置明确的参数（如支出限制、购买类别或时间段）将购买完全委托给他们的代理，并在现有保护措施的基础上预先批准这些购买，包括生物识别检查和明确的授权记录。

代理贸易仍处于早期阶段。随着代理商开始承担更多的购物和采购任务，许多网站和支付系统仍在适应这种模式。一些网站可能会无意中阻止通过 ChatGPT 钱包或其他代理支付产品进行的购买，我们致力于帮助企业实现这一转变。

除了 ChatGPT 钱包之外，我们还发布了商业合作伙伴手册（在新窗口中打开），其中包含工具和实用指南，可帮助企业通过现有网站和系统为使用代理的客户提供支持。它包括提供产品信息、确保代理访问以及与支付和风险提供商合作以减少不必要的拒绝。企业可以从与客户最相关的领域开始：

帮助客户找到准确的产品信息。在 ChatGPT 中声明您的业务，并在验证后更新您的业务详细信息并上传包含当前定价和库存情况的产品 Feed。

确保 ChatGPT 代理可以访问您的网站。配置您的 CDN 或防火墙以识别使用 Web Bot Auth 的签名请求，并确认您的常规站点安全措施不会无意中阻止 ChatGPT 代理。浏览器访问不需要插件或产品提要。

与您的付款和风险提供商合作以支持代理购买。钱包的支付代币可与现有结账流程配合使用，但风险系统仍可能标记代理商进行的合法购买，从而导致拒绝或取消。您可以与您的提供商合作，了解他们如何识别这些交易。我们还与 Forter、Riskified、Sardine 和 Signifyd 等欺诈预防合作伙伴以及 Adyen、Checkout.com 和 Stripe 等支付服务提供商合作，帮助他们的系统识别代理商的合法购买行为。

为代理商提供更多与您的企业合作的方式。构建一个插件，让代理检查可用性、管理购物车或通过现有系统执行其他操作。网站还可以添加WebMCP工具。

title: What’s really at stake in the Jensen Huang saga
title_en: What’s really at stake in the Jensen Huang saga
author: The Verge AI
article_content:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

On The Vergecast: The many spiraling stories in the AI world, the fate of streaming services, Mark Zuckerberg’s meat, and more.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

One part of the saga surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang ended on Thursday, when Huang resigned from his position at the top of AI’s most important company. But in the coming weeks and months, a much bigger story may be about to unfold. A story about Nvidia’s dealings in China, about the US government’s willingness to turn a lot of blind eyes to protect a powerful ally, and about the very stability of the AI industry as a whole. It’s a lot.

On this episode of The Vergecast, David and Nilay start by trying to unpack the many parts of the story. We’re all going to learn a lot more about Megaspeed than we ever planned or wanted, and we’re going to hear a lot of people — particularly newly elected Democrats — asking questions about who knew what and when. In the meantime, who will replace Huang as the AI industry’s front man? And will everyone survive the scrutiny that’s coming?

After that, the hosts tackle a week filled with small-ish news from streaming services that adds up to Hollywood’s plan to properly take on TikTok. We’re about to find out whether microdramas, free tiers, and a deep obsession with vertical video will save the Netflixes and Paramounts of the world. Will it work? Probably not. Is it the only rational thing to try? You bet. Finally, in the lightning round, it’s time for Brendan Carr Is a Dummy, Mark Zuckerberg’s AI experiments, the Cybertruck era, and more.

title: Claude’s Duet agent is a little neurotic and surprisingly helpful
title_en: Claude’s Duet agent is a little neurotic and surprisingly helpful
author: The Verge AI
article_content:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Duet is a decent helper, if a little jumpy at times.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Normally, the products I test don’t offer to help me write up my experience with them. Duet is different.

Claude Duet is Anthropic’s AI agent for consumers, the latest attempt by an AI company to try to convince us that agents can be useful for people who don’t write code. It’s been an interesting couple of months: Instinct gave us an impressive text-based assistant, Meta offered us its cute little guy, Muse, to help us buy things, and OpenAI gave us the more work-oriented Dots. Claude Duet is even more focused on work than those. It’s also more consumer-friendly than Claude Cowork, which was more consumer-friendly than Claude Code — the coding agent that kicked off a whole hype cycle earlier this year. I’ve been testing it over the past week as I navigate a busy travel and work schedule. At turns it has been truly useful, kind of a nag, and very eager to write about itself.

Like Meta’s Muse, Duet has its own app. (If you’re keeping score at home, yes, it has been updated to fully support the iPhone Duo). Duet uses Claude’s characteristically cheery, minimalist design. The app is consumer-friendly and approachable. Once you’ve connected all the productivity and chat services you want, it’ll look for ways to help out with and suggest them as cards you can swipe left or right to hide or accept — kind of a to-do list Tinder.

In the name of testing, I went all in on Duet and gave it everything: my work email, calendar, Google Docs, and Slack. This gave it plenty of grist for the mill in more ways than I’d even realized at first. Because our biweekly staff meeting is automatically summarized in an email from Gemini, and Duet had access to my email, it was able to connect the dots between something said in a meeting and a direct message in Slack. Duet also worked out who my boss is because we have a shared Google Doc for our weekly 1:1 meetings. AI is at its most useful when it can suck up lots of data, and Duet wasted no time doing so.

Duet has started each morning by greeting me with a brief message and some quick highlights for my day, like reminding me to pack an item required for a video shoot before my flight. Below that, it would suggest to-dos, usually ending in an offer to help draft a message or add an item to an agenda.

This has often been helpful, though it sometimes felt like interacting with a slightly neurotic personal assistant. In one instance, I’d emailed someone I interviewed for a story that the article was likely to go up on Tuesday and that I’d send a link when it did. I submitted my draft to my editors late at night on Monday, and Tuesday morning Duet was beside itself. It wasn’t quite 9AM yet when it pointed out that the story was still waiting for an edit and I needed to get on that — or else I wouldn’t be able to send the link I promised. The concern was a bit misplaced. And it didn’t pick up on the nuance in my message implying that this was not a hard deadline, nor the fact that it was only 7AM local time for my editor.

In other cases, it was surprisingly helpful. In planning out the next few weeks I’d missed the fact that upcoming time off would only leave me with a couple of working days before another big draft was due. Duet proposed a solution, offered to update the Google Doc with weekly notes for my editor, and drafted a Slack message for him noting the update. Reader, the message was a little too good. It copied my millennial habit of writing in all lowercase — which it pointed out in a slightly self-congratulatory aside — and used an abbreviation we often use to refer to our CMS. But it also shortened the word “signature” to “sig,” which I never would and made me laugh out loud. In any case, there’s no fooling anyone; the Slack message was tagged with a “sent with Claude” label.

Duet often volunteered to help start my drafts, which is always a hard no for me. I’ll type up my own little blogs, thank you very much Claude. If you’re not a writer, I can see how taking care of little writing chores here and there would be helpful. But this started feeling like a Spider-Man-pointing-at-Spider-Man moment when the task it wanted to help with was reviewing itself.

It was a little uncanny, too. Even setting aside the fact that I was writing about Duet, it’s kind of weird knowing that it can read every email, draft, and Slack I send. It can read all of that because I opted in to sharing that data, and I knew full well what I was doing. But it’s another thing to see it in practice. I wonder if it would change how I work if I knew I didn’t really need to take responsibility for putting things on my calendar, writing down a to-do list, or paying attention in a meeting because Duet will just handle it. Maybe that’s how CEOs live. Not that I cherish creating calendar entries, but I wonder if I would end up feeling a bit disconnected from my workplace.

I don’t think Duet or any other AI agent is quite ready to make us feel like we’re all the CEOs of our own little worlds. There’s a key word in the title “personal assistant”: personal. A person can pick up on nuances in tone to understand what’s a big deal and what isn’t. A person will pick up on communication norms and deploy them sensibly. A person can be tactful. Anthropic’s blog post mentions that the company is continuing to “test its judgment about when to message you,” so it’s possible Duet will calibrate a little better over time. But AI overall isn’t good at understanding nuance or tone, and it’s not clear if it ever will be.

For me, Duet made it a little more clear what I want AI to do for me and what I don’t. Communication happens all over the place in a modern workplace — in emails, DMs, meetings, shared docs. Having AI find discrepancies that have been overlooked between all of these sources and point them out proactively is really helpful. I like it as a backstop for my own organizational systems, not as a replacement for them. I don’t like it in the creative process. Like, at all. I want to find “my own ways into and around a topic,” as Hank Green said of his own reliance on AI. If you send a robot to do the legwork, you miss the opportunity to stumble across something unexpected. It’s part of what makes the work enjoyable. And I’m certainly not about to let an agent review itself for me. You hear that, Duet?

通常，我测试的产品不会帮助我写下我的使用体验。二重奏是不同的。

Claude Duet 是 Anthropic 面向消费者的人工智能代理，这是一家人工智能公司的最新尝试，试图让我们相信代理对于不编写代码的人来说也是有用的。这是有趣的几个月：Instinct 为我们提供了一个令人印象深刻的基于文本的助手，Meta 为我们提供了它可爱的小家伙 Muse，帮助我们购买东西，而 OpenAI 为我们提供了更以工作为导向的 Dots。克劳德·杜埃（Claude Duet）甚至比那些更专注于工作。它也比 Claude Cowork 更适合消费者，而 Claude Cowork 又比今年早些时候启动了整个炒作周期的编码代理 Claude Code 更适合消费者。过去一周，我在繁忙的旅行和工作日程中一直在测试它。有时它确实很有用，但又有点唠叨，而且非常渴望写下它自己。

与 Meta 的 Muse 一样，Duet 也有自己的应用程序。 （如果您在家记分，是的，它已经更新为完全支持 iPhone Duo）。 Duet 采用了克劳德特有的欢快、简约的设计。该应用程序对消费者友好且平易近人。一旦你连接了所有你想要的生产力和聊天服务，它就会寻找帮助的方法，并将它们建议为卡片，你可以向左或向右滑动来隐藏或接受——有点像 Tinder 的待办事项列表。

以测试的名义，我全力投入 Duet，并为它提供了一切：我的工作电子邮件、日历、Google Docs 和 Slack。这给工厂带来了比我一开始意识到的更多的好处。因为我们每两周一次的员工会议会自动总结在 Gemini 发送的电子邮件中，而 Duet 可以访问我的电子邮件，因此它能够将会议中所说的内容与 Slack 中的直接消息联系起来。 Duet 还找出了我的老板是谁，因为我们有一个共享的 Google 文档用于每周的 1:1 会议。当人工智能能够吸收大量数据时，它才是最有用的，而 Duet 没有浪费时间这样做。

Duet 每天早上都会向我发送一条简短的消息和一些当天的亮点，比如提醒我在起飞前收拾好拍摄视频所需的物品。下面，它会建议待办事项，通常以帮助起草消息或将项目添加到议程中的提议结束。

这通常很有帮助，尽管有时感觉就像是在与一个有点神经质的私人助理互动。有一次，我给采访过一篇报道的人发了一封电子邮件，称这篇文章可能会在周二发表，届时我会发送一个链接。周一深夜，我将草稿提交给编辑，而周二早上，Duet 就疯狂了。当时还不到上午 9 点，它指出这个故事仍在等待编辑，我需要继续编辑——否则我将无法发送我承诺的链接。这种担心有点多余。它没有注意到我的消息中的细微差别，暗示这不是一个硬性的截止日期，也没有注意到我的编辑现在只是当地时间早上 7 点这一事实。

在其他情况下，它却出奇地有帮助。在计划接下来的几周时，我忽略了这样一个事实：即将到来的休假只会让我在另一次重大选秀到期之前只剩下几个工作日。 Duet 提出了一个解决方案，提出为我的编辑提供每周更新 Google 文档的笔记，并为他起草了一条 Slack 消息来记录更新。读者，这个消息有点太好了。它复制了我千禧一代用小写字母书写的习惯——它在旁边稍微沾沾自喜地指出了这一点——并使用了我们经常用来指代我们的 CMS 的缩写。但它也将“signature”这个词缩短为“sig”，这是我永远不会做的，这让我笑出了声。无论如何，谁都骗不了； Slack 消息被标记为“与 Claude 一起发送”标签。

Duet 经常自愿帮助我开始草稿，这对我来说总是很难拒绝。我会写我自己的小博客，非常感谢克劳德。如果你不是作家，我可以看出，在这里或那里处理一些写作琐事会有多大帮助。但这开始感觉就像是蜘蛛侠指着蜘蛛侠的时刻，因为它想要帮助完成的任务正在自我审查。

这也有点不可思议。即使抛开我正在写 Duet 的事实，知道它可以阅读我发送的每封电子邮件、草稿和 Slack 也有点奇怪。它可以读取所有这些，因为我选择共享这些数据，并且我完全清楚自己在做什么。但在实践中看到它是另一回事。我想知道如果我知道我不需要负责将事情放在日历上、写下待办事项列表或在会议中集中注意力，因为 Duet 会处理这些事情，这是否会改变我的工作方式。也许这就是CEO的生活方式。并不是说我珍惜创建日历条目，但我想知道我最终是否会感到与工作场所有点脱节。

我不认为 Duet 或任何其他人工智能代理已经准备好让我们感觉我们都是自己小世界的首席执行官。 《私人助理》的标题中有一个关键词：个人。一个人可以通过语气的细微差别来理解什么是大事，什么是小事。一个人会掌握沟通规范并明智地运用它们。一个人可以很委婉。 Anthropic 的博客文章提到，该公司正在继续“测试其对何时向您发送消息的判断”，因此，随着时间的推移，Duet 可能会更好地进行校准。但总体而言，人工智能并不擅长理解细微差别或语气，而且目前还不清楚它是否会如此。

对我来说，Duet 让我更清楚地知道我希望人工智能为我做什么以及我不做什么。在现代工作场所中，沟通无处不在——通过电子邮件、私信、会议、共享文档。让人工智能发现所有这些来源之间被忽视的差异并主动指出它们确实很有帮助。我喜欢它作为我自己的组织系统的后盾，而不是替代它们。我不喜欢创作过程。就像，完全一样。正如汉克·格林谈到自己对人工智能的依赖时所说，我想找到“我自己的方式来进入和围绕一个主题”。如果你派一个机器人去跑腿，你就会错过偶然发现意想不到的事情的机会。这是使工作变得愉快的一部分。我当然不会让代理人为我自我审查。你听到了吗，二重奏？

title: The Download: Silicon Valley’s blind spot and Nvidia’s chip-tracking plan
title_en: The Download: Silicon Valley’s blind spot and Nvidia’s chip-tracking plan
author: MIT Tech Review
article_content:
The self-styled visionaries of Silicon Valley have built careers claiming to see the future. Yet five weeks before the midterms, many gathered at the White House to pose with Trump and endorse his “Super Intelligence” agenda, despite growing opposition to AI and data centers.

Their decision to lash themselves to President Trump was a catastrophic misreading of the political landscape. Now, not only have they jeopardized their companies’ fates, but they’ve also raised questions about their vision and judgment.

Here’s why Silicon Valley’s tech leaders may be less visionary than they think.

Nvidia representatives told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it was possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review on Thursday, despite an industry group claiming they were “potentially infeasible.”

Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips and prevent their smuggling to China.

The act is drawing renewed attention following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair. Find out what the proposed tracking measures would involve.

Scientists have been working on ways to decode brain activity for decades. Teams have developed brain implants that can control robotic limbs and computers, and even “speak.”

The people who volunteer for trials of these devices play a vital role in that research, and they ought to be recognized for their contributions, says Ian Burkhart, who had one implanted in his own brain back in 2014.

He’s been working on a set of guidelines for ethical trials to respect participants’ autonomy—and access their own brain data whenever they want.

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

(NBC News)+ And who could get the permanent role? (NYT $)+ Trump has backed Apple's Tim Cook for the job. (WP $)+ Nancy Pelosi's replacement plans to regulate AI. (MIT Technology Review)

3 An Alice Huang-linked firm procured banned Nvidia chips in ChinaThe servers were first sold to an Nvidia partner in Singapore. (Bloomberg $)+ Singapore says US failed to help in the spy probe. (NYT $)+ The city-state faces growing scrutiny over its chip links to China. (CNBC)+ The turmoil at Nvidia puts billions in Chinese AI at risk. (Reuters $)+ Taiwan's “silicon shield” is weakening. (MIT Technology Review)

4 Parents are demanding an AI moratorium in schoolsGemini allegedly encouraged a teenager to plan suicide. (Ars Technica)+ Schools are caught in Big Tech’s education experiment. (New Yorker $)+ We need smarter AI use in the classroom. (MIT Technology Review)

5 Advocacy groups have sued five frontier AI labs to stop developmentThey’re targeting Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and SpaceXSI. (AP)+ Anti-AI protests are increasing. (MIT Technology Review)

6 SpaceX has denied throttling Ukraine’s Starshield networkZelenskyy says the curbs are hampering drone defenses. (Axios)

7 A robot has assembled a structure in space for the first timeIt’s a step towards in-orbit manufacturing. (New Scientist $)

8 AI companion users want to make their digital partners immortalThey’re building chatbots that can survive model updates. (Atlantic $)

9 Scientists have identified a protein that accelerates ageingThe discovery could lead to drugs that slow ageing. (Nature $)

10 A huge new galaxy map could reveal the dark universe.The data includes 15,000 potential gravitational lensing cases. (Guardian)+ The search for dark matter has been blown open. (MIT Technology Review)

—Donald Trump shares his succession plan for Nvidia on Truth Social, The Verge reports.

I’m currently around 1,000 feet beneath the North Sea, in a dark, dank cave. It smells weird. And I’m increasingly aware of the pressure from millions of tons of seawater just above my head.

I’m under the iconic fjords of Norway to visit what will soon become the world’s longest and deepest subsea road tunnel—an exceptional engineering feat that will carry drivers deep beneath the North Sea.

I’m here to understand how you make a 16.6-mile highway that sits 1,280 feet below the sea at its deepest point. And also—at a time when it can feel hard to get anything done—to reassure myself that ambitious engineering is still possible. That we can still make things.

Step inside Norway’s Rogfast tunnel and see how engineers are making it happen.

A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line.)

article_content_zh:
硅谷自诩为有远见的人所建立的职业生涯声称能够预见未来。然而，在中期选举前五周，许多人聚集在白宫与特朗普合影并支持他的“超级智能”议程，尽管人们越来越反对人工智能和数据中心。

他们决定向特朗普总统发起攻击，这是对政治格局的灾难性误读。现在，他们不仅危及公司的命运，而且还对他们的愿景和判断力提出了质疑。

这就是为什么硅谷的科技领导者可能没有他们想象的那么有远见。

福斯特周四告诉《麻省理工科技评论》，英伟达代表告诉伊利诺伊州代表比尔·福斯特，实施《芯片安全法》中要求的反走私措施是可能的，尽管一个行业组织声称这些措施“可能不可行”。

福斯特是科学、空间和技术委员会的民主党人，也是该法案的共同发起人之一，该法案将引入地理跟踪要求，以验证先进人工智能芯片的位置并防止其走私到中国。

在英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋辞职并被报道出丑闻后，这一行为再次引起人们的关注。了解拟议的跟踪措施将涉及哪些内容。

几十年来，科学家们一直致力于研究解码大脑活动的方法。团队已经开发出可以控制机器人肢体和计算机，甚至可以“说话”的大脑植入物。

伊恩·伯克哈特 (Ian Burkhart) 于 2014 年在自己的大脑中植入了一个设备，他表示，自愿参与这些设备试验的人们在这项研究中发挥着至关重要的作用，他们的贡献应该得到认可。

他一直在制定一套伦理试验指南，以尊重参与者的自主权，并在他们想要的时候访问他们自己的大脑数据。

阅读完整的故事，了解如何为脑植入试验中的志愿者提供更多权利。

3 一家与 Alice Huang 有联系的公司在中国采购了被禁的 Nvidia 芯片。服务器首先出售给新加坡的 Nvidia 合作伙伴。 (Bloomberg $)+ 新加坡表示美国未能协助进行间谍调查。 (NYT $)+ 这个城邦国家因其与中国的芯片联系而面临越来越严格的审查。 (CNBC)+ 英伟达的动荡使中国数十亿美元的人工智能面临风险。 (Reuters $)+ 台湾的“硅盾”正在减弱。 （麻省理工科技评论）

Usually, we’d be offering to answer your questions about a news event, but honestly we don’t really have any answers about what the hell is going on over at Nvidia. I can’t speak for Nilay but at the rate Jensen Huang’s new mistresses are dropping, I am concerned we are approaching an affair Singularity. If things don’t decelerate soon, we may be looking at existential risk. Maybe the future of AI really does depend on Jensen’s sex life, but not in the way I was thinking!

As much fun (?) as we are having with all the assorted ladies, it’s important to stay focused on what’s really important: Chips and China. President Donald Trump was reportedly warned about Alice “No Relation” Huang’s possible connections to China’s spy apparatus last year, and again before his China trip in May. Nvidia reportedly intervened into a Commerce Department investigation into Alice’s company.

Did Alice girlboss too close to the sun? Have I been wrong all this time about AI being an important productivity tool, freeing everyone up to have multiple affairs at once? What do CEOs do at their jobs anyway? Is Jensen’s leather jacket really an alien symbiote? Can’t I just go for a hike in peace? Let’s discuss. Nilay and I will be joining you at 1PM ET.

title: More autonomy, fewer NDAs: Volunteers have new requests for brain implant trials
title_en: More autonomy, fewer NDAs: Volunteers have new requests for brain implant trials
author: MIT Tech Review
article_content:
Scientists have been working on ways to decode brain activity for decades. Teams have developed brain implants that can be used to control robotic limbs and computers, and even to “speak.”

The people who volunteer for trials of those devices play a vital role in that research, and they ought to be recognized for their contributions, says Ian Burkhart, who had one implanted in his own brain back in 2014. He’s been working on a set of guidelines for researchers developing brain-computer interfaces (BCIs).

Ethics guidelines for clinical trials already exist. But BCI trials are different, says Jennifer Chandler, a professor of law and neuroethics at the University of Ottawa who also worked on the guidelines. “These are people who have a device embedded in their brain, are in trials sometimes for years and years … [and contribute] a significant investment of time, of the body, and of intellectual effort.”

Burkhart was left paralyzed from the chest down following a diving accident in 2010, when he was 19 years old. Around four years later, he volunteered to become the first person to trial a brain implant designed for hand control.

He had an array of 96 electrodes inserted into the part of his brain that controls movement. The electrodes were connected to a computer via a cable that essentially plugged into his head. Algorithms on the computer were designed to interpret those signals and deliver them to another sleeve of electrodes worn on Burkhart’s arm, allowing him to control it.

The first movements were small, but Burkhart was ultimately able to use the system to pour beads from bottles, move small and delicate objects, and even play Guitar Hero, if only during lab visits. It was a scientific breakthrough.

Burkhart took part in two years-long clinical trials over the seven-and-a-half-year period he had the electrode array implanted in his brain. “It was a fantastic experience,” he says. “But there’s certainly some things that, knowing what I know now, I would want to do a little differently.”

In 2022, Burkhart cofounded BCI Pioneers Coalition—an organization through which people who have taken part in BCI trials can share their experiences, both with each other and with researchers. Over the last year, members of the group have been developing a set of guidelines based on those experiences. The idea is to help academics, clinicians, and companies run ethical trials that respect participants’ autonomy.

The guidelines, published on Tuesday, lay out a list of recommendations that fall within 13 categories. One, for example, focuses on recognizing and compensating trial participants. During the trials that Burkhart participated in, “I was going into the lab two or three days a week, for four hours at a time,” he recalls. “That’s [easily] a part-time job if you just count the hours you’re putting in.”

As the trial progressed, Burkhart says, he learned more and was able to give more constructive feedback on what was working and what wasn’t. He says he was a key member of the research team. Others who find themselves in a similar position might appreciate being listed as a coauthor on scientific publications or publicly named as a research collaborator, he says. Burkhart and his colleagues acknowledge that not everyone will want this, however.

The guidelines also address the thorny question of privacy. That’s important: The public will always be interested in cutting-edge biotechnologies like these—and the guidelines say researchers also have a duty to prepare participants for the possibility of media attention. In some cases, it might be difficult to completely conceal the identity of trial participants.

Things get even more complicated when it comes to the privacy of participants’ brain data. Research teams will need to access, analyze, and—at least temporarily—store this data. Burkhart wasn’t too bothered about that in his case, where scientists were collecting neural activity related to movement. But people who have brain implants designed for turning thoughts into words might feel differently.

The guidelines state that brain data “should be understood as the participant’s personal information.” They are pushing for participants to be able to access their own brain data whenever they want—something that has not always been possible—and want to make sure people aren’t prevented from sharing it with their own doctors because of embargoes or nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) designed to keep findings under wraps from competitors.

“It’s not super common for there to be firm NDAs within a lot of the trials,” says Burkhart. “But it’s something where we want to make sure that that does not happen.”

The guidelines also address what comes after a trial. Around five years after Burkhart had his device implanted, the research team ran into some issues with funding. When we last spoke a few years ago, he recalled how he was told he would have to have the implant removed and could have it put back in once the team had secured funding. (And we’re talking about brain surgery here.)

Ultimately, he kept the implant until 2021, when it was removed after an infection started to develop at the point where the cable led into his scalp. But losing the device after all those years was difficult; he’d regained the ability to move his arm—and then lost it again.

Rita Leggett, an Australian woman who had a device implanted in her brain to treat her epilepsy, has said she felt she “became one” with her implant. When the company that made it went bust two years later, the device was removed against her will—an act ethicists have described as a potential breach of human rights.

Researchers should instead commit to maintaining brain devices for a “reasonable period” after a trial ends, according to the guidelines. Participants should be given plenty of time to prepare for the surgery to remove it. And researchers should set aside extra funds to support trial participants who have to do that.

Some of the guidelines are vague and may overlap with existing ethics standards. They don’t all spell out explicit solutions. They were also developed with feedback from a small group of individuals—the number of people living with BCIs is still very low. The team hopes to grow and expand on the guidelines over time. Burkhart also plans to discuss them with researchers at an upcoming neuroscience conference.

“This is a living document, and this is version one,” says Chandler. “It’s just the starting point.”

article_content_zh:
几十年来，科学家们一直致力于研究解码大脑活动的方法。团队已经开发出大脑植入物，可以用来控制机器人肢体和计算机，甚至可以“说话”。

伊恩·伯克哈特 (Ian Burkhart) 于 2014 年在自己的大脑中植入了一个设备，他表示，自愿参与这些设备试验的人们在这项研究中发挥着至关重要的作用，他们的贡献应该得到认可。他一直在为开发脑机接口 (BCI) 的研究人员制定一套指南。

临床试验的伦理指南已经存在。但 BCI 试验是不同的，渥太华大学法学和神经伦理学教授 Jennifer Chandler 说，她也参与了该指南的制定。 “这些人的大脑中嵌入了一个设备，有时需要多年的试验……[并贡献]大量的时间、身体和智力投入。”

2010 年，19 岁的伯克哈特在一次潜水事故中受伤，导致胸部以下瘫痪。大约四年后，他自愿成为第一个尝试用于手部控制的大脑植入物的人。

他的大脑控制运动的部分插入了一系列 96 个电极。电极通过一根电缆连接到计算机，电缆基本上插入了他的头部。计算机上的算法旨在解释这些信号，并将它们传送到伯克哈特手臂上佩戴的另一套电极，让他能够控制它。

最初的动作很小，但伯克哈特最终能够使用该系统从瓶子里倒出珠子，移动小而精致的物体，甚至玩吉他英雄，即使只是在实验室参观期间。这是一个科学突破。

伯克哈特在将电极阵列植入大脑的七年半期间，参加了为期两年的临床试验。 “这是一次美妙的经历，”他说。 “但肯定有一些事情，根据我现在所知道的，我想做一些不同的事情。”

2022 年，Burkhart 与他人共同创立了 BCI 先锋联盟，通过该组织，参与 BCI 试验的人们可以相互分享经验并与研究人员分享经验。去年，该小组成员根据这些经验制定了一套指导方针。这个想法是为了帮助学者、临床医生和公司进行尊重参与者自主权的道德试验。

该指南于周二发布，列出了 13 个类别的建议清单。例如，其中之一侧重于认可和补偿试验参与者。在伯克哈特参与的试验中，“我每周去实验室两三天，每次四个小时，”他回忆道。 “如果你只计算你投入的时间，那（很容易）是一份兼职工作。”

伯克哈特说，随着试验的进展，他学到了更多东西，并且能够就哪些有效、哪些无效提供更具建设性的反馈。他说他是研究团队的关键成员。他说，其他处于类似职位的人可能会喜欢被列为科学出版物的合著者或公开任命为研究合作者。然而，伯克哈特和他的同事承认，并不是每个人都会想要这样。

该指南还解决了棘手的隐私问题。这很重要：公众永远对此类尖端生物技术感兴趣，指南称研究人员还有责任让参与者为可能受到媒体关注做好准备。在某些情况下，可能很难完全隐藏试验参与者的身份。

当涉及到参与者大脑数据的隐私时，事情变得更加复杂。研究团队需要访问、分析并（至少暂时）存储这些数据。伯克哈特对此并不太在意，因为科学家们正在收集与运动相关的神经活动。但那些植入了旨在将思想转化为语言的大脑植入物的人可能会有不同的感觉。

该指南指出，大脑数据“应被理解为参与者的个人信息”。他们正在推动参与者能够随时访问自己的大脑数据（这并不总是可行），并希望确保人们不会因为旨在向竞争对手保密研究结果的禁运或保密协议（NDA）而无法与自己的医生分享这些数据。

伯克哈特说：“在许多试验中，达成严格的保密协议的情况并不常见。” “但我们希望确保这种情况不会发生。”

title: Silicon Valley claims to know the future. So why did it get the midterms so wrong?
title_en: Silicon Valley claims to know the future. So why did it get the midterms so wrong?
author: MIT Tech Review
article_content:
The self-styled visionaries of Silicon Valley, leaders like OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman and SpaceX boss Elon Musk, have built careers claiming to see the future. Long-term vision is currency: Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg built a 10-year road map for Facebook in 2016, and Google famously told investors before its public offering that it was unconcerned with short-term results. And yet there they all were, a mere five weeks before the midterm elections, gathered at the White House to smile for photos with President Trump and sign on to his “Super Intelligence” agenda.

Even by the diminished standards of today’s corporate governance, this was a shockingly foolish decision. Despite dozens of polls showing a rising tide of anti-Trump sentiment and bipartisan rejection of AI and data centers, the futurists of the tech elite cast aside long-term corporate interests for short-term political favor. And now, their industry is very squarely in the new victors’ crosshairs.

For an industry obsessed with pattern recognition, their decision to lash themselves to President Trump has proved to be a catastrophic misreading of the political landscape. Now, not only have they jeopardized their companies’ fates, but they’ve also raised questions about their vision and judgment.

The people who work for them are just as confused as the rest of us. Tech workers I’ve spoken to at OpenAI, Meta, and other firms have noted an absence of commentary from their leaders post-election. Zuckerberg has yet to address the results internally, while an employee at another AI firm said that “leadership has been pretty silent on Slack.” Most employees share concern about potential anti-data-center legislation and are curious how leadership will adjust to a Democratic Washington, DC. But more than anything, they don’t understand how their bosses didn’t see what was so blindingly obvious to everyone else.

In Silicon Valley, the Gretzkyism “skate to where the puck is going, not where it has been” is a management maxim; it preaches anticipation and foresight over reactiveness to the present moment. Tech entrepreneurs love a good “pivot,” and companies that can’t change with the times get disrupted and die.

Which is why I find it so strange that Zuckerberg, OpenAI cofounder Greg Brockman, and so many of Silicon Valley’s other prominent AI leaders and venture capitalists have put themselves in a potentially inescapable political bind. In going all in on President Trump’s cultural and business agenda instead of playing both sides of the aisle as corporate America usually does, they’ve built identities they may not be able to pivot out of. Will anyone really believe that Palantir CEO Alex Karp is suddenly progressive after a year of promising “violence and death to our enemies” and telling investors that the company is “completely anti-woke”?

I believe this is less a surprise than a very public exposure of a fundamental reality: that tech’s most visible leaders are not all-knowing visionary masterminds after all. Insights about social media or artificial intelligence do not make Zuckerberg or Altman experts on politics, the economy, or much else outside of technology. The instant gratification of presidential access, subsidies, and a say in their own regulation blinded them to the basics of political math that they clearly did not understand.

There’s a reason the chief executives of Chase, Boeing, and other Fortune 500 staples don’t go on podcasts to talk about “masculine energy,” or call the president from the stage of a MAGA-friendly AI summit to label fears about AI a “hoax” and a “scam.” This is the learned wisdom of decades operating in an environment where the customer changes every four years but contracts run for 10. Most companies play to both sides of the aisle because they know that their business models and multibillion-dollar projects must outlast the current administration. Instead, Big Tech tied itself to Trump and made its most important goals and investments—many related to grid access and data center permits—immediate targets for Democrats.

In tech, you can always sunset a feature or update some code. But in politics, there is no undo button for failures that change public perception. The tech elites’ decision to visibly align their businesses with a temporary movement has left them no credible way to pivot now that the climate has changed. As one Meta employee who has worked closely with Zuckerberg put it, “Mark is a long-term thinker, but he never charts a plan of how to get there. It’s spray and pray and see what happens.” As for whether employees expect the company to do a strategic postmortem? “Facebook has never really done that.”

“Move fast and break things” might work in a startup, but it’s a terrible strategy for building reputational goodwill. Previous technological leaps, like the rollout of fiber-optic technology and wireless infrastructure, avoided partisan politics. But by kowtowing to the Trump administration, Silicon Valley made artificial intelligence a culture-war issue. Now, when citizens vote on data center proposals from California to Florida, they are no longer considering only technical or economic concerns, but political ones.

Tech leaders didn’t see this coming because they were too focused on the urgency of the AI race to understand how reputational damage could undermine the intangible goodwill—and ultimately the very tangible infrastructure—necessary to win it. The industry’s misreading of the moment has already punctured one myth Silicon Valley holds dear: that its leaders can always see what’s next.

Aaron Zamost is a tech communications consultant and a former executive at Square.

key_points_en: Key Development: Silicon Valley claims to know the future. So why did it get the midterms so wrong?

article_content_zh:
OpenAI 首席执行官山姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 和 SpaceX 老板埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 等硅谷自诩为梦想家的领导者在职业生涯中声称能够预见未来。长期愿景就是货币：Meta 的马克·扎克伯格 (Mark Zuckerberg) 在 2016 年为 Facebook 制定了 10 年路线图，谷歌在公开募股前告诉投资者，它不关心短期业绩。然而，距离中期选举仅五周，他们都聚集在白宫，微笑着与特朗普总统合影，并签署了他的“超级情报”议程。

即使按照当今公司治理标准的降低，这也是一个极其愚蠢的决定。尽管数十项民意调查显示反特朗普情绪高涨，两党都拒绝人工智能和数据中心，但科技精英的未来主义者为了短期政治利益而放弃了长期的企业利益。现在，他们的行业正成为新胜利者的瞄准目标。

对于一个痴迷于模式识别的行业来说，他们向特朗普总统发起攻击的决定已被证明是对政治格局的灾难性误读。现在，他们不仅危及公司的命运，而且还对他们的愿景和判断力提出了质疑。

为他们工作的人和我们其他人一样困惑。我在 OpenAI、Meta 和其他公司采访过的科技工作者都注意到，他们的领导人在选举后没有发表评论。扎克伯格尚未在内部讨论这一结果，而另一家人工智能公司的一名员工表示，“领导层对 Slack 一直保持沉默。”大多数员工都对潜在的反数据中心立法感到担忧，并好奇领导层将如何适应民主的华盛顿特区。但最重要的是，他们不明白为什么他们的老板没有看到其他人都如此显而易见的事情。

在硅谷，格雷茨基主义“滑向冰球要去的地方，而不是它曾经去过的地方”是一条管理格言；它宣扬的是对当前时刻的预期和远见，而不是被动反应。科技企业家喜欢良好的“支点”，而无法与时俱进的公司就会被颠覆并消亡。

这就是为什么我觉得扎克伯格、OpenAI 联合创始人格雷格·布罗克曼 (Greg Brockman) 以及硅谷其他许多杰出的人工智能领导者和风险投资家将自己置于潜在的不可避免的政治困境中如此奇怪。他们全力支持特朗普总统的文化和商业议程，而不是像美国企业界通常所做的那样左右逢源，他们已经建立了自己可能无法摆脱的身份。有人真的相信 Palantir 首席执行官亚历克斯·卡普 (Alex Karp) 在承诺“对我们的敌人使用暴力和死亡”并告诉投资者该公司“完全反觉醒”一年后突然进步了吗？

我认为这与其说是令人惊讶，不如说是对一个基本现实的公开曝光：科技界最引人注目的领导者毕竟不是无所不知的有远见的策划者。对社交媒体或人工智能的见解并不能使扎克伯格或奥特曼成为政治、经济或技术以外的许多其他领域的专家。总统准入权、补贴和在自己的监管中的发言权所带来的即时满足感使他们对他们显然不理解的政治数学基础知识视而不见。

大通银行、波音公司和其他财富 500 强企业的首席执行官不会在播客上谈论“男性能量”，也不会在支持 MAGA 的人工智能峰会的舞台上给总统打电话，将人们对人工智能的恐惧称为“骗局”和“骗局”，这是有原因的。这是几十年来在客户每四年更换一次但合同有效期为十年的环境中学到的智慧。大多数公司都在两边进行游戏，因为他们知道他们的商业模式和数十亿美元的项目必须比现任政府更长久。相反，大型科技公司将自己与特朗普联系在一起，并将其最重要的目标和投资（许多与电网接入和数据中心许可相关）作为民主党的直接目标。

在技​​术领域，您始终可以取消某个功能或更新某些代码。但在政治上，对于改变公众看法的失败，没有撤销按钮。由于气候已经发生变化，科技精英们决定将自己的业务与临时运动进行明显调整，这让他们没有可靠的方式进行转型。正如一位与扎克伯格密切合作的 Meta 员工所说，“马克是一位长期思考者，但他从未制定过如何实现这一目标的计划。只是不断地祈祷，看看会发生什么。”至于员工是否期望公司做战略事后剖析？ “Facebook 从未真正这样做过。”

“快速行动，打破陈规”可能对初创公司有效，但对于建立声誉商誉而言，这是一个糟糕的策略。以前的技术飞跃，例如光纤技术和无线基础设施的推出，都避免了党派政治。但通过向特朗普政府屈服，硅谷让人工智能成为了文化战争问题。现在，当公民对从加利福尼亚州到佛罗里达州的数据中心提案进行投票时，他们不再只考虑技术或经济问题，而是考虑政治问题。

科技领导者没有预见到这一点，因为他们过于关注人工智能竞赛的紧迫性，以至于无法理解声誉受损如何会破坏赢得这场比赛所需的无形商誉，并最终破坏非常有形的基础设施。业界对当下的误读已经戳破了硅谷所珍视的一个神话：其领导者总能预见接下来会发生什么。

Aaron Zamost 是一名技术传播顾问，也是 Square 的前高管。

AlphaGo 与围棋冠军李世石的比赛已经过去十年了，今天的人工智能仍然没有利用让这场胜利成为可能的机制。

对研究员尼克·卡马拉塔 (Nick Cammarata) 的独家采访，他的 26,000 字病毒博客文章让人工智能安全人士欢呼不已。

title: Shield helps technicians hand off legacy portal work with OpenAI
title_en: Shield helps technicians hand off legacy portal work with OpenAI
author: OpenAI 官方动态
article_content:
With GPT‑6 Astra, the agents in Shield’s Forge platform navigate legacy portals so technicians can focus on issues that need their attention.

For many small and medium-sized businesses, an outsourced IT services provider handles everything from an employee locked out of their laptop to a misconfigured firewall that took the office offline.

Shield built Forge⁠(opens in a new window), an AI operating system for IT services providers. The platform brings together business data and customer context to help providers complete IT support tasks end to end. That means its agents also need to work in the older portals technicians use every day. With OpenAI’s GPT‑6 Astra, Shield can now hand supported browser tasks to agents instead of leaving a technician to log in and finish them manually.

“If a customer is locked out of their computer or there’s a phishing attack, speed is paramount,” says Jain. “Whether you’re going to solve their issue or you’re going to escalate to a human, you want to do either as fast as possible.”

Before using GPT‑6 Astra, Forge’s agents could get stuck at systems they could not access. Customers then had to wait for a technician to complete that step.

Shield tried computer use, where an AI model reads the screen, clicks, and types, with earlier models. Jain says they were not reliable or fast enough. “Usually, a system that doesn’t have an API is an old-school system that also doesn’t look very nice and is very hard to use, even by a human,” Jain says.

Technicians spend much of their day in portals that manage tickets, devices and software licenses. Many of those systems lack APIs, so an agent needs to navigate the screen much as a person would.

Forge’s AI Engineer assigns the work to a computer-use agent, and GPT‑6 Astra navigates the interface to complete supported tasks. Technicians decide which actions it can take on its own and where they need to review or approve the work.

Shield says these browser workflows are live, with thousands of runs each month across its IT providers. Phone calls, on-site work and remote-desktop tasks still need human involvement.

“GPT‑6 Astra allows our agents to embody what a technician does by logging into portals and legacy websites that might not have API access and performing tasks that only a human could six months ago,” says Mayank Jain, Head of Technology at Shield.

Jain says GPT‑6 Astra was 35-40% faster on average than the legacy models Shield had used for computer-use tasks. He also says customer satisfaction is higher on tickets where AI is used, with speed of resolution being a critical factor.

Shield reports faster execution, fewer failures and fewer timeouts. Its teams also spend less time writing detailed instructions to an agent or helping it through a task.

Shield is testing remote-desktop workflows that would let agents perform more complex actions directly on a computer’s desktop.

Jain says, “With GPT‑6 Astra, Forge is now truly an extension of our human technicians.”

article_content_zh:
借助 GPT‑6 Astra，Shield Forge 平台中的代理可以导航旧门户，以便技术人员可以专注于需要他们关注的问题。

对于许多中小型企业来说，外包 IT 服务提供商会处理一切事务，从员工无法使用笔记本电脑到因防火墙配置错误导致办公室脱机等。

Shield 构建了 Forge⁠（在新窗口中打开），这是一个面向 IT 服务提供商的人工智能操作系统。该平台汇集了业务数据和客户背景，帮助提供商完成端到端的 IT 支持任务。这意味着它的代理还需要在技术人员每天使用的旧门户中工作。借助 OpenAI 的 GPT‑6 Astra，Shield 现在可以将支持的浏览器任务交给代理，而不是让技术人员手动登录并完成这些任务。

“如果客户被锁定在计算机之外或存在网络钓鱼攻击，速度就至关重要，”Jain 说。 “无论你是要解决他们的问题，还是要升级到人工处理，你都希望尽快做到这一点。”

在使用 GPT-6 Astra 之前，Forge 的代理可能会陷入无法访问的系统。然后，客户必须等待技术人员完成该步骤。

Shield 尝试了计算机的使用，其中人工智能模型在早期模型中读取屏幕、点击和打字。杰恩说他们不够可靠或不够快。 “通常，没有 API 的系统是一个老式系统，看起来不太漂亮，而且很难使用，即使对于人类来说也是如此，”Jain 说。

技术人员每天的大部分时间都花在管理票证、设备和软件许可证的门户上。其中许多系统缺乏 API，因此代理需要像人一样在屏幕上导航。

Forge 的 AI 工程师将工作分配给计算机使用代理，GPT-6 Astra 导航界面以完成支持的任务。技术人员决定可以自行采取哪些操作以及需要在何处审查或批准工作。

Shield 表示，这些浏览器工作流程是实时的，其 IT 提供商每月运行数千次。电话、现场工作和远程桌面任务仍然需要人工参与。

“GPT-6 Astra 允许我们的代理通过登录可能没有 API 访问权限的门户和旧网站并执行六个月前只有人类才能完成的任务来体现技术人员的工作，”Shield 技术主管 Mayank Jain 说道。

Jain 表示，GPT-6 Astra 比 Shield 用于计算机使用任务的传统模型平均快 35-40%。他还表示，使用人工智能的机票客户满意度更高，解决速度是一个关键因素。

Shield 报告执行速度更快、故障更少、超时更少。其团队还花更少的时间向代理编写详细说明或帮助其完成任务。

Shield 正在测试远程桌面工作流程，该工作流程将允许代理直接在计算机桌面上执行更复杂的操作。

Jain 说：“借助 GPT-6 Astra，Forge 现在真正成为了我们人类技术人员的延伸。”
