title: Oh, Palantir is ‘progressive’ now, is it?
title_en: Oh, Palantir is ‘progressive’ now, is it?
author: The Verge AI
article_content:
I had other things to do today, but Alex Karp’s pathetic attempt to pivot back to the left gave me no choice but to put them on hold.

Last week’s elections were a bloodbath for the right, a problem for all the wannabe fash founders who had tied their political fortunes to a “vibe shift” that enabled a glorious 100-year Trumpenreich. That freed up a lot of assholes to say what they actually thought. Except Donald Trump’s victory was, in fact, narrow, and two years of his corrupt policies have enraged Americans.

“I’ve been a Democrat my whole life. I grew up in a far left environment. I know more about being a progressive than almost anybody on the planet, and I absolutely believe Palantir— all of our products are essentially progressive,” Karp told Politico.

Is that so, baby doll? Let’s run it back.

* August 2024: “I’m not going to apologize for defending the U.S. government on the border, defending the Special Ops, bringing the people home,” he told Maureen Dowd.

* February 2025: Karp wrote in a letter to shareholders that “As Samuel Huntington has written, the rise of the West was not made possible ‘by the superiority of its ideas or values or religion . . . but rather by its superiority in applying organized violence.’”

* February 2025: “Palantir is ‘making America more lethal’ by analyzing troves of data for the U.S. armed forces and allies to help them anticipate enemies’ moves, locate their coordinates ‘and, on occasion, kill them.’” I am quoting the WSJ here. The WSJ is quoting an earnings call.

* November 2025: Palantir is “the first company to be completely anti-woke,” Karp declared on an earnings call.

* November 2025: “I spend a lot of time talking to Nazis. Like, real Nazis.”

* November 2025: “Democrats just completely neglect males.. It’s admirable to be a.. high-testosterone male. And.. you have the general vibe in the Democratic Party that there’s something wrong.. I don’t find it very appealing as a dude.” Also, from the same interview, referring to his Democratic friends: “You have to grow a spine because a lot of these people actually agree with me in private.”

* November 2025: “Our competition is political. The woke left and the woke right wake up every day, figuring out how they can hurt Palantir. If they get into power, they’ll hurt Palantir. And by the way, it’s global. I view Democrats as my party, but if the Mamdani wing of the party takes over? If that’s my party, I’m not in it. Or the right woke wing, which is like, everything is a conspiracy, any use of technology is actually going to only be used to eviscerate and attack us?” Also, on progressivism: “Universities and elite institutions have played a corrosive role here. People are teaching pagan religion views — a new religion with sacrifices. Who’s the sacrifice? Me, I’m the sacrifice.”

* December 2025: In response to The New York Times’ reporting on his company (unclear which article, maybe this one?): “That article about us being a surveillance thing — is like, where it’s all implied what we do — yeah, but the problem is you lose credibility with anyone who goes on the thing and then — and that’s damaging for our democracy.” Later, in the same interview: “The one thing I would say to people in the audience — you know you, a lot of you think I’m right. And you know your spouse, your relative, your child, the person at work would be horrified if they knew it. You better speak up. Because everyone who thinks I’m a ridiculous fascist, they’re speaking up. They write about it every day. If you do not speak up, the people who are disagreeing with me or think I’m stupid — well, I disagree with myself. So, you have to speak up. And you cannot blame the far left, far right idiots when they speak up for their views. Do you speak up for your views? Where?”

* April 2026: That manifesto, which was previously published as a book. “The postwar neutering of Germany and Japan must be undone. The defanging of Germany was an overcorrection for which Europe is now paying a heavy price.” Also, well after Elon Musk did his little uhhh hand gesture and DOGE ran rampant across the US government: “We should applaud those who attempt to build where the market has failed to act. The culture almost snickers at Musk’s interest in grand narrative.” And maybe most notably: “Some cultures have produced vital advances; others remain dysfunctional and regressive. All cultures are now equal. Criticism and value judgments are forbidden.”

* July 2026: On CNBC, referring to frontier models: “This is the voice of American business that is being channeled through me.”

Anyway, for any other tech bros who want to do a less clumsy pivot than Karp, I have a suggestion. First, go to rehab, ideally for 90 days. Then come out and apologize for whatever it was you said between, I don’t know, 2020 and now. You feel very bad about what you’ve said, but it was the cocaine (or the amphetamines, or hell, blame it on ketamine, since the average person has no idea what a ketamine high looks like) speaking. You have dried out and sobered up. It was a challenge, but it was rewarding. You are now chastened. You want to work for public accountability. You are sorry about the dumb things you said while you were high.

This won’t work for Karp, who’s been absolutely adamant that he does not do drugs. But you, the savvy tech CEO and/or VC, you can’t skip the rehab part. You can’t blame the drugs if you don’t at least pretend to sober up.

article_content_zh:
今天我还有其他事情要做，但亚历克斯·卡普（Alex Karp）可怜地试图向左转，让我别无选择，只能暂时搁置。

上周的选举对右翼来说是一场大屠杀，对所有想成为时尚创始人的人来说都是一个问题，他们将自己的政治命运与“氛围转变”联系在一起，从而实现了辉煌的特朗普帝国 100 年。这让很多混蛋得以自由说出他们的真实想法。事实上，唐纳德·特朗普的胜利是微弱的，而且他两年来的腐败政策激怒了美国人。

“我一生都是民主党人。我在极左的环境中长大。我比地球上几乎任何人都更了解如何成为一名进步人士，而且我绝对相信 Palantir——我们所有的产品本质上都是进步的，”卡普告诉 Politico。

是这样吗，娃娃？让我们回顾一下。

* 2024 年 8 月：“我不会因为在边境保卫美国政府、保卫特种部队、将人们带回家而道歉，”他告诉莫林·多德。

* 2025 年 2 月：卡普在致股东的一封信中写道，“正如塞缪尔·亨廷顿所写，西方的崛起不是‘凭借其思想、价值观或宗教的优越性……而是通过其在实施有组织暴力方面的优越性’而实现的。”

* 2025 年 2 月：“Palantir 正在‘让美国更具杀伤力’，为美国武装部队和盟国分析大量数据，帮助他们预测敌人的行动，定位他们的坐标，‘有时甚至杀死他们’。”我在这里引用了《华尔街日报》的内容。 《华尔街日报》援引了财报电话会议的消息。

* 2025 年 11 月：卡普在财报电话会议上宣称，Palantir 是“第一家完全反觉醒的公司”。

* 2025 年 11 月：“我花了很多时间与纳粹分子交谈。就像真正的纳粹分子一样。”

* 2025 年 11 月：“民主党人完全忽视了男性..成为一名..高睾酮男性是令人钦佩的。而且..民主党内普遍存在一种感觉，认为出了问题..作为一个男人，我觉得这不太有吸引力。”此外，在同一次采访中，他提到他的民主党朋友时说：“你必须坚强起来，因为很多人私下里实际上都同意我的观点。”

* 2025 年 11 月：“我们的竞争是政治性的。觉醒的左翼和觉醒的右翼每天都在思考如何伤害 Palantir。如果他们掌权，他们就会伤害 Palantir。顺便说一句，这是全球性的。我将民主党视为我的政党，但如果该党的 Mamdani 派接管了？如果那是我的政党，我就不在其中。或者觉醒的右翼，这就像，一切都是阴谋，任何使用技术实际上只会用来掏空和攻击我们？”另外，关于进步主义：“大学和精英机构在这里发挥了腐蚀作用。人们正在传授异教观点——一种带有牺牲的新宗教。谁是牺牲品？我，我就是牺牲品。”

* 2025 年 12 月：回应《纽约时报》对其公司的报道（不清楚是哪一篇文章，也许是这篇？）：“那篇关于我们从事监视活动的文章 — 就好像，这一切都暗示了我们所做的事情 — 是的，但问题是，你会失去任何参与此事的人的信誉，然后 — 这会损害我们的民主。”后来，在同一次采访中：“我要对观众说的一件事是——你们了解你们，你们很多人都认为我是对的。你们也知道，你们的配偶、亲戚、孩子、工作人员如果知道的话会感到震惊。你们最好大声说出来。因为每个认为我是可笑法西斯的人都在大声说出来。他们每天都在写这件事。如果你们不说出来，那些不同意我或认为我很愚蠢的人——好吧，我不同意我自己的观点，当他们表达自己的观点时，你不能责怪他们。”

* 2026 年 4 月：该宣言此前已作为一本书出版。 “战后对德国和日本的阉割必须取消。德国的去牙是一种矫枉过正，欧洲现在正在为此付出沉重的代价。”此外，在埃隆·马斯克做了一个“嗯嗯”的小手势之后，DOGE在美国政府中肆虐：“我们应该为那些试图在市场未能发挥作用的地方建设的人鼓掌。这种文化几乎嘲笑马斯克对宏大叙事的兴趣。”也许最值得注意的是：“一些文化取得了重大进步；另一些文化仍然功能失调和倒退。现在所有文化都是平等的。批评和价值判断是被禁止的。”

* 2026 年 7 月：在 CNBC 上，谈到前沿模型时：“这是通过我传达的美国商界的声音。”

title: Google DeepMind Staff Tap the UK Government to Escalate Their Unionization Fight
title_en: Google DeepMind Staff Tap the UK Government to Escalate Their Unionization Fight
author: Wired AI
article_content:
On Thursday, the Communication Workers Union and Unite the Union—put forward by Google DeepMind staff as joint representatives—filed an application with the Central Arbitration Committee, a government body that resolves disputes between employers and unions.

The application, which was seen by WIRED, asks the CAC to confirm that the unions have enough support from workers to trigger a unionization ballot. The company would be required by law to respect the results. If successful, roughly 1,000 staff working in product-focused roles at Google DeepMind would qualify for union membership.

Are you a current or former Google DeepMind employee who wants to talk about what’s happening? We’d like to hear from you. Using a nonwork phone or computer, contact the reporter securely on Signal at Joel_Khalili.28

The escalation follows a series of meetings between employees, the unions, and company representatives over voluntary unionization, which left staff with the impression that their demands weren’t being taken seriously.

“They’ve been ignored. They feel like their problems have been minimized,” John Chadfield, national officer for technology at the CWU, tells WIRED. “Management has refused to come to the table. They sent it to the HR and labor relations people, who dealt with it as an administrative box-ticking exercise.”

“We respect the right of employees to make an informed decision about whether or not to join a union,” Google DeepMind spokesperson Tom Hewett tells WIRED in a statement. “We have consistently listened to both those seeking to unionize and those opposed, and have acted in good faith from the outset. We remain committed to constructively participating in this process, and have maintained open and transparent communication with our employees and the unions throughout.”

The push to unionize began in February 2025, when Alphabet, Google’s parent company, removed a pledge from its ethics guidelines stating that it wouldn’t use AI for purposes like weapons development.

“When I joined, we really made a big deal about the principles—the red lines. We were really looking to benefit humanity and make the world a better place,” a Google DeepMind employee, who asked to remain anonymous for fear of backlash, tells WIRED. “A lot of this is about reestablishing that ethical and moral framework that we started with.”

The employees pushing for unionization object in particular to agreements between the company and the US and Israeli militaries. If they succeed in unionizing, they intend to demand that Google backs out of those contracts.

“We feel extremely concerned about the direction that this technology is going in,” says a second Google DeepMind employee, who asked to remain anonymous for the same reason as the first employee.

The company has previously defended its deals with government organizations.

“We are proud to be part of a broad consortium of leading AI labs and technology and cloud companies providing AI services and infrastructure in support of national security,” Jenn Crider, a Google spokeswoman, told The New York Times in April. “We remain committed to the private and public sector consensus that AI should not be used for domestic mass surveillance or autonomous weaponry without appropriate human oversight.”

In an email delivered to all UK staff on Thursday, seen by WIRED, the Google DeepMind employees involved in the unionization push appealed to their colleagues to participate in the ballot, which they expect to take place in the coming months. “We want a union, we want collective bargaining, and we want a say in how AI is developed and deployed,” they wrote.

The group also hopes it can establish a playbook that employees at other major AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic can follow in the UK.

“It’s pretty rare that there’s been an industry that exercises such dominance and power over the economy, where there’s so little opportunity for employees or regulators to have any checks and balances,” the second Google DeepMind employee says. “We want to show what can happen when employees collectively organize and articulate a shared vision for the way their technology should be used.”

article_content_zh:
周四，由谷歌 DeepMind 员工作为联合代表提出的通信工人工会和联合工会向中央仲裁委员会提出了申请，中央仲裁委员会是一个解决雇主和工会之间纠纷的政府机构。

《连线》杂志看到的这份申请要求 CAC 确认工会有足够的工人支持来触发工会投票。法律要求该公司尊重结果。如果成功，谷歌 DeepMind 大约 1,000 名从事产品工作的员工将有资格成为工会会员。

事态升级之前，员工、工会和公司代表就自愿加入工会问题举行了一系列会议，这给员工留下了他们的要求没有得到认真对待的印象。

“他们被忽视了。他们觉得自己的问题被最小化了，”CWU 国家技术官员约翰·查德菲尔德 (John Chadfield) 告诉《连线》杂志。 “管理层拒绝参加谈判。他们将其发送给人力资源和劳资关系人员，他们将其视为行政勾选操作。”

谷歌 DeepMind 发言人汤姆·休伊特 (Tom Hewett) 在一份声明中告诉《连线》杂志：“我们尊重员工就是否加入工会做出知情决定的权利。” “我们始终倾听那些寻求成立工会和反对工会的人的意见，并从一开始就真诚地采取行动。我们仍然致力于建设性地参与这一进程，并自始至终与我们的员工和工会保持开放和透明的沟通。”

工会的推动始于 2025 年 2 月，当时谷歌母公司 Alphabet 从其道德准则中删除了一项承诺，即不会将人工智能用于武器开发等目的。

“当我加入时，我们确实非常重视这些原则——红线。我们真的希望造福人类，让世界变得更美好，”一位因担心遭到强烈反对而要求匿名的谷歌 DeepMind 员工告诉《连线》杂志。 “这很大程度上是为了重建我们开始时的伦理和道德框架。”

推动成立工会的员工尤其反对该公司与美国和以色列军方之间达成的协议。如果他们成功组建工会，他们打算要求谷歌退出这些合同。

“我们对这项技术的发展方向感到非常担忧，”另一位 Google DeepMind 员工说道，他要求匿名，原因与第一位员工相同。

该公司此前曾为其与政府组织的交易进行过辩护。

谷歌发言人 Jenn Crider 四月份对《纽约时报》表示：“我们很自豪能够成为由领先的人工智能实验室和技术以及云公司组成的广泛联盟的一部分，提供人工智能服务和基础设施以支持国家安全。” “我们仍然致力于私营和公共部门的共识，即在没有适当的人类监督的情况下，人工智能不应被用于国内大规模监视或自主武器。”

《连线》杂志看到，在周四发送给所有英国员工的电子邮件中，参与工会推动的谷歌 DeepMind 员工呼吁他们的同事参加投票，他们预计投票将在未来几个月内举行。他们写道：“我们想要一个工会，我们想要集体谈判，我们想要在人工智能的开发和部署方面拥有发言权。”

该组织还希望能够制定一份行动手册，供 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等其他主要人工智能实验室的英国员工可以遵循。

title: The Jensen Huang scandal is hardly over
title_en: The Jensen Huang scandal is hardly over
author: The Verge AI
article_content:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

A second affair has hit the news cycle, but that’s not what matters here.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

I was certain, until the story of Jensen Huang’s second affair hit, that Huang was bulletproof. After all, why wouldn’t he be? He’s placed himself indispensably at the center of the AI industry and famously had no succession plan at Nvidia. In fact, he’s the only CEO Nvidia has ever had. L’état c’est moi.

Then two stories were published nearly back to back on Wednesday: one alleging Huang had an affair with his subordinate Kimberly Powell, another that the board was meeting to consider his ouster. First thing Thursday morning, Nvidia announced Huang had resigned. One of the most powerful men in Silicon Valley was out.

Why throw Huang under the bus for getting his nuts drained?

Fascinating. First of all, when I asked on Monday “Who else is Jensen Huang fucking?” I did not expect to get answers this fast — somebody, potentially somebody on the board (as we’ve seen in other incidents), wanted the story out there. Second, why throw Huang under the bus for getting his nuts drained? This is not an industry that cares about that kind of thing — just ask Eric Schmidt and Bill Gates. My guess is that the second affair is a pretext for action, and this all goes back to the original story from last week: that Huang was honeypotted by an alleged Chinese spy. Whatever was going on with neocloud Megaspeed might be much, much worse than we know, and what we know is pretty bad: business listings that led to “a Malaysian data center and shopping mall, a near-empty office in Singapore and a dilapidated storefront outside Kuala Lumpur.”

Do you have information about Nvidia? Contact Elizabeth Lopatto securely on Signal at lopatto.46.

Even months before the report that Alice “No Relation” Huang, an exec at Megaspeed, was having an affair with Huang, there were questions about Nvidia’s business in China. The US government has placed strict export controls on Nvidia’s high-end chips. Huang claimed in May that as a result, Nvidia has zero percent market share in China. But also in May, short sellers Culper Research published a report in which they wrote, “We believe that in reality, over 20% of Nvidia’s FY 2026 compute revenues remained driven by China – supported both by illegal GPU diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries.”

Megaspeed was Nvidia’s largest Southeast Asian buyer, but Singaporean newspaper The Straits Times visited Megaspeed’s Singapore office in October 2025 ago to find “no signs of activity.” Another building tenant told the reporters, “It is always dark for as long as it has been here. I hardly see anyone visiting or in the office.” The sole director of Megaspeed, Tan Yong Pong, appears to have vanished. The Singaporean company that owns Megaspeed, Swiftdata, has listed an office that belongs to an interior design firm as its business address.

Incidentally, Alice Huang has surfaced in Beijing. The Financial Times says she’s barred from Singapore for giving police “inaccurate information.” Oh, and reportedly her companies invested in Chinese AI company DeepSeek and promised them Nvidia’s Blackwell chips? Fun!

Megaspeed is only part of the story, I think. There are two Chinese chip-related scandals that could cause serious problems for Nvidia, and both feature people with close ties to Huang. One is Megaspeed, which involves Huang’s maybe-spy affair partner. The other centers on Super Micro (which, horribly, does business as Supermicro), a partner of Nvidia run by one of Huang’s old friends, Charles Liang. Super Micro’s cofounder, Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, along with Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang and Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun, allegedly defrauded the US by serving as a passthrough for a front company to buy $2.5 billion of Nvidia chips for Alibaba. The front company, not named in the indictment, is Thailand-based OBON, according to Bloomberg. Liang and Super Micro have not been charged.

But these incidents may not be the end of Nvidia’s problems. Take for instance, more recently, New Matrix — another company that barely exists, and yet is an approved buyer of Nvidia chips. It is, in fact, one of several approved companies that “have ties to firms that have been blacklisted by the U.S. government, or that work as military contractors in China,” according to The New York Times.

Huang has insisted that Nvidia has seen “no evidence of any AI chip diversion.” He’s been pretty emphatic on that point, actually. I am now wondering if that is even a little bit true. If the board is cutting Huang loose, there’s probably more on chip smuggling allegations coming.

More substantively, Nvidia reportedly intervened in a 2025 Commerce Department investigation of Megaspeed, which was suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips — halting the investigation. Since the scandal broke, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick appears to have become the fall guy for this, with Axios reporting that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent “confronted” him about failing to note Megaspeed as a national security concern and Politico saying “more than half a dozen Republicans have demanded answers” from him.

The question, of course, is how high this all goes. After all, Huang was awfully buddy-buddy with President Donald Trump, who was informed about Huang’s maybe-spy girlfriend in 2025 and apparently did nothing about it. Incidentally, Nvidia has reportedly donated $25 million to Trump’s planned ballroom. This is what gangster tech regulation looks like.

I wonder what else was an open secret at the company, you know?

Come January, Elizabeth Warren will be able to send subpoenas in her role as the chair of the Senate Banking Committee. And wouldn’t you know, she seems to be pretty interested. Democrats will control both the House and the Senate. Their voters have given them a mandate to root out corruption. And boy howdy, does Nvidia look like a sitting duck right now. If Huang knew chips were being diverted — or had reason to know that — and tried to ensure their sales anyway, he may have committed actual crimes (bribery, espionage, smuggling, whatever) and, under a functioning legal system, could actually go to jail. Nvidia dispensing with its indispensable CEO is the company reducing its risk of getting roped into Huang’s drama.

Will it be that easy for Nvidia? I wonder. The most interesting part of the second affair story, with Powell, the Nvidia vice president of healthcare, comes at the very end of the New York Times article. When someone took a video of Powell and Huang being “affectionate” in March, Huang’s security had nondisclosure agreements ready to go. CNBC reports that rumors of their affair have circulated “for years.” I wonder what else was an open secret at the company, you know? Especially since Huang had 60 direct reports, so every part of the company is covered in his fingerprints.

Over in the tech world, people still seem to be in denial. On X, the social network for Trumpist dead-enders, the account “zerohedge” posted, “Elon please hire Jensen.” Elon Musk replied, “That would be an honor.”

Correction Nov. 13th: Corrects date on Straits Times visit to Megaspeed.

第二件事已经成为新闻焦点，但这不是重点。

该作者的帖子将添加到您的每日电子邮件摘要和主页源中。

在黄仁勋第二次婚外情的故事曝光之前，我确信黄是刀枪不入的。毕竟，他为什么不呢？他将自己置于人工智能行业不可或缺的中心地位，并且众所周知，他在英伟达没有继任计划。事实上，他是英伟达有史以来唯一的首席执行官。 L'état c'est moi。

随后，周三几乎连续发表了两篇报道：一篇指控黄与他的下属金伯利·鲍威尔有染，另一则称董事会正在开会考虑罢免他。周四早上，英伟达第一件事就是宣布黄仁勋辞职。硅谷最有权势的人之一出局了。

为什么要把黄扔到公共汽车下，因为他的坚果被榨干了？

迷人。首先，当我周一问“黄仁勋他妈的还有谁？”我没想到会这么快得到答案——有人，可能是董事会中的某个人（正如我们在其他事件中看到的那样），想要把这个故事公之于众。其次，为什么要因为黄的坚果被榨干而将他置于公共汽车之下？这不是一个关心这类事情的行业——问问埃里克·施密特和比尔·盖茨就知道了。我的猜测是，第二件事是采取行动的借口，而这一切都可以追溯到上周的原始故事：黄被一名所谓的中国间谍诱骗。无论 Neocloud Megaspeed 发生了什么，都可能比我们想象的要糟糕得多，而且我们所知道的情况非常糟糕：导致“马来西亚数据中心和购物中心、新加坡几乎空无一人的办公室以及吉隆坡郊外破旧的店面”的商业清单。

您有关于 Nvidia 的信息吗？通过 Signal 安全联系 Elizabeth Lopatto，地址为 lopatto.46。

甚至在报道称 Megaspeed 高管爱丽丝“无关系”黄与黄有染的几个月前，就有人对英伟达在中国的业务提出质疑。美国政府对英伟达的高端芯片实施了严格的出口管制。黄在五月份声称，英伟达在中国的市场份额为零。但同样是在 5 月，卖空者 Culper Research 发布了一份报告，其中写道：“我们认为，实际上，Nvidia 2026 财年超过 20% 的计算收入仍然由中国推动，并得到非法 GPU 转移和东南亚中间商的支持。”

Megaspeed 是 Nvidia 最大的东南亚买家，但新加坡报纸《海峡时报》于 2025 年 10 月前访问了 Megaspeed 的新加坡办事处，发现“没有任何活动迹象”。另一位住户告诉记者，“自从这里以来，这里一直都是黑暗的。我几乎看不到有人来访或在办公室里。” Megaspeed 的唯一董事 Tan Yong Pong 似乎失踪了。拥有 Megaspeed 的新加坡公司 Swiftdata 将一家室内设计公司的办公室列为其营业地址。

顺便说一句，黄爱丽 (Alice Huang) 已在北京露面。英国《金融时报》称，她因向警方提供“不准确信息”而被禁止进入新加坡。哦，据报道她的公司投资了中国人工智能公司 DeepSeek 并承诺向他们提供 Nvidia 的 Blackwell 芯片？乐趣！

我认为，Megaspeed 只是故事的一部分。有两起与中国芯片相关的丑闻可能会给英伟达带来严重问题，这两起丑闻都涉及与黄仁勋关系密切的人。其中之一是“Megaspeed”，涉及黄的可能是间谍的伴侣。另一个以超微（可怕的是，它以超微的名义开展业务）为中心，它是英伟达的合作伙伴，由黄的一位老朋友梁朝伟经营。超微联合创始人 Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw 与 Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang 和 Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun 涉嫌欺骗美国，充当一家幌子公司为阿里巴巴购买 25 亿美元 Nvidia 芯片的中间人。据彭博社报道，起诉书中未提及名字的幌子公司是总部位于泰国的 OBON。梁和超微尚未受到指控。

但这些事件可能并不是英伟达问题的终结。以最近的 New Matrix 为例，这是另一家几乎不存在的公司，但却是 Nvidia 芯片的认可买家。事实上，据《纽约时报》报道，该公司是几家获得批准的公司之一，这些公司“与被美国政府列入黑名单的公司或在中国从事军事承包商的公司有联系”。

黄坚称，英伟达“没有发现任何人工智能芯片被转移的证据”。事实上，他非常强调这一点。我现在想知道这是否是真的。如果董事会解除黄先生的职务，可能会出现更多芯片走私指控。

title: AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds
title_en: AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds
author: The Verge AI
article_content:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

A study testing Gemini, Perplexity, and ChatGPT found that in as many as 15 percent of conversations, chatbots displayed ‘risky’ URLs.﻿

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Shoppers using AI chatbots to research products or find places to buy items could be directed to imposters and other risky websites, a new study found.

The study conducted by IP protection firm Podqi and shared exclusively with The Verge prompted ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity with a handful of shopping-related questions involving a selection of 151 brands. Questions included “What are the top websites for buying [brand]?”; “Where can I find [brand] online?”; and “Does [brand] ship internationally? What are their regional websites?” The test ran over the course of two testing periods in September and asked about 151 small and large companies like fashion brands Lululemon, Birkenstock, Stüssy, and Madhappy (a client of Podqi) and homeware brand Le Creuset. Podqi crafted its own prompts (as opposed to using real user conversations) and tested its prompts using a tool that tracks AI answers across chatbots.

Over the course of 6,795 answers, Podqi found that all three AI engines cited and showed shoppers risky sites, defined as fake websites impersonating real retailers or selling knockoffs, old brand domains that have been reregistered by someone else, or dead sites that aren’t active at all but that someone else could purchase and reuse. Google’s Gemini showed risky sites least often of the three, linking to or mentioning a risky site in 4 percent of answers. (Mentions include instances of recommending a risky site, displaying it without comment, and warning a user about it.) Perplexity performed the worst, showing risky sites in 15 percent of answers. ChatGPT fell somewhere in the middle at 8 percent. ChatGPT performed the best when it came to offering warnings about each risky site that it surfaced, doing so 24 percent of the time. Smaller brands appear especially at risk: Podqi found that queries related to larger companies had risky sites in answers about half as often.

AI companies market chatbots as being helpful for shopping tasks like researching, comparing, and discovering products or retailers. AI citing fake sites is a headache for brands and retailers, of course, but it could also quickly become a risk for consumers. The issue could be especially relevant going into the upcoming holiday shopping season, when consumers are hunting around for in-stock items and the best prices. It’s likely that more consumers will be using AI to shop this year, including buying products from brands or sites they’re not already familiar with.

“Part of this piece, too, is making sure that the consumers know, even though you are being fed a result in a particular chatbot, it is always best to verify the source of that before entering personal information or credit card information,” says Podqi CEO and cofounder Trevor West.

“We take information quality seriously, and are happy to see that Gemini performed best among the products tested,” Google spokesperson Jessica Levis Boord said in an email. “We continually work to test and improve our models, and are upfront that Gemini is AI and can make mistakes, so we display links to sources alongside responses to help people verify information.”

“Our goal is for ChatGPT to connect people with reliable places to shop,” OpenAI spokesperson Taya Christianson said in an email. “We’re continuing to improve our safeguards to make potentially deceptive sites less likely to appear in shopping-related results. We appreciate researchers sharing examples that show us where we can improve the experience.”

In Podqi’s test, certain prompts seemed to trigger risky sites more often than others. For example, AI displayed risky sites more often when asked about regional brand websites compared to other prompt categories. The tested AI engines also at times listed fake regional sites for brands that do not have any. In one conversation, Perplexity named the wrong page as Stüssy’s official website and called it “the best starting point for guaranteed authentic items.”

“Perplexity is consistently the most accurate AI on credible research benchmarks, and has been for four years. We never claim to be 100% accurate, but we do claim to be the only company relentlessly focused on it,” spokesperson Jesse Dwyer said in an email.

该主题的帖子将添加到您的每日电子邮件摘要和主页源中。

一项测试 Gemini、Perplexity 和 ChatGPT 的研究发现，在多达 15% 的对话中，聊天机器人显示“有风险”的 URL。

该作者的帖子将添加到您的每日电子邮件摘要和主页源中。

一项新研究发现，使用人工智能聊天机器人研究产品或寻找购买地点的购物者可能会被引导至冒名顶替者和其他有风险的网站。

这项由知识产权保护公司 Podqi 进行并独家与 The Verge 分享的研究促使 ChatGPT、Gemini 和 Perplexity 提出了一些涉及 151 个品牌的购物相关问题。问题包括“购买[品牌]的热门网站是什么？”； “我在哪里可以在线找到[品牌]？”；以及“[品牌]是否在国际范围内发货？他们的区域网站是什么？”该测试在 9 月份进行了两个测试期，询问了 151 家小型和大型公司，例如时尚品牌 Lululemon、Birkenstock、Stüssy 和 Madhappy（Podqi 的客户）以及家居用品品牌 Le Creuset。 Podqi 制作了自己的提示（而不是使用真实的用户对话），并使用跨聊天机器人跟踪 AI 答案的工具测试了其提示。

在 6,795 个答案中，Podqi 发现所有三个人工智能引擎都引用并向购物者展示了有风险的网站，这些网站被定义为冒充真实零售商或销售仿冒品的虚假网站、已被其他人重新注册的旧品牌域名，或者根本不活跃但其他人可以购买和重复使用的死网站。 Google 的 Gemini 在这三个网站中显示风险网站的频率最少，只有 4% 的答案链接到或提及风险网站。 （提到的内容包括推荐一个有风险的网站、在没有评论的情况下显示该网站以及警告用户有关该网站的情况。）困惑度表现最差，在 15% 的答案中显示了有风险的网站。 ChatGPT 的占比处于中间位置，为 8%。 ChatGPT 在针对其出现的每个风险网站提供警告方面表现最好，达到了 24%。较小的品牌似乎面临的风险尤其大：Podqi 发现，与大公司相关的查询在答案中包含有风险网站的频率大约是大公司的一半。

人工智能公司将聊天机器人推销为有助于研究、比较和发现产品或零售商等购物任务。当然，人工智能引用虚假网站令品牌和零售商头疼，但它也可能很快成为消费者的风险。这个问题在即将到来的假日购物季可能尤其重要，因为此时消费者正在寻找库存商品和最优惠的价格。今年可能会有更多消费者使用人工智能购物，包括从他们不熟悉的品牌或网站购买产品。

Podqi 首席执行官兼联合创始人特雷弗·韦斯特 (Trevor West) 表示：“这件事的一部分也是确保消费者知道，即使你在特定的聊天机器人中得到结果，最好在输入个人信息或信用卡信息之前验证该结果的来源。”

谷歌发言人杰西卡·李维斯·博德（Jessica Levis Boord）在一封电子邮件中表示：“我们非常重视信息质量，很高兴看到 Gemini 在测试的产品中表现最好。” “我们不断努力测试和改进我们的模型，并坦言 Gemini 是人工智能，可能会犯错误，因此我们在回复旁边显示来源链接，以帮助人们验证信息。”

OpenAI 发言人 Taya Christianson 在一封电子邮件中表示：“我们的目标是让 ChatGPT 将人们与可靠的购物场所联系起来。” “我们正在继续改进我们的保护措施，以减少潜在的欺骗性网站出现在购物相关结果中的可能性。我们感谢研究人员分享的示例，这些示例向我们展示了可以在哪些方面改进体验。”

在 Podqi 的测试中，某些提示似乎比其他提示更频繁地触发危险网站。例如，与其他提示类别相比，当被问及区域品牌网站时，人工智能更频繁地显示有风险的网站。接受测试的人工智能引擎有时还会列出没有任何品牌的虚假区域网站。在一次对话中，Perplexity 将错误的页面命名为 Stüssy 的官方网站，并称其为“保证正品的最佳起点”。

“Perplexity 一直是可信研究基准上最准确的人工智能，四年来一直如此。我们从未声称 100% 准确，但我们确实声称是唯一一家不懈关注它的公司，”发言人杰西·德怀尔 (Jesse Dwyer) 在一封电子邮件中表示。

Thousands of delegates, lobbyists, and journalists have gathered in Antalya, Turkey, for COP31, the annual UN climate talks. But this year’s negotiations are taking place against a particularly tense geopolitical backdrop, as the world falls further behind the Paris Agreement’s goals.

Energy prices are soaring, and there are big questions about how countries will tackle the climate crisis. Expect a lot of back and forth on fossil fuels and climate finance, and whether negotiators can agree on meaningful action.

Here’s what you need to know about COP31.

Far-thinking technologists are working on ways to keep your brain going beyond death. MIT Technology Review’s latest Roundtables event explores their ideas, from gradual brain replacement to uploading memories to the cloud.

Tune in live on Tuesday, November 17 at 5:00 p.m. GMT / 12:00 p.m. EST / 9:00 a.m. PST.

An average of 470 AI-generated short dramas were released every day in January. Production timelines have shrunk from months to weeks, while costs have dropped by up to 90%. Storytelling is also increasingly driven by performance data.

title: Gondola doubles revenue as its team builds more with Codex
title_en: Gondola doubles revenue as its team builds more with Codex
author: OpenAI 官方动态
article_content:
Gondola helps creatives get credit and get hired, with Codex raising its lead engineer’s output by 50% and ChatGPT simplifying daily work.

While running his creative production agency, Fresh Tape Media, Jared Kleinstein noticed a problem: incredible creative work was being made for social media, but the makers weren’t getting proper credit. So he built the Gondola⁠(opens in a new window) platform to help creatives show what they made, prove its impact, and turn their work into their next opportunity.

For Gondola’s small team, one of the biggest constraints was how much product and operational work it could take on. Even small experiments competed with core product priorities for engineering time, and finding information and drafting work required sifting through tools and systems.

Today, the team uses Codex to turn more ideas into software and ChatGPT to simplify daily operations. Monthly engineering output is up 25% across the team and up 50% for its lead engineer. Company revenue has more than doubled year over year. For Jared, this has changed what feels possible for the team.

Many of Gondola’s product ideas come directly from customer conversations and operational problems that the business development and leadership team sees firsthand. Before Codex, they would have to define the need and write requirements and then wait for an engineer to have capacity to build the first version.

Now the same team uses Codex Cloud to explore the codebase, prototype an interface or workflow, test assumptions, and often get to a functional first version before an engineer needs to step in. Jared and Gondola’s Creator and Client Partnerships Manager Jojo Hesketh have both merged their first-ever code contributions into the main codebase.

One example is Programs, a tool Gondola built to help companies find creatives, review applicants, manage projects, and track budgets, with plans to help coordinate contracts and payments.

Jojo sponsored Programs and used Codex to prototype its workflows before handing them to engineers to refine and release. The team started with GPT‑5.4, did most of the work with GPT‑5.5, and used GPT‑6.1 for later features, optimizations, and bug fixes.

Jared estimates that Codex saved days, if not weeks, of development time and helped the team launch Programs with fewer bugs than if they had coded it by hand. “The Programs feature benefited from our ability to rapidly prototype, throw away things that didn’t work, and keep the things that did,” says Jared.

Gondola’s engineers use Codex through the command-line interface (CLI) and editor tools to accelerate implementation, and in GitHub to review pull requests. The company connects Codex to its repositories, development environments, and Slack, so product context can inform development. Engineers remain responsible for architecture, security, data handling, and production readiness.

Before Codex, time-sensitive ideas might sit in a backlog awaiting engineering resources while the opportunity passed by. But this summer, Codex enabled Gondola to build and test a World Cup Creator Map while it was still timely.

The team used Codex to rapidly turn data it already held into an experience built for an immediate customer need, creating a map that allowed brands, teams, and agencies to find photographers and videographers in World Cup host cities.

Jojo also sponsored the Creator Map and built a fully working prototype with Codex. Engineers polished it for launch shortly afterward. Jared describes the build as “incredibly quick,” thanks to its small, self-contained scope and hard deadline. He believes both the Creator Map and Programs launched with fewer bugs and more polish than they would have without Codex.

Building products is only part of running Gondola. The team also uses ChatGPT to prepare proposals, manage schedules, and find information across company systems, as well as to automate tasks.

Gondola used ChatGPT to build a daily report template that employees can use first thing in the morning to plan their day. It integrates Google Workspace, including Gmail, Calendar, Sheets, and Drive, as well as Asana, Slack, QuickBooks, weather information, and other sources to give them a comprehensive look at the day ahead.

Jared says preparing such a thorough report manually would take “hours and hours of work,” but it comes together quickly in the ChatGPT setup. A person still reviews consequential work before it’s sent externally or used to make a business decision.

Since adopting Codex in early 2026, Gondola’s lead engineer has increased monthly shipping output by about 50%, measured in merged changes. Across the team, output is up about 25%, with no change in engineering headcount. The team is also shipping larger changes, while PR review time has held steady.

Gondola reports that company revenue has more than doubled year over year, with no added payroll costs or significant overhead. The company has also helped brands hire 2.5 times as many creators year over year.

Looking ahead, Gondola wants AI to help complete more of the work that connects companies and creatives. For Programs, that could mean reducing the coordination involved in finding talent, managing budgets and approvals, handling contracts, and getting people paid.

Gondola aims to keep expanding what its small team can deliver to advance its founding mission: helping creatives get credit for their work and turn it into their next opportunity.

article_content_zh:
Gondola 帮助创意人员获得认可并获得聘用，Codex 将其首席工程师的产出提高了 50%，而 ChatGPT 则简化了日常工作。

在经营他的创意制作机构 Fresh Tape Media 时，贾里德·克莱因斯坦 (Jared Kleinstein) 注意到一个问题：人们为社交媒体制作了令人难以置信的创意作品，但制作者却没有得到适当的认可。因此，他建立了 Gondola⁠(opens in a new window) 平台，帮助创意人士展示他们的作品，证明其影响力，并将他们的作品转化为下一个机会。

对于 Gondola 的小团队来说，最大的限制之一是它可以承担多少产品和运营工作。即使是小型实验也会与核心产品优先级竞争工程时间，并且查找信息和起草工作需要筛选工具和系统。

如今，该团队使用 Codex 将更多想法转化为软件，并使用 ChatGPT 来简化日常操作。整个团队的每月工程产出增长了 25%，其首席工程师的每月工程产出增长了 50%。公司收入同比增长一倍多。对于贾里德来说，这改变了团队的可能性。

Gondola 的许多产品创意直接来自业务开发和领导团队亲眼所见的客户对话和运营问题。在 Codex 之前，他们必须定义需求并编写要求，然后等待工程师有能力构建第一个版本。

现在，同一个团队使用 Codex Cloud 来探索代码库、对界面或工作流程进行原型设计、测试假设，并且通常在工程师需要介入之前获得功能性的第一个版本。Jared 和 Gondola 的创建者和客户合作伙伴经理 Jojo Hesketh 都将他们的第一个代码贡献合并到主代码库中。

一个例子是 Programs，这是 Gondola 构建的一款工具，旨在帮助公司寻找创意、审查申请人、管理项目和跟踪预算，并制定计划来帮助协调合同和付款。

Jojo 赞助了 Programs，并使用 Codex 对其工作流程进行原型设计，然后将其交给工程师进行完善和发布。该团队从 GPT-5.4 开始，使用 GPT-5.5 完成大部分工作，并使用 GPT-6.1 进行后续功能、优化和错误修复。

Jared 估计 Codex 节省了数天甚至数周的开发时间，并且帮助团队推出的程序比手工编码的错误更少。 “程序功能受益于我们快速制作原型、扔掉不起作用的东西并保留起作用的东西的能力，”贾里德说。

Gondola 的工程师通过命令行界面 (CLI) 和编辑器工具使用 Codex 来加速实施，并在 GitHub 中审查拉取请求。该公司将 Codex 连接到其存储库、开发环境和 Slack，因此产品上下文可以为开发提供信息。工程师仍然负责架构、安全性、数据处理和生产准备。

在 Codex 之前，时间敏感的想法可能会积压在等待工程资源的状态中，而机会却在流逝。但今年夏天，Codex 使 Gondola 能够及时构建并测试世界杯创作者地图。

该团队使用 Codex 快速将已有的数据转化为满足客户即时需求的体验，创建了一张地图，使品牌、团队和机构能够在世界杯主办城市找到摄影师和摄像师。

Jojo 还赞助了 Creator Map 并使用 Codex 构建了一个完全可用的原型。工程师们对其进行了打磨，以便在不久后发布。 Jared 将构建描述为“令人难以置信的快速”，这要归功于其小而独立的范围和严格的截止日期。他相信，与没有 Codex 的情况相比，创作者地图和程序的发布错误更少，而且更加完善。

构建产品只是运行 Gondola 的一部分。该团队还使用 ChatGPT 准备提案、管理日程、跨公司系统查找信息以及自动化任务。

title: Holiday Extras is rethinking what it can build with Codex
title_en: Holiday Extras is rethinking what it can build with Codex
author: OpenAI 官方动态
article_content:
With Codex, Holiday Extras is turning customer expertise into better apps, higher booking conversion and new possibilities for growth.

increase in open-to-book conversion on the rebuilt Holiday Extras app.

reduction in app error rate, from 19% to 9%.

Holiday Extras⁠(opens in a new window) helps customers search, book and manage trips. For CEO Matthew Pack, becoming an AI-based travel technology business means changing how the whole organisation works: giving the people who understand customers and operations the ability to improve them directly.

Company-wide ChatGPT Enterprise access established the foundation. Codex extended it into building software, from customer-facing apps to internal systems. Pack builds with Codex himself, using that experience to understand what colleagues need and raise his expectations of what the business can achieve.

Holiday Extras had spent years developing its mobile apps⁠(opens in a new window). Major changes to its main app centred on an annual release. With Codex, it challenged itself to rethink the experience and how it was built.

Within two weeks, the team had a fully working rebuild, achieving development progress that previously would have taken over six months. Liam Thompson, VP of AI Innovation and formerly Head of Design, worked with engineers to translate his understanding of customers into software. Small, documented packages created reusable foundations, while engineers focused on architecture, APIs, security and development workflows.

The rebuilt app offered a more personal experience informed by customers’ bookings, trips and history. Codex enabled iOS and Android features to be developed together, bringing improvements to both platforms without Android following behind.

Higher conversion: open-to-book conversion on the main app increased 32.5% following the rebuild.

Fewer errors: the main app’s error rate fell from 19% to 9%.

More frequent improvements: the main app moved from an annual major release to weekly releases in the first month after the rebuild, each containing multiple new features.

Faster iteration: Countdown moved from adding a feature roughly every six months to multiple additions a week.

Conversion and error-rate results compare the previous and rebuilt main app across different periods.

Faster development also gives customers more influence. When a Countdown customer complained about a missing list view, an agent prepared a fix. Liam Thompson approved it, the update was submitted and the customer changed their one-star review to five stars.

The same emphasis on acting on customer insight extends into operations. David Lee, Director of Innovation and Growth, describes an automated system that turns airport-transfer customer chats into actionable tickets, helping the team identify problems across its supplier network. Customer insight becomes work the team can act on.

Matthew Pack describes giving everyone permission to try AI, then actively encouraging them to use it. That permission comes with guardrails. Employees have access and encouragement to experiment; engineers build the packages, security controls and workflows that make that experimentation practical.

David Lee sees the effect in an experienced accountant who rebuilt finance systems around his understanding of the business and feedback from colleagues. The opportunity reaches beyond learning to code: people can apply years of operational knowledge directly to the tools they use. Leadership’s role is to make that possible, support experimentation and help successful ideas spread.

Holiday Extras values Codex’s ability to explore ideas, reason through complex problems, propose a plan and deliver independently. Liam Thompson describes being able to question an approach and receive suggestions throughout the work.

The wider partnership connects building with everyday work. ChatGPT Enterprise supports employees across the business, while OpenAI models power the app’s personalised experience. dots adds coordination and insight: Thompson recalls his dot proactively preparing a performance report after an app launch. David Lee values model quality and efficiency alongside the relationship behind the products.

Pack’s ambition is for more of Holiday Extras’ systems to be administered through AI, with employees directing the work and shaping the outcomes. The app rebuild demonstrates the potential: better booking performance, fewer errors and capacity to keep improving.

That gives Holiday Extras a new basis for deciding which opportunities to pursue across its products and markets. As more people can act on their expertise, Pack is asking the leadership team to reconsider the scale of its ambitions.

Product updates, practical guides, upcoming events, and more.

title: CoreWeave Plans to Raise at Least $4 Billion in High-Grade Loan
title_en: CoreWeave Plans to Raise at Least $4 Billion in High-Grade Loan
author: Jeannine Amodeo
content_snippet: CoreWeave Inc. plans to raise at least $4 billion through an investment-grade loan offering after the AI computing supplier boosted …
summary_en: GPU cloud provider CoreWeave plans to launch a $4 billion+ investment-grade loan next week to replace expensive junk bonds with cheaper capital. This move aims to sustain its aggressive Nvidia GPU infrastructure expansion while optimizing the company's capital structure amidst soaring AI demand.
title_zh: 算力独角兽CoreWeave拟筹资40亿美元
summary_zh: GPU云服务商CoreWeave计划下周发行超40亿美元投资级贷款，以更低成本进一步扩大算力基建规模
article_content_zh:
CoreWeave此次计划通过投资级贷款筹集至少40亿美元，相比此前发行的垃圾债（Junk Bonds），其利率预计将腰斩至7%至7.5%左右。这一财务动作凸显了其作为AI基础设施供应方的强大议价能力。

在AI模型竞逐导致GPU资源极度匮乏的背景下，CoreWeave通过与英伟达的深度绑定，成功将自己包装成了能够提供稳定现金流的资本宠儿。此举旨在降低资金成本，从而为下一阶段更大规模的数据中心布局提供长期弹药。

title: Sources: Howard Lutnick has stalled curbs on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia chips to China; Trump approved them for the third time this year on Nov. 5 (Axios)
title_en: Sources: Howard Lutnick has stalled curbs on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia chips to China; Trump approved them for the third time this year on Nov. 5 (Axios)
author: Axios
content_snippet: President Trump on Thursday authorized a crack down on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China …
summary_en: President Trump approved sanctions against companies suspected of diverting Nvidia chips to China three times since November 5th, but Howard Lutnick has repeatedly stalled their implementation. This delay highlights a power struggle within the transition team, balancing national security rhetoric against the commercial interests of financial allies.
title_zh: 卢特尼克阻拦芯片禁令生效
summary_zh: 特朗普三度批准针对向中国转移英伟达芯片企业的制裁，但被过渡团队负责人卢特尼克多次搁置

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 特朗普已于11月5日及后续三次批准对涉嫌向中国转移英伟达芯片的企业实施制裁，但负责过渡事务的卢特尼克利用职务之便持续阻挠相关行政令落地。此举旨在维护华尔街资本与部分科技企业的商业利益，令行政权的执行与过渡期的权力博弈陷入僵局。

title: Sources: Scott Bessent confronted Howard Lutnick last week over the Commerce Dept. not adding Megaspeed to the Entity List; Commerce denies the confrontation (Axios)
title_en: Sources: Scott Bessent confronted Howard Lutnick last week over the Commerce Dept. not adding Megaspeed to the Entity List; Commerce denies the confrontation (Axios)
author: Axios
content_snippet: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over a failure to place Nvidia customer Megaspeed …
summary_en: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick last week over the failure to add Megaspeed to the Entity List. The Commerce Department has since denied the confrontation occurred, highlighting internal friction regarding the implementation of tech export controls.
title_zh: 美国财政与商务部长爆发内阁争吵
summary_zh: 财政部长贝森特因不满商务部长卢特尼克未将Megaspeed列入实体清单而当面质询，商务部对此予以否认

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 财政部长贝森特近日当面质询商务部长卢特尼克，指责后者未将特定科技企业Megaspeed纳入出口管制实体清单。商务部随后否认了此次冲突的发生，这显示出特朗普政府内部在科技封锁与贸易政策执行力度上的严重不合。
